# SS14 fork feature catalog

What each fork in the ecosystem built on top of Wizard's Den, where it lives in their
tree, and — for the 298 units assessed so far — what it does to a round.
A row says a fork *has* the feature; only the shortlist says anything about taking it.

27 forks · 132 features · 803 authored · 680 vendored from another fork · 298 assessed · 29 verified takes

Portability is measured, not assumed. An independent pass re-read 289
assessments trying to refute them and corrected the graft shape of 41,
including eight of the ten features first judged self-contained. The cause is a limit of
the path data: it indexes the directories a fork *claims*, so it cannot see upstream files
a fork edits in place. Treat an unverified portability claim as a hypothesis.

● the fork authored it &nbsp;&nbsp; ○ the fork vendored it from another fork

Generated by `Tools/graft/build_markdown.py`. Edit `fork-features.yml`, not this file.

## Shortlist

22 features (29 fork implementations) of 298 assessed,
through two narrow filters. Every one was
re-read by a second agent whose job was to refute it, and nothing gets in on an
unverified claim. On top of that a feature has to be somewhere this server wants to
go, which is judgement and lives in `fit.yml` rather than being inferred.

### Take now

Verified as genuinely self-contained: the files live entirely under the fork's own namespace and nothing has to be patched upstream to make them work.

**[Server rules, space law and SOP guidebook](#guidebook-rules-and-sop) — corvax, cosmatic-drift, funky, gaby-station-now-dumont-station, goobstation, harmony-station, impstation, monolith, rmc14, serbia-strong, sunrise, viva-station**

*loop-change · drop-in · high confidence · 11 forks carry it*

Opening the in-game guidebook gives players a full shelf of server-written reference material instead of just upstream's mechanical guides: numbered server rules (Cosmatic Drift's Rule 1.0 through 3.9, Harmony's R0-R8 and S1-S3), a written space/corporate law codebook listing named offences with sentences, and a Standard Operating Procedure tree split department by department and often job by job (Funky Station has separate SOP pages for Captain, HoP, Warden, Detective, Chemist, Paramedic, Roboticist, Bartender, Mime, and so on, plus a page per alert level explaining what Green through Delta actually authorise). Security and Command can look up the charge or the procedure mid-round rather than arguing from memory, and a new player can read the server's actual expectations before their first shift. Viva Station goes further with a Command-only hidden SOP: the pages exist but are metashielded, and your character only "knows" them once you physically find a head of staff's issued guidebook, with higher-clearance books unlocking more of the document, which is what gives an RP-led riot something concrete to be leaking. Sunrise and RMC-14 attach onboarding on top of the text (a guided tutorial and new-player popups), which is a much larger build than the documentation itself.

- **Take** — It is pure content in fork-namespaced XML plus guideEntry prototypes, and it is the cheapest way to make Security and Command play to a codified law and procedure instead of improvising a different standard every shift.
- **Skip** — None of the text is yours: SOP, space law and numbered rules only work if they describe your server's actual policy, so grafting is really a rewrite of every page plus permanent upkeep as your rules drift, and nothing here is mechanically enforced.
- **Touches** — all-players, security, command, service, medical, engineering, cargo, science
- **Verified** — supported. Every checkable specific held up: CD's guides.ftl lists exactly Rule 1.0-3.9 plus per-department SOP and a crimes list; Harmony's guides.ftl lists exactly R0-R8 and S1-S3; Funky's sop.yml defines per-job guideEntry pages for every job named (Captain, HoP, Warden, Detective, Chemist, Paramedic, Roboticist, Bartender, Mime) plus Green-through-Delta alert pages whose XML (GreenAlert.xml) does spell out what is authorised; Corvax's CorporateLaw dir has numbered offence chapters plus Punishments.xml/CrimeList.xml; Viva's CommandHiddenStandardOperatingProcedure.xml states verbatim the metashield and the three clearance tiers unlocked by finding specific heads' guidebooks (worth knowing: enforcement is AHelp/admin convention, not a mechanic, which the claim's "metashielded" framing correctly implies); Sunrise has _Sunrise/Tutorial and RMC-14 has _RMC14/NewPlayer, backing the onboarding aside. Drop-in is confirmed at the mechanism level: upstream GuidebookWindow.GetSortedEntries computes roots as all entries ExceptWith children, so parentless fork-namespaced guideEntry prototypes (like Funky's SOP101) surface as top-level guidebook roots with zero upstream edits. One small practical trim: Funky's sop.yml references an OctarineAlert page and alert-level-octarine locale key from its cosmic-cult port, and Violet/Octarine alert levels are fork-specific, so a graft drops or rewrites those child entries — content pruning, not entanglement.

**[Cosmic cult](#cosmic-cult) — deltav**

*structural · drop-in · high confidence · 3 forks carry it*

A team of converted crew quietly drains "entropy" from living people (a touch that steals a bit of their health over time), carries it back to an invisible Monument hidden somewhere on the station, and feeds it in to grow the Monument through three stages. Each stage unlocks new powers the cult buys individually — freezing someone in place, blasting doors open, going invisible as a floating spirit, becoming immune to vacuum, healing near the Monument — plus chalk glyphs that convert bystanders standing on them, turn spacesuits into cult armour, turn knives into cult weapons, and turn a portable scrubber into a spire that eats the room's air. Cultists who find and absorb the rifts that start appearing become permanently empowered and can trap a borg in a shell that hatches into a huge Entropic Colossus, or overwrite the station AI's laws to serve the cult; the crew fights back with mindshields, the chaplain's bible and a censer that deconverts, and if the cult finishes the final ritual at the fully-powered Monument the station is destroyed and the round ends.

- **Take** — It is a complete, fully documented round type with its own escalation curve, counterplay and losing condition — a whole alternate way for a shift to go, not another uplink antag.
- **Skip** — It is roughly 300 files of bespoke systems (monument, glyphs, transmutation, influences, astral forms, colossus mob, AI lawset corruption, borg capture) that hooks mindshields, bibles, the AI upload console and borg chassis, so it is a permanent maintenance surface that will fight every upstream merge touching those systems.
- **Touches** — antagonist, all-players, security, epistemics, science, chaplain, silicon, command, ghost-roles
- **Verified** — supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. The gameplay description (entropy siphon, three-stage Monument, purchasable influences, glyph conversion/transmutation, deconversion via censer/bible/mindshield, Colossus mob, AI-law/borg corruption, station-destroying final ritual) is directly confirmed by the guidebook XML and prototype/system files I fetched myself. But the graft_shape verdict is overclaimed: a full recursive tree search of the DeltaV repo (299 cosmic/cult-tagged paths) found zero files outside _DV namespace directories, and reading the actual C# (DeconversionSystem.cs, CosmicFragmentationSystem.cs) shows the 'hooks' into mindshields/bible/borg/AI-laws are done entirely via SubscribeLocalEvent from the fork's own self-contained files consuming stable, already-existing upstream components/events — no upstream file was edited to register or wire in the feature (registration itself, e.g. game_presets.yml, is also under _DV). That is much closer to the seed's original 'drop-in' than the assessor's downgrade suggests, with the caveat that it is a large, deeply-coupled maintenance surface if those upstream APIs ever change shape.
  - unsupported: "needs-upstream-edits" as the graft_shape: the repo tree (299 files matched, all under _DV directories; zero non-_DV files mention "cosmic" anywhere in the repo) shows the feature is 100% self-contained with no upstream files edited to wire it in, contradicting the 'fork-patches-upstream' reading entirely
  - unsupported: The framing that it 'hooks mindshields, bibles, the AI upload console and borg chassis' implies edits to those systems; in fact the actual C# (DeconversionSystem.cs, CosmicFragmentationSystem.cs) shows it only subscribes to pre-existing upstream events/components (MindShieldComponent, BibleComponent, BorgChassisComponent, SiliconLawUpdaterComponent, AILawUpdatedEvent) from its own _DV files — the upstream files themselves (MindShieldSystem.cs, BibleSystem.cs) contain zero references to CosmicCult and are completely unmodified

**[Alternate round types](#alternate-round-types) — serbia-strong**

*structural · drop-in · medium confidence · 1 forks carry it*

Dead players and observers can open an "Arena Lobby" window listing the fights currently running, then create or join one: you get pulled into a small randomly-picked arena map with a randomly-assigned kit, wait out a countdown while barriers hold you apart, and then fight until one side is left standing or the five-minute timer calls a draw, with winners announced over an arena channel. Lobby slots are sorted into duel, creative, social and misc categories and can be one-on-one or small teams, so it works as a parallel side activity for people who are out of the round rather than something the station notices. Separately, the fork ships whole-round faction war events on their own maps, where NT, USSP and Iron Squad crews fly out on faction shuttles, plant and pull each other's flags on capture pedestals over a fifteen-second struggle, earn points for every stretch of time they hold a pedestal, and score a big lump for blowing up an enemy shuttle's console, alongside a handful of themed event maps (a snow holiday village, an orbital village, a cooking event, a rift map).

- **Take** — It solves the two hardest problems at once: dead players get a real, repeatable thing to do instead of orbiting, and the faction-war half gives you a complete team-versus-team event round (capture points, faction shuttles, scoring) you can run on a slow night.
- **Skip** — Every SS220 file here carries a custom EULA/CLA header with a hosting restriction rather than the usual MIT/AGPL, so grafting it into an AGPL fork is a licensing problem before it is an engineering one; on top of that the faction war is only as good as its bespoke maps and shuttles, which you would have to maintain and rebalance yourself.
- **Touches** — ghost-roles, all-players, antagonist, security, admins-and-event-hosts
- **Verified** — supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. Gameplay is unusually well-supported: arena.ftl confirms the lobby verb/window, duel/creative/social/misc categories, countdown, and draw/timeout text; ArenaRuleComponent.cs confirms MaxFightDuration=300s (exactly "five-minute timer") and barrier/countdown fields; ArenaFightBarrierComponent and the ghost-role locale ("has no connection to the station... any interaction outside the arena is prohibited") back the "side activity, station doesn't notice" framing; arena_gamerule.yml + Arenas/*.yml (2v2, 3v3, single maps) confirm "one-on-one or small teams". FractWar checks out equally precisely: EventCapturePointComponent.cs has FlagManipulationDuration=15s exactly matching "fifteen-second struggle" and RetentionTimeForWinPoint=15s for the hold-points mechanic; ShuttleConsolePointsComponent/System confirms PointsOnDestroy=500 for "a big lump" on console kill; the tree shows dedicated NT.yml/USSP.yml/IronSquad.yml faction shuttles and ai_factions.yml with EbentUssp/EbentNanoTrasen/EbentIronSquad, confirming the three-faction claim even though none of the 5 cited evidence files show the faction names directly. All four named theme maps (GorgosiaSnowHoliday.yml, GoladraOrbVillage.yml, CookingEventMap.yml, RiftEventMap.yml) exist verbatim. One overclaim outside the gameplay text: skip_because says "Every SS220 file here carries a custom EULA/CLA header" but Content.Shared/SS220/FractWar/ShuttleConsolePointsComponent.cs (one of the 5 cited files) has no such header at all — it starts directly with a using statement. On graft_shape: I found the FractWar round type registered as a `gamePreset` entirely inside the fork's own Resources/Prototypes/SS220/game_presets.yml, with zero matches for "arena"/"fractwar" in the upstream Resources/Prototypes/game_presets.yml — i.e. the fork did not patch that upstream file in place. Every file I found for this feature (Content.Server/Shared/Client/SS220/{Arena,FractWar,EventCapturePoint}, Resources/{Locale,Prototypes,Maps}/*/ss220/...) lives under the fork's own SS220 namespace, and SS14 prototypes/systems are reflection-discovered rather than centrally registered, so there's no positive evidence integration would even require upstream edits. This contradicts the claim's downgrade to needs-upstream-edits; the seed's drop-in call holds up better than the claim being tested.

**[Role slot management and join queue](#role-slots-and-join-queue) — cosmatic-drift**

*loop-change · drop-in · medium confidence · 6 forks carry it*

Command gets a "Job Slots Console" they can walk up to and use mid-round: a searchable list of every job on the station, each row showing the job's icon, its name and how many slots are still open, with plus and minus buttons to open another seat or close one off. So the Head of Personnel can add a second engineer slot when the department is drowning, or shut the last security slot so no more latejoiners can take it. Certain jobs are locked and just show a "this job's slots cannot be adjusted" tooltip, and using the console without the right ID access gets you a rejection buzz instead. Separately, on the join side the server can reserve seats for whitelisted players: once the general (non-whitelist) slots are all taken, an unwhitelisted player trying to connect is told the open slots are currently full and to try rejoining later.

- **Take** — Gives command a real in-world lever over station staffing instead of leaving the latejoin roster fixed at round start, and the whitelist-slot condition lets a busy server keep seats for its regulars without hard-closing the door.
- **Skip** — The unit ships no prototypes at all, so the console entity, its machine board and its placement in an office have to be authored and mapped in yourself before a player ever sees it, and handing HoP the power to close job slots invites round-souring griefing that you then have to write policy for.
- **Touches** — command, all-players, server-operators
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. Every file touched by this feature — C# (Server/Client/Shared), locale, prototypes, and even the maps that place the console — lives under _CD namespaces/directories; nothing outside the fork's own tree was found for it. The whitelist half plugs into an upstream extension point (WhitelistCondition is `[ImplicitDataDefinitionForInheritors]` in vanilla space-wizards/space-station-14, confirmed by fetching the same path from upstream) rather than editing an upstream file. The claim's downgrade to needs-upstream-edits rested on the false premise that no prototypes ship; a git tree/grep of the actual repo shows a full entity+board+flatpack+map chain already exists, so the seed's drop-in path-data read was actually correct here.
  - unsupported: "The unit ships no prototypes at all, so the console entity, its machine board and its placement in an office have to be authored and mapped in yourself before a player ever sees it" — false. The fork ships a complete, wired entity prototype (Resources/Prototypes/_CD/Entities/Structures/Machines/Computers/computers.yml, id ComputerJobSlots, parent BaseComputerAiAccess, AccessReader restricted to HeadOfPersonnel, JobSlotsConsole component with a real blacklist), a matching circuitboard (Resources/Prototypes/_CD/Entities/Objects/Devices/Circuitboards/computer.yml, id JobSlotsComputerCircuitboard), a portable flatpack variant (Resources/Prototypes/_CD/Entities/Objects/Devices/flatpack.yml, id JobSlotsComputerFlatpack) and a tabletop variant (tabletopcomputer.yml, ComputerTabletopJobSlots) — and it is already placed on three of the fork's live station maps (Resources/Maps/_CD/cluster.yml, gemini.yml, aspid.yml).

**[Baseline midround antagonists](#upstream-midround-antags) — serbia-strong**

*loop-change · drop-in · medium confidence · 1 forks carry it*

Adds a stealth objective for the space ninja: go the whole round without ever being seen. Whenever the ninja is uncloaked, out of a locker and standing in clear line of sight of a living crewmember within about twelve tiles, their own screen starts breaking up with a glitching reveal warning that builds over five seconds; duck behind a wall, cloak, or climb into a container before it fills and the warning fades and the timer resets. Let it complete once and the objective is failed for good, so a ninja playing this one has to treat every corridor sightline as a hard fail state rather than something to shrug off. Ghosts and observers watching do not count against them.

- **Take** — It turns the ninja from a hit-and-run raider into a genuine ghost, and the escalating on-screen glitch gives the player real, readable tension instead of a silent pass/fail check.
- **Skip** — It is a one-strike objective with no partial credit, so a single unlucky latejoiner walking round a corner early can dead-end the ninja's round; you would also be porting a custom screen shader and a per-second line-of-sight scan whose cost scales with nearby players.
- **Touches** — antagonist, all-players
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. All 5 cited C# files sit inside SS220 namespace directories and only reference upstream extension points (StealthComponent, GhostComponent, IdentityComponent, ContainerSystem, ExamineSystemShared, the generic ObjectiveAfterAssignEvent/ObjectiveGetProgressEvent hooks) rather than editing them. The objective's own prototype entry lives in a separate fork-owned file, Resources/Prototypes/SS220/Objectives/ninja.yml (bracketed by \"# Imperial/SS220 start/end\" comments), parenting upstream BaseNinjaObjective/BaseCodeObjective purely by composition — the upstream file Resources/Prototypes/Objectives/ninja.yml itself is untouched. Crucially, that same upstream file documents that ninja objectives are not drawn from a weighted-random pool the way Traitor/Thief objectives are (verified: Resources/Prototypes/Objectives/objectiveGroups.yml has Traitor/Thief groups extensively SS220-edited in place, but zero Ninja group) — instead \"all [ninja] objectives are picked,\" so a new RoleRequirement:NinjaRole prototype is auto-included with no wiring step. That undercuts the claim's needs-upstream-edits downgrade of the drop-in seed.
  - unsupported: "standing in clear line of sight of a living crewmember" — SharedLeaveNoTraceSystem.EntitySeesNinja only excludes GhostComponent (`if (HasComp<GhostComponent>(entity)) return false;`); it never checks MobState/alive status, so a corpse or SSD body with an IdentityComponent in unoccluded range would also trigger the reveal timer. "Living" is not something the code verifies.
  - unsupported: graft_shape: "needs-upstream-edits" is asserted with an empty depends_on array and no upstream file cited as evidence — internally inconsistent, and contradicted by what the base prototype itself documents: Resources/Prototypes/Objectives/ninja.yml's BaseNinjaObjective carries the comment "difficulty isn't used since all objectives are picked," meaning any RoleRequirement:NinjaRole objective (which LeaveNoTraceObjective inherits) is automatically assigned to every ninja with no registration list to edit anywhere.

**[Player-authored documents and books](#player-authored-text) — corvax**

*activity · drop-in · high confidence · 11 forks carry it*

A document printer sits in offices as a paper-fed machine: you feed it blank paper, slot your ID card into it, and pick from a menu of about sixty ready-made Nanotrasen forms — situation reports, employment and dismissal statements, access and weapon-carry permits, search warrants, death and marriage certificates, indictments and sentences, euthanasia and shuttle requests. The printed sheet comes out already filled in with your name, your job title, the station name and the current station time, so you only write the actual content and stamp it. It also ships department stamps for the Internal Affairs Agent and the Magistrate, a legal-department pen, and a shelf of in-universe lore books players can read. Emagging the printer unlocks a handful of joke/hostile forms like liquidation notices and a declaration of military action.

- **Take** — It turns "write a form on blank paper" roleplay into a one-click, pre-filled bureaucratic workflow, giving lawyers, IAAs, command and clerks a real prop library instead of freehand typing.
- **Skip** — Every one of the ~60 form bodies and all the lore books exist only as Russian locale strings — en-US has just the four substitution tags — so grafting it means writing sixty documents of English bureaucratic prose yourself and then maintaining them.
- **Touches** — command, security, service, all-players
- **Verified** — supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. Every gameplay specific checks out: printer.yml has MaterialStorage(Document tag)+ItemSlots(IdCard), DocumentPrinterSystem.cs substitutes doc-var-date/station/name/job exactly as described, CorvaxDocumentsPack has 59 recipes (matches "about sixty") spanning reports/certificates/permits/indictments named as claimed, CorvaxEmagDocumentsPack has 5 joke recipes including NoticeOfLiquidation and NoteBeginningMilitaryActions, rubber_stamp.yml has RubberStampIAA and RubberStampMagistrate, pen.yml has PenLegal, books.yml has a dozen+ BookLoreBase lore entries. The skip_because claim is exactly confirmed: en-US/corvax/paper/ contains only doc-printer-tags.ftl (4 tag lines), while ru-RU/corvax/paper/ has the real doc-printer.ftl, books-lore.ftl, book-busido.ftl, book-rulebook.ftl content files. Where the claim is shakier is graft_shape: every file I found (Content.Shared/Corvax/Documents/DocumentPrinterComponent.cs, Content.Server/Corvax/Documents/DocumentPrinterSystem.cs, all the Resources/Prototypes/Corvax/* yml, Resources/Locale/*/corvax/paper/*) sits inside Corvax-namespaced paths with zero upstream-directory files touched, and I found no evidence that wiring it into another codebase requires editing any upstream file (it just references generic BaseLathe/Paper/IdCard/ItemSlots APIs). The claim's own justification for "needs-upstream-edits" is a translation/content-authoring burden (60 documents untranslated), not a code-integration dependency on upstream files, so it conflates two different senses of "graft cost." Structurally this reads as drop-in with a large content-completeness caveat, not as needs-upstream-edits in the taxonomy's own terms.

**[Tape recorder and cassettes](#tape-recorder) — cosmatic-drift, deltav, goobstation, rmc14, starlight, sunrise**

*activity · drop-in · high confidence · 5 forks carry it*

A pocket-sized tape recorder that you load with a cassette and switch between Record, Playback, Rewind and Pause from a small on-item menu. While recording it picks up anything spoken within a few tiles and writes it to the tape (about two minutes per side), timestamped with the speaker's name; voices it cannot identify come back as "Unknown" or "Unintelligible", and damaged stretches play back as garbled fragments. Hit Playback and the recorder speaks the conversation back out loud to everyone nearby, or hit "Print record transcript" and it spits out a paper transcript you can hand to security, post in the bar, or wave at the captain. Tapes can be ejected and swapped (though not while it's running), and a tape that gets unspooled has to be wound back in with a pen or screwdriver before it works again. RMC-14's take splits this into a speech recorder that prints reports plus a separate cassette player that plays music tracks.

- **Take** — It turns spoken roleplay into a physical, stealable, forgeable object, giving security real evidence, journalists real quotes and traitors a real reason to smash a tape.
- **Skip** — It quietly records everything nearby, so you inherit the moderation and consent headaches of persistent speech logs plus the ongoing cost of keeping the listener hooks working through upstream speech/radio refactors.
- **Touches** — security, service, command, all-players
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. Fetched the actual C# sources (Content.Server/_CD/TapeRecorder/TapeRecorderSystem.cs, Content.Shared/_CD/TapeRecorder/Components/*.cs) behind the cited YAML/FTL evidence: every file lives under the fork's own _CD namespace, and the system only SubscribeLocalEvent's on ListenEvent, plus consumes ActiveListenerComponent, VoiceOverrideComponent, ChatSystem and PaperSystem — all of which I confirmed exist as stock upstream (space-wizards/space-station-14) types, not fork additions. No upstream file is patched by the fork's own copy, and nothing in the code requires editing an upstream file to wire it up (it just needs those already-standard hooks to exist, which any SS14-derived fork has). That contradicts the claim's downgrade to needs-upstream-edits; the seed's drop-in read holds up better against the evidence.
  - unsupported: "about two minutes per side" — TapeCassetteComponent.cs sets MaxCapacity = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(120) as a single continuous capacity with one CurrentPosition float and one RecordedData/Buffer list; there is no A/B-side mechanic (no flip action, no second buffer) in the code. The "on either side" phrasing is flavor text on the entity description only, not a coded two-sides system, so "two minutes per side" overstates total capacity (it reads as up to ~4 minutes, when the actual cap is 2 minutes total).

**[Mech and exosuit overhaul](#mech-overhaul) — backmen, frontier, gaby-station-now-dumont-station, monolith, serbia-strong**

*activity · drop-in · medium confidence · 3 forks carry it*

These forks bolt extra hardware onto the mechs the game already has rather than rebuilding piloting. Cargo gets the biggest win: a forklift attachment lets a pilot spend mech power to scoop up to five crates, lockers or vending machines into the suit with a short hydraulic whine and set them back down beside the mech, and one fork adds a wearable powered exosuit with its own control panel and a "Lift cargo" action so a worker can haul heavy objects without climbing into a full chassis. Elsewhere you get a two-seat Space Buoy escape pod that flies well in vacuum and handles badly under gravity, a bolt-on air recycler module that burns mech battery to make oxygen and scrub toxins so a pilot can sit in a breach longer, buildable control and targeting boards for extra combat chassis, and a pilot mech whose mounted guns are driven from a proper "Mech weapons" hands panel instead of the generic equipment list.

- **Take** — The forklift and cargo-lifting exosuit give cargo and salvage a genuinely new physical job loop (moving crates, lockers and vendors around the station) using a chassis the game already ships.
- **Skip** — This is five unrelated bolt-ons from five forks rather than one coherent system, and the listed files are visibly incomplete (the fork equipment entity, its toggle action prototype and the construction graphs consuming the Monolith board tags all live outside this unit), so grafting any one piece means chasing prototypes and sprites the file list does not name.
- **Touches** — cargo, engineering, science, security
- **Needs** — [exotic-gas-expansion](#exotic-gas-expansion)
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. Every file I fetched (backmen's vova-mech.ftl, frontier's MechForkComponent.cs and mech.ftl, dumont's SpaceBuoy pod, monolith's Broadsword/Flail control-and-targeting electronics, serbia-strong's SS220 mech actions) sits inside that fork's own namespaced directory (_backmen, _NF, _Gabystation, _Mono, SS220), matching the seed's path-data drop-in signal. The claim's downgrade to needs-upstream-edits leans on a companion file (the toggle-action prototype) it says 'lives outside this unit' — but when I fetched that exact file it turned out to be Resources/Prototypes/_NF/Actions/mech.yml, still inside frontier's own _NF tree, not an upstream directory. That means the stated reasoning describes an incomplete evidence list within the fork's own namespace, not a genuine fork-patches-upstream or wiring-requires-upstream-edits situation, so I could not confirm either upstream_reading option; the concrete gameplay specifics (forklift MaxContents=5 and hydraulic-whine sound, MechAirRecycler's battery-for-oxygen description, Space Buoy's vacuum-good/gravity-bad text, Broadsword/Flail control+targeting modules, SS220's Control Panel/Lift cargo actions) all check out against the raw files.
  - unsupported: "the fork equipment entity, its toggle action prototype and the construction graphs consuming the Monolith board tags all live outside this unit" (used to justify graft_shape: needs-upstream-edits) — I fetched the toggle action prototype directly at Resources/Prototypes/_NF/Actions/mech.yml (ActionMechForkToggleInsert) and it lives inside frontier's own _NF namespace, not an upstream directory. The files are missing from the cited evidence list, but that's an evidence-completeness gap within the fork's own tree, not proof of an upstream-editing dependency.
  - unsupported: "a pilot mech whose mounted guns are driven from a proper \"Mech weapons\" hands panel instead of the generic equipment list" — the only cited file (vova-mech.ftl) contains a single locale string `bkm-vova-mech-hands-label = Mech weapons`; that confirms the label text but not the specific claim that this replaces/differs from 'the generic equipment list' UI behavior.

**[Rideable vehicles](#rideable-vehicles) — serbia-strong**

*activity · drop-in · medium confidence · 3 forks carry it*

You climb onto a vehicle the way you'd strap into a chair, then drive it around the station with a horn you can sound as you go; some vehicles won't move unless a key has been left in them, and the rider is drawn sitting on top of or behind the frame depending on which way it faces. Wheelchairs run on the same handling, with a deliberately slower struggle to get back out of one. The other half is hitching: walk a cart or trailer up to something that tows, right-click to attach it, and after a brief moment it's locked on, so nobody can yank it loose or fold it up until someone spends that same moment unhitching it, and a heavier cart visibly drags on whoever is towing it.

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 4 forks carry it*

Engineers get a nuclear reactor as an alternative to the station's usual engine: a big vessel whose interior is a grid you physically fill in, slotting fuel rods, control rods, heat exchangers and gas channel pieces into a 5x5 or 7x7 layout, then piping cool gas in one side and running the hot gas out into a gas turbine that spins up and feeds the power grid. The control computer lets you flip between temperature, neutron and fuel views of the grid and raise or lower the control rods, and it will yell at you as the core climbs past dangerous into critical, with the reactor visibly smoking, catching fire, then triggering a station-wide meltdown announcement telling everyone to evacuate; a melted reactor fuses to the hull and cannot be unbolted. The turbine is its own maintenance job, with blades and stators that accumulate stress and damage, overspeed and stall warnings, welder repairs, and a failure mode where it tears itself apart and fires blade shrapnel across the room. Spent fuel goes into a centrifuge that reprocesses it into plutonium, and there are salvage-flavoured variants plus procedurally generated reactor complexes for crews to find derelict.

- **Take** — It is a genuinely deep, hands-on engine with a build-your-own-core puzzle, a real maintenance loop on the turbine, and a spectacular failure mode, all sitting in its own fork-namespaced folder rather than woven through upstream power code.
- **Skip** — The centrifuge (and likely more of the reactor) is a port from Goonstation carrying a CC-BY-NC-SA-3.0 header, which is non-commercial and does not sit cleanly alongside an AGPL fork licence, and beyond that it needs new sprites, new ores/materials (bohrum, cerenkite), guidebook pages, damage modifier sets and a map that actually has room for a reactor hall before any player sees it.
- **Touches** — engineering, atmospherics, cargo, salvage
- **Verified** — supported. Every specific gameplay beat checked out against the actual files: 5x5/7x7 grid prefabs with fuel rods/control rods/heat exchangers/gas channels (nuclear_reactor_prefabs.yml), temperature/neutron/fuel view toggle and control-rod raise/lower (nuclear-reactor.ftl, DeviceLinkSink InsertControlRods/RetractControlRods), dangerous->critical->smoke->fire->station-wide meltdown announcement telling people to evacuate (nuclear-reactor.ftl messages), melted reactor fused to the hull ("You cannot unanchor... it's melted into the hull!"), turbine blade/stator stress+damage+overspeed/stall+welder repair+explode-into-shrapnel (gas-turbine.ftl + GasTurbineBladeShrapnel projectile entity), spent fuel -> centrifuge -> plutonium (NuclearCentrifugeComponent.cs), salvage variants (NuclearReactorNormalSalvage etc.), and procedurally generated derelict reactor complexes (dungeon_presets.yml room packs ReactorBox/Long/Star/Double + Maps/_FarHorizons/Dungeon/Reactor). Nothing in the gameplay paragraph goes beyond what the files show. On graft shape: I cloned the repo and confirmed the license concern is real and verbatim ("Ported and modified from goonstation... CC-BY-NC-SA-3.0" in NuclearCentrifugeComponent.cs), so that part of skip_because is solid. I also confirmed every file for this feature (materials, sprites, guidebook pages, damage modifier sets, and even the fork's own parallel station map copies) lives under _FarHorizons namespaces only, i.e. Far Horizons itself never edits an upstream file in place - it forks its own full copies of station maps (Stations/Cog.yml, Manor.yml, meta.yml, etc.) rather than patching the vanilla ones. So the fork's own copy is self-contained (not fork-patches-upstream); the "needs-upstream-edits" label is earned because using this as an actual station engine (not just a derelict find) means a target fork must edit its OWN station maps to carve out a reactor hall, exactly the kind of upstream-adjacent map surgery Far Horizons already had to do for itself. One caveat worth flagging even though it doesn't rise to a gameplay-text overclaim: skip_because lists "new sprites, new ores/materials, guidebook pages, damage modifier sets" as outstanding costs, but I found all of these already fully built inside the fork's namespace (complete animated turbine/reactor .rsi sprite sheets, Bohrum/Cerenkite/Plutonium material defs, 5 guidebook XML pages, a StructuralReactorCasing damage set) - a graft would port these wholesale rather than create them from scratch. The map-room requirement is the one skip_because item that's genuinely still open.

**[Spreading fire](#spreading-fire-system) — ephemeral-space**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 2 forks carry it*

Fire becomes a thing that sits on the floor and creeps: a burning tile crackles with its own flame sprite and sound, slows anyone who walks through it, scorches the floor with burn marks, and once a second tries to jump to a neighbouring tile, preferring tiles that are already hot and skipping ones with no oxygen or nothing flammable to catch. Flames come in four visible intensities and burn themselves down as they spread, eventually smouldering to a weaker flame or dying out on their own, so a blaze that gets going grows into a wandering front the crew has to cut off rather than a single fire they stand next to and extinguish. Anything that triggers, from a thrown incendiary to a rigged device, can drop a fire of a chosen intensity, and every fire remembers who started it, so an arsonist's whole spreading blaze is traceable back to them.

- **Take** — It turns fire from a per-entity status effect into a spatial hazard that moves through the station, giving atmos and engineering an actual firefighting job and giving arsonist play a real tool.
- **Skip** — It is not the self-contained fork-namespaced drop-in it looks like: the prototype leans on flammable fields (firestack visual divisor, minimum/maximum firestacks, delete-on-extinguish, basic fire spread) and a per-tile Flammability value that upstream does not have, so grafting it means patching upstream flammable and tile-definition code and then re-patching them on every sync.
- **Touches** — engineering, atmospherics, security, antagonist, all-players
- **Verified** — supported. Every gameplay beat checks out in the actual code: the ESTileFire prototype has four staged sprites/sounds (red_1..4, fire1..4.ogg), SpeedModifierContacts 0.8/0.8 for the floor-slow, TryAddBurntDecalsToTile for scorch marks, edge_spreaders.yml sets updatesPerSecond:1 for spread cadence, OnSpreadNeighbors weights neighbor tiles up for high temperature and zeroes tiles with tileDef.Flammability<=0 or low oxygen, fires lose firestacks on each spread (AdjustFireStacks negative) and the Update() loop either deletes or downgrades to a weaker stage once SmolderTime passes, ESTileFireOnTriggerComponent lets any BaseXOnTriggerComponent consumer (grenades, rigged devices) spawn a chosen Stage, and Origin/ESTileFireOriginComponent propagate through every child fire spawned by a spread, so a whole blaze traces to one originating entity. I then went beyond the cited evidence to settle the graft_shape question, diffing the fork's own Content.Shared/Atmos/Components/FlammableComponent.cs and Content.Shared/Maps/ContentTileDefinition.cs against space-wizards/space-station-14 master. Both files are NOT under the _ES/ namespace and both carry literal '// ES START ... // ES END' blocks in the fork's own tree: FlammableComponent.cs adds FirestackVisualDivisor, DeleteOnExtinguish, BasicFireSpread (and several atmos-energy fields the tile-fire system doesn't even use); ContentTileDefinition.cs adds the Flammability field the spread-scoring code reads. That is direct proof the fork edits upstream-named files in place, not just files that would need editing to integrate elsewhere - the needs-upstream-edits downgrade from the drop-in seed is correct, and correct in the stronger 'fork-patches-upstream' sense. One inaccuracy in the claim's own reasoning: it lists 'minimum/maximum firestacks' as fields 'upstream does not have', but upstream FlammableComponent.cs already defines MinimumFireStacks and MaximumFireStacks (and FireSpread) - only FirestackVisualDivisor, DeleteOnExtinguish and BasicFireSpread are actually new. This doesn't change the verdict (real new fields still force upstream edits) but the claim overstates which specific fields are novel.

**[Chemical plumbing network](#chemical-plumbing) — starlight**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 0 forks carry it*

Chemists get a build-out toy: a hand-held Rapid Plumbing Device places hidden floor ducts (on three separate layers, with straight, bend, T, fourway and manifold pieces) and snaps together a chain of fluid machines, so reagents flow between them on their own instead of being ferried by hand in beakers. You pour into an input tank or a sink, then route the fluid through filters that split named reagents onto two outlets, reactors that pull set quantities and heat them until a reaction fires, synthesizers that conjure basic reagents like iron, oxygen and sugar straight out of battery power, buffer and 2000u storage tanks, a smart dispenser that fills a labeled jug automatically, and a pill press that stamps pills or patches at whatever dosage you set (including blending two feeds at a chosen ratio). Floor drains suck up spilled puddles into the network, a disposal unit quietly vaporises whatever you do not want, connectors show red for inlet and blue for outlet and look visibly jagged when you have misaligned a machine, and a plunger flushes anything stuck onto the floor.

- **Take** — It turns chemistry from repetitive beaker-shuffling into a buildable factory the chemist can design, debug and expand over a round, which is the single biggest depth upgrade available to that role and something upstream has no answer for.
- **Skip** — It is a large new node-network subsystem with roughly a dozen machines, six client UIs and its own construction tool, and its own guidebook advertises hooks into upstream ChemMaster, chemical dispenser and reagent grinder, so it will not sit quietly in a fork namespace and will need re-reconciling against upstream chemistry changes forever.
- **Touches** — science, medical, engineering, service
- **Verified** — supported. The two guidebook pages read almost line-for-line match the gameplay claim: RPLD tool building three-layer ducts (straight/bend/T/fourway/manifold), red=inlet/blue=outlet connector coloring with jagged-when-disconnected visuals, plumbing input/sink/drain, 2000u tank and 200u buffer, filter splitting up to 4 named reagents into filtered/passthrough outlets, reactor pulling set quantities and heating to trigger reactions, synthesizer generating iron/oxygen/sugar/etc from battery power, smart dispenser with labeled-jug auto-fill, pill press with configurable dosage and two ratio-mixing inlets for pills/patches, disposal that vaporizes reagents, and a plunger to flush buffers. Nothing in the gameplay text goes beyond what these files show. Critically, I fetched the actual upstream prototype files cited by the guidebook's own claim that ChemMaster and Industrial Reagent Grinder support plumbing connections, and both files contain literal in-place edits marked '# Starlight-edit' / '# Starlight-start: Plumbing integration', adding PlumbingDevice/PlumbingInlet/PlumbingOutlet components directly onto the upstream chem_master.yml and reagent_grinder.yml prototypes (outside any _Starlight namespace directory). This confirms the claim's own graft_shape of 'needs-upstream-edits' is correct and specifically the fork-patches-upstream flavor: the feature's own source tree already touches upstream files, contradicting a naive drop-in reading and validating the assessor's downgrade from the seed's 'drop-in' guess.

**[Cortical borer](#cortical-borer) — monolith**

*activity · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 1 forks carry it*

A dead player can come back as a tiny brain worm that crawls into a living crewmate's head (blocked by any helmet, and by sugar in the victim's stomach). Once inside it rides along invisibly, listens to everything the host hears, reads their vitals like a health analyzer, and spends a slowly regenerating pool of "chemicals" from a menu to dose them straight into the bloodstream, anything from bicaridine and painkillers to mute toxin, ephedrine, blinding acid or knockout sleep drugs. Every few minutes it can seize the host's body outright for 40 seconds and walk them around, and while in control it can spend a big chunk of its chemical pool to make the host vomit up an egg that another ghost can take over as a new borer. Hosts get freed by drinking sugar to suppress it and then having brain surgery to pull the worm out; borers share a private hive chat with each other.

- **Take** — It is a complete, self-driving parasite role with real counterplay already designed in (helmets block entry, sugar suppresses, brain surgery removes), so it gives ghosts something to do and gives medical a new patient problem without touching the round's win conditions.
- **Skip** — The prototypes lean on several non-upstream systems Monolith already has (a universal-language speaker tag, a collective-mind hive channel, thermal vision, a custom surgery step and a radio-overheard hook), so a graft means either bringing those along or stripping features out, and the role itself hands one player quiet control over another player's body, which needs admin attention and a playtime gate (Monolith uses 50 hours) to not be miserable.
- **Touches** — ghost-roles, antagonist, medical, all-players
- **Needs** — [language-system](#language-system), [surgery-and-limb-wounds](#surgery-and-limb-wounds)
- **Verified** — supported. Every specific gameplay beat checks out against actual source: GhostRole+GhostTakeoverAvailable ghost role with a 50hr (180000s) playtime gate matches the skip_because note; the .ftl strings and OnInfestHostAttempt code confirm helmet-blocks-entry and sugar-blocks; CorticalBorerComponent has ChemicalPoints/ChemicalPointCap=250 regenerating at 1/sec, and the chemicals yml lists exactly bicaridine, mute toxin, ephedrine, a blinding acid (NorepinephricAcid) and a sleep drug (Nocturine); ActionControlHost has useDelay 340s (5:40) wrapping a 40s ControlDuration, matching '40 seconds every few minutes'; EggCost=200 against a 250 cap is genuinely 'a big chunk' of the pool; BorerRadioReceive literally forwards every heard radio message to the borer's player session, confirming 'listens to everything the host hears'; CollectiveMind channel 'CorticalBorer' confirms the private hive chat; the guidebook text is a near-verbatim match for the sugar+surgery removal claim. The graft_shape call is not just confirmed but understated: I found the actual diffs. Content.Server/Radio/EntitySystems/HeadsetSystem.cs (a plain, non-namespaced upstream file) has an explicit '// Mono - Borers begin/end' block raising RadioMessageHeardEvent, and Resources/Prototypes/_Shitmed/Entities/Surgery/{surgeries.yml,surgery_steps.yml} carry '# mono change' blocks wiring SurgeryCorticalBorerRemoval into the brain-surgery graph. So the path-data 'drop-in' seed is wrong in the strongest sense (fork-patches-upstream, confirmed by name), and separately, a different destination fork without an identical HeadsetSystem/_Shitmed surgery tree would have to hand-write those same hook points (integration-would-require-upstream-edits) — hence 'both'. UniversalLanguageSpeaker (_EinsteinEngines/Language), CollectiveMind (_Starlight), and ThermalVision (_White/Overlays) are all separate borrowed-namespace systems the species prototype depends on, matching depends_on and skip_because exactly.

**[Disease and virology](#disease-and-virology) — backmen**

*activity · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 0 forks carry it*

People catch named illnesses like space cold, space flu, bird flew, plague and OwOnavirus, and start sneezing, coughing, vomiting, dropping items or taking slow damage while the sickness spreads to anyone nearby who is not wearing a mask. A medic swabs a patient's mouth, feeds the swab into a diagnoser machine, and gets a printed report naming the disease, whether it is contagious, how resistant it is to spaceacillin, and exactly how to cure it: drink so many units of a specific chemical, rest in bed for a while, run a fever or chill yourself, or just wait it out. Once a disease has been identified it can be loaded into a vaccinator that spends biomass to print vaccines, so the crew can be inoculated before the outbreak reaches them; the nastier strains escalate in stages, with things like the robovirus eventually turning its victim into a cyborg and the xeno strain twisting the body into something else entirely.

- **Take** — It hands medical a genuine second job loop (swab, diagnose, brew the cure, mass-vaccinate) that runs on its own clock and creates crew-wide urgency without needing an antagonist.
- **Skip** — It is a large content system whose infection, cure, effect and diagnosis pieces all have to land together, and it reaches into rotting/miasma plus mob and mask prototypes to work, so it is a long-lived maintenance surface rather than a file you drop in and forget.
- **Touches** — medical, science, all-players, custom-station-events
- **Verified** — supported. The gameplay description matches the fetched files almost line for line: named diseases in infectious.yml/disease-proto.ftl (SpaceCold, SpaceFlu, BirdFlew, Plague, OwOnavirus), symptom effects (DiseaseSnough Sneeze/Cough, DiseaseVomit, wet-hands-drop, DiseaseHealthChange tick damage), diagnoser.ftl strings matching "printed report... Infectious/Spaceacillin Resistance... cure-bedrest/reagent-units/wait/temp" verbatim, vaccine.ftl showing biomass-cost vaccinator, VanAusdallsRobovirus's DiseaseCyborgConversion effect, and XenoVirus's DiseasePolymorph into XenoDroneMorph/XenoQueenMorph. I also confirmed the unverified mask-spread detail directly in DiseaseSystem.cs (comment "if the snougher is not wearing a mask", checks inventory slot "mask" for IngestionBlockerComponent). On graft_shape, the claim's own downgrade from the drop-in seed to needs-upstream-edits holds up, but the evidence shows it in both senses: the fork's own copy already places disease.yml (DiseaseSwab/Vaccine entities, tagged inline "# backmen") and disease_diagnoser.yml inside vanilla-style directories (Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Objects/Specific/Medical/, .../Structures/Machines/Medical/) rather than under an isolated _Backmen prototype folder — directly contradicting the path-data's "zero files outside namespace" assumption (fork-patches-upstream). Separately, DiseaseSystem.cs only reacts to DiseaseCarrierComponent via ComponentInit/MobStateChangedEvent subscriptions, meaning that component must be explicitly present on mob prototypes to work; I could not find it added anywhere in base.yml, human.yml, or humanoid.yml, implying another fork would need to add it to its own species/mob prototypes to wire diseases onto players (integration-would-require-upstream-edits). The C# systems themselves (DiseaseSystem, VaccineSystem, DiseaseInfectionSpread, BkRottingSystem) are fully self-contained under Content.Server/Backmen/Disease, Content.Shared/Backmen/Disease, and Content.Client/Backmen/Disease.

2 forks built this; the assessment above is the best-verified one.

These passed verification and were still turned down. Kept visible with the reason,
because "we considered that and said no" is what gets lost and re-proposed later.

- [Round modifiers and game director](#round-modifier-presets) — A game director is a game master by another name, so the same call applies.
- [Ghost roles, respawn and game-master roles](#gamemaster-and-ghost-roles) — Anything with a game master is too much.
- [Games, instruments and performance](#games-instruments-and-performance) — Not really interesting.

## Features

## Antag

### Objective and uplink store rework

<a id="antag-objectives-and-uplink-rework"></a>

Extends or replaces the antagonist objective framework and the uplink storefront with new conditions, currencies, catalog categories and round-end summaries.

**rmc14**

*structural · entangled · high confidence · 9 forks carry it*

Instead of personal antag objectives, the whole marine side works one shared intelligence economy. Players scavenge the colony for paper scraps, progress reports, folders and technical manuals, read them in order (you can't understand a manual until you've read simpler documents), type what they learned into the intel computer, then store the document back in the intel room. Other point sources include hauling out experimental devices, decrypting data disks at a SIGINT terminal using a password found in earlier clues, hacking planetside data terminals (which need colony power and comms restored first), cracking safes whose combinations come from document clues, rescuing survivors back to the ship, morgue-ing dead colonists, and dragging dead xenos into the research containment room (bigger corpse, more points). A handheld detector pings the direction of nearby intel, a shared "View Intel Objectives" action shows team progress, and the points get spent at a CIC tech tree console on tiered unlocks: an armoured vehicle, extra requisitions and dropship budget, orbital bombardment warheads, waking reinforcement troops, each with a station-wide announcement when it lands.

- **Take** — It turns "objectives" from a private checklist into a visible, shared side-wide economy where exploration and corpse recovery buy real round-changing assets, giving non-combat players a concrete way to shape how the round goes.
- **Skip** — Nothing about it is portable as-is: the point sources assume RMC-14's colony/warship map layout, xeno corpses, survivors and dedicated intel jobs, and the spend side buys orbital cannon warheads, dropship and requisitions budgets and reinforcement waves that only exist in that fork, so you'd be rebuilding both ends around your own round structure.
- **Touches** — command, cargo, science, medical, security, all-players
- **Needs** — [alternate-round-types](#alternate-round-types), [extra-job-roster](#extra-job-roster), [cargo-bounties-and-market](#cargo-bounties-and-market)
- **Verified** — supported. Re-fetched both cited files plus the Content.Shared/_RMC14/Intel component directory listing and the detector system source. Every specific gameplay beat in the claim checks out against the guidebook text almost verbatim: read-order gating (scrap->report->folder->manual), entering knowledge into the intel computer then re-storing the document, SIGINT terminal disk decryption with clue-derived keys, planetside data terminals gated on colony power+comms, safe combinations from clues, survivors counted on ship arrival, colonist corpses to morgue, xeno corpses to research containment scaled by size, and a CIC tech tree spending intel points on an ARC vehicle, requisitions/dropship budget increases, orbital-cannon warheads, and waking cryo troops/specialists, each firing a TechAnnounceEvent. The detector system I read independently (not in the cited evidence) confirms a motion-detector-style blip mechanic keyed to IntelDetectorTrackedComponent (present on all intel item prototypes), matching the 'pings nearby intel' claim. On graft_shape: all files I found (Resources/Prototypes/_RMC14/..., Content.Shared/_RMC14/Intel/...) stay inside the fork's own _RMC14 namespace, so the seed's path-based 'zero files outside namespace' finding holds — but the detector system's imports (Xenonids.Parasite, motion detector, requisitions inventory) and the tech tree's direct calls into RMCOrbitalCannonWarhead*, VehicleHumveeARC, dropship/requisitions budget events, and cryo-marine waking confirm genuine functional entanglement with other RMC14-specific systems, exactly matching the claim's own 'entangled' downgrade and its listed reasons.
  - unsupported: "each with a station-wide announcement when it lands" — the TechAnnounceEvent fires at the moment the tech-tree purchase is made, not tied specifically to a delivery/landing event; every tier purchase (including non-delivery ones like tier unlocks) gets the same announcement, so 'when it lands' slightly over-specifies the trigger.

**starlight**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 9 forks carry it*

Traitors get a set of open-ended "story" objectives aimed at a randomly chosen department instead of only steal/kill tasks: frame someone in Engineering as a Syndicate agent, spread rumours that Medical is starting an uprising, publicly disgrace a department head, impersonate a Cargo tech and trash their reputation, stir up a feud between two departments, or waste a department's resources however you like. Because nothing checks those automatically, an antagonist gets a "Write objective summary" button and a text window they can edit all shift to explain how they pulled it off; whatever they wrote is printed under their name in the round-end report. The uplink also grows a "Second Hand" tab that stocks 8-14 random cut-price used Syndicate items per round (one each, then the entry vanishes), plus limited-stock listings, listings that only appear for certain roles, at certain player counts, or when you rolled a specific objective (for example a whole Die-A-Glorious-Death aisle of grenade rigs, ammo duffels and Antimov boards that only unlocks if you drew the suicide-mission objective), and extra aisles for allied cyborgs, cybernetics, implants and joke purchases.

- **Take** — The story objectives plus the player-written round-end summary turn traitoring from a checklist into social play, and they are the rare antag content that makes the whole crew's shift more interesting rather than just arming one player harder.
- **Skip** — Unverifiable objectives lean entirely on player honesty and admin attention, and the bundle drags in a pile of antag-specific conditions (abductor, absorb, blood drain, damn, brighteye) that are dead weight unless you already run those antags.
- **Touches** — antagonist, traitor, all-players, command, security
- **Needs** — [abductors](#abductors), [changeling](#changeling), [vampire](#vampire), [devil-pacts](#devil-pacts)
- **Verified** — supported. Cloned the fork and traced SecondHandSystem's `StoreInitializedEvent` back to its definition in Content.Server/StoreDiscount/Systems/StoreDiscountSystem.cs — a file OUTSIDE any _Starlight namespace dir (not in evidence_cited, invisible to the path-data seed). Diffing against space-wizards/space-station-14 master's identical-path file proves the fork added a `UseSecondHand` field to the record struct and a `using Content.Server._Starlight.StoreDiscount;` import that upstream's version does not have — a real in-place edit of an upstream file, not just a same-fork dependency. This falsifies the drop-in seed on its own strict terms (files outside fork namespace exist and were edited) independent of the claim's own (weaker) reasoning about changeling/vampire/abductor/devil-pact files, which I also confirmed exist as genuine siblings in the same Objectives folder/namespace (self-contained, not themselves upstream edits).
  - unsupported: "extra aisles for allied cyborgs, cybernetics, implants and joke purchases" implies these are general traitor-uplink additions, but allies.yml shows most cyborg-ally listings (kitted/speed borgi, all four cyborg reinforcement radios, both mech-teleporter crates) are gated behind `StoreWhitelistCondition` requiring `NukeOpsUplink` or `LoneOpsUplink` tags — only one basic borgi-kit listing is unrestricted for a general traitor uplink; the touches list also omits nukeops/lone-ops entirely, so framing this as a traitor-facing aisle overstates general availability.
  - unsupported: "8-14 random cut-price used Syndicate items" — the code confirms the 8-14 count and one-each/vanish-on-purchase mechanic precisely (SecondHandSystem.cs), but no discount/cost-reduction field was found on SecondHandCategoryPrototype or in the SecondHand wiring itself; 'cut-price' is a reasonable inference (there's a companion duffelbag_secondhand.yml and the sibling StoreDiscount system already does price cuts) but isn't directly confirmed in the files inspected.

**impstation**

*loop-change · entangled · medium confidence · 9 forks carry it*

A traitor opening their uplink sees a much bigger, more personalised shop: extra shelves of gear (attack animals and card packs, chem darts, bullet-catchers, zombie-plague injectors), items that only appear if you hold a specific job (hot sauce crates for the chef, shock darts for the zookeeper), items that only appear if you drew a specific objective (a suicide-mission traitor gets offered a destabilising crystal), rotating discounts, and one-off stock that has to restock before you can buy again. Security gets its own separate storefront, SecLink, spending three distinct token types on batons, disablers and utility gear: stun sabres, a pocket disabler, a citationator that fires tickets, a collapsible shield, surplus night-vision goggles and a handheld criminal-records terminal, with drained items needing a recharge before they can be refunded. Alongside that, several fork-only antagonist roles get their own objective sets, such as a Syndicate recruiter who must talk a handful of disgruntled crew into signing a contract in blood with their pen, keep that pen safe, and escape with their new hires, or a chem-dealing specialist who must peddle concoctions and survive to the shuttle.

- **Take** — It turns the uplink from a flat price list into a shop that reacts to your job and your objective, and the SecLink token store gives security a progression-flavoured loadout choice they normally never get.
- **Skip** — The catalogue entries are mostly pointers at dozens of fork-only item entities and fork-only antag roles, so grafting the storefront without those first gives you a menu full of missing prototypes; the custom client uplink window also has to displace the upstream store UI rather than sit beside it.
- **Touches** — antagonist, security, service, all-players
- **Needs** — [traitor-uplink](#traitor-uplink), [minor-antag-roles](#minor-antag-roles), [changeling](#changeling), [heretic](#heretic), [wizard-magic](#wizard-magic)
- **Verified** — partly supported. Every other specific in the gameplay text checks out against the actual files: SecLink's three tokens (BT/DT/UT) and its stun sabre, pocket disabler, citationator, collapsible shield, night-vision goggles and handheld records terminal all appear verbatim in seclink-catalog.ftl/currency.ftl; the recharge-before-refund line matches store.ftl's `store-currency-not-charged`; job-gated items (chef hot sauce, zookeeper shock darts) and the objective-gated destabilizing crystal (BuyerJobCondition/BuyerObjectiveWhitelistCondition with DieCondition) are real in job.yml/objective.yml, with restockTime and ListingLimitedStockCondition backing the 'rotating discounts / one-off restock' claims; the recruiter (sign-in-blood pen, keep-pen-safe StealCondition) and synthesis specialist (peddle concoctions, survive) objective sets are real in _DV/Objectives. Beyond the one overclaim about escaping 'with new hires,' the description holds. On graft_shape: the claim's own downgrade to 'entangled' is correct and I'd keep it — categories.ftl shows the identical store/listing framework is shared live across Changeling stings, Wizard spellbook, SecLink and Uplink in one file, the recruiter/synthesis objectives depend on fork-only Content.Server/_DV/Recruiter C# systems, and Content.Client/_Impstation/Uplink/UplinkBoundUserInterface.cs is a bespoke BoundUserInterface (not a thin extension of Content.Client/Store/Ui) that would have to replace whatever UI key an upstream/other-fork uplink component points at rather than sit alongside it. None of this is upstream files edited in place (everything I found lives under _Impstation/_DV/_EstacaoPirata namespaces) but it is deeply woven into several of the fork's own other systems, which is exactly what 'entangled' is meant to flag.
  - unsupported: escape with their new hires — RecruiterEscapeObjective (Resources/Prototypes/_DV/Objectives/recruiter.yml) is just `parent: [BaseRecruiterObjective, EscapeShuttleObjective]`, i.e. the recruiter personally escaping on the shuttle; nothing in the fetched files ties completion to the recruited NPCs also being aboard, only flavor description text ('Assist the syndicate with briefing your recruited operatives on their new goals').

**ephemeral-space**

*structural · entangled · high confidence · 9 forks carry it*

Antagonists no longer get a private shopping list of "steal X, kill Y" tasks. Instead the whole traitor side shares one visible chain: a handful of smaller jobs first (kill a specific crewmember, bug a department's APC, sabotage the comms computer, crew monitoring server, criminal records, emergency access terminal or telecom processor), and only once those are done can they hack three Security Override Terminals scattered in the HoP's secure room, the captain's office and secure tech storage to unlock the nuclear code, then arm the nuke with the captain's disk. Each objective shows in a panel tagged Team or Solo with a live percentage of how far along it is, and at round end each line reads Success or Failed with that percentage. Kill targets can be handed to you under a codename rather than a name, and an ability lets you sense roughly how far away and in which direction your target is. The crew have their own counterpart objective (keep the station powered, outrun the radstorm and charge the warp drive to escape), and a sympathizer variant simply asks a hidden helper to work out who the traitors are and help them set off the nuke.

- **Take** — It turns antag objectives from a private end-of-round scorecard into the round's actual spine: a visible, prerequisite-gated team chain with live progress percentages that both sides are effectively racing over, which is a far stronger driver of round narrative than upstream's independent steal/kill list.
- **Skip** — It is not an objective library you can bolt on, it is Ephemeral Space's whole round: the objectives assume secret identities and organisations to assign them, a warp drive and radstorm for the crew side, fork-only consoles (emergency access terminal, radio scrambler, crypto nuke terminals) as sabotage targets, and a three-terminal nuke flow that replaces the standard nuke round. Grafting it means importing those systems or rewriting every condition against your own station's machines.
- **Touches** — antagonist, all-players, command, security, engineering, ghost-roles
- **Needs** — [secret-identities](#secret-identities), [warp-drive](#warp-drive), [alternate-round-types](#alternate-round-types)
- **Verified** — supported. Every specific gameplay beat checks out against the raw files: objective.ftl has the Team/Solo tags and "(N%)" / Success-Failed summary line verbatim; ESTargetCodenameComponent and ESSenseTargetDistanceSystem confirm codenamed kill targets and the directional-sense popup with adjacent/close/moderate/far tiers; traitor.yml lists exactly the minor sabotage set (comms, crew monitoring, criminal records, emergency access terminal, telecom processor, bug an APC) gated by ESNukePrereqObjective before ESObjectiveTraitorHackCryptoNukeConsoles ("HoP's secure room, the captain's office, and secure tech storage"), then ESObjectiveTraitorDetonateNuke with the captain's disk; crew.yml's ESObjectiveWarpDrive description matches the "outrun the radstorm/charge the warp drive" line word for word; ESObjectiveSympathizerDetonateNuke matches the sympathizer description. The claim's own downgrade from the seed's "drop-in" to "entangled" is itself correct: repo-tree search shows ESSecretIdentityRole is a hook into a large separate SecretIdentity system (Arsonist/Avenger/Burstworm/Cryojunkie sub-roles), ESWarpDriveObjective hooks a full separate WarpDrive gamerule/singularity system, and Resources/Prototypes/_ES/GameRules/presets.yml shows the whole objective chain is wired into the fork's own always-on ESMasqueradeManaged/ESExtended presets (with ESWarpDriveRule baked in) rather than being an optional bolt-on round type. depends_on (secret-identities, warp-drive, alternate-round-types) is accurate.

**backmen**

*loop-change · entangled · medium confidence · 9 forks carry it*

Antagonists get a wider spread of things to be told to do and a much bigger shop to spend on. New assignments include hijacking the evacuation shuttle (allowed to leave with cuffed hostages and fellow agents alive), stealing the nuke disc as a non-command traitor, impersonating a specific crew member and holding that identity until the shuttle leaves, gaining psychic powers and keeping them, and, for a blob, spreading to a set tile count. Steal lists add fork-only prizes like an energy shotgun and a telescopic baton. The syndicate uplink stocks a lot more: magazines and ammo boxes for the fork's guns, a short-range teleport knife with four charges, a chainsword, a codespeak language manual readable twice, mime and clown disguises, and a spread of psionic, BZ and exotic-gas grenade bundles. Some antags shop in their own currency instead of telecrystals, for example the flesh cultist trading harvested mutation points for one-off body upgrades like a blade arm or immunity to shocks, pressure and cold, and the station itself gets a round-start goal drawn from a long list (build a singularity, set up a zoo, repair xenobiology, run security training).

- **Take** — It turns a thin objective pool into real variety, and the impersonate and hijack conditions in particular push traitors toward social play instead of another murder checklist.
- **Skip** — Most of the catalogue is a shopfront for content the fork already has, so grafting it without the fork's guns, psionics, blob and flesh cult leaves you with a store full of items that do not exist; and a chunk of the listing text is untranslated Russian you would have to rewrite.
- **Touches** — antagonist, security, command, all-players
- **Needs** — [traitor-uplink](#traitor-uplink), [firearms-content-expansion](#firearms-content-expansion), [psionics-and-glimmer](#psionics-and-glimmer), [blob](#blob), [station-goals](#station-goals), [language-system](#language-system)
- **Verified** — partly supported. Re-fetched all 15 cited files. Nearly every specific gameplay claim checks out verbatim or near-verbatim: HijackShuttleObjective description literally allows handcuffed hostages/syndicate agents alive; NukeDiskStealObjective carries NotCommandRequirement (non-command traitor steals disc); become-psionic-condition.ftl and BecomePsionicObjective match 'gain and keep psionics'; BlobCaptureObjective has a numeric target (400); steal-target-groups ftl files confirm energy shotgun and telescopic baton as new steal prizes; uplink_catalog.yml confirms MagazineBoxRifleLightSniper, Chainsword, psi/anti-psi/BZ and multiple exotic-gas grenade bundles, the 4-charge teleporter, and a codespeak manual 'readed 2 times'; flesh_cultist_catalog.yml confirms StolenMutationPoint currency buying one-off (stock:1) FleshCultistBlade and shock/pressure/cold immunity mutations; goals.yml confirms Singularity, Zoo, XenobiologyRepair, SecurityTraining as round-start goals; and UplinkBogomol's untranslated Russian description corroborates the 'skip_because' complaint. The one specific miss: only a mime costume is present in the two catalog files, no clown disguise entity, so 'mime and clown disguises' overclaims. On graft_shape, the claim's downgrade from the drop-in seed to 'entangled' holds up: the catalog/objective files reference dozens of productEntity/productAction ids (blob capture component, psi-grenade bundles, gun magazines, flesh-cultist mutation actions, codespeak book) that live in the fork's own other feature namespaces, not upstream — so it's a content/functional entanglement with sibling fork systems rather than literal upstream file-patching, matching how the claim itself framed 'entangled' (not 'needs-upstream-edits').
  - unsupported: Some antags shop in their own currency instead of telecrystals ... mime and clown disguises — the two cited catalog files (uplink_catalog.yml, uplink_nomad.yml) only contain a mime costume (UplinkCostumeMime -> ClothingBackpackDuffelSyndicateCostumeMime). The only 'Clown' entry is UplinkCannedClown, a canned-soup joke item restricted to the Clown job by BuyerJobCondition, not a disguise/costume. No clown disguise entity exists in the cited evidence.
