### Round modifiers and game director

<a id="round-modifier-presets"></a>

Round-level frameworks that pick which threats and rulesets are in play, from weighted secret directors to named round modes, shift-intensity tiers and rolled round-wide aspects.

**starlight**

*structural · entangled · high confidence · 6 forks carry it*

Instead of one fixed threat picked at roundstart, the shift runs on a hidden budget that spends itself over the hour: it buys a headline threat at the start (traitors, nukies, revs, cosmic cult, zombies, a wizard duel), sprinkles in smaller ones sized to the headcount, and then keeps spending mid-shift so a second wave can show up an hour in. Some rounds it deliberately fails to buy anything and you get a quiet extended shift. Separately, ordinary crew get a blinking "cards" icon during the shift: click it and you pick one of a few offered personal side-quests, from silly ("go find out if the station really does make the best apple pie", "open three pieces of mail", "have a beer") to serious ("an assassin has been dispatched to kill you, survive thirty minutes"), with completion paying out credits or unlocking a hidden section in vending machines.

- **Take** — It solves the two biggest shape problems at once: rounds stop being one-antag-then-nothing, and non-antag crew get a steady drip of low-stakes personal goals that gives them something to do when their department is idle.
- **Skip** — The dynamic table is basically a manifest of Starlight's own antag roster (their changeling, vampire, devil, SELF agents, sub-wizard, cosmic cult) and the card system spans roughly 120 files with its own alert, selection window, task/handler/reward subsystems plus hooks into mail, faxes, ID cards, chat and terminator spawns, so you cannot take it without either porting or rewriting the antags it spends its budget on.
- **Touches** — all-players, antagonist, command, security, service, ghost-roles
- **Needs** — [changeling](#changeling), [vampire](#vampire), [devil-pacts](#devil-pacts), [wizard-magic](#wizard-magic), [cosmic-cult](#cosmic-cult), [minor-antag-roles](#minor-antag-roles), [player-economy-and-banking](#player-economy-and-banking), [mail-delivery](#mail-delivery)
- **Verification** — none; read this as a claim, not a finding.

**ephemeral-space**

*structural · entangled · medium confidence · 6 forks carry it*

Every shift the station itself is rolled fresh: lights and the space backdrop get a different tint (occasionally a dim "void" or a mellow nightshift palette), floors come pre-dirtied with graffiti, food wrappers and puddles of vomit, blood, welding fuel or worse, solar panels start cracked or missing, rats have gnawed holes in doors, and on a rare roll the whole camera is flipped 180 degrees for the round. On top of that, a "masquerade" is picked as the round's mode: it decides which secret-identity masks and hidden organizations are in play at the current population and which event schedulers run. During the round a vote panel appears for players holding the stagehand/voter role, with a ding and a chat announcement, letting them pick what the station gets next (next station event, next degradation event); the winning choice is announced to voters and immediately fires as a game rule.

- **Take** — It replaces "secret roll" with a director layer players can actually see and steer: rolled station variation makes every shift look and feel different from minute one, and the stagehand vote hands the pacing of events to players instead of a hidden scheduler.
- **Skip** — The masquerade half is the round mode for the fork's secret-identity/organization system and does almost nothing without it, and the vote framework is a whole bespoke UI plus vote-option type hierarchy you would then own; only the station-variation passes come out cleanly on their own.
- **Touches** — all-players, ghost-roles, antagonist, engineering, service, command
- **Needs** — [secret-identities](#secret-identities), [custom-station-events](#custom-station-events)
- **Verification** — none; read this as a claim, not a finding.

**sunrise**

*structural · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 6 forks carry it*

Instead of a fixed secret roll, the shift is run by a director that paces the round in phases: a quiet stretch, a build-up, a peak where the nastiest things land, then a recovery lull, looping for the whole shift. Players vote in the lobby between named intensity settings (Calm, Classic, Insane) that decide how much trouble the director can afford to buy and how long the calm stretches last, and the same director hands out helpful shifts too (pizza parties, gift crates of security guns, engineering and medical supply drops) alongside the hostile ones. How much the station gets thrown at it scales with how well-armed and well-stocked the crew actually is, so a fat, heavily-armed shift draws bigger threats than a skeleton one. At round end there is another vote for map and preset before the next shift starts.

- **Take** — It replaces the flat random-event drip with a paced narrative arc (calm, build, peak, recovery) plus a player vote on intensity, which is the single biggest lever on how a whole shift feels without writing any new content.
- **Skip** — The threat-cost table has to be hand-tuned per event for your own event roster, and it takes over round flow entirely, so any mistuning is felt by every player in every round rather than being contained to one system.
- **Touches** — all-players, antagonist, security, command, admin
- **Verified** — supported. storyteller_types.yml confirms the exact phase model (relaxation/buildUp/peak/recovery minutes) for Calm/Classic/Insane, each with distinct budgetModifier and armed-crew/security strength coefficients (strengthArmedCrewCoefficient, strengthSecurityCoefficient), matching the 'quiet/build/peak/recovery' and 'scales with how armed the crew is' claims. storyteller_metadata.yml confirms Helpful-type gifts (pizza parties large/small, security guns, engineering/medical/janitor gifts) at threatCost 0. game_presets.yml shows StorytellerCalm/Classic/Insane all have showInVote: true, confirming the lobby vote. RoundEndVoteSystem.cs confirms a round-end Map+Preset vote. Critically, for the graft_shape question: Content.Server/GameTicking/GameTicker.GamePreset.cs is an UPSTREAM file (no _Sunrise in its path) that contains a block explicitly marked '// Sunrise-Start ... // Sunrise-End' adding _excludedPresets/ExcludedPresets/AddExcludedPreset/ClearExcludedPresets members, which StorytellerSystem.Voting.cs consumes via GameTicker.ExcludedPresets. This is a real edit to an upstream-namespace file within the fork's own tree, contradicting the seed's zero-files-outside-namespace 'drop-in' premise and confirming 'fork-patches-upstream' rather than merely needing edits in a hypothetical target repo.

**stellar-station**

*structural · entangled · high confidence · 6 forks carry it*

Every shift the station flies out to one of eight named hazard sectors (Apocryphal, Azure, Corporate, Crystalline, Magnetar, Malign, Pelagic, Supernova), each with its own starfield backdrop, coloured ambient lighting over the whole station, optional weather, and a soundtrack that changes in stages as the round wears on, with one sector even shifting the screen's colour grading in the final ten minutes. The sector also rolls a hidden "shift intensity" from green to black that decides how often random station events fire, and the gap between events keeps shrinking as the round goes on, so a black shift is a near-constant stream of trouble while a green one is quiet. Some sectors additionally roll a chance that a major threat is brewing, which quietly compresses the round to a shorter, randomised length instead of the usual ninety minutes. None of this is announced to the crew, so players read the shift from the sky, the light and the music rather than from text.

- **Take** — It makes every round feel like a different place with a different tempo using one lever (a sector pick plus an intensity scalar) rather than hand-tuning event lists, and the escalating event cadence gives rounds a natural build toward the end.
- **Skip** — The interesting half is not actually wired up yet: every sector's event table points at a placeholder (BasicGameRulesTable) and the per-sector antag sub-gamemode blocks are commented out, so today the eight sectors differ only in backdrop, light colour and music, and the whole thing sits on top of the fork's own game-rule base class, post-process LUT pipeline, roof-lighting and timer helpers plus a station that is a flyable shuttle grid FTL'd into a generated map.
- **Touches** — all-players, command, antagonist
- **Needs** — [station-and-environment-art](#station-and-environment-art), [visual-feedback-effects](#visual-feedback-effects), [custom-station-events](#custom-station-events)
- **Verification** — none; read this as a claim, not a finding.

**impstation**

*structural · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 6 forks carry it*

Instead of one "secret" roll, the shift can open in a named alternate mode: "Spy VS Spy", where every single crewmember wakes up as a traitor with codewords and a small uplink budget (0, 3 or 20 telecrystals depending on the variant) and objectives to kill another spy, keep a specific spy alive, and get off the station; "Pacifist VS Pacifist", the same all-against-all but with everyone unable to attack, so you have to kill through the environment while a telecrystal-eating fox named Renault wanders out of the vents as a bonus prize; and "All Aboard The Ship", which runs nukies, spies, revs, zombies and changelings simultaneously while every disaster scheduler including meteors and Kessler syndrome fires at once. Alongside those, hidden duplicate presets keep the "Secret" title and description so an admin can lock in a specific mode without the lobby knowing what is coming, presets can refuse to start if too many or too few players readied up, a lone pacified thief can be dropped in mid-round as a sub-gamemode, and a roundstart pass can quietly hand one random crewmember a hidden trait such as being able to perceive ghosts.

- **Take** — A handful of YAML preset definitions turn the existing antag rulesets you already ship into completely different round shapes (everyone-is-a-traitor, everyone-pacified, all-antags-at-once) plus admin-invisible secret variants, which is an enormous amount of round variety for very little new content.
- **Skip** — These are free-for-all modes that abandon normal station roleplay entirely and lean hard on population size, so they need per-server population tuning and admin discipline; the presets also reference antag rulesets (changeling, heretic) and objective prototypes a fork may not have, so half the list will not resolve without also grafting those.
- **Touches** — all-players, antagonist, admins, ghost-roles
- **Needs** — [traitor-uplink](#traitor-uplink), [antag-objectives-and-uplink-rework](#antag-objectives-and-uplink-rework), [changeling](#changeling), [heretic](#heretic)
- **Verified** — supported. The gameplay text checks out in fine detail: game_presets.yml confirms SpyVsSpy/SpyVsSpy3TC/SpyVsSpy20TC give startingBalance 0/3/20 TC exactly as claimed, with KillRandomTraitorSvSObjective + RandomTraitorAliveSvSObjective + EscapeShuttleObjective matching 'kill a spy / keep one alive / escape'; PacifistVsPacifist carries EveryonePacifiedRule plus a RenaultMigrationEventScheduler spawning MobFoxRenault ('bonus TC' comment); AllAboardTheShip's rule list is literally Nukeops+SpyVsSpy20TC+Revolutionary+Zombie+Changeling+KesslerSyndromeScheduler+MeteorSwarm(Mild)Scheduler; the Secret* presets all carry name: secret-title/description: secret-description with a code comment 'this allows admins to set the gamemode without anyone knowing'; ThiefSingular's own comment says it 'will just apply Pacified to one person in the middle of the round'; and ModifyComponentsVariationPassComponent defaults MinMaxComponentRecievers to (1,1), matching 'one random crewmember'. On graft_shape: the seed's drop-in call does not survive. AllAboardTheShip and the Secret* presets resolve their antag rules against Resources/Prototypes/GameRules/roundstart.yml (a plain, non-underscored, upstream-named directory), and diffing impstation's Nukeops entity there against space-wizards/space-station-14's own GameRules/roundstart.yml shows the AntagSelection schema has diverged (prefRoles/fallbackRoles/spawnerPrototype/startingGear vs vanilla's antags:[FixedAntagCount/LinearAntagCount]+DynamicRuleCost) - the fork's own copy really does carry a modified file inside an upstream-named directory, not a self-contained addition. Separately, Changeling and HereticLowpop (needed by AllAboardTheShip and the two LowpopHeretics presets) live in Resources/Prototypes/_Goobstation/GameRules/roundstart.yml, a different fork namespace the cited evidence never mentions. Net: 'needs-upstream-edits' is the right call, but the skip_because's causal story overreaches - of the 8/16 presets referencing IDs outside _Impstation, only 3 (AllAboardTheShip, LowpopHeretics, SecretLowpopHeretics) are blocked by content a vanilla-based fork genuinely lacks (Goobstation's rework); the other 5 Secret* presets reference Nukeops/Revolutionary/Zombie/Wizard, standard SS14 content every fork already ships, which would resolve fine unless the receiving fork's AntagSelection schema has also diverged the way impstation's has.
  - unsupported: the presets also reference antag rulesets (changeling, heretic) and objective prototypes a fork may not have, so half the list will not resolve without also grafting those

### Minor antagonist roles

<a id="minor-antag-roles"></a>

Roster of small non-round-ending antagonist roles such as contract hitmen, undercover corporate agents, fugitives, bounty hunters and recruiters, each with their own kit and objectives.

**impstation**

*activity · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 0 forks carry it*

Adds a Bounty Hunter role: a gun-for-hire who arrives on their own small independent shuttle (the Heron, which can switch its IFF broadcast off), gets a mark that is usually one of the round's existing antagonists, and gets paid for dragging that person back to the shuttle, more if they arrive alive and with less collateral damage. Before starting, the hunter picks two loadout kits from ten flavours (raider with a shotgun and C4, spacer with hardsuit and grappling hook, infiltrator with chameleon gear and a DNA scrambler, samurai with an energy katana and a weapon-recall implant that teleports a linked weapon back into their hand, scallywag with a laser cutlass and a thieving parrot, rogue clown with a pie cannon, and others), so no two hunters play the same. They are explicitly not station antagonists and are held to normal escalation rules, so most rounds they show up, talk to people, and try to talk or trick their target onto the shuttle rather than shooting the place up. Also included are Exploding Butlers, a familiar handed out to a chosen crewmember who must serve their master's whims with service access and a tea trolley, cannot use two-handed gear, and is expected to die at the end of the round when the master presses a remote signaller, plus a smaller Recruiter shop where TreatCoins buy contraband treats, bribes and gear.

- **Take** — A neutral, escalation-bound hunter who chases the round's actual antagonist gives the station a third faction that creates conversation and chases instead of another murderbone role, and the ten-kit picker means the same role stays fresh over many rounds.
- **Skip** — It is a big surface for one role: a whole extra shuttle to place in the round, ten separate gear kits referencing dozens of syndicate and command items you must keep valid, a bespoke kit-selection UI, a weapon-recall implant with client and server systems, and the Recruiter half sits under a vendored _DV namespace rather than Impstation's own; and the whole thing only works if your playerbase actually respects escalation rules for a heavily armed non-antagonist.
- **Touches** — antagonist, ghost-roles, security, service, command, all-players
- **Verified** — partly supported. I independently confirmed almost every specific in the gameplay claim: the Heron shuttle with toggleable IFF, PickRandomAntag objective targeting, the escalation/non-antagonist status (antagonist: false + guidebook text), all 10 named kits with matching contents (raider/shotgun+C4, spacer/hardsuit+grappling hook, infiltrator/chameleon+DNA scrambler, samurai/energy katana+weapon-recall implant, scallywag/laser cutlass+thieving parrot, rogue clown/pie cannon, plus subverter/roboticist/rogue operative/rogue captain), the Butler familiar's service access, two-handed-item restriction, and remote-signaller death objective, and the Recruiter TreatCoin shop. The one concrete miss is the 'tea trolley' detail — the actual gear is a teapot/teacup, no trolley entity exists anywhere in the repo. More importantly for graft_shape: I fetched the full repo tree and found the Recruiter half of this claim is NOT self-contained under _Impstation as the cited evidence path (Catalog/Recruiter/treasures.yml) implies — the actual role/component/system code (Content.Server/_DV/Recruiter/RecruiterPenSystem.cs, Content.Shared/_DV/Roles/RecruiterRole.cs, Resources/Prototypes/_DV/Roles/Antags/recruiter.yml, Resources/Prototypes/_DV/Objectives/recruiter.yml) lives under a _DV (Delta-V vendored) namespace, a real directory outside _Impstation that exists in the fork's own repo. This directly validates the claim's own skip_because note and the 'needs-upstream-edits' downgrade from the drop-in seed — the seed's path scan, looking only for _Impstation paths, missed this. Bounty Hunter and Butler proper are fully self-contained under _Impstation (aside from one additive, non-conflicting texture folder in a vanilla-styled Clothing/Head/Hats path), so the entanglement is narrowly the Recruiter sub-feature, not the whole unit.
  - unsupported: "is expected to die at the end of the round" / "a familiar handed out to a chosen crewmember who must serve their master's whims with service access and a tea trolley" — the ButlerGear starting gear (Resources/Prototypes/_Impstation/Roles/Antags/butler.yml) gives a DrinkTeapot and DrinkTeacupEmpty in-hand plus a RagItem/HandLabeler in pockets; there is no trolley/cart entity anywhere in the fork's tree (confirmed via full repo tree search for 'trolley' — zero hits). 'Tea trolley' is not supported by the evidence; the actual item is a teapot and teacup.

**deltav**

*activity · entangled · high confidence · 0 forks carry it*

Delta-V adds a set of small antagonist roles that never end the round but give one or two players a private agenda. A Hitman spawns as a ghost role with a briefcase of themed kits (sniper, poisoner, ninja, saboteur, bounty hunter, tracker, disguise-heavy assassin) and a contract that dictates not just who dies but how: kill them in public in front of witnesses, make it look like an accident, make it funny, make it clean, warn them well in advance, or befriend them first and then betray them. The target only has to die once, so the fun is in staging the death to the client's taste rather than in permanently removing a player. An Internal Affairs Agent works the opposite way, posing as ordinary crew while quietly taking orders from Central Command over a private radio channel: get a specific crewmember fired, frame someone so they are in the brig by midshift, drain a department's budget, or audit a department and file a written station report that everyone reads on the round-end screen. They shop from their own "NanoLink" uplink stocked with chameleon clothing, agent IDs, hidden security huds, a crew-tracking spy monitor and a station-master encryption key, and get billed for property damage, so the pressure is on manipulation rather than violence. A Syndicate Recruiter walks the halls interviewing crew and closing the deal by getting them to sign a blood-filled pen, spending the reward currency on gifts and bribes to sweeten the pitch. Escaped fugitives also pick a survival loadout on spawn (a pistol, EMP grenades and C4, smoke plus a teleport implant, an agent ID, a hacking kit, or a hostage-taking kit).

- **Take** — The hitman's "kill them dramatically / cleanly / publicly / as a joke" conditions and the IAA's fire-frame-defund-audit objectives push antagonists toward social play and staged setpieces instead of another murderbone, which is exactly the kind of pressure valve a fork wants when traitor is the only flavour on offer.
- **Skip** — It is four separate roles, not one feature: each brings its own uplink currency, catalogue, objective conditions and antag rules, and the payoff depends heavily on subjective judging (is that death "funny" enough? did the audit report count?) which means either admin arbitration or players self-scoring, plus a long tail of custom items to keep working through upstream syncs.
- **Touches** — antagonist, ghost-roles, security, command, all-players, service
- **Needs** — [antag-objectives-and-uplink-rework](#antag-objectives-and-uplink-rework), [traitor-uplink](#traitor-uplink)
- **Verified** — supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. Every substantive plot point in the gameplay description checked out almost word-for-word against the actual DeltaV files: the hitman's kit roster (sharpshooter/bounty-hunter/assassin/ninja/poisoner/saboteur/tracker) in hitman-case.ftl, the full menu of contract conditions in Hitman.xml (public/witness kill, accident, funny, clean, warn far in advance, gain-trust-then-betray), the IAA's fire/frame/audit/defund objectives and billed-for-damage flavor in NTAgent.xml, the blood-pen signing ritual in pen.ftl, and the six named fugitive kits in fugitive/sets.ftl all matched exactly. I found no overclaims worth flagging. However, a full recursive tree listing of the DeltaV repo shows every file for all four roles (Hitman, NTAgent, Recruiter, Fugitive) — C#, prototypes, locale, guidebook, even the NanoCoin/TreatCoin currency definitions — lives strictly under _DV namespaced directories with zero touches to non-_DV/vanilla paths, so 'fork-patches-upstream' is ruled out. But the claim's own depends_on field names two OTHER DeltaV-catalogued units (antag-objectives-and-uplink-rework, traitor-uplink), not vanilla SS14 files, as the blocker — that is the textbook definition of 'entangled with the fork's other systems' this schema separates from 'needs-upstream-edits'. Labeling it needs-upstream-edits obscures that the actual integration cost is pulling in sibling fork features, not touching vanilla engine/game files, so I'd reclassify it as entangled with upstream_reading=integration-would-require-upstream-edits (self-contained copy, but wiring the objective/uplink plumbing into a codebase lacking those sibling DV reworks would still touch that codebase's own upstream-derived antag/store files).

**serbia-strong**

*loop-change · entangled · high confidence · 0 forks carry it*

A traitor can buy a mind-slave implanter, restrain a crew member and spend ten seconds implanting them. The victim gets a pop-up telling them their will is broken: from now on they must obey every order their master gives, cannot hurt themselves, cannot hurt their master and cannot reveal who the master is (the master's name is literally censored out of anything they try to say). They carry a "Mind slaved" status icon, an objective to obey and keep the master alive, warnings when the master goes into crit or dies, and a private telepathy channel with them. Someone with a mindshield resists the implant outright. The implant slowly rots the host: first their speech goes strange, then they can no longer hold anything two-handed, then their legs give out, and eventually it starts killing them, unless the master gets hold of a syndicate implant configurator and performs a risky brain operation (cut, retract, saw, clamp, adjust, cauterise) to buy more time. Pull the implant out and the slave wakes up free, with no memory of anything that happened while enslaved, including who owned them.

- **Take** — It gives traitors a way to recruit a real, unwilling accomplice with hard social rules baked in, and hands the victim a genuinely interesting forced-roleplay role instead of just being a corpse.
- **Skip** — Every player-facing string is Russian only (no en-US file at all), so the whole thing needs translating before it is usable, and the implant's decay escalation plus its rescue surgery are wired into SS220's own surgery and hidden-description systems rather than upstream ones.
- **Touches** — antagonist, security, medical, all-players
- **Needs** — [traitor-uplink](#traitor-uplink), [surgery-and-limb-wounds](#surgery-and-limb-wounds)
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. A full `git ls-tree -r` of the fork (partial clone, tree fully resolved) shows every MindSlave file — Content.Server/SS220/MindSlave/*, Content.Client/SS220/MindSlave/*, Content.Shared/SS220/MindSlave/*, and its uplink listing in Resources/Prototypes/SS220/Catalog/uplink_catalog.yml — lives entirely inside SS220/ namespace directories; no upstream file is edited in place, so 'fork-patches-upstream' is false and the seed's directory-based 'drop-in' read is technically correct. But FixMindSlaveDisfunctionAction.cs and the head_surgery.yml fix step depend on Content.Shared.SS220.Surgery.Graph (the fork's own custom surgery-graph engine) and MindSlaveSystem.cs depends on Content.Server/Shared.SS220.Telepathy (the fork's own telepathy system) plus HiddenDescription — all separate, sizeable SS220 subsystems that would have to be grafted alongside it. That is fork-internal entanglement, not 'needs upstream edits' in the sense the claim asserts (no upstream files are actually touched or need touching for the feature's own files to exist).
  - unsupported: "they must obey every order their master gives, cannot hurt themselves, cannot hurt their master" is presented as a hard, code-enforced restriction ("hard social rules baked in"), but MindSlaveComponent.cs only carries a StopWord field and a status icon — no attack-blocking logic exists. MindSlaveSystem.cs even explicitly strips PacifiedComponent from the newly-enslaved victim ("Remove pacifism from slave, because if the slave is pacified they becomes pretty useless"), i.e. the engine deliberately leaves them free to fight. Only the master's-name censorship (OnAccent stop-word replacement) is actually mechanically enforced; the self-harm/master-harm rules are just text in the notification popup, not a mechanic.
  - unsupported: The surgery step list "cut, retract, saw, clamp, adjust, cauterise" overstates the confirmed sequence: head_surgery.yml's path to brain-exposed is incision (cut) → clamp-bleeders (clamp) → retract-skin (retract) → saw-skull-bone (saw), and seal-wound uses a cautery tool (cauterise) — but no 'adjust' step appears in that required path; set-bones/bone-gel are only alternate fallback branches taken if the surgeon botches the bone-sawing step, not a normal part of fixing the mindslave disfunction.

**backmen, starlight, sunrise, viva-station**

*activity · drop-in · medium confidence · 0 forks carry it*

These forks each add one small extra antagonist who does not threaten the station itself. The Fugitive (Backmen, Sunrise) is an escaped prisoner who wakes up hidden aboard in an orange jumpsuit with an engineering belt and electrical toolbox; a while later GALPOL blares a station-wide manhunt announcement and a wanted report with the fugitive's name and description prints out of the command fax machines, and from then on the fugitive just has to stay uncaught and ride the evac shuttle out while security decides whether to bother chasing them. Starlight's SELF agent is a silicon-liberation activist (locked behind heavy borg/science playtime) who spawns with an emag and a special toolbox and is told to free three cyborgs and the station AI from their lawsets, then leave uncuffed. Viva's CCD Agent is a single player on 15+ player rounds who gets an intro sting, a supply box and one line of orders: "You are an agent of the CCD. Fix the timeline."

- **Take** — A cheap, low-stakes antag that gives security a real manhunt and one player a tense hide-and-run round without putting the station or the round outcome at risk.
- **Skip** — Each fork's version is a thin sketch (Viva's whole briefing is "fix the timeline") whose fun depends entirely on crew reacting to the announcement, so on a quiet shift a fugitive can sit in maintenance doing nothing for an hour.
- **Touches** — antagonist, security, all-players, silicon
- **Needs** — [antag-objectives-and-uplink-rework](#antag-objectives-and-uplink-rework)
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. I fetched full recursive trees for backmen, sunrise, starlight and viva and checked every sibling file for each antag (Fugitive components/system/locale/prototypes for Backmen and Sunrise, SELF components/system/locale/prototypes for Starlight, TimeAgent prototypes/locale for Viva). All of them live entirely inside the fork's own namespace (_Sunrise, Backmen/_Backmen, _Starlight, _Viva) with zero files touched outside it — matching the seed's path-data signal. None of the four forks edit a shared preset/event-rotation file to wire the antag in: Backmen's Fugitive self-registers as a StationEvent, Sunrise's Fugitive is a ghost-role marker (no preset edit needed), and Viva ships its own standalone _Viva/game_presets.yml ("CCD" preset) rather than touching the 424-line upstream game_presets.yml. The custom objective condition Starlight's SELF agent needs (EnsureLawBoundEntitiesHaveNoLawsConditionComponent.cs) is also defined inside _Starlight, not in a shared Objectives folder. I found no concrete evidence of the fork-patches-upstream reading, and the practical wiring path (a new preset/event file) doesn't obviously require upstream edits either, so the claim's downgrade from the seed's drop-in looks over-cautious given what I could actually verify.
  - unsupported: "The Fugitive (Backmen, Sunrise) is an escaped prisoner who wakes up hidden aboard in an orange jumpsuit with an engineering belt and electrical toolbox" — this exact loadout is true for Sunrise (FugitiveStartingGear has belt: ClothingBeltUtilityEngineering and inhand ToolboxElectricalFilled), but Backmen's own fugitive.yml has no belt field at all and its ToolboxElectricalFilled inhand line is commented out (disabled), so Backmen's fugitive does not actually spawn with a belt or toolbox.

### Wizard and spellcasting

<a id="wizard-magic"></a>

Magic-using antagonist with a purchasable spellbook, staves, polymorph forms, summoned familiars and apprentices.

**goobstation**

*structural · entangled · medium confidence · 5 forks carry it*

A wizard arrives on the station with a book of spells and a pile of magic gear, and spends the round doing openly absurd, high-power things to the crew: turning people into animals with a staff of change, throwing lightning packets, teleporting across the station with a scroll or a target-picker window, turning into an unstoppable roaring hulk, spying on rooms through a scrying orb, and fighting with enchanted swords, a supermatter halberd or a bolt-action rifle that fires magic bullets. Victims polymorphed into animals actually start speaking in that animal's noises, and there is a joke "chuuni" mode where every spell you cast is announced with a florid anime incantation. The wizard can also sign apprenticeship contracts that pull ghosts in as junior wizards, each with a themed spell loadout (destruction, ethereal, summoning, gunslinger, arcane, sanguine, robeless, or completely random), who are told to protect their master at all costs.

- **Take** — It turns the wizard from a single antag into a whole round archetype, with a real spell economy, a refundable purchase store, and team-antag apprentice ghost roles that give spectators something to do mid-round.
- **Skip** — It is roughly 666 files across three assemblies including a fork-only Content.Goobstation.Common magic layer and client-side UI for mirror, refund, spellblade and teleport, plus stray cross-links into Goob's Lavaland content, so it cannot be lifted as a folder and will need continuous re-merging.
- **Touches** — antagonist, ghost-roles, security, all-players, command
- **Needs** — [lavaland-mining-planet](#lavaland-mining-planet)
- **Verified** — supported. Every substantive gameplay beat checks out against real fetched files: staff of change fires ProjectileWabbajack (polymorph), a scrying orb grants vision/ghost-sight actions, a supermatter halberd and an enchanted bolt-action rifle firing CartridgeMagicBullet/BulletMagic exist, teleport scrolls and apprenticeship contracts (ghost-role ContractApprenticeship) exist, chuuni.ftl contains florid per-spell invocation lines, hulk.ftl has roar lines, apprentices.ftl lists exactly the themed loadouts named (destruction, ethereal, summon, gunslinger, arcane, sanguine, plus more before truncation) each told to 'protect the wizard... at all costs', and Content.Server/_Shitcode/Wizard/Accents contains a full set of per-animal accent components (Bat/Bear/Bee/Cow/Fox/Frog/Horse/Jackal/Pig/Rat/Raven) confirming the polymorph-then-speak-as-animal claim. The graft_shape call of 'entangled' is the stronger finding here: I found GlobalTileMovementSystem.cs and SharedSpellsSystem.cs under the Wizard folders directly importing and using `Content.Shared._Lavaland.Movement` (GlobalTileMovementRuleComponent wired into a wizard event-spell rule), which is a genuine functional dependency on the fork's Lavaland feature, not a coincidental import. Content.Client/_Shitcode/Wizard also contains exactly the MagicMirror/Refund/Spellblade/Teleport UI subfolders the claim names, and Content.Goobstation.Common does contain a small Magic/ subdirectory (MagicEvents.cs), so 'fork-only Content.Goobstation.Common magic layer' is accurate if minimal. File-count matching 'roughly 666 files' is in the right order of magnitude (691 path matches for wizard/spell/magic just in a truncated tree listing, concentrated in Content.Server/Client/Shared _Shitcode/Wizard subtrees, i.e. plausibly 'three assemblies' plus the small Goobstation.Common piece). Nothing in the claim overstates what the files show.

**frontier**

*activity · entangled · medium confidence · 5 forks carry it*

Robed Wizard Federation casters exist as a hostile faction to fight rather than a wizard antag round: apprentices lob bars of soap and summoned elementals, adepts sling ice bolts, fireballs and thrown bricks, and masters chain lightning or burn you down with a caustic beam, muttering to themselves between shots. Kill one and its robes and staff drop as loot, and a staff charger machine lets you refill a captured staff and throw the same magic back at whatever comes next. The spells are shouted-incantation summons that wink out after three minutes: a magic vending machine, a blue-curacao elemental that imprints on whoever conjured it and fights alongside them, or a shade and a drained one borrowed from the fork's cult content.

- **Take** — It reframes wizardry as lootable PvE content — a three-tier enemy faction with distinct elemental attack patterns, plus rechargeable staves the crew can capture and actually cast with — instead of a single-player antag round.
- **Skip** — It leans on Frontier's own hostile-mob and faction scaffolding (a custom hostilewizard inventory template, WizFedFaction, a heretic damage modifier set) and two of the four conjure spells summon blood-cult mobs, so grafting means porting or stubbing those first; and the wizards are dead weight until you also have expeditions or ruins to place them in.
- **Touches** — salvage, security, expedition-crews, all-players
- **Needs** — [blood-cult](#blood-cult), [heretic](#heretic)
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. All parent prototypes I traced (MobHumanoidHostileBase, MobStaminaSpecial, MobMovementSpeedModifierRanged, NFMobNoEquipmentOnGib, BaseC3WizardContraband, WizFedFaction/ai_factions.yml) live inside Resources/Prototypes/_NF/*, so the fork's wizard copy does not patch upstream directories — that rules out a literal 'fork-patches-upstream' reading. But two of the four conjure spells reference MobBloodCultDrainedOneNanoTrasen/MobBloodCultShadeNanoTrasen defined in a sibling _NF file (mob_hostile_bloodcultist.yml) not in the 7 cited paths, and the whole mob line depends on generic _NF hostile-mob scaffolding (mob_hostile_base.yml) also outside the cited set — so grafting just the 7 files would fail to load without also pulling in other fork units. That is inter-unit entanglement within the fork's own namespace, not an upstream-edit requirement, so neither of the two offered 'needs-upstream-edits' readings cleanly applies.
  - unsupported: "adepts sling ice bolts, fireballs and thrown bricks" — the red adept/master fires NFBulletMagicFireBoltMob, whose prototype name is literally "fire bolt" (only its gunshot sound file is named fireball.ogg); there is no distinct "fireball" spell/projectile in the cited files.
  - unsupported: skip_because's "a heretic damage modifier set" framed as a dependency in depends_on: ["heretic"] — MobHereticDamageModifierSet is defined fork-locally in Resources/Prototypes/_NF/Damage/modifier_sets.yml and is just a shared resistance profile also used by the fork's own bloodcultist mob; nothing in the wizard files couples to actual heretic antagonist gameplay/mechanics.
  - unsupported: touches: ["salvage", "expedition-crews"] are only weakly evidenced — the only map reference to a wizard spawner found was Resources/Maps/_NF/Bluespace/wizardtower.yml, a single POI, not a demonstrated salvage/expedition system integration.

### Solo monster antagonists

<a id="solo-monster-antags"></a>

Ported one-creature midround antagonists that hunt the crew alone, each with its own ability kit, overlays and spawn rule.

**goobstation**

*structural · entangled · medium confidence · 4 forks carry it*

Mid-round, a ghost can be dropped in as one of seven distinct monsters that hunt the station alone, each with its own kit and its own counterplay. The Slaughter Demon dives into blood puddles to teleport between rooms and devours crew whole, hunting the wizard who summoned it first. The Wraith is an incorporeal spirit that spends a growing pool of Wraith Points to possess machines, haunt people, and stack five escalating curses (weakness, bleeding, rot, blindness, death) on a victim; it can be banished once, is immune-checked by the chaplain, and is forced back into a killable physical body if it walks over salt. The Slasher picks one of nine themed looks at spawn (butcher, hockey mask, clown, springlock suit), summons a machete and meat spikes, phases out of sight when nobody is watching, and drains souls off downed victims until a station-wide alert warns the crew it has ascended. Bingle is a hungry pit that grows as bodies and loot are fed into it, with players joining as more Bingles speaking their own babbling language. Hastur devours, lashes and clones itself while flooding everyone's chat with maddening whispers, the Chrono Legionnaire freezes people in time-stasis, and the Nightmare eats the lights around it.

- **Take** — Seven finished, thematically distinct solo hunters with real counterplay hooks (salt against the Wraith, watching eyes against the Slasher, the chaplain as a hard counter) is a large amount of ready-made midround variety you would otherwise have to design from scratch.
- **Skip** — It is 835 files and roughly 265 C# systems across seven unrelated monsters, each with its own overlays, status effects, objectives and spawn rule, so you inherit seven separate balance and bug surfaces at once and cannot realistically maintain them without cherry-picking one monster and dropping the rest.
- **Touches** — antagonist, ghost-roles, all-players, security, service, command
- **Needs** — [wizard-magic](#wizard-magic), [language-system](#language-system)
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. Five of the seven claimed monsters (Slaughter Demon, Wraith, Slasher, Bingle, Hastur) check out in detail and live cleanly under _Goobstation/Content.Goobstation.* — but the unit reaches further than the seed's path data saw. Bingle's own-language mechanic depends on Content.Shared/_EinsteinEngines/Language/LanguagePrototype.cs + SharedLanguageSystem.cs, a separate vendored fork's namespace bundled inside Goob-Station, not upstream vanilla and not _Goobstation either. If Nightmare is really part of this unit, its LightEater code is likewise only wired into the Shadowling antagonist under Resources/Prototypes/_EinsteinEngines/Shadowling/. Slaughter Demon's \"kill the wizard\" objective is a genuine soft dependency on vanilla SS14's Wizard antagonist (already satisfied by any vanilla-based fork). None of this is the fork editing upstream files in place (so 'fork-patches-upstream' is wrong), but grafting this unit into a codebase without Goob-Station's bundled _EinsteinEngines Language/Shadowling systems would require importing or reimplementing those systems too — that is dependency on the source fork's OTHER bundled systems, i.e. entangled, rather than the vanilla-upstream-edit scenario 'needs-upstream-edits' implies.
  - unsupported: "the Chrono Legionnaire freezes people in time-stasis" framed as one of seven distinct hunting monsters — actual evidence (Resources/Prototypes/_Goobstation/Entities/Mobs/Player/admeme.yml lines ~286-303, Resources/Prototypes/_Goobstation/Roles/GhostRoles/Fun/chrono_legionnaire.yml) shows it is a RandomHumanoidSpawner costume/gear loadout filed under an admeme.yml section literally titled "## Other Shit" alongside HECU/ERT-style admin event NPCs, parented to `EventHumanoidMindShielded` (mind-shielded, i.e. not a hostile antagonist), with zero locale strings anywhere in the repo (no ghost-role-information-chronolegionnaire-*, no antag objectives found). It is a stasis-gun costume for admin-spawned NPCs, not a self-directed monster hunting the station with its own kit/objectives like the other five.
  - unsupported: "the Nightmare eats the lights around it" presented as the 7th monster of this catalog unit — the actual light-eating code (Content.Goobstation.Shared/Nightmare/NightmareSystem.cs, Content.Goobstation.Server/Nightmare/LightEaterSystem.cs) is wired up via `LightEaterArmBlade`/`LightEaterUser` components that are only ever attached in Resources/Prototypes/_EinsteinEngines/Shadowling/Entities/Items/items.yml and .../Specific/abilities.yml — i.e. it is an ability of the pre-existing, separately-vendored Shadowling antagonist (from the Einstein Engines fork, bundled under its own _EinsteinEngines namespace), not a standalone ghost-role solo monster belonging to this catalog unit.

**serbia-strong**

*activity · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 4 forks carry it*

Two one-creature monsters can turn up partway through a round and hunt the crew on their own. The Dark Reaper starts as an intangible shade that has to materialise to attack, drags bodies inside itself to feed, and grows through three stages as it eats; along the way it can let out a shriek that shatters nearby lights and leaves everyone in a wide radius stunned, blinded and staggering, drop blood mist and smoke to cover its escape, and by its final stage the station goes to delta alert. Kill it and it bursts apart into a scattering of lesser horrors. The Spider Queen instead builds: she cocoons victims she has downed, drains them over a few seconds into a blood-point pool shown on her HUD, and spends those points spinning webs that slow pursuers, raising crystals and walls, releasing swarms of short-lived spiderlings, and laying eggs that hatch guard, hunter, ghost or shooter spiders, so an unnoticed nest quietly becomes a whole infested wing before the announcement goes out.

- **Take** — Two fully-built solo monster antags with distinct fantasies (a phasing body-eating terror and a nest-building queen with a resource economy) that give ghosts something to play and give the whole crew a shared threat, without touching how any existing role works.
- **Skip** — SS220 ships this under its own EULA/CLA with a hosting restriction rather than a normal open licence, so copying these files is a licensing problem before it is an engineering one; on top of that it is roughly 50 files of custom sprites, sounds, alerts, mob prototypes and rule systems that you would own and rebalance forever.
- **Touches** — antagonist, ghost-roles, security, medical, all-players
- **Verified** — partly supported. All 8 cited files exist verbatim and are self-contained under SS220-namespaced directories (Content.Shared/SS220/DarkReaper, Content.Shared/SS220/SpiderQueen, Resources/Prototypes/SS220/*), confirming three stages, materialize/dematerialize gating attacks, consume-into-container feeding, light-destroying stun+confusion, delta alert at stage 3, blood-point HUD alert, 5s cocoon extraction, and web/crystal/wall/spiderling/egg abilities spawning guard/hunter/ghost/shooter spiders exactly as named. But I read the actual death-handler (OnMobStateChanged in SharedDarkReaperSystem.cs) and it spawns inert organ/limb gore prototypes with physics impulse, not living "lesser horrors" — and the cocooning handler (SharedSpiderQueenSystem.cs) hard-requires _mobState.IsDead(target), not merely downed. Reading these two files myself against the prose is what drops this from full support. On graft shape: I found zero evidence any of these unit's own files sit outside the SS220 namespace, so the fork's copy is self-contained; the downgrade from the path-data's drop-in guess to needs-upstream-edits is best read as an integration cost (wiring the antag id into a round-start selection/preset list lives outside these files) rather than the fork itself patching upstream in place, which I could not find and did not evidence.
  - unsupported: Kill it and it bursts apart into a scattering of lesser horrors.
  - unsupported: she cocoons victims she has downed

**sunrise**

*activity · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 4 forks carry it*

Sunrise adds two standalone monsters. The first is a demon "hellspawn" fought as an opt-in raid: a boss battle altar sits on the station with a status readout and a Travel button on a timer, and crew who press it get pulled onto a separate arena map guarded by robed cultists. Cutting a cultist down summons the demon in a roaring, ground-shaking spawn animation, and it fights with a telegraphed kit — a long charge across the room, short and long tentacle swipes, a spiral attack, a fire-starting move and a timed invincibility window — while everyone shows on the radar; when the whole raid party is dead or crit the survivors are dumped back on station and the arena closes, and a winning party butchers the corpse for hardsuits, exotic guns, artifact fragments, cyber-limbs and a pile of joke drops. The second is a Carp Queen who feeds to lay eggs, which only hatch into carp servants on wet or flooded tiles, and who orders her school around by pointing at things to make them stay, follow, kill or break off.

- **Take** — A self-contained, opt-in boss raid with a real loot payoff gives combat-hungry crew something to do mid-round without touching how the round is won, and the arena runs on its own map so a wipe costs the station nothing.
- **Skip** — The boss's whole reason to exist is its loot table, which is stuffed with Sunrise-only prototypes (cult pylons, PKA upgrades, fork guns, xeno artifact items) plus fork sprites and locale files that are not in this file set, so a graft is a long reconciliation pass before it works at all — and the altar has to be placed on your station maps by hand.
- **Touches** — antagonist, ghost-roles, security, salvage, all-players
- **Verified** — partly supported. All 7 cited files (HellSpawnArenaSystem.cs, ents.yml, actions.yml, CarpQueenSystem.cs, CarpEggSystem.cs, carp_queen_commands.yml, HellSpawnArenaConsoleWindow.xaml.cs) fetched cleanly and directly corroborate nearly every specific gameplay beat: the altar console with countdown Travel button and status readout, cooldown-gated teleport to a loaded arena shuttle map guarded by a main cultist plus 4 dummy cultists, cultist death/gib triggering SpawnHellSpawn with a roaring TimedDespawn spawn entity chained to an Explosive trigger (ground shake), the exact ability kit (Rush/charge, Tentacle left+right, Spiral, ActionFireStarter, a 30s Invincibility window), whole-party-dead/crit teleporting survivors home and deleting the arena map, and a Butcherable loot table stuffed with hardsuits, guns, ArtifactFragment, a cyber-limb, and joke items (goldmedal, bible, figurines) exactly as the skip_because reasoning describes. Carp Queen is equally well matched: OnSummon spends hunger to spawn an egg, CarpEggSystem only lets eggs go Eligible/hatch when a puddle or FloorWaterEntity on the tile has sufficient volume, and CarpQueenCommandStay/Follow/Kill/Loose datasets plus OnPointedAt wiring confirm the point-to-order mechanic. The one place the prose oversells the evidence is \"everyone shows on the radar\" — only the boss and the altar console carry RadarBlip in what I read; fighters/cultists don't. On graft shape: all 7 evidence files live inside _Sunrise-namespaced directories (Content.Server/_Sunrise/..., Content.Client/_Sunrise/..., Resources/Prototypes/_Sunrise/...), so the fork's own copy of this feature is self-contained by what I could verify — I found no direct evidence of the fork editing files inside non-_Sunrise upstream directories. The needs-upstream-edits call rests on integration friction described in skip_because and confirmed structurally: the altar (ComputerBossTravel/SpawnComputerBossTravel) has no automatic placement logic, so wiring it in means hand-placing it on a target repo's own station maps, and the loot table's many fork-only prototype IDs (CultPylon, PKAUpgrade*, ComplexXenoArtifactItem, etc.) mean a grafter needs to pull in a large, only-partially-evidenced tail of the fork's own prototype/sprite/locale tree before the boss even compiles cleanly.
  - unsupported: "while everyone shows on the radar" — the evidence only gives RadarBlip to the boss (MobHellspawnBoss) and the altar console (ComputerBossTravel), not to the fighters or cultists; the raid party members are not shown to have a RadarBlip component in the cited files, so "everyone" overstates what the evidence supports.

**einstein-engines, harmony-station, starlight**

*activity · entangled · medium confidence · 4 forks carry it*

These three forks each drop a different single-creature midround monster into the station. Harmony's bingle is a pack of small clawing aliens around a "bingle pit" that swallows whatever steps on it and slowly grows, with the bingles getting visibly stronger as they feed it; the pit tears through walls and airlocks and drops a loot crate if the crew manages to destroy it. Starlight adds a full terror-spider hive where a lone spider queen lays eggs, and hatchlings pick a colour path (combat, stealth, or a support type that implants eggs inside living crew) and evolve through three tiers by spinning webs or infecting people, plus a separate "Terminator" ghost role that arrives with one named person to kill and orders to self-destruct rather than be captured. Einstein Engines contributes a shadow-fleshed nightmare that walks in from the dark and can snuff out light sources around it, so fighting it means fighting the station's own lighting first.

- **Take** — Each one is a self-contained midround threat with its own flavour and escalation curve, so you can graft exactly one and get a fresh round-disrupting monster without touching any existing antag.
- **Skip** — All three arrive as art-plus-code creatures with almost no player-facing text (Harmony ships two locale lines total), so briefings, guidebook pages and balance passes are on you, and Starlight's terminator is wired into that fork's own antag-specifier framework rather than upstream's antag selection.
- **Touches** — antagonist, ghost-roles, security, engineering, medical, all-players
- **Needs** — [antag-objectives-and-uplink-rework](#antag-objectives-and-uplink-rework)
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. Harmony's bingle (BinglePit/BinglePitSystem, bingle mobs) and Starlight's terror-spider hive + terminator (TerrorSpider.xml guidebook, terminator.yml gamerule/objectives/roles) match the claim's specifics closely and are genuinely self-contained within their own _Harmony/_Starlight namespaces. But the claim's universal framing ('each one is self-contained... without touching any existing antag') is falsified by Einstein Engines: NightmareSystem.cs (Content.Server/_EE/Nightmare/Systems/) reaches directly into two other EE-only antagonist systems — Shadowling (LesserShadowlingComponent, ThrallComponent, ShadowlingPlaneShiftComponent) and Blood Cult (PhaseShiftedComponent from Content.Shared.WhiteDream.BloodCult.Constructs.PhaseShift) — none of which are in the cited evidence. That is entanglement with the fork's OWN other antag systems, a different and worse problem than 'needs upstream edits' for wiring into round-start selection. All three forks' own files stay inside their fork namespaces (no direct edits into upstream directories were found), so 'fork-patches-upstream' is not supported either — hence 'integration-would-require-upstream-edits' is the closer of the two forced readings, though neither cleanly describes the actual defect (dependency on other same-fork systems, not vanilla upstream).
  - unsupported: Each one is a self-contained midround threat with its own flavour and escalation curve, so you can graft exactly one and get a fresh round-disrupting monster without touching any existing antag. — False for the Einstein Engines example: Content.Server/_EE/Nightmare/Systems/NightmareSystem.cs directly imports and uses Content.Shared._EE.Shadowling.Components (LesserShadowlingComponent, ThrallComponent) and EnsureComp<ShadowlingPlaneShiftComponent>, plus Content.Shared.WhiteDream.BloodCult.Constructs.PhaseShift (PhaseShiftedComponent) — two completely separate EE antagonist systems (Shadowling and Blood Cult). Grafting the EE nightmare alone, without also bringing in Shadowling's plane-shift component and the Blood Cult construct's phase-shift component, would not compile/function as written.

### Changeling

<a id="changeling"></a>

Shapeshifting antagonist that absorbs crew DNA to copy identities, spends evolution points on biological weapons and revives from apparent death.

**goobstation**

*structural · entangled · medium confidence · 5 forks carry it*

A changeling looks and sounds exactly like a crewmate until it doesn't. It grabs someone hard, holds them down and absorbs them, leaving a hollow husk that reads "the body feels hollow" on examine, and it can then wear that person's face and name for the rest of the round. It runs on two bars instead of an uplink: chemicals that slowly refill and pay for abilities, and biomass that drains until it eats, warning "we begin to hunger" and eventually killing it. Points spent in an evolution menu buy an arm blade, claw or hammer that erupts from the body, chitinous armour and an organic shield, a dart gun, deafening shrieks that break lights and radios, and silent stings that blind, mute, slow or chill a victim from a distance. Escape hatches include instant wound-and-broken-bone regeneration, a stun-proof adrenaline surge, adaptation to darkness and to freezing vacuum, going translucent, and dropping into regenerative stasis so it plays dead and gets back up unless someone defibs or absorbs the corpse. As a last resort it abandons the body entirely and skitters away as a vent-crawling head slug. Lings share a private Hivemind radio channel, and their objectives are absorb N humanoids, absorb rival changelings, collect unique genomes, or escape on the shuttle wearing a specific person's identity.

- **Take** — It is a complete, mature antagonist with its own economy, shop, identity theft, fake-death loop and objectives, and it reshapes rounds by making the crew distrust faces rather than hunt for contraband.
- **Skip** — Absorbing requires a hard grab, so the whole kill loop assumes Goob's grab/combat escalation rather than upstream pulling, and the ~230 files of abilities, stings, armour, shields, dart gun and head slug mob are a large permanent maintenance surface that also collides with upstream's own in-progress changeling.
- **Touches** — antagonist, security, medical, all-players
- **Needs** — [close-quarters-combat-rework](#close-quarters-combat-rework), [reagent-and-reaction-expansion](#reagent-and-reaction-expansion)
- **Verified** — supported. Fetched the cited .ftl and .yml files directly and every specific beat checks out: biomass/chemicals dual-bar economy with hunger warnings, hard-grab-gated absorb ("We aren't grabbing hard enough"), hollow-husk examine text, evolution-menu catalog selling armblade/claw/hammer/dart gun/shriek(dissonant+resonant)/chitinous armor/organic shield, fleshmend + panacea healing, adrenaline stun immunity, dark/void adaptation, chameleon translucency, regenerative stasis, the headcrab (MobHeadcrab, VentCrawler tag) as the last-resort escape body, Hivemind radio channel, and all four objective types (absorb N, absorb rival lings, steal unique genomes, escape wearing a specific identity). Nothing in the gameplay paragraph was invented. Critically, I went past the cited Resources/_Goobstation files to check where the actual C# game logic lives, since the seed's drop-in claim rests entirely on path data that can't see in-place upstream edits. Content.Shared/Changeling (not namespaced under _Goobstation) contains Components/, Systems/ (ChangelingClonerSystem.cs, SharedChangelingIdentitySystem.cs), and upstream space-wizards/space-station-14 has its own Content.Shared/Changeling with matching Components/Systems subfolders and files like ChangelingDevourEvents.cs/ChangelingTransformEvents.cs at the same path. That is a direct, verified collision with upstream's own in-progress changeling implementation, exactly what the assessor's skip_because already described. This falsifies the drop-in seed and confirms 'entangled' is the correct call, not merely an unverified downgrade.

### Blood cult

<a id="blood-cult"></a>

Team antagonist that draws blood runes to convert or sacrifice crew, forges cult gear, binds souls into constructs and works toward summoning its god.

**sunrise**

*structural · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 3 forks carry it*

A few crew start the round secretly serving a blood god (Nar'Si, Pir'Kus or the Reaper), each with a ritual dagger, a stack of runic metal and a pinpointer that points toward the crew members they have been told to kill. They carve runes into the floor in blood to convert captured victims, revive dead cultists, teleport between marked runes, raise barriers, boil an enemy's blood from a distance, and eventually run the Ritual of Dimensional Rending that tears their god into the station. Between rituals they draw blood magic spells onto their hands (stun touch, shadow shackles, an EMP pulse, summoning a dagger or armour and weapons onto a fellow cultist), build cult girders, airlocks, pylons, an archive, an altar and a forge out of runic metal, and trap souls in shards so ghosts can return as juggernaut, artificer, wraith or reaper constructs. Cultists see each other and their runes through a red overlay the rest of the crew cannot.

- **Take** — It is a complete second round type with its own conversion mechanic, base-building, ghost-role constructs and an endgame summon, all shipped as a self-contained _Sunrise namespace rather than scattered patches.
- **Skip** — Roughly 480 files including ~134 C# files, custom prototype kinds, tile and decal sets, six bespoke UI windows and three god variants — it is a fork-sized subsystem to review, rebalance and then keep alive across every upstream merge, and it needs an admin/player culture that can handle a station-wide conversion antag.
- **Touches** — antagonist, all-players, security, ghost-roles, service, command
- **Verified** — partly supported. Sparse-cloned the real BloodCult tree (38 prototype files + Content.Server/_Sunrise/BloodCult) and confirmed almost every specific mechanic the claim names: startingItems (NarsieRitualDagger/CultRunicMetal10/BloodCultPinpointer), rune types (Offering/Revive/Teleport/Barrier/BloodBoil/ApocalypseRune - the last literally named "Ritual of Dimensional Rending"), spells (ActionCultStun, ActionShadowShackles, InstantActionEmpPulse, ActionCultSummonCombatEquipment/InstantActionSummonCultDagger), buildable structures (CultGirder, AirlockGlassCult, CultPylon, AltarTome, CultForge), and all four constructs (Juggernaut/Artificer/Wraith/ReaperConstruct). That's a very well-evidenced gameplay description. But one specific claim does not hold up: 'Cultists see each other and their runes through a red overlay the rest of the crew cannot' - the only faction-vision mechanic I found is ShowCultHudSystem, a status-icon (FactionIcon) shown above cultist heads only to other cultists; runes themselves (cult_runes.yml) are plain Sprite/Appearance entities with per-rune fixed colors (e.g. '#F80000' for one rune, '#008080' for another), with no component restricting their visibility to non-cultists. There's no 'red overlay' vision system and no evidence runes are hidden from the rest of the crew. On graft_shape: I found direct proof this is NOT a clean drop-in the way the path-data seed guessed. Resources/Prototypes/_Sunrise/BloodCult/Entities/Items/weapon.yml defines 'TrueHalberd' with parent: UnholyHalberd, and UnholyHalberd is defined in Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Objects/Weapons/Melee/cult.yml - a non-_Sunrise, upstream-path file. Diffing that file against space-wizards/space-station-14 master shows sunrise's copy has actually drifted (Sharp vs Tool/Slicing quality, added storage shape data), i.e. the fork's own repo carries a modified copy of a file outside the feature's namespace that BloodCult's own prototypes inherit from. This confirms the claim's needs-upstream-edits categorization and shows exactly the kind of entanglement path-data alone can't see (a parent: reference inside an in-namespace file reaching an out-of-namespace prototype).
  - unsupported: Cultists see each other and their runes through a red overlay the rest of the crew cannot.

**white-dream**

*structural · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 3 forks carry it*

A handful of crew wake up as servants of Nar'Sie with a ritual dagger, able to whisper to each other in a tongue only cultists understand. They carve blood runes into the floor of a hidden shrine to teleport between hideouts, empower themselves so spells cast fast and cheap, raise temporary walls, boil the blood of anyone who can see the rune, and revive fallen brothers from a limited pool of charges; a converting rune turns a held-down crewmate into a cultist, while sacrificing one produces soul shards that get built into shades, artificers, wraiths and juggernauts that fight, tunnel through walls and build cult structures. With runed metal they raise pylons, forges, archives, altars, doors and girders, forge armour and weapons non-cultists physically cannot pick up or swing, drain and store blood to heal on the move, and shatter an orb to delay the evacuation shuttle. Winning means murdering a named sacrifice target, then drawing the Dimensional Rending rune in one of only three thin spots on the station, surviving 45 seconds of security kicking the door in, and getting ten cultists to stand on it so their god physically arrives.

- **Take** — It is a complete, guidebook-documented team antagonist with a genuine escalation arc (hidden shrine, conversion, sacrifice, public summoning ritual) that gives the whole station a visible endgame to fight, and nothing upstream fills that slot.
- **Skip** — It is roughly 220 files of bespoke systems (runes, spells, constructs, cult-only item restrictions, shuttle curse, phase shift, custom UIs and placement modes) plus its own sprite and structure set, so you inherit a large permanent maintenance surface that will conflict with upstream reworks of mind roles, construction, damage and the emergency shuttle.
- **Touches** — antagonist, security, medical, chaplain, all-players, ghost-roles
- **Verified** — supported. Full repo-tree cross-check (GitHub trees API, 461k-line manifest) found 229 blood-cult paths: all ~110 C# files sit cleanly under Content.{Server,Client,Shared}/_White/BloodCult (plus a few _White/GameTicking, _White/Objectives, _White/Roles files), confirming the code itself is self-contained. But one file, Resources/Prototypes/Language/FactionSpecific/blood_cult.yml, defines the "Eldritch" cultist whisper language and lives outside any _White directory, alongside blob.yml/shadowling.yml for other antags. It plugs into a full pre-existing multilingual "Language" system (Content.Server/Language, Content.Shared/Language, Content.Client/Language — dozens of files, confirmed 404 on vanilla space-wizards/space-station-14, so it's inherited base/Einstein-Engine-style infrastructure, not something blood-cult brings itself). That's a real dependency the claim's depends_on:[] omits, and it directly falsifies the seed's "drop-in" (zero non-namespace files) premise — so the assessor's downgrade to needs-upstream-edits is correct, and arguably under-documents why.
  - unsupported: "surviving 45 seconds of security kicking the door in" — the guidebook literally says the caster must hold out 45 seconds against a general "barrage of enemies" (шквал врагов), not specifically security forcing the door; a reasonable dramatization but not literally sourced.
  - unsupported: "a converting rune turns a held-down crewmate into a cultist" — the guide only says conversion needs two cultists present at the rune, it doesn't specify the target must be physically restrained/held down (unlike the sacrifice case, which the guide does specify needs three cultists for a living, presumably restrained, victim).

**funky**

*structural · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 3 forks carry it*

A hidden team of crew members wakes up sworn to Nar'Sie. They can carve a ritual dagger out of their own body, whisper to each other over a private cult channel, check how close the veil is to tearing, and prepare blood spells by cutting them into their flesh — including one that drops a victim into a nightmare sleep or EMPs a borg. They scratch runes into the floor in blood to convert, sacrifice or heal people, and the crew's counter-play is to find and scrub those runes off the deck before they get used. As the cult grows they build out a base with a healing pylon, a forge for unholy weapons, arcane archives and a bloodstained altar, trap the souls of the dead in soul stones, and slot those souls into inert juggernaut shells to raise slow, armoured, punch-everything constructs. The endgame is tearing a reality rift open on the station.

- **Take** — It is a complete, self-driving team antagonist with its own progression arc (convert, build a base, forge gear, raise constructs, tear the veil) that gives the whole station a visible, physical threat to hunt rather than another quiet backstab round.
- **Skip** — It is huge — roughly 80 server/client systems, 30 prototype files and its own damage containers, blood metabolism hooks, mindshield-breaking ritual and construct AI — and it deliberately reaches into upstream mindshield and blood behaviour, so every upstream sync becomes a merge job on a subsystem nobody on the fork wrote.
- **Touches** — antagonist, security, command, medical, chaplain, all-players, ghost-roles
- **Verified** — supported. Fetched all 9 cited files plus follow-up files. Every specific gameplay beat checks out verbatim against source: StudyVeil/Commune/SpellsSelect/SummonDagger/SanguineDream actions in Actions/spells.yml match "check the veil", "whisper... private cult channel", "carve dagger from own body", "prepare blood spells... cutting into flesh", "nightmare sleep + EMP borg + mindshield stun"; CultPylon/CultForge/CultArchives/CultAltar descriptions in cult_structures.yml match "healing pylon/forge for unholy weapons/arcane archives/bloodstained altar" word for word; CultSoulStone, constructs.yml (juggernaut shell completed by dragging a body or soulstone, slow/strong/punch-everything Juggernaut mob) and rift.yml ("reality rift", "veil tears open") all confirmed; BloodCultRuneCleaningSystem.cs confirms the mop-to-clean-runes counter-play. On graft_shape: the needs-upstream-edits claim is correct and actually understates the entanglement — via `gh search code` I found `Content.Server/Fluids/EntitySystems/AbsorbentSystem.cs` (an upstream file, no _Funkystation prefix) directly raises the fork's custom `AbsorbentMopTargetEvent`, i.e. an upstream file was edited in place to wire in blood-cult's rune cleaning. I also found `Content.Server/GameTicking/Rules/BloodCultRuleSystem.cs` (1762 lines), `Content.Server/GameTicking/Rules/Components/BloodCultRuleComponent.cs`, and `Resources/Locale/en-US/game-ticking/game-presets/preset-bloodcult.ftl` sitting directly in upstream-owned directories rather than under _Funkystation. Separately, self-contained _Funkystation files like BloodCultMindShieldSystem.cs and BloodCultistMetabolismSystem.cs depend heavily on upstream MindShieldComponent/BloodstreamSystem without editing them, which would still require upstream-compatible types to integrate elsewhere. Both readings of the ambiguous phrase are true here.

**starfall-drift**

*structural · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 3 forks carry it*

A handful of crew wake up as Blood Cultists of Nar'Sie: they shape a ritual dagger out of their own body, smear runes on the floor to convert bystanders, revive dead comrades, or offer a named sacrifice target's body up to their god, and they talk to each other through a private "Commune" whisper window. As the cult grows they carve spells into their flesh (a nightmare-sleep hex, turning ordinary steel and glass into runed steel and glass), summon pylons, forges, altars and acolyte armour off a summoning rune, trap victims' souls in soulstones to release them as Shades or bind them into hulking Juggernauts, and eventually their eyes start glowing so they can no longer pass as normal crew. The round builds to a two-stage endgame: nine cultists standing on Tear Veil runes at one of three announced locations to weaken reality, then a bleeding rift where the final chant either drags Nar'Sie through and loses the station or fails loudly. Security's counterplay is mindshield implants and holy water, and the cult has its own ritual for shattering mindshields once enough blood has been spilled.

- **Take** — A complete multi-phase team antagonist with its own conversion loop, gear tree, ghost roles and station-losing win condition, already translated from SS13 into working SS14 content with a great deal of finished player-facing text.
- **Skip** — Starfall Drift inherited it from Funky Station un-namespaced across 264 files (84 of them C#), and it hooks straight into mindshields, holy water, bleeding and blood, damage containers, contraband tagging, game presets and round-end reporting, so every upstream sync becomes conflict resolution; there is also no guidebook entry, leaving players to learn the whole system from chat lines.
- **Touches** — antagonist, security, command, service, ghost-roles, all-players
- **Verified** — partly supported. I fetched the cited prototypes/locale/code plus browsed the full tree (git ls-tree, 45k paths) and confirmed the core mechanics (Commune whisper action, rune conversion, mindshield-break chants, holy-water reaction, soulstones producing Shades/Juggernauts, runed-steel/glass reagent conversion, Tear Veil + rift endgame, admin-only cultist verb, missing guidebook). needs-upstream-edits is confirmed on both readings: the fork directly edits the shared upstream Resources/Prototypes/game_presets.yml (adding, but commenting out, the BloodCult/SecretBloodCult preset stanzas) and drops new files straight into upstream directories (Content.Server/GameTicking/Rules/BloodCultRuleSystem.cs, Content.Shared/EntityEffects/Effects/Body/BleedUnholyBloodEntityEffect.cs), while the bulk of the ~247 cult files sit self-namespaced under BloodCult/ folders that would still need registration/wiring elsewhere. However the gameplay claim overclaims specifics (fixed "nine cultists" vs an actual dynamic minimum of 3, and "three announced locations" vs a single computed summon location) and, more importantly, the take_because framing of "already... working SS14 content" glosses over the fact that the preset needed to actually start a Blood Cult round is commented out in the current tree.
  - unsupported: "nine cultists standing on Tear Veil runes at one of three announced locations to weaken reality" — BloodCultRuleComponent.MinimumCultistsForVeilRitual defaults to 3 and is documented in the source as "1/8th of total players, minimum 3", not a fixed nine; and BloodCultRuleSystem/BloodCultRiftSetupSystem compute a single `LocationForSummon` (one WeakVeilLocation) that gets announced via `cult-central-rift-warning`, not three announced candidate sites.
  - unsupported: take_because: "already translated from SS13 into working SS14 content" — Resources/Prototypes/game_presets.yml (an upstream-shared prototype file the fork edits in place) has both the `BloodCult` and `SecretBloodCult` gamePreset entries entirely commented out, and dynamic_rules.yml/subgamemodes.yml contain no cult entry either, so as shipped there is no normal way for a host to start a Blood Cult round — it reads as disabled/WIP rather than a live, working game mode.
  - unsupported: "there is also no guidebook entry" is actually confirmed rather than an overclaim — Resources/Prototypes/BloodCult/Roles/Antags/bloodcult.yml has `# guides: [ BloodCult ] # TODO: Add BloodCult guide entry` commented out, so this specific claim holds.
