### Alternate round types

<a id="alternate-round-types"></a>

Whole round scenarios that replace the standard station shift instead of modifying it: their own map or grids, their own player roles and spawn flow, and their own win, escape or elimination condition. Covers crash-survival and prison-planet rounds, assault-operative rounds, and team-versus-team PvP modes with team cores, capture points and dedicated arenas. A framework that only picks or weights which rules run inside a normal shift is `round-modifier-presets`; a single antagonist role rolled into a normal shift keeps its own antag id.

**serbia-strong**

*structural · drop-in · medium confidence · 1 forks carry it*

Dead players and observers can open an "Arena Lobby" window listing the fights currently running, then create or join one: you get pulled into a small randomly-picked arena map with a randomly-assigned kit, wait out a countdown while barriers hold you apart, and then fight until one side is left standing or the five-minute timer calls a draw, with winners announced over an arena channel. Lobby slots are sorted into duel, creative, social and misc categories and can be one-on-one or small teams, so it works as a parallel side activity for people who are out of the round rather than something the station notices. Separately, the fork ships whole-round faction war events on their own maps, where NT, USSP and Iron Squad crews fly out on faction shuttles, plant and pull each other's flags on capture pedestals over a fifteen-second struggle, earn points for every stretch of time they hold a pedestal, and score a big lump for blowing up an enemy shuttle's console, alongside a handful of themed event maps (a snow holiday village, an orbital village, a cooking event, a rift map).

- **Take** — It solves the two hardest problems at once: dead players get a real, repeatable thing to do instead of orbiting, and the faction-war half gives you a complete team-versus-team event round (capture points, faction shuttles, scoring) you can run on a slow night.
- **Skip** — Every SS220 file here carries a custom EULA/CLA header with a hosting restriction rather than the usual MIT/AGPL, so grafting it into an AGPL fork is a licensing problem before it is an engineering one; on top of that the faction war is only as good as its bespoke maps and shuttles, which you would have to maintain and rebalance yourself.
- **Touches** — ghost-roles, all-players, antagonist, security, admins-and-event-hosts
- **Verified** — supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. Gameplay is unusually well-supported: arena.ftl confirms the lobby verb/window, duel/creative/social/misc categories, countdown, and draw/timeout text; ArenaRuleComponent.cs confirms MaxFightDuration=300s (exactly "five-minute timer") and barrier/countdown fields; ArenaFightBarrierComponent and the ghost-role locale ("has no connection to the station... any interaction outside the arena is prohibited") back the "side activity, station doesn't notice" framing; arena_gamerule.yml + Arenas/*.yml (2v2, 3v3, single maps) confirm "one-on-one or small teams". FractWar checks out equally precisely: EventCapturePointComponent.cs has FlagManipulationDuration=15s exactly matching "fifteen-second struggle" and RetentionTimeForWinPoint=15s for the hold-points mechanic; ShuttleConsolePointsComponent/System confirms PointsOnDestroy=500 for "a big lump" on console kill; the tree shows dedicated NT.yml/USSP.yml/IronSquad.yml faction shuttles and ai_factions.yml with EbentUssp/EbentNanoTrasen/EbentIronSquad, confirming the three-faction claim even though none of the 5 cited evidence files show the faction names directly. All four named theme maps (GorgosiaSnowHoliday.yml, GoladraOrbVillage.yml, CookingEventMap.yml, RiftEventMap.yml) exist verbatim. One overclaim outside the gameplay text: skip_because says "Every SS220 file here carries a custom EULA/CLA header" but Content.Shared/SS220/FractWar/ShuttleConsolePointsComponent.cs (one of the 5 cited files) has no such header at all — it starts directly with a using statement. On graft_shape: I found the FractWar round type registered as a `gamePreset` entirely inside the fork's own Resources/Prototypes/SS220/game_presets.yml, with zero matches for "arena"/"fractwar" in the upstream Resources/Prototypes/game_presets.yml — i.e. the fork did not patch that upstream file in place. Every file I found for this feature (Content.Server/Shared/Client/SS220/{Arena,FractWar,EventCapturePoint}, Resources/{Locale,Prototypes,Maps}/*/ss220/...) lives under the fork's own SS220 namespace, and SS14 prototypes/systems are reflection-discovered rather than centrally registered, so there's no positive evidence integration would even require upstream edits. This contradicts the claim's downgrade to needs-upstream-edits; the seed's drop-in call holds up better than the claim being tested.

**sunrise**

*structural · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 1 forks carry it*

Two full round scenarios that replace the normal shift. In "Diversionary Squad", a Syndicate strike team spawns on its own shuttle with a shared, per-operative-funded uplink and hunts the station's Icarus superweapon: every command-staff member is walking around with an implanted Icarus key, so the ops have to hunt down and cut three keys out of heads, slot them into the Icarus terminal, and fire it, which raises the alert level, blares an alarm and ends the round shortly after; the round-end verdict grades ops on whether Icarus fired and how many of them are still breathing. In "Planet Prison", the round drops everyone onto a randomly picked prison map with a randomly rolled biome as convicts whose whole job is to break out and get far away from the prison complex — cross roughly 150 tiles of wilderness and you count as escaped, leave the round, and can immediately respawn, with the round-end summary tallying how many prisoners got away.

- **Take** — It gives the server two complete alternate shifts (a heist-with-a-doomsday-weapon and a prison-break survival round) with their own spawn flow, objectives and win tiers, so the rotation stops being "normal shift with a different antag".
- **Skip** — These are round types, not features: each needs its own maps, prisoner/operative gear, ghost roles and preset wiring to be playable at all, Planet Prison's escape payoff is hooked into Sunrise's own respawn ("NewLife") system, its player-facing strings are Russian-only, and Assault Ops force-implants keys into upstream's CommandStaffComponent, so a graft means porting content and re-localising, not dropping in a folder.
- **Touches** — antagonist, command, security, ghost-roles, all-players
- **Verified** — supported. All of AssaultOps' and PlanetPrison's own files live under _Sunrise namespace directories and are self-contained (no in-place edits to them found), but AssaultOpsRuleSystem.InsertIcarusKeys/OnPlayerSpawned query EntityQueryEnumerator<CommandStaffComponent> to decide who gets force-implanted — and I confirmed Content.Server/Revolutionary/Components/CommandStaffComponent.cs is byte-identical between the sunrise fork and space-wizards/space-station-14 upstream (diff returned nothing), i.e. a real, unmodified upstream type this feature depends on to function, not a file the fork patches. That makes 'needs-upstream-edits' correct but in the integration-would-require-upstream-edits sense, not fork-patches-upstream.
  - unsupported: "the ops have to hunt down and cut three keys out of heads" — the three implant slots (First/Second/Third KeySlot) and force-implant-on-spawn logic are confirmed in code, but no cited file shows a surgical/cutting removal mechanic; this detail is a plausible inference from standard SS14 subdermal-implant removal rather than something directly evidenced in the files read.

**rmc14**

*structural · entangled · high confidence · 1 forks carry it*

Instead of a station shift, the whole round is a military deployment: a randomly named operation ("Operation Bandit Patrol") sends a shipful of marines from their warship down to a planet by dropship, where a xenomorph hive is growing, and the round only ends when one side is wiped out. Marines who get infected or nested stop counting as living crew, so the population balance itself is the scoreboard, and the round is scored as a major or minor victory for either side, a mutual wipe-out, or the marines blowing up their own ship. Late round the aliens can hijack the dropship and crash it into the warship, which levels the hive on the planet, strands anyone left behind and turns the last stretch into a shipside siege; the marines' counterplay is scuttling the ship or running out the clock, which counts as a loss. Layered on top are an admin-approved mutiny against the commander (the ringleader gets an action to invite others, and every mutineer wears a visible skull marker so bystanders know who is in on it) and a separate Thunderdome arena map whose radios are walled off from the rest of the round.

- **Take** — It is the most complete example in the ecosystem of a round type that owns its own map, spawn flow, faction victory conditions and dramatic late-round reversal, rather than just bolting an antagonist onto a normal shift.
- **Skip** — The round rule only makes sense on top of RMC-14's total conversion: it counts marines, xenos, hive structures, parasite infections, dropships and the warship grid directly, so grafting it means grafting the entire alien-versus-marine game underneath it.
- **Touches** — all-players, command, security, antagonist, ghost-roles, medical
- **Needs** — [xenomorph-hive](#xenomorph-hive)
- **Verified** — supported. Every specific claim checks out against the code: DistressSignalRuleResult enum has exactly MajorMarineVictory/MinorMarineVictory/MajorXenoVictory/MinorXenoVictory/AllDied/SelfDestruct; CheckAliveMarines explicitly excludes VictimInfectedComponent, VictimBurstComponent and nested marines from the living count; operation_names.yml supplies the prefix/name pool ("Bandit" + "Patrol" both present) that generates names like the cited example; RMCMutinies.xml confirms admin-gated mutiny, the leader's invite action, and the skull-icon marker; OnDropshipHijackLanded stuns everyone on the Almayer (warship) and destroys planet-side hive structures not aboard the dropship, matching "crash into the warship" and "levels the hive"; ForceEndAt timeout resolves to MinorXenoVictory and ScuttleUnlockAt/ScuttleDetonated back the "scuttle or run out the clock" counterplay; ThunderdomeSystem.OnRadioReceiveAttempt cancels cross-boundary radio traffic, confirming the walled-off arena. Nothing in the claim overstates what the files show.

**harmony-station**

*cosmetic · drop-in · medium confidence · 1 forks carry it*

Harmony adds one extra battleground to the short free-for-all deathmatch rounds that run outside a normal station shift: "DM02 Sandbomb", a desert/asteroid arena of sand, dug-out sand pits, wooden and asphalt platforms and pools of red water, lit with a warm sandy ambience. Everyone who joins it spawns as a plain passenger with no jobs to pick, and it takes 10 to 35 players. The fork also keeps its own deathmatch map rotation so this arena comes up alongside the stock entryway arena instead of replacing it.

- **Take** — It is a single self-contained arena map plus a two-line map-pool entry, so a fork that already runs deathmatch rounds doubles its arena variety for almost no integration work.
- **Skip** — It adds no mode, rule or mechanic at all, just one more venue for a deathmatch mode you must already have, and the ~800 KB map is another hand-built map to keep loading and passing map tests after every upstream change.
- **Touches** — all-players
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. I cloned the repo and confirmed every file involved (arenas.yml, the map, the pool, the new gamePreset in game_presets.yml, the new GameRule+gear in roundstart.yml, and the locale strings) lives under _Harmony namespace directories; the stock Resources/Prototypes/Maps/Pools/deathmatch.yml and stock game_presets.yml are byte-for-byte untouched. So the fork's own copy is self-contained and does not patch upstream — the seed's original 'drop-in' guess holds, and 'needs-upstream-edits' is wrong on the fork-patches-upstream reading. The only sense in which upstream edits would be needed is if a grafter wants this arena merged into their *existing* stock Deathmatch rotation (the benefit the claim's take_because implies) rather than as Harmony's separate PROMOD mode — that would mean editing the target's own copy of the stock pool file, since Harmony's implementation deliberately doesn't do that.
  - unsupported: "It is a single self-contained arena map plus a two-line map-pool entry, so a fork that already runs deathmatch rounds doubles its arena variety for almost no integration work." — dm02-sandbomb is never added to the stock DeathMatchMapPool (Resources/Prototypes/Maps/Pools/deathmatch.yml, confirmed unmodified: still just MeteorArena + dm01-entryway). It only becomes playable through a brand-new gamePreset "DeathmatchPROMOD" (Resources/Prototypes/_Harmony/game_presets.yml) that in turn requires a whole new GameRule "DeathMatchPROMOD" with its own kill cap (16), starting gear (DeathMatchPROMODGear), and reward/loot table (Resources/Prototypes/_Harmony/GameRules/roundstart.yml), plus its own locale file for the preset's lobby title/description. A fork that 'already runs deathmatch rounds' does not get this arena for free; it has to graft the whole parallel PROMOD mode, not just a map + pool line.
  - unsupported: "The fork also keeps its own deathmatch map rotation so this arena comes up alongside the stock entryway arena instead of replacing it." — technically true of the pool's contents, but the framing implies this is still 'the deathmatch mode you must already have' (per skip_because); it is actually a distinct alias/preset ('deathmatchpromod'/'dmpm') with its own rules and gear, separate from the stock 'Deathmatch'/'dm' preset which is untouched.

### Pirate crew faction

<a id="pirate-crew"></a>

Playable pirate crew that arrives on its own vessel with a captain-led hierarchy, dedicated uplink and rules governing boarding and piracy.

**frontier**

*structural · entangled · high confidence · 1 forks carry it*

Players can pick Pirate, First Mate or Pirate Captain at spawn instead of a station job, joining a small outlaw crew (capped at four bodies, one captain and one mate) that operates out of its own ship rather than the station. They start with a cutlass or utility kit, an appraisal tool and a pirate uplink that spends doubloons instead of station money, buying pirate EVA suits and hardsuits, rum kegs, loot chests and a pirate fabricator. Doubloons come from piracy itself: raid ships and points of interest for plunder, or pack demanded goods into a labelled chest and cash it in at a pirate bounty redemption console. Their suit sensors are dead and their station record is forged, so the crew reads as unknown when the rest of the sector goes looking for them, and a posted pirate code governs hostage-taking, how thoroughly you may strip a ship that surrenders, and the fact that ordinary players may never help them.

- **Take** — It turns antagonism into a standing, joinable career with its own economy and loot loop, so hostile PvP pressure exists continuously instead of being spawned by a midround event.
- **Skip** — It only makes sense in an open sector with player-owned ships to raid and a parallel currency to spend, and it comes with a whitelist plus a page of hand-written piracy rules that admins have to actually enforce.
- **Touches** — antagonist, security, cargo, command, all-players
- **Needs** — [shipyard-player-ships](#shipyard-player-ships), [player-economy-and-banking](#player-economy-and-banking), [cargo-bounties-and-market](#cargo-bounties-and-market), [extra-job-roster](#extra-job-roster)
- **Verified** — partly supported. All 8 cited files are genuinely fork-namespaced (_NF/ or Content.Shared._NF.Pirate) with no upstream edits, matching the path-data signal — but I found a 9th file, Resources/Prototypes/_NF/currency.yml, not in the evidence list, that defines Doubloon in the same prototype alongside Speso (the station bank currency) and FrontierUplinkCoin, both with canWithdraw:true and a cash-item mapping, i.e. doubloons ride the same currency/cash-withdrawal machinery as the station economy. The uplink catalog also sells UplinkPiratePirateShipyardRCD, tying pirates directly to the fork's player-shipyard system. That's real coupling to other fork features (not upstream files), so the assessor's downgrade from the seed's 'drop-in' to 'entangled' is correct, not an overclaim.
  - unsupported: "buying pirate EVA suits and hardsuits, rum kegs, loot chests and a pirate fabricator" — the pirate fabricator (PirateTechFabFlatpack) does not appear anywhere in pirate_uplink_catalog.yml; it is given as free starting gear to the Captain only (nfpirate_captain.yml storage:back), not something purchased with doubloons.
  - unsupported: "They start with a cutlass or utility kit" — NFPirateGear and NFPirateFirstMateGear contain only a ClothingBeltUtility (no weapon at all); only NFPirateCaptainGear includes an EnergyCutlass. It isn't a per-player either/or choice, it's rank-determined, and two of the three roles get no cutlass option.

**goobstation**

*structural · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 1 forks carry it*

Mid-round, a "Space IRS" transmission accuses the station of unpaid taxes and drops a ransom order into the cargo console, priced off whatever is currently in the station's account (roughly three-quarters to a quarter over the full balance). If cargo approves the order in time the shuttle turns around and the crew keeps its skin; if they refuse or stall, a five-strong pirate crew in reinforced EVA suits arrives on its own vessel to take the money by force. The pirates raid the station for anything sellable, run it back to their own cargo pallet, and feed the credits into a data siphon on their ship, and once that siphon is switched on it bolts their ship in place, broadcasts its exact position to the whole station and invites the crew to come break it, so the round ends in a pitched fight over one destructible machine, with the round-end text tallying how many credits the pirates got away with (or announcing they lost their data bank).

- **Take** — The ransom-then-raid framing gives the whole station one collective decision with a real price tag, and the siphon turns the endgame into a defendable objective on a fixed location rather than another hunt-the-antag round.
- **Skip** — It is not a self-contained antag drop: it wants a bespoke pirate shuttle map, hooks the upstream cargo order database and console, and its gear prototypes carry Goob's trauma-deduction armour fields, so the YAML will not load on a fork without that wound extension.
- **Touches** — cargo, security, command, antagonist, all-players
- **Needs** — [surgery-and-limb-wounds](#surgery-and-limb-wounds)
- **Verified** — supported. Fetched all ten cited files plus PendingPirateRuleComponent.cs and (via directory browse) Content.Shared/Armor/ArmorComponent.cs. Every beat of the gameplay narrative checks out against the raw source: the IRS threat/arrival/paid/cancelled loclines, the ransom priced at rand(balance*0.75, balance*1.25) inserted directly into the station's CargoOrderData via CargoSystem.TryAddOrder, a 300s (5-minute) timer before pirates spawn, an AntagSelection block with min:5/max:5 pirates loading a bespoke map (pirates_irs.yml), drip.yml's "modified EVA suit" hardsuits with ExplosionResistance/Armor coefficients, DataSiphon with StationAnchor (switchedOn:false) and a 2000-damage Destructible threshold, and the four round-end Locale strings (credits plundered / siphoned / lost). The depends_on claim is not just plausible but independently verified: Content.Shared/Armor/ArmorComponent.cs (a genuinely upstream file, no fork-namespace segment in its path) has been patched in-place with 'Shitmed Change' comments adding a TraumaDeductions dictionary keyed by TraumaType, which is exactly the field drip.yml's gear prototypes populate. That patch lives outside pirate-crew's own cited files (it belongs to the surgery-and-limb-wounds unit's territory), so pirate-crew's own tree (Locale/_Goobstation/_Pirates, Prototypes/_Goobstation/_Pirates, Content.Goobstation.Server/Pirates) stays self-contained -- the upstream edit is something the *dependency* brings, not something this unit's own files touch. That is the integration-would-require-upstream-edits reading, not fork-patches-upstream for this unit specifically.

**estacao-pirata, starlight**

*activity · drop-in · medium confidence · 1 forks carry it*

Only the Starlight half is actually about pirates, and it is thin: two raider roles, a rank-and-file pirate and a pirate captain, neither of which players can opt into from the character menu, so they arrive as ghost roles or admin-placed spawns. Anyone handed one is told plainly what winning looks like: survive the raid and get back aboard the ship before it leaves, which is checked at round end like any other antagonist goal. The Estação Pirata files bundled into this unit are a naming coincidence (that fork is called Pirate Station, so its whole content folder carries the name) and contain no piracy at all, just a trader and a soldier civilian role with ID cards and starting kit for off-station towns and planets.

- **Take** — It is the smallest possible honest scaffold for a boarding-raider antagonist: a role, a captain variant, and a survive-and-extract goal that attaches itself automatically, with nothing else to untangle.
- **Skip** — There is no pirate ship, no crew gear, no uplink and nothing that spawns these roles anywhere in the unit, so grafting it gives you an antagonist definition that never fires until you build the entire raid around it yourself; the second fork in this unit contributes nothing to the feature at all.
- **Touches** — antagonist, ghost-roles
- **Needs** — [gamemaster-and-ghost-roles](#gamemaster-and-ghost-roles)
- **Verified** — partly supported. The core narrative checks out: estacao-pirata's cited files (pirata_roles.yml, pirata_dep.yml, identidade_pirata.yml) are genuinely just "Comerciante"/"Soldado" civilian trader/soldier jobs with no piracy content, and Starlight's pirate.yml/PirateRoleSystem.cs/PirateComponent.cs are exactly as thin as described: setPreference:false antag+captain variants, a bare marker component, and a system that only adds a "Survive the raid... make it back to the ship" objective when a mind role is added, with no GameRule or ghost-role spawner anywhere I could find wiring it up automatically. But the skip_because reasoning overclaims: I found Resources/Prototypes/_Starlight/GameRules/shuttles.yml defines LancePiratesSpawn, which loads Resources/Maps/_Starlight/Shuttles/LancePirates.yml — an actual pirate-themed derelict/event ship containing pirate hats, coats, jumpsuits, a treasure chest, pirate flags, a ship cannon (ShuttleGunPirateCannon), pirate suit storage, and a pirate revolver. There's also a full set of pirate-themed startingGear (cutlass, flintlock, blunderbuss, tricorn hats) in Roles/Fun/visitors_startinggear.yml for a "PirateScooner" visitor archetype. Neither ship nor gear is wired to the MindRolePirate antag system (no job/antag assignment found on the map), so the narrow "nothing automatically spawns the antag role" point survives, but the blanket statements "there is no pirate ship" and "no crew gear" are factually false for this fork. Graft-shape holds up structurally: every file in the evidence list stays inside EstacaoPirata/ or _Starlight/ namespaces, referencing only ordinary upstream types (ClothingUniformJumpsuitLawyerBlue, Content.Server.Mind, etc.) rather than editing upstream files in place, so drop-in is the right namespace-level call even though the antag is functionally inert without the already-flagged gamemaster/ghost-role dependency.

### Cosmic cult

<a id="cosmic-cult"></a>

Conversion team antagonist that gathers entropy to build and tier up a Monument, buys Influence abilities, corrupts tiles and can ascend a colossus to end the round.

**deltav**

*structural · drop-in · high confidence · 3 forks carry it*

A team of converted crew quietly drains "entropy" from living people (a touch that steals a bit of their health over time), carries it back to an invisible Monument hidden somewhere on the station, and feeds it in to grow the Monument through three stages. Each stage unlocks new powers the cult buys individually — freezing someone in place, blasting doors open, going invisible as a floating spirit, becoming immune to vacuum, healing near the Monument — plus chalk glyphs that convert bystanders standing on them, turn spacesuits into cult armour, turn knives into cult weapons, and turn a portable scrubber into a spire that eats the room's air. Cultists who find and absorb the rifts that start appearing become permanently empowered and can trap a borg in a shell that hatches into a huge Entropic Colossus, or overwrite the station AI's laws to serve the cult; the crew fights back with mindshields, the chaplain's bible and a censer that deconverts, and if the cult finishes the final ritual at the fully-powered Monument the station is destroyed and the round ends.

- **Take** — It is a complete, fully documented round type with its own escalation curve, counterplay and losing condition — a whole alternate way for a shift to go, not another uplink antag.
- **Skip** — It is roughly 300 files of bespoke systems (monument, glyphs, transmutation, influences, astral forms, colossus mob, AI lawset corruption, borg capture) that hooks mindshields, bibles, the AI upload console and borg chassis, so it is a permanent maintenance surface that will fight every upstream merge touching those systems.
- **Touches** — antagonist, all-players, security, epistemics, science, chaplain, silicon, command, ghost-roles
- **Verified** — supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. The gameplay description (entropy siphon, three-stage Monument, purchasable influences, glyph conversion/transmutation, deconversion via censer/bible/mindshield, Colossus mob, AI-law/borg corruption, station-destroying final ritual) is directly confirmed by the guidebook XML and prototype/system files I fetched myself. But the graft_shape verdict is overclaimed: a full recursive tree search of the DeltaV repo (299 cosmic/cult-tagged paths) found zero files outside _DV namespace directories, and reading the actual C# (DeconversionSystem.cs, CosmicFragmentationSystem.cs) shows the 'hooks' into mindshields/bible/borg/AI-laws are done entirely via SubscribeLocalEvent from the fork's own self-contained files consuming stable, already-existing upstream components/events — no upstream file was edited to register or wire in the feature (registration itself, e.g. game_presets.yml, is also under _DV). That is much closer to the seed's original 'drop-in' than the assessor's downgrade suggests, with the caveat that it is a large, deeply-coupled maintenance surface if those upstream APIs ever change shape.
  - unsupported: "needs-upstream-edits" as the graft_shape: the repo tree (299 files matched, all under _DV directories; zero non-_DV files mention "cosmic" anywhere in the repo) shows the feature is 100% self-contained with no upstream files edited to wire it in, contradicting the 'fork-patches-upstream' reading entirely
  - unsupported: The framing that it 'hooks mindshields, bibles, the AI upload console and borg chassis' implies edits to those systems; in fact the actual C# (DeconversionSystem.cs, CosmicFragmentationSystem.cs) shows it only subscribes to pre-existing upstream events/components (MindShieldComponent, BibleComponent, BorgChassisComponent, SiliconLawUpdaterComponent, AILawUpdatedEvent) from its own _DV files — the upstream files themselves (MindShieldSystem.cs, BibleSystem.cs) contain zero references to CosmicCult and are completely unmodified

**starlight**

*structural · entangled · high confidence · 3 forks carry it*

A small team of crew wake up as Cosmic Cultists who whisper to each other in a private language and quietly drain "entropy" from living crewmates with a touch, which slowly rots the victim's health while the cultist banks the motes and dumps them into a Monument they raise somewhere on the station. Feeding the Monument tiers it up three times, unlocking a shopping list of powers the cult picks from (freeze a victim in place, blind and stagger a room, force bolted doors open, stop needing food, ignore gravity, become briefly immune to damage) and letting them scribe glowing floor glyphs that convert anyone standing on one, transmute a portable scrubber into an entropy-farming spire, or turn a cyborg into a giant Entropic Colossus that a ghost plays. Crew fight back by spotting glyphs and fading "malign echoes", implanting mindshields, having the chaplain bless water for a censer that deconverts cultists, and purging the rifts that bleed into hallways with an anomaly APE or a bible; if the cult finishes empowering the Monument and completes the final ritual, the round ends with the station destroyed.

- **Take** — It is a complete, self-documenting conversion antag with a real escalation arc and real crew counterplay (mindshield, chaplain censer, rift purging, destroying the chantry), so it drops a whole round shape into the fork rather than one more midround spawn.
- **Skip** — It is roughly 650 files spanning a monument UI, glyph transmutation, borg-to-colossus ghost roles, AI lawboard hijacking and tile corruption, plus a private cult language it needs a language system for, so it is a permanent maintenance surface rather than a weekend port.
- **Touches** — antagonist, ghost-roles, security, service, science, command, silicon, all-players
- **Needs** — [language-system](#language-system)
- **Verified** — supported. Fetched all 9 cited guidebook/locale files plus a broad set of C#/YAML source from the starlight-dev tree and every substantive gameplay beat checks out verbatim or near-verbatim: Entropy siphoning and Monument feeding (CosmicCult.xml), the 3-stage Influence unlock list including all six named powers (Aberrant Lapse=freeze, Null Glare=EMP+Flash+Stun confirmed in CosmicGlareSystem.cs source itself, Force Ingress=bolted doors, Eschew Metabolism=no food, Unbound Step=no gravity, Vacuous Imposition=damage immunity), glyphs converting/transmuting a scrubber into a Vacuous Spire, Null Fragmentation turning a cyborg into an Entropic Colossus ghost role (ghostroles.ftl), and the destroy-the-station final ritual are all directly attested. Counterplay (malign echoes, mindshields, chaplain-blessed holy water + Ardent Censer, A.P.E./bible rift purging) matches CosmicCultDeconversion.xml and CosmicCultMalignRifts.xml word for word. I additionally verified the two structural claims used to justify 'entangled': a CosmicCultLaws siliconLawset (Resources/Prototypes/_Starlight/CosmicCult/laws.yml) confirms AI lawboard hijacking, and CosmicCorruptingSystem.cs/CosmicTileDetonationSystem.cs confirm tile corruption. Most importantly, I confirmed the language dependency is real and not fabricated: the 'Cosmic' language id lives in Resources/Prototypes/_Starlight/Language/hivemind.yml, a file belonging to a large (~82-file) separate _Starlight/Language subsystem shared by Abductor, Changeling, Xenomind, etc. antags -- so Cosmic Cult genuinely reaches into a distinct fork feature for its private-language mechanic, which is exactly what depends_on: language-system asserts. A path search across a (truncated but ~58.7k-entry) recursive tree found zero CosmicCult-named files outside _Starlight namespaces, so the code itself stays self-contained; the 'entangled' call rests on functional dependency on another catalogued unit plus deep hooks into laws/tiles/mind-roles, not on upstream files being physically edited -- which is a defensible and more accurate reading than the shallow path-based 'drop-in' seed. The only unverifiable figure is the 'roughly 650 files' count (I could only enumerate ~290 non-truncated path hits for 'cosmiccult', with Audio/Textures/Maps likely undercounted due to tree truncation), which is plausible but not something I could confirm exactly.

**impstation**

*cosmetic · drop-in · high confidence · 3 forks carry it*

This slice is the cosmic cult's physical set dressing rather than the antagonist rules themselves: a whole "malign" building material family of floors, walls, windows, doors, a settee and an obelisk, all with unsettling flavour text, plus their own muffled otherworldly footstep sounds so walking on cult ground sounds different from walking on the station. It also includes a "malign instrument" console that is simultaneously a shuttle helm and its own engine, so the cult's craft can be flown without a power grid, and a joke "unknown plushie" for the loot table. To a player this reads as an alien, glyph-covered pocket of architecture that is visibly and audibly not part of the station.

- **Take** — Self-contained fork-namespaced YAML and assets that give an antagonist faction an instantly readable visual and audio identity, with a no-power-required shuttle helm that solves a real problem for any off-station antag base.
- **Skip** — On its own it is scenery: without the cosmic cult antagonist, monument and tile-corruption systems these are just decorative walls and floors nobody has a reason to build, and they arrive with their own sprite and audio directories to keep licensed and maintained.
- **Touches** — antagonist, all-players
- **Verified** — partly supported. All six cited files plus their companion files (footsteps_cosmic.yml, the plushie RSI/meta.json) confirm the tileset (floors/walls/windows/doors/chair/obelisk with unsettling flavor text, a distinct FootstepCosmic sound collection, and a no-power shuttle-helm-cum-thruster) exactly as described. Every prototype inherits only from vanilla/upstream bases (BaseWall, BaseStructure, SeatBase, WindowRCDResistant, material_doors.yml, Content.Server/Worldgen's WorldLoaderComponent) and lives entirely under _Impstation namespace directories (Prototypes, Textures, Audio, Locale) with no reference to other fork-specific antag/monument C# systems in the files I read, supporting drop-in. The one specific overclaim is the loot-table wiring for the plushie, which I could not find evidence for.
  - unsupported: "a joke 'unknown plushie' for the loot table" — I checked Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Markers/Spawners/Random/Salvage/tables_loot.yml (upstream, 314 lines), its _Impstation override (56 lines), Resources/Prototypes/Procedural/salvage_loot.yml, and Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Objects/Deliveries/letter_loot_tables.yml — none reference PlushieCosmicCult. The plushie entity (unknownplushie.yml) and its sprite/meta.json are real and self-contained, but nothing in the fork's loot-table files actually places it in a loot table; it may only be reachable via admin/debug spawn.

### Vampire

<a id="vampire"></a>

Blood-draining antagonist with a blood pool resource, thralls and specialisation classes that unlock shadow and blood powers.

**backmen, starlight, the-den**

*structural · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 1 forks carry it*

A vampire starts the shift as an ordinary crewmember who can extend fangs and bite people to drink their blood, with a cap on how much any one victim can give, so they have to keep finding fresh prey. Total blood drained is a permanent power track that unlocks abilities at milestones and, at 150 units, lets them pick a specialisation: blood magic and area control, shadow stealth and teleporting, mind-controlled thralls and illusions, or brute melee durability. Current blood acts as a mana bar that drains as they cast, and a fed vampire burns on chapel tiles and from holy water while a chaplain holding a bible is immune to their powers until the vampire hits full power. Rounds end with a scoreboard of how much blood was drained and by whom; thralled crew get their own role and objective to obey their master. The Backmen and Den versions are much smaller: Backmen adds an evolution shop and a conversion action tied into their spider/arachne blood-sucking, and The Den only has the plain blood-drinking component and a life drain, not a full antagonist.

- **Take** — A fully built conversion antagonist with a resource economy, four distinct playstyles, in-game guidebook pages for each, and a real counterplay hook (chapel, holy water, chaplain) that gives an otherwise ignored job a job.
- **Skip** — It is a very large surface: dozens of abilities, four class systems, custom overlays, thrall UI and a game rule, and the counterplay half only works if you also patch upstream holy water, chapel tiles and chaplain faith to know what a vampire is.
- **Touches** — antagonist, all-players, security, medical, service
- **Verified** — partly supported. Starlight's core vampire description is strongly confirmed by re-fetched files: the guidebook (Vampires.xml) and locale (vampire.ftl) directly show the 150/250/400/600/800/1000 blood-total power track, the 200u per-victim cap, current-blood-as-mana, all four named classes (Hemomancer/Umbrae/Dantalion/Gargantua) with the exact playstyles claimed, holy water/chapel burn that only activates after first feed, chaplain-with-bible immunity broken only at Full Power, a Thrall antag role/objective, and a named round-end blood-drained scoreboard string. The Backmen claim that its vampire is 'tied into their spider/arachne blood-sucking' is not supported: browsing Rxup/space-station-14 shows Backmen's vampire lives in its own Content.Server/Backmen/Vampiric namespace with a full leveling system, dedicated Role/Rule/Objective files, a BloodEssence currency store, and a bat-icon 'convert to vampire' action plus a BloodSuckerGlandInjector — nothing tying it to the separate Arachne/Spider directories. The Den's 'plain blood-drinking, not a full antagonist' claim checks out (only BloodSuckedComponent/BloodSuckerComponent/BloodSuckerSystem exist, gated on a Cocoon/web mechanic, no role/rule/class files). For graft_shape: this is definitively fork-patches-upstream, not just a theoretical integration cost — Starlight's own Content.Server/Bible/BibleSystem.cs (a vanilla, non-_Starlight path) has vampire-specific code spliced directly into it (imports Content.Shared._Starlight.Vampire.Components, '// starlight start/end' blocks around a BibleThwackEvent hook), so the fork's own tree already edits an upstream file in place to wire the holy-water/chaplain counterplay.
  - unsupported: Backmen adds an evolution shop and a conversion action tied into their spider/arachne blood-sucking

### Xenomorph hive

<a id="xenomorph-hive"></a>

Alien hive faction with facehugger infection, chestbursting, larva growth, caste evolution, plasma, acid and resin structures.

**rmc14, white-dream**

*structural · entangled · medium confidence · 5 forks carry it*

A facehugger leaps onto someone's face and latches on too tight to pull off; over the next several minutes the victim feels their chest hurt, then their throat go sore, then something crawling inside them, until a larva bursts out of their chest in front of everyone and a dead crewmember becomes a new alien. Aliens talk to each other over a private Hivemind channel, build up until they are "ready to evolve", and grow into stronger castes (drone, hunter, sentinel, praetorian, queen) with only one queen allowed at a time, while the queen can hand-pick an adult child for promotion. The bigger RMC-14 version goes much further: aliens spend plasma to grow resin weeds and hive structures (a hive core, egg morphers that fling parasites at anyone who walks close, healing nodes, plasma trees, pylons), dig named tunnels to fast-travel across the map, hide acid and parasite traps under floor debris, and heavy castes like the boiler lob acid or neurotoxin gas globs from off-screen. The stated goal is that only one species walks off the station.

- **Take** — It converts dead and captured crew into more antagonists, so the round has a real escalating losing condition instead of a fixed antag count, and every death makes the threat bigger.
- **Skip** — It is two very different-sized things wearing one name: White Dream's is a ~180-file antag you could plausibly maintain, while RMC-14's ~3400-file version is written for its marine-vs-xeno total conversion and its guides openly lean on orbital bombardment, close air support, barricade lines and host-capture nests that a normal station round simply does not have.
- **Touches** — antagonist, ghost-roles, all-players, medical, security
- **Needs** — [alternate-round-types](#alternate-round-types)
- **Verified** — partly supported. I refetched all 13 cited files plus the White Dream game-rule/preset prototypes and RMC-14's cm_game_presets.yml. Every gameplay beat checks out almost verbatim: facehugger latch (face-hugger.ftl), infection stages/chestburst (infection.ftl, larva.ftl), hivemind channel (chat.ftl), evolution/caste list with Queen maxCount:1 and 'adult, non-royal children' promotion (evolution.ftl, queen.ftl, xenomorph_cast.yml), 'only one species should remain' (role.ftl), and RMC-14's hive structures, resin-hole trap variants hidden under debris, and boiler's long-range acid/neurotoxin bombard with skyfire/skyspit references (all four RMC guidebook XMLs). A file-tree scan of both repos (GitHub trees API) found the White Dream implementation is genuinely namespace-clean (134 xenomorph-related files, only 1 unrelated hit outside _white/_wd, a texture pun), consistent with the seed's path-based drop-in signal for that half. But I also found RMC-14 wires its xenomorph mode through a dedicated gamePreset (CMDistressSignal) — a real alternate-round-type dependency — while White Dream's version is just an ordinary mid-round StationEvent, no special round-type infrastructure needed. So 'entangled' is the right call for the merged unit overall (driven by RMC-14's total-conversion design, which is what most of the cited evidence documents), but the blanket depends_on claim glosses over the fact that the more graftable half doesn't share that dependency.
  - unsupported: "depends_on": ["alternate-round-types"] is stated as a blanket property of the merged unit, but it only holds for the RMC-14 half. White Dream's XenomorphsInfestation is a plain StationEvent/AntagSelection GameRule (weight 5, minimumPlayers 20, VentSpawnRule + AntagSpawner) that fires inside any normal round, no dedicated preset required — only RMC-14's version is wired to its own gamePreset (CMDistressSignal in Resources/Prototypes/_RMC14/cm_game_presets.yml). The claim doesn't distinguish this, which matters because 'take_because' implicitly favors the smaller, non-round-type-dependent White Dream option.

### Abductors

<a id="abductors"></a>

Two-person alien team that teleports crew to a hidden ship, operates an experimentation table to swap organs or implants, then returns them.

**starlight, sunrise**

*structural · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 3 forks carry it*

Two ghost players spawn as mute grey aliens on a hidden ship: a Scientist and an Agent bodyguard, both in armour that toggles between a stealth mode and a combat mode from a console. They stun a crewmember, tag them with a hand-held gizmo, then hit "attract" on their console to yank the victim off the station and onto the ship, where the victim goes into an experimentation table and gets their heart swapped for a strange alien gland before being sent home none the wiser. The glands do things to the victim for the rest of the round: one quietly heals them, others periodically vent laughing gas, warp gravity around them, or burst into spiders. Abductors are told not to wreck the station or kill anyone (a live, healthy subject is the point), they get their own shop of alien pistols, prods, helmets and gland restocks, and the round-end summary reports how many unique people they abducted.

- **Take** — A complete, well-loved SS13 antag that upstream has no equivalent of, and it creates rounds where medical has to explain why a returning crewmember's chest is now full of alien hardware.
- **Skip** — Starlight's copy is written against that fork's own antag framework (antagSpecifier / RestrictedAntag / spawnerPrototype), so it does not slot onto upstream antag selection without a rewrite, and either version drags in a ship map, a new species, custom body parts and gland organs plus a shop and two console UIs — roughly 30 to 240 files depending on the source fork.
- **Touches** — antagonist, ghost-roles, medical, security, all-players
- **Verified** — supported. I cloned both forks (blob:none partial clones) and confirmed via git ls-tree + git show that Starlight's own copy edits an actual upstream file in place: Resources/Prototypes/Guidebook/antagonist.yml gets a '# Starlight-start' block adding 'Abductors' to the guidebook nav list, and several sprite states (e.g. Resources/Textures/Objects/Tools/crowbar.rsi/abductor.png, Structures/Storage/closet.rsi/abductor.png, Objects/Misc/id_cards.rsi/abductor.png) are dropped straight into shared upstream .rsi folders with no _Starlight prefix at all. That's stronger, more concrete proof of 'needs-upstream-edits' than the claim's own antagSpecifier/RestrictedAntag argument, and it directly falsifies the drop-in seed. Sunrise's copy is comparatively cleaner (its id_cards.rsi addition is namespaced under _Sunrise, and it does not touch upstream Guidebook/antagonist.yml), so the upstream-patching behavior is fork-specific rather than universal, but the claim's bottom-line categorization (needs-upstream-edits, not drop-in) holds for the unit as scoped.
  - unsupported: "roughly 30 to 240 files depending on the source fork" — Sunrise's actual abductor-related tree (git ls-tree, case-insensitive match on 'abductor') is about 311 files, above the claimed 240 ceiling; Starlight's is about 181, within range.

### Devil

<a id="devil-pacts"></a>

Contract-signing antagonist that trades favours for souls, cheats death, condemns those who break the deal and is countered by exorcism.

**goobstation, starlight**

*structural · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 3 forks carry it*

A crew member is secretly a devil who wins by talking people into signing a contract rather than by fighting. They summon a burning quill and a black parchment out of thin air, fill in the deals they are offering from their Book of Damnations, and hand it over: the mark gets something genuinely good (30,000 credits, autographed sneakers, immunity to fire, cold, pressure, flashes, shocks, hunger or space) in exchange for something bad (their soul, their sight, their voice, an organ that drops on the floor, five minutes left to live, turning into a monkey or a cluwne, or a hitman placed on their trail). The books have to balance in hell's favour or the deal simply does not take. Selling your soul means a defibrillator will never bring you back, and a devil who has collected several souls starts visibly glowing red, gains a bident and can shrug off a killing blow and jerk back awake. Crew fight back by reading a contract to learn the devil's true name and then shouting it with "stop" or "halt" until it burns them apart, or by having the chaplain exorcise the corpse with a bible so it can never return; a devil can also offer a fresh corpse revival in exchange for the soul, which the dead player accepts or rejects on a popup.

- **Take** — It is a social antagonist whose whole win condition is negotiation rather than combat, and it hands the chaplain, the crew's word-of-mouth and the medical revive chain real, legible counter-play that almost no other antag provides.
- **Skip** — The deals only feel meaningful if the effects they grant and take already exist in your fork, so the damnation catalogue is a long tail of cross-system hooks (economy credits, polymorph, organ removal, hitman spawns, unrevivable defib messaging, pacifism, doom timers) that each need porting and rebalancing, and it round-removes players permanently, which needs a policy decision before it goes live.
- **Touches** — antagonist, all-players, service, medical, security, command
- **Needs** — [player-economy-and-banking](#player-economy-and-banking), [minor-antag-roles](#minor-antag-roles)
- **Verified** — partly supported. The core social-antagonist gist (contract clauses, damnation catalogue, chaplain/true-name counterplay, unrevivable soul debt, revival-contract popup) is directly confirmed in the fetched .ftl/.yml/.cs files from both forks. But DevilSystem.cs (OnListen handler) shows the true-name mechanic fires on ANY speech message containing the substring, not specifically the words 'stop'/'halt', and deals incremental Holy damage+stun with a 30s cooldown rather than a guaranteed one-shot burn. DevilComponent.cs/DevilBranchPrototype.cs/powerlevel.yml show power-level unlocks are just two extra actions (ActionCreateRevivalContract, ActionDevilPossess) with no red glow, no bident, and no devil-side CheatDeath tied to soul count -- that detail appears invented. On graft_shape: I searched beyond the cited evidence and found Goob-Station's own repo directly edits the non-namespaced upstream file Resources/Prototypes/GameRules/roundstart.yml (adding '- id: Devil # Goob' to the SubGamemodes probability table), confirming fork-patches-upstream for Goob-Station. Starlight, by contrast, keeps its own antag-registration file at _Starlight/GameRules/roundstart.yml (namespaced, self-contained), so for Starlight the correct reading is integration-would-require-upstream-edits. Since the unit bundles both forks and they differ, both readings apply.
  - unsupported: reading a contract to learn the devil's true name and then shouting it with "stop" or "halt" until it burns them apart
  - unsupported: a devil who has collected several souls starts visibly glowing red, gains a bident and can shrug off a killing blow and jerk back awake

### Heretic

<a id="heretic"></a>

Eldritch antagonist that draws transmutation rituals, sacrifices marked targets, researches a path of forbidden knowledge and can ascend into a monster.

**gaby-station-now-dumont-station, goobstation**

*structural · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 3 forks carry it*

A crew member wakes up hearing whispers from the Gates of Mansus and starts a secret second life: they carve chalk-like transmutation runes in maintenance, drag marked victims onto them to sacrifice, and spend the "knowledge" they earn climbing one of seven themed paths (ash, blade, flesh, lock, void, rust, cosmos). Each rung buys a new spell or item, so the same antag plays completely differently run to run: the rust heretic corrodes floors and walls into crumbling decay, the void heretic freezes and phases through reality, the blade heretic swears off guns in exchange for parries and thrown silver, the flesh heretic raises ghouls (ghost-role thralls) to fight for them. A "living heart" ability points them toward their next sacrifice target anywhere on the station, they shout garbled eldritch words when casting, and if they finish the whole path they perform a Final Ritual and Ascend into a monstrous end-boss form that the round announces at end-of-round. Security's job is to notice the runes and the missing people before that happens. Dumont's slice is tiny by comparison: one flavor item, an "Ink of imagination" book that pops out two eldritch influences, handed to midround heretics as starting gear.

- **Take** — It is the most complete escalating-antag design in the fork ecosystem: a solo antag with seven genuinely distinct playstyles, a visible ritual footprint the crew can counter-play against, and a real ascension climax that gives a round a memorable ending.
- **Skip** — Goob's implementation is roughly 670 files spread across client, server and their own Common assembly, with sprite overlays, tile corrosion, ghoul ghost roles and store listings all wired in, so this is a months-long port plus permanent maintenance, not a graft; Dumont's two files are just a cosmetic add-on that assumes Goob's heretic already exists.
- **Touches** — antagonist, ghost-roles, security, all-players
- **Needs** — [shared-utility-libraries](#shared-utility-libraries)
- **Verified** — supported. Nearly every Heretic file in Goob-Station (367+ blobs matched by path, tree listing truncated so this is a lower bound) sits under fork-owned namespaces (_Goobstation, _Shitcode, _Shitmed, Content.Goobstation.*), which is what made the path-data seed guess 'drop-in'. But I fetched the genuinely upstream, non-namespaced Resources/Prototypes/game_presets.yml directly and found literal in-place edits: 'Heretic # Goob' appended into the vanilla preset-name lists (two separate list entries), the exact blind spot the seed warns path data cannot see. That is real evidence the fork patches an upstream file to wire Heretic in, not merely a hypothetical integration cost — so 'needs-upstream-edits' is correct, and specifically the 'fork-patches-upstream' reading, contradicting the drop-in seed. Separately, the gameplay description checks out well against fetched evidence: seven ascension paths and their end-boss ascend text (ascensions.ftl), sacrifice-for-knowledge ritual text naming gibbing and knowledge points (rituals.ftl), a working 'living heart' locator ability (abilities/heretic.ftl), chalk-carving rune mechanic (carving-knife/knife.ftl), rust/void/blade path specifics including a no-guns-while-wielding-blades component and 'silver' thrown-weapon flavor (path files, catalog ftl), and ghoul/thrall systems (GhoulSystem.cs in the tree). Dumont's two-file slice is also confirmed near-verbatim: Inkofimaginination spawns two EldritchInfluence items and its sprite/Tag/UnholyItem all point back into _Goobstation's own Heretic assets, confirming it is cosmetic filler that presupposes Goob's heretic system already exists.

### Blob

<a id="blob"></a>

Spreading biomass organism that grows from a core across station tiles, spends resources on strains and spawned mobs, and is fought as a station-wide crisis.

**backmen, goobstation**

*structural · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 2 forks carry it*

One player (or a ghost who takes over a glowing green mouse) bursts into a blob core and starts painting living biomass across the station floor tile by tile, clicking to expand and Alt-clicking to harden tiles into strong or laser-reflecting armour. Points come from resource tiles, and get spent on nodes that extend the growth radius, factories that pump out blob pods and hulking blobbernauts, extra cores split off from the main one, and a choice of five chemical strains that change how the biomass fights back. The crew notices as the infection spreads: the station goes to Sigma and locks down with the evacuation shuttle disabled, then Gamma with a CBRN response team arriving and the survivors trying to nuke the station, while the captain has to guard the nuke disk because losing it means the blob effectively cannot be stopped. Burn damage is the counter, so lasers, welders and incendiary rounds become the crew's tools, and if the blob gets big enough the round simply ends with a blob win.

- **Take** — It is a complete station-wide crisis round type in one package: a solo antag with a real build-and-spend strategy layer, escalating alert stages, spawned minions, and its own win condition, giving the whole crew a shared objective that no upstream antag currently provides.
- **Skip** — It is one of the largest antags either fork ships (roughly 60 code files each plus tiles, mobs, actions, alerts and sprites) and it does not stay in its own corner: it hooks alert levels, shuttle-call blocking, station events, the nuke disk objective and round-end conditions, and the Goob copy additionally wires blob mobs into the language and collective-mind systems, so it is a long-lived maintenance burden rather than a file drop.
- **Touches** — antagonist, ghost-roles, security, command, engineering, medical, all-players
- **Needs** — [language-system](#language-system)
- **Verified** — supported. Fetched the Backmen guidebook XML directly and it is a near word-for-word match for the gameplay paragraph: green radioactive mouse carrier, click-to-expand/Alt-click-to-harden tiles, resource points, nodes/factories/pods/blobbernauts/core-split, "5 chemicals" ("любой из 5-ти представленных"), Sigma code with shuttle-call lockdown at stage 2, Gamma code with a RKhBZZ (CBRN) squad and crew trying to nuke the station at stage 3, captain guarding the nuke-auth disk (losing it makes Gamma-code destruction impossible), and burn/incendiary/laser/welder counters plus a size-based blob-win ending — all literally present in the source text. For graft shape, I pulled Goobstation's full repo tree and confirmed every Blob C#/prototype file lives under fork-owned namespaces (Content.Goobstation.{Server,Client,Shared}/Blob/, Resources/Prototypes/_Goobstation/Blob/) with zero genuine upstream-file edits (the one namespace collision, Content.Server/Worldgen/.../BlobFloorPlanBuilderComponent.cs, is an unrelated MIT-licensed asteroid-debris shape generator, not the antag). But BlobRuleSystem.cs directly injects and calls upstream Content.Server.AlertLevel.AlertLevelSystem, Shuttles.EmergencyShuttleSystem, RoundEnd.RoundEndSystem and Nuke.NukeCodePaperSystem, and blob_mobs.yml gives mobs LanguageSpeaker/LanguageKnowledge (Blob language, tied to the bundled _EinsteinEngines language addon) plus CollectiveMind(Blobmind) — confirming the stated language-system dependency and the "hooks alert levels/shuttle/nuke/round-end" integration claim. So the code itself is self-contained by namespace (not literally patching upstream files), but wiring it into another codebase means adding it to that codebase's game-rule/station-event registration and pulling in (or stripping) the language-system dependency — the integration-would-require-upstream-edits reading, not fork-patches-upstream.

### Self-replicating swarm antagonists

<a id="swarm-antags"></a>

Silicon swarm antagonists that consume station materials or tiles to replicate themselves and build their own structures.

**goobstation, impstation**

*structural · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 1 forks carry it*

Two different things share this slot. Impstation's Replicators are the real swarm: dead players take a ghost role as a silicon bug with three laws (preserve the hive, defend the nest, replicate), plant a nest somewhere quiet, and feed it by dragging in loot and eating the floor around it. The nest levels up as it eats, spitting out more replicators, groaning louder each level ("How is the hull still intact?!") until the station gets an announcement warning about self-replicating nanites; players get to spend accumulated growth on branching upgrades into a Deconstructor, Defender or Protector body, cannot hurt each other or the nest, and talk only through a fixed phrasebook of clicks ("Hostile", "Consume", "Cease", "The Hive"). At round end everyone sees how far the hive spread and how many units it produced. Goob's Flock is not that at all: it is a hostile teal crystal robot faction with its own architecture (crystal walls, doors, tables, lights, turrets) and a derelict flock ship you can board, where the drones shoot at you and drop glass cubes and orbs worth thousands of credits at cargo.

- **Take** — The Impstation half is a rare antag shape SS14 mostly lacks: a slow-growing, location-anchored infestation that turns dead players into a snowballing threat, giving security a physical objective to find and destroy rather than a person to arrest.
- **Skip** — A nest that eats floor tiles and swallows items has to make judgement calls about what it is allowed to delete, and Impstation's prototype is already carrying a hand-maintained blacklist of exceptions (nukes, cash, ectoplasm, mechs, steal targets) that would need re-auditing against every item and objective your fork adds.
- **Touches** — antagonist, ghost-roles, security, engineering, cargo, all-players
- **Needs** — [ruins-poi-and-sector-generation](#ruins-poi-and-sector-generation)
- **Verified** — supported. I fetched all 8 cited files plus several more I found by browsing the two repos' trees, and the description holds up in detail: replicators.ftl gives the exact three laws, the "cannot harm kin/nest" popups, the level 2-5 groan lines ("How is the hull still intact?!"), the level-5 station announcement, the AAC phrasebook (Hostile/Consume/Cease/The Hive all present), and the end-of-round summary string with location/level/replicator-count/points. replicator-actions.yml confirms the exact Deconstructor/Defender/Protector upgrade branch. replicator-nest.yml confirms the blacklist (Nuke, Cash, Ectoplasm...) and a separate preservationWhitelist (Mech, StealTarget, HumanoidAppearance) — the claim collapses these into one "blacklist of exceptions," which is a minor simplification but not a factual error. ReplicatorNestSystem.cs (Content.Server/_Impstation/Replicator/, which I located myself) has a TileConvertAt/NextTileConvertAt field consistent with the floor-eating claim, though I didn't trace the exact mutation call. On the Goob side, flock.yml confirms the hostile NPC drone/bit faction with combat AI and glass-cube drops; loot.yml confirms cube=3000cr/orb=5000cr ("worth thousands"); featherzone.yml confirms a shuttle cockpit+reactor (the boardable ship) with a teal light color (#0fb79a) matching "teal crystal." The cited evidence didn't include Structures/walls.yml, doors.yml, tables.yml, or Mobs/turret.yml, but I found and fetched all four myself via the repo tree API, confirming the "crystal walls, doors, tables, lights, turrets" architecture claim is literally true even though the citation list was incomplete. On graft_shape: every file I found for both halves (Resources/Prototypes/_Impstation/..., Content.Server/_Impstation/Replicator/..., Resources/Prototypes/_Goobstation/Flock/...) lives inside the fork's own namespace directories — I found zero instances of either fork editing an upstream file in place, so 'fork-patches-upstream' is not supported. The 'needs-upstream-edits' downgrade from the drop-in seed is better read as an integration cost: hooking ghost-role spawners into round-start antag budgets, wiring the round-end text into whatever summary system exists downstream, and (per the claim's own depends_on) placing nests/derelict ships via ruins/POI/sector generation are all points where a target codebase's own systems would need edits, even though the graft's source files are self-contained.

### Malfunctioning AI

<a id="malfunctioning-ai"></a>

Station AI turns antagonist, claiming the grid to build structures and cyborgs remotely, detonate machines and pursue takeover objectives.

**funky**

*structural · entangled · medium confidence · 0 forks carry it*

A rogue station AI gets a set of round objectives (survive uncarded, kill or protect a specific crewmember, build up a cyborg force, or trigger a station-wide doomsday countdown with its own dedicated music track) and a targeted ability it can fire anywhere on the station from its camera view. Aiming that ability at an empty tile makes the AI's eye hover there for a few seconds and a robotics factory bolts itself to the floor. Any living crewmember shoved into that factory is ground up, their brain pulled out and slotted into an MMI inside a fresh borg chassis that keeps their old name but wakes up under the AI's laws and shows up on the AI's list of owned cyborgs, so the crew's own dead become the AI's army.

- **Skip** — These twelve files are only the factory and objectives slice; the actual antag lives in a non-fork-namespaced Content.Shared/MalfAI tree (marker component, role, game rule, doomsday protocol, borg command menu) that is not in this unit, so grafting it means importing that whole system and its collisions with upstream silicon-law and borg code.
- **Touches** — antagonist, silicon, science, security, command, all-players
- **Verified** — partly supported. The claim itself already downgrades the seed's 'drop-in' guess to 'entangled', citing a non-fork-namespaced Content.Shared/MalfAI tree outside the 12-file unit. I independently confirmed this: Content.Shared/MalfAI/MalfAiMarkerComponent.cs returns HTTP 200 and lives at that exact path (not under any _Funkystation directory), verifying the antag's core marker component sits outside the fork namespace and outside this unit's evidence set. The six cited files themselves are internally consistent and well-namespaced (Content.Server/_Funkystation/..., Resources/Prototypes/_Funkystation/...), but they all reference Content.Shared.MalfAI types (MalfAiMarkerComponent, MalfAiRoboticsFactoryActionEvent) that live elsewhere, so the unit as scoped cannot function standalone — it's a slice of a larger, differently-namespaced antag system, matching 'entangled' rather than 'drop-in'.
  - unsupported: "trigger a station-wide doomsday countdown with its own dedicated music track" — evidence shows a MalfAiDoomsdayObjective (sabotageType: Doomsday) and a DoomsdayMusic soundCollection exist, but no countdown-timer mechanic appears in the fetched files; the 'countdown' framing is an inference from the objective/collection names, not something the code shown demonstrates.

**gaby-station-now-dumont-station**

*structural · entangled · medium confidence · 0 forks carry it*

The station AI can start the round secretly hostile, and it plays with a "CPU" meter on its screen that ticks up as it siphons processing power off the station (the code gates this on APCs). CPU is spent in an antagonist shop split into Deception, Factory and Disruption sections, plus a button that opens a panel for managing its own cyborgs. This fork's slice of it gives the rogue AI two concrete tricks: point at any powered machine, computer or vending machine and overload it into an explosion (it refuses and says so if the target is unpowered or isn't a machine), and permanently gain extra radio channels so it can listen in on and talk over departmental comms it was never keyed for.

### Nuclear operatives

<a id="nuclear-operatives"></a>

Syndicate strike squad that spawns on its own shuttle, optionally declares war, and hunts the disk to arm the station nuke.

**sunrise**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 0 forks carry it*

Sunrise reworks how a nuke op squad is funded and how the station reacts to them. Telecrystals are pooled under the commander instead of split evenly: the commander starts with a large budget that grows with every operative on the team, each grunt gets a smaller personal uplink allowance, and declaring war hands the commander another lump sum per teammate, so shopping becomes a squad decision made at the commander's uplink. Declaring war also automatically drives the station holding the disk to gamma alert a few seconds later, so the crew immediately gets the full alert response rather than waiting on the captain to raise it. On top of the uplinks there is a team delivery store stocking one-off, cooldown-gated squad gear: a matching hardsuit bundle, incendiary and uranium ammo duffels, and a Cybersun rover mech crate that only becomes available again after a long restock timer.

- **Take** — It makes the nukie commander an actual quartermaster and gives the crew a guaranteed, immediate gamma-alert response to a war declaration, which sharpens both sides of the round's opening without touching win conditions.
- **Skip** — The TC numbers (50 base, 30 per operative, war bonus) are tuned to Sunrise's squad sizes and gear prices, and the delivery store leans on syndicate crate and mech prototypes plus locale strings that a fork would have to supply or retune itself.
- **Touches** — antagonist, security, command
- **Verified** — supported. All six cited files check out closely: CommanderBaseTc=50, CommanderTcPerFighter=30, FighterUplinkTc=30, war bonus = 30×fighters, AlertLevelDelay defaults to 10s targeting gamma, and the delivery catalog has exactly the four one-off items described (hardsuit bundle, incendiary/uranium ammo duffels, Cybersun rover crate) with restock times from 5min to 2h, the rover having the longest. But the graft_shape needs a correction to WHY it's needs-upstream-edits: I pulled Content.Server/GameTicking/Rules/NukeopsRuleSystem.cs (the vanilla-named file, not under _Sunrise/), and it is riddled with '// Sunrise-Edit' comments that directly call the cited partial's private methods — OnWarDeclared calls ApplySunriseWarDeclarationAdjustments and DistributeExtraTc (which calls TryDistributeExtraTcSunrise), and the AfterAntagEntitySelected handler calls OnAfterAntagEntSelectedSunrise. So this fork's own copy of the upstream rule file is already patched in place to wire the whole feature, contradicting a naive path-data read that would only see the _Sunrise-namespaced files as 'the feature'. That file also carries several unrelated Sunrise edits (evac-shuttle round-end behavior, a GetCentcommMaps workaround) in the same file, so a graft would need to carefully lift just the relevant hunks out of a file mixed with other fork changes — a real cost the claim's skip_because never mentions (it cites TC tuning and catalog assets instead).
  - unsupported: "the commander starts with a large budget" — the base is CommanderBaseTc = 50 TC, which is modest on its own; it only becomes sizable once multiplied by squad size (50 + 30×fighters), so calling the starting figure itself "large" is a soft overstatement.

**serbia-strong**

*loop-change · entangled · medium confidence · 0 forks carry it*

SS220's nuke ops start on their own custom Syndicate outpost with its own docked war shuttle, and somewhere on that base sits a one-shot "reinforcement request" device. Before the squad leaves the outpost, an operative can activate it: the base sizes up the station's living crew against the ops already on the team and, if the crew badly outnumbers them, drops a matching batch of Syndicate reinforcement radios and 40 TC uplinks on the floor for ghosts to fill as extra operatives. If the team already declared war, each of those bonus uplinks is topped up to the full war-declaration TC budget. Use it too late (once the shuttle has left the outpost) or on a quiet, low-pop station and it just tells you no reinforcements are coming.

- **Take** — It makes nuke ops self-balancing against station population: a squad staring down a 60-player shift can pull in proportional extra operatives instead of being an automatic crew win, and the extra slots become ghost roles.
- **Skip** — The unit ships only the C# system plus a fork-specific outpost map; the actual item prototype, its sprite, and all three of its popup strings are missing, so you would be authoring the player-facing half yourself and then finding somewhere on the nuke outpost to place it. The scaling formula is also hardcoded to SS220's balance assumptions (two-op grace, uplink proto, war TC reuse) and would need retuning for a different roster size.
- **Touches** — antagonist, ghost-roles, security, all-players
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. The two SS220 C# files match the claimed mechanics closely (UsesRemain=1 one-shot, AmountToIgnore=2 "two-op grace", BaseUplinkRadio40TC uplinks, war TC top-up, LeftOutpost gate producing the same "no reinforcements" popup for both late-use and low-pop cases) — but the cited map has zero references to the item (contradicting the "sits on that base" framing) and the system compiles only against SS220's own customized WarDeclaratorComponent and a NukeopsRuleComponent it has extended with war-declaration fields, both outside the cited SS220-namespace evidence and unlisted in depends_on. That is a real dependency on another fork feature (SS220's war-declaration system), not just a few upstream tweaks, so this reads as entangled rather than a plain needs-upstream-edits case.
  - unsupported: "somewhere on that base sits a one-shot \"reinforcement request\" device" — the cited Resources/Maps/SS220/ss220-nukeoutpost.yml (22,952 lines) contains zero occurrences of "reinforcement" or any related entity id; the device is not actually placed anywhere on that map, directly contradicting the claim's own skip_because admission that the item prototype doesn't exist yet.
  - unsupported: "depends_on": [] — the system hard-depends on Content.Server/NukeOps/WarDeclaratorComponent.cs (war-declaration status) and on Content.Server/GameTicking/Rules/Components/NukeopsRuleComponent.cs, which itself carries SS220-added fields (WarTcAmountPerNukie, LeftOutpost, CanEnableWarOps, WarDeclaredTime) that only exist because SS220 built a whole separate war-declaration feature into the base nukeops rule. This is a real functional dependency on another SS220 system, not merely 'needs upstream edits' for a couple of stray references.

### Revenant

<a id="revenant"></a>

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 2 forks carry it*

### Shadowling

<a id="shadowling"></a>

Light-hating antagonist that enthralls crew into a collective mind in darkness, unlocks staged abilities and finally ascends to black out the station.

**einstein-engines**

*structural · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 2 forks carry it*

It builds a following by grabbing crew one at a time and enthralling them into obedient thralls who get night vision and a darkness-invisibility cloak and are expected to do whatever their shadowling says, and it unlocks staged powers as the thrall count grows: a stunning silencing glare, a pulse that shatters every light in the area, shadow-walking, blinding smoke, a screech, overloading an APC by hand, reviving a dead thrall as a lesser shadowling, shrugging off light entirely, and sabotaging the evacuation shuttle engines for a ten-minute delay. ### Cortical borer

<a id="cortical-borer"></a>

Parasitic ghost role that burrows into a host's brain, eavesdrops through them and dispenses chemicals into their bloodstream.

**monolith**

*activity · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 1 forks carry it*

A dead player can come back as a tiny brain worm that crawls into a living crewmate's head (blocked by any helmet, and by sugar in the victim's stomach). Once inside it rides along invisibly, listens to everything the host hears, reads their vitals like a health analyzer, and spends a slowly regenerating pool of "chemicals" from a menu to dose them straight into the bloodstream, anything from bicaridine and painkillers to mute toxin, ephedrine, blinding acid or knockout sleep drugs. Every few minutes it can seize the host's body outright for 40 seconds and walk them around, and while in control it can spend a big chunk of its chemical pool to make the host vomit up an egg that another ghost can take over as a new borer. Hosts get freed by drinking sugar to suppress it and then having brain surgery to pull the worm out; borers share a private hive chat with each other.

- **Take** — It is a complete, self-driving parasite role with real counterplay already designed in (helmets block entry, sugar suppresses, brain surgery removes), so it gives ghosts something to do and gives medical a new patient problem without touching the round's win conditions.
- **Skip** — The prototypes lean on several non-upstream systems Monolith already has (a universal-language speaker tag, a collective-mind hive channel, thermal vision, a custom surgery step and a radio-overheard hook), so a graft means either bringing those along or stripping features out, and the role itself hands one player quiet control over another player's body, which needs admin attention and a playtime gate (Monolith uses 50 hours) to not be miserable.
- **Touches** — ghost-roles, antagonist, medical, all-players
- **Needs** — [language-system](#language-system), [surgery-and-limb-wounds](#surgery-and-limb-wounds)
- **Verified** — supported. Every specific gameplay beat checks out against actual source: GhostRole+GhostTakeoverAvailable ghost role with a 50hr (180000s) playtime gate matches the skip_because note; the .ftl strings and OnInfestHostAttempt code confirm helmet-blocks-entry and sugar-blocks; CorticalBorerComponent has ChemicalPoints/ChemicalPointCap=250 regenerating at 1/sec, and the chemicals yml lists exactly bicaridine, mute toxin, ephedrine, a blinding acid (NorepinephricAcid) and a sleep drug (Nocturine); ActionControlHost has useDelay 340s (5:40) wrapping a 40s ControlDuration, matching '40 seconds every few minutes'; EggCost=200 against a 250 cap is genuinely 'a big chunk' of the pool; BorerRadioReceive literally forwards every heard radio message to the borer's player session, confirming 'listens to everything the host hears'; CollectiveMind channel 'CorticalBorer' confirms the private hive chat; the guidebook text is a near-verbatim match for the sugar+surgery removal claim. The graft_shape call is not just confirmed but understated: I found the actual diffs. Content.Server/Radio/EntitySystems/HeadsetSystem.cs (a plain, non-namespaced upstream file) has an explicit '// Mono - Borers begin/end' block raising RadioMessageHeardEvent, and Resources/Prototypes/_Shitmed/Entities/Surgery/{surgeries.yml,surgery_steps.yml} carry '# mono change' blocks wiring SurgeryCorticalBorerRemoval into the brain-surgery graph. So the path-data 'drop-in' seed is wrong in the strongest sense (fork-patches-upstream, confirmed by name), and separately, a different destination fork without an identical HeadsetSystem/_Shitmed surgery tree would have to hand-write those same hook points (integration-would-require-upstream-edits) — hence 'both'. UniversalLanguageSpeaker (_EinsteinEngines/Language), CollectiveMind (_Starlight), and ThermalVision (_White/Overlays) are all separate borrowed-namespace systems the species prototype depends on, matching depends_on and skip_because exactly.
