### Revolutionaries

<a id="revolutionaries"></a>

Head revolutionaries convert crew with flashes to overthrow command, countered by mindshield implants and the heads of staff.

**starlight**

*structural · entangled · medium confidence · 1 forks carry it*

Head revolutionaries get their own black-market store, stocked with Soviet-flavoured kit and paid for with two separate currencies: points earned by converting crew buy the "passive" shelf (cheap sunglasses, an uplink implanter, a Soviet radio key, a commander's whistle, rally banners, a communist AI lawboard), while a second war currency buys the armed shelf (Makarov, Finka knife, Mosin, sawn-off TOZ, Stechkin duffel, DP28 and PPSh bundles), Soviet EVA suits, bandoliers, gas masks, greatcoats and a marine hardsuit, plus shuttle-sabotage odds and ends. Every listing has a hard stock limit, so a revolution can only field so many rifles. The centrepiece purchase is a supply rift the head rev plants somewhere on the station: dropping it fires a station-wide broadcast naming the comrade who placed it and its location, it then charges in view of the whole rev team as a live percentage, and if the crew fails to smash it in time CentCom pushes the station to gamma alert and locks out evacuation shuttle calls. Conversions are also tracked back to the head rev who made them, so only your own recruits can be handed your implanters. A separate playtime-gated Soviet strike-force antag role exists alongside all this, though the files read do not spell out how it enters the round.

- **Take** — It turns revs from a flash-and-brawl mob into an escalating faction with an economy, a defensible objective the whole station has to respond to, and a real "the revolution is winning" beat when the rift finishes and evac is cut off.
- **Skip** — The store is welded to a large Soviet-themed weapon and clothing set (Makarov, PPSh, DP28, marine hardsuit, mech bundles, custom sprites) and to the fork's own store purchase events, so grafting it means importing an entire content pack and patching upstream conversion and store code, not dropping in one system.
- **Touches** — antagonist, security, command, all-players
- **Needs** — [traitor-uplink](#traitor-uplink), [firearms-content-expansion](#firearms-content-expansion), [clothing-and-wardrobe-pack](#clothing-and-wardrobe-pack)
- **Verified** — partly supported. Read all seven cited files plus rev_uplink_catalog.yml in full and StarlightCCVars.Game.cs for the autogamma cvar. The store/currency/conversion-tracking mechanics and the huge Soviet weapon/clothing catalog (Makarov, Finka, Mosin, Toz106, Stechkin/DP28/PPSh duffels, EVA bundle, marine hardsuit, bandolier, gas mask, coat, ushanka, etc., all under Telebond/Conversion listings with per-item stock limits) check out almost exactly as described, and RevSupplyRiftSystem.cs confirms the converter/implant tracking and confirms the rift literally reuses the vanilla DragonRiftComponent/DragonRiftState machinery plus vanilla Store, AlertLevel and RoundEnd systems and vanilla Revolutionary/HeadRevolutionary components — genuinely entangled with a large custom content pack, matching the skip_because narrative. But two specific narrative beats in 'gameplay' are wrong: the rift-placement message (SendRiftPlacedMessage) is sent only to Revolutionary/HeadRevolutionary-tagged mind-holders, ghosts and admins, never to the whole crew, so 'station-wide broadcast naming the comrade' is false; and the gamma-alert/evac-lockout only fires if the server cvar game.autogamma_enabled is turned on (it defaults to false) and only once game.autogamma_minimum_rifts (default 2) rifts finish charging, not simply 'if the crew fails to smash it in time' on the one rift described as the centrepiece purchase.
  - unsupported: "dropping it fires a station-wide broadcast naming the comrade who placed it and its location" — the code (SendRiftPlacedMessage) sends this only via private ChatChannel.Radio to entities with RevolutionaryComponent/HeadRevolutionaryComponent, plus ChatChannel.Dead (ghosts) and ChatChannel.Admin; it is never broadcast to the general crew.
  - unsupported: "if the crew fails to smash it in time CentCom pushes the station to gamma alert and locks out evacuation shuttle calls" — this is gated behind the server cvar game.autogamma_enabled, which defaults to false, and additionally requires game.autogamma_minimum_rifts (default 2) separate rifts to reach the Finished state, not the single rift the claim frames as the centrepiece purchase.

<a id="upstream-midround-antags"></a>

The stock midround threat roster: infiltrating ninjas, spreading zombie infections and rift-opening space dragons.

**serbia-strong**

*loop-change · drop-in · medium confidence · 1 forks carry it*

Adds a stealth objective for the space ninja: go the whole round without ever being seen. Whenever the ninja is uncloaked, out of a locker and standing in clear line of sight of a living crewmember within about twelve tiles, their own screen starts breaking up with a glitching reveal warning that builds over five seconds; duck behind a wall, cloak, or climb into a container before it fills and the warning fades and the timer resets. ### Hidden secret identities

<a id="secret-identities"></a>

Social-deduction framework where any player may carry a hidden identity drawn from themed organisations, each with its own objectives, targets and abilities.

**ephemeral-space**

*structural · entangled · high confidence · 0 forks carry it*

Every player starts the round with a hidden "mask" instead of most of them being plain crew, and the set of masks in play is chosen by a "Masquerade" that acts as the round's gamemode. Masks range from quietly weird to outright dangerous: an Arsonist who must light a running tally of fires and loses progress whenever anyone extinguishes one, an Avenger assigned a random person to keep alive who flips to a hunt-and-kill objective with a proximity-sensing ability if that person is murdered, a Cannibal who eats corpses to steal the dead player's identity and objectives, a Hater given a randomly generated grudge ("they stole your lunch from the fridge") they must act on without killing, a Daredevil who needs to take specific damage from grilles or shotgun pellets to feel alive, a Hitman working a codenamed contract, a Pickpocket with a one-per-person steal, a Stalker who picks marks, and an Empath who senses auras like "dangerous killing intent" on people nearby. Whole organisations sit on top of that: Parasites are infected hosts who win by getting themselves killed and cannot kill anyone without dying instantly, and if they infect most of the living station a worm bursts from every member's arm and the round ends in their favour. Disguise state (face covered, voice masked, wearing someone else's ID) is shown to you as a live status icon, so faking a persona is a tracked, readable act rather than an honour system.

- **Take** — It converts the round from "crew plus a few antags" into a social-deduction game where nobody is safely ordinary, and it ships dozens of small, self-contained objective flavours plus a disguise-visibility system that would improve paranoia even in a conventional round.
- **Skip** — It is not a feature you bolt on, it is the fork's entire round framework: Masquerades replace gamemode presets, the baseline crew objective is Ephemeral Space's Warp Drive, and win conditions, ghost mobs like the cryohusk and phantom, and round-end reporting all assume it, so grafting it means adopting that round structure and then maintaining ~170 server files of per-mask objective systems.
- **Touches** — all-players, antagonist, security, medical, ghost-roles, command
- **Needs** — [warp-drive](#warp-drive), [alternate-round-types](#alternate-round-types)
- **Verified** — partly supported. Crew.xml and SecretIdentities/organizations.yml show the baseline Crew organization's win objective literally is ESObjectiveWarpDrive, and Masquerades.xml frames Masquerades as the round's gamemode-selection layer, which matches the claim that this is the fork's entire round framework rather than a bolt-on feature. A full repo-tree search turned up ~330 files across Content.Server/_ES/SecretIdentity, Content.Shared/_ES/SecretIdentity, Content.Server/_ES/WarpDrive, Content.Server/_ES/Organizations, and matching Masquerade prototypes/guidebook pages, corroborating the claimed depth of interconnection (roughly the '~170 server files' order of magnitude cited, once you count Client/Shared/Tests too it's larger). ## Medical

### Resuscitation and life support

<a id="resuscitation-and-life-support"></a>

Keeping a dying patient alive without surgery: chest compressions, blood transfusion equipment and live vitals readouts.

**goobstation**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 3 forks carry it*

This is a grab-bag of keep-them-alive tools rather than one system. A medic can slap a medical patch onto a patient and it drip-feeds its chemicals into them over time (some dump a dose the instant it goes on, and cheap ones crumple into trash once empty), or wield a healing beam gun that pours a continuous heal into a crewmate and charges up a meter as it works, which can then be spent on a short burst of supercharged healing on both of you. The health analyzer readout gains a total vital damage line plus disease information, telling you the genotype, how far the infection has progressed and how much immunity the patient has built. Elsewhere, an officer can spend about eight seconds scanning a crewmate to slip in a command tracking implant so they show up on crew monitors and call out when they die, and anyone who takes a nasty shock has their suit sensors randomly knocked to a different setting, so the monitoring console quietly starts lying about where they are until someone resets it.

- **Take** — The medical patch and healing-beam pieces give medics something to do on a patient who is not on an operating table, which is exactly the gap upstream leaves between "inject chems" and "do surgery".
- **Skip** — It is four loosely related mini-features stapled together, and the parts that matter most to players (the analyzer disease and vital-damage readouts, the suit sensor scrambling) plug into upstream health analyzer and suit sensor code, so you inherit merge friction on upstream files for what is otherwise small self-contained content.
- **Touches** — medical, command, security, all-players
- **Needs** — [disease-and-virology](#disease-and-virology), [surgery-and-limb-wounds](#surgery-and-limb-wounds), [character-traits](#character-traits)
- **Verified** — partly supported. I fetched Content.Server/Medical/HealthAnalyzerSystem.cs (an upstream-path file, not under any _Goobstation/Content.Goobstation.* namespace) and it contains inline additions tagged '// Goobstation' (vitalDamage calc via MobThresholdSystem.CheckVitalDamage, bloodLow flag, extra args threaded through the analyzer message) directly inside the pre-existing upstream method. That flatly contradicts the drop-in seed's premise of zero non-namespace files, and confirms the claim's own needs-upstream-edits assessment as the fork-patches-upstream flavor (the fork's tree itself edits an upstream-originated file in place, not merely "would need edits if grafted").
  - unsupported: which can then be spent on a short burst of supercharged healing on both of you -- MedigunSystem.cs only calls _damage.TryChangeDamage on entities in HealedEntities (the beamed target(s), default MaxLinksAmount=1); the wielder/ParentEntity is never passed to the damage-change call, so uber mode heals only the target(s) being beamed, not the medic wielding the gun.

**sunrise**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 3 forks carry it*

The crew monitoring console gets a lot louder and more usable. A doctor can switch the console to alarm mode, and every fifteen seconds it will beep an alarm if anyone wearing a working suit sensor is dead or in crit anywhere except inside a morgue, so the medbay hears about a body in maintenance instead of noticing it twenty minutes later. The list can be filtered down to only the people you care about: by health band (healthy, hurt, badly hurt, critical, dead) and by department, with the option to hide implant trackers. Separately, a medical borg's hypospray speaks aloud what it just injected into whom (with a short cooldown so it does not spam), and some entities carry a healing aura that quietly ticks damage off nearby mobs every two seconds within a few tiles, capped so it stops once the target is healthy enough.

- **Take** — The corpse alarm plus department/health filtering turns the crew monitor from a wall of dots you squint at into something that actively tells medical where the bodies are, which is the single biggest quality-of-life lift the console can get.
- **Skip** — It is not one feature but three loosely related ones bolted together (console alerts, borg hypospray voice lines, a generic healing aura), and the console half is a partial class hanging off upstream's CrewMonitoringConsoleSystem and its UI, so it rides along with every upstream crew-monitor refactor; the alarm also reuses an SMG empty-magazine sound as its siren and has no locale of its own, with Russian-only comments throughout.
- **Touches** — medical, silicon, command, security
- **Verified** — supported. I fetched all 8 cited files plus, critically, the fork's own Content.Server/Medical/CrewMonitoring/CrewMonitoringConsoleSystem.cs (an upstream-path file NOT under _Sunrise). That file is already altered in place: `public sealed partial class CrewMonitoringConsoleSystem : EntitySystem // Sunrise - edit` and `InitializeAlert(); // Sunrise - Add` inside Initialize(). This proves the corpse-alert half is literally a partial-class bolt-on requiring the upstream class to already be marked partial and to call InitializeAlert — both fork-patches-upstream (this edit already exists in the fork's own tree, outside _Sunrise) and integration-would-require-upstream-edits (porting to another codebase needs the same partial+Initialize hook added to that codebase's copy). Every numeric/behavioral claim I checked matched exactly: CorpseAlertTime=15f, HasCorpsesOutsideMorgue logic (dead-or->=100%-critical, excluding MorgueComponent parents), CrewMonitoringFilterComponent's AllowedHealthStates/AllowedDepartmentIds/IncludeTrackers, BorgHyposprayComponent's 5s AnnouncementCooldown with Loc.GetString announcement, and AoEHealSystem's 2-second tick, 5f default range, and Threshold-gated stop condition. The reused SMG-empty-magazine siren sound and Russian-only comments in AoEHeal/CrewMonitoringCorpseAlert files are also directly confirmed. Overall this is a strong, well-evidenced needs-upstream-edits call, not a drop-in — the assessor undercounted the fork-patches-upstream severity slightly since the seed's path scan (limited to cited _Sunrise paths) couldn't see the sibling upstream-path file that actually carries the edit.
  - unsupported: "health band (healthy, hurt, badly hurt, critical, dead)" compresses the actual CrewMonitoringHealthState enum (Unknown, Healthy, Good, NotGreat, Bad, Terrible, Critical, Dead, Alive — 5 non-critical bands plus Critical/Dead/Alive), so the 5-label gloss understates the granularity actually implemented.
  - unsupported: "A doctor can switch the console to alarm mode" — the toggle verb (AddToggleVerb) is gated only on CanInteract/CanAccess, not on any medical-role check, so any crew member with console access can toggle it, not specifically doctors.

**rmc14**

*loop-change · entangled · high confidence · 3 forks carry it*

A medic can drop to their knees beside a dying marine and pump their chest by hand, buying roughly seven seconds of extra revival time per cycle and clawing back suffocation damage, with a nag popup if they push too fast ("Incorrect rhythm. Do it slower.") and faster compressions if they are trained. Around that sit wheeled IV stands you drag onto a patient to either pump blood in or draw it out, blood packs you jab into someone's arm by hand, portable dialysis units that scrub chemicals out of a bloodstream, and stretchers that can call a dropship down for a medevac pickup. In the field hospital, a sleeper pod console gives a live readout of the occupant's name, health, temperature, pulse, blood level and brute/burn/toxin/oxygen split, and lets the doctor inject measured doses of stocked chemicals, run dialysis, or set the pod to spit out anyone who dies in it; handheld health scanners and body scanners show the same vitals plus wounds and whether the patient can still be shocked back at all.

- **Take** — Gives medics a full pre-surgery toolkit - hands-on CPR, transfusions, dialysis, live vitals and a pod that keeps someone stable - so a crit patient becomes an ongoing job rather than a defib prompt.
- **Skip** — It is wired into RMC-14's own skill tiers, wound model, custom bloodstream/pulse/reagent-metabolism systems and even marine-vs-xeno checks, so almost none of it works without dragging those in or rewriting each gate against upstream equivalents.
- **Touches** — medical, combat-medic, all-players
- **Needs** — [squads-ranks-and-skills](#squads-ranks-and-skills), [surgery-and-limb-wounds](#surgery-and-limb-wounds), [reagent-and-reaction-expansion](#reagent-and-reaction-expansion), [mob-damage-and-movement](#mob-damage-and-movement), [xenomorph-hive](#xenomorph-hive)
- **Verified** — supported. Read all 9 cited files (CPRSystem.cs, SharedIVDripSystem.cs, SharedRMCDefibrillatorSystem.cs, SleeperSystem.cs, MedevacStretcherSystem.cs, HealthScannerUiData.cs, cpr/iv/sleeper.ftl). Every specific gameplay beat checks out exactly: CPRCooldownSeconds=7s feeding AddRevivableTime (the "seven seconds" claim), Asphyxiation-only heal of 10, the literal locale string "Incorrect rhythm. Do it slower.", SkillsSystem.GetSkillDelayMultiplier shortening the CPR do-after for trained medics, drag-and-drop IVDripComponent/BloodPackComponent/PortableDialysisComponent all requiring _skills.HasAllSkills, MedevacStretcherSystem wiring StrapComponent occupants into a DropshipTargetComponent CAS beacon, and SleeperSystem's UpdateUI building the exact console readout (name/health/status/temperature/brute/burn/toxin/oxygen/blood level/pulse/chemical injection/dialysis toggle/auto-eject-dead) matching sleeper.ftl's label set precisely. Every file imports the fork's own SkillsSystem, RMCBloodstream/RMCPulse/RMCReagent/RMCTemperature/SharedWounds systems, MarineComponent, and XenoComponent checks — confirming the claim's own downgrade from the seed's naive path-data 'drop-in' guess to 'entangled' is correct; the feature is thoroughly wired into RMC's marine/skill/bloodstream/wound/xeno subsystems, and MedevacStretcherSystem additionally pulls in Dropship/CAS/Area systems not even listed in depends_on, making the entanglement if anything broader than stated.

**backmen, frontier, funky, harmony-station, impstation, serbia-strong**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 3 forks carry it*

This is a grab-bag of small additions around bringing dead people back. SS220 caps how many times one person can be defibrillated: after two revives you start taking brain damage a few minutes after each one, and there is a good chance of picking up a lasting ailment from the death, so a body that keeps dying eventually stops being worth saving. Funky Station adds a wheeled crash cart that medics roll to the patient with a compact defib and an oxygen (or nitrogen, plasma, laughing gas) tank slotted into visible holders, plus privacy curtains, auto-injector cartridge cases, a body scanner wired to the operating table, and objects that trickle healing into whoever is on them. - **Skip** — It is six unrelated slivers from six forks rather than one system, so grafting it means cherry-picking and separately maintaining a revive limiter, a furniture pack, a species-reroll table and two cloning flags, each hooking upstream medical or cloning code at a different point.

### Mob damage, movement and gravity

<a id="mob-damage-and-movement"></a>

Baseline damage types and groups, crit and death thresholds, movement modifiers, pulling, climbing, buckling and gravity handling for mobs.

**rmc14**

*loop-change · entangled · medium confidence · 1 forks carry it*

Combat feels heavier and more punishing: getting flung into a wall or crate at speed hurts you for real, staggers you, flashes you red and bounces you back, with the damage scaling off how big you are and how fast you were moving. Being downed is no longer a safe holding pattern either — while you are in crit you can go deaf, your vision blurs out, and someone dragging you across the floor keeps chipping away at you, so a rescue is a race rather than a formality. Around that sit tuned armour and material toughness values (barricades, sandbags, girders, foam walls, vehicle plating, alien resin and weeds each resist different damage types), plus health HUD icons that let medics read at a glance whether a body is fresh, nearly unrecoverable, or flagged do-not-resuscitate, and colour-coded triage holocards pinned over patients.

- **Take** — The obstacle-slam and crit-degradation pieces make fights and rescues dramatically more tense, and the triage HUD icons give medics real information instead of a guess.
- **Skip** — It is a whole-pipeline rebalance tuned for RMC-14's marines-versus-aliens setting, wired into that fork's own size, slow, stun and status-effect systems, so lifting it means retuning every damage number on the station and maintaining a permanent divergence from upstream's damage handling.
- **Touches** — all-players, medical, security, antagonist
- **Needs** — [xenomorph-hive](#xenomorph-hive), [hud-and-status-readouts](#hud-and-status-readouts)
- **Verified** — partly supported. Every other specific in the gameplay text checks out against the actual files: RMCObstacleSlammingSystem.cs implements exactly the described slam-into-obstacle mechanic (damage = f(MobSizeCoefficient/size, ThrowSpeedCoefficient*speed), red color flash via _color.RaiseEffect, knockback via _size.KnockBack, plus optional stun/slowdown bonuses); DamageOnPulledWhileCritComponent.cs confirms drag-damage-while-downed; DeafenWhileCritComponent.cs confirms crit-deafness; health_hud.yml has exactly the Healthy/DeadAlmost/DeadDNR icon tiers described as "fresh/nearly unrecoverable/do-not-resuscitate"; holocard.yml has orange/red/black/purple triage icons; marine_modifier_sets.yml and xeno_modifier_sets.yml define per-material damage resistance for barricades, sandbags, girders, foam walls, vehicle armor/frames, resin, and weeds, matching the claim precisely. On graft_shape: the ObstacleSlammingSystem file itself imports and depends on Content.Shared._RMC14.Slow (RMCSlowSystem) and Content.Shared._RMC14.Stun (RMCSizeStunSystem) — other _RMC14 subsystems living in sibling namespace directories the seed's blunt path heuristic would not flag as "outside the fork's own directories" since they're still under _RMC14, but which are functionally separate catalogued systems this unit cannot run without. That is genuine entanglement with the fork's other features, so the assessor's downgrade from the seed's "drop-in" to "entangled" is correct and, if anything, understated relative to what a literal drop-in would require.
  - unsupported: "your vision blurs out" as a crit-specific mechanic paired with going deaf: DeafenWhileCritComponent confirms the deafness half, but no cited or discoverable file ties a blur/blindness component to the crit state the way DeafenWhileCritComponent does for deafness. The only blur-related fork file, Content.Shared/_RMC14/BlurredVision/RMCBlindedComponent.cs, is an empty marker component with no crit hookup found anywhere in the tree — the vision-blur claim may just be describing vanilla SS14 blindness-on-crit, not a bespoke piece of this unit.

**sunrise**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 1 forks carry it*

Getting knocked down while you are running no longer just drops you in place: your character tumbles forward in the direction they were facing, skidding a tile or so, loses stamina from the impact and needs a moment before getting back up, and if you are already too winded you simply flop down with a "can't fall" message instead. Thrown objects hit according to how bulky they are, so a heavy toolbox or crate can floor someone and dent walls while small junk just bruises. Around that sit a pile of smaller body-and-motion tweaks: a visible dragging animation when you pull someone, the ability to fall asleep while strapped into a bed (with certain bedding making the bed heal you faster or slower), a stasis ability that freezes and hides a creature until it is woken, mobs that crumble into ectoplasm instead of leaving a corpse, character height and build actually changing how heavy and hard to shove you are, and extra damage resistance profiles so felinids, synthetics, dragons and similar take blunt, burn, shock and poison differently.

- **Take** — The tumble-on-knockdown and weight-scaled throwing turn two flat upstream mechanics into readable, physical moments that change how every melee fight and chase feels, without adding any new role or objective.
- **Skip** — It is a grab bag rather than one system, and the good parts (falling, throwing) sit next to unrelated pieces (stasis, ectoplasm death, profile-driven mass) whose value depends on fork content you may not have; the falling rules also rebalance every stun-and-beat encounter, so security and antag balance need retuning after the graft.
- **Touches** — all-players, security, medical, antagonist
- **Needs** — [extra-playable-species](#extra-playable-species), [character-markings-and-editor](#character-markings-and-editor)
- **Verified** — partly supported. Cloned the repo directly and found Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Mobs/Species/base.yml (the upstream BaseMobSpecies prototype, not under any _Sunrise directory) has `type: CanFall` added in place inside a `# Sunrise-Start / # Sunrise-End` block, alongside unrelated additions (CanJump, InjectNeed, clothing sprite layers). This proves the path-data 'drop-in' seed was wrong for the reason the tool itself can't see (in-place upstream edits), and independently confirms the claim's own downgrade to needs-upstream-edits — but as fork-patches-upstream, not merely integration-would-require-edits: Sunrise's own copy already touches upstream files, interleaving the falling feature with unrelated species tweaks in the same edit block. Most of the gameplay narrative checks out against the cited C# components: fall-throw distance/velocity/stamina cost and the literal 'cant-fall-no-stamina' popup in StandingStateSystem.cs, weight-thresholded knockdown/structure damage in SunriseThrownItemDamageComponent, CanSleepOnBuckle + BedHealModifierClothingComponent for bed sleeping, BecomeDustOnDeathComponent spawning 'Ectoplasm', HumanoidPhysicalStatsComponent tracking per-profile fixture densities, the Starlight-sourced StasisComponent with hide/heal-while-frozen fields, and Felinid/Silicon/Dragon/Predator/Cybernetic entries in modifier_sets.yml. Two problems surfaced: (1) 'needs a moment before getting back up' is not actually shown — FallStatusEffectComponent is an empty marker with no cited system logic, and its 1s duration reads more like a re-trigger cooldown than a proven stand-up delay; (2) one of the 16 cited evidence files, Resources/Prototypes/_Sunrise/StatusEffects/job.yml, is entirely JobIcon sprite prototypes and has nothing to do with status effects or this feature — a wrong citation. Separately, StandingStateSystem.cs hard-depends on a distinct fork feature (Content.Shared._Sunrise.Jump / JumpStatusEffectComponent) not listed in depends_on, and the visible pull-drag animation (SharedPullingAnimationSystem.cs / ActivePullingAnimationComponent.cs under Content.Shared/_Sunrise/Movement/Pulling) is real but wasn't in the cited evidence list either — a citation-completeness gap rather than a false claim.
  - unsupported: "needs a moment before getting back up" — no cited file shows logic delaying standing after a fall; FallStatusEffectComponent is an empty marker component with no attached behavior in evidence, and the 1s duration looks like a fall re-trigger cooldown rather than a stand-up delay.
  - unsupported: Evidence file Resources/Prototypes/_Sunrise/StatusEffects/job.yml is cited as support but contains only JobIcon sprite prototypes (IAA, Magistrat, BlueShield, borg icons, etc.) — nothing about status effects, damage, or movement.

**backmen**

*loop-change · entangled · medium confidence · 1 forks carry it*

Any crewmember can deliberately drop to the floor with a keybind and keep crawling around at about a quarter of normal speed, then spend a second getting back up; lose your legs and you stay down until they are replaced. On top of that the fork reroutes how hurt bodies work, so damage lands as actual wounds on the part that was hit rather than a single pooled health bar, adds an armour-piercing damage type and a Holy/immaterial damage category, and gives races like spirits, arachne, oni, harpies and shadowkin their own resistances and weaknesses (a spirit takes triple heat and quintuple holy but shrugs off cold). There is also a gib-on-collide behaviour where certain hazards splatter whoever runs into them outright, with a sound and a taunting popup.

- **Take** — Voluntary lying down and crawling is a genuinely expressive movement verb that makes downed and injured play feel active instead of just being a ragdoll, and the per-race damage modifier sets are a clean way to give species real combat identity.
- **Skip** — The damage half is not separable: BackmenDamageModelSystem is built on top of the fork's Consciousness, Wounds and body-part Targeting systems, so grafting it drags in the whole Backmen surgery rework, and even the laying-down system reaches into the fork's body/leg-counting code.
- **Touches** — medical, security, all-players, antagonist
- **Needs** — [surgery-and-limb-wounds](#surgery-and-limb-wounds), [extra-playable-species](#extra-playable-species)
- **Verified** — supported. SharedLayingDownSystem.cs imports Content.Shared.Backmen.Body.Systems (BkmBodySharedSystem, used for GetEffectiveRequiredLegs/HasLegs) and Content.Shared.Backmen.Targeting; BackmenDamageModelSystem.cs directly consumes Content.Shared.Backmen.Surgery.Consciousness.Components, Content.Shared.Backmen.Surgery.Wounds.Components (InjurableComponent, WoundableComponent, WoundComponent) and Targeting.TargetBodyPart to route damage per-limb. Both are genuinely wired into the fork's other Consciousness/Wounds/Body-part subsystems, not just co-located in the same directory, so the entangled downgrade from the drop-in path-data seed is correct.

**deltav, ephemeral-space, estacao-pirata, monolith, serbia-strong**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 1 forks carry it*

Five forks each bolt a small piece onto how hits land. The biggest is Ephemeral Space's rule that any hit below a set threshold simply bounces off with no effect at all, paired with a retuned table of what hurts what, so a fire axe chews through a wall while a knife does nothing to it, bullets shatter normal windows but only crack bulletproof ones, and lighters burn plants alarmingly fast. Alongside that: things that shock or stun anyone who walks into them and then keep hurting whoever is stuck, robotic crew who buzz audibly instead of gasping while bleeding out in crit, a chemical that raises or lowers how much punishment a body can take before dropping, and a shout when someone slams into someone else at speed.

- **Take** — The damage-deflection idea (small hits are ignored outright rather than shaved down) is a clean, self-contained way to stop chip damage from trivialising walls, windows and armour, and it reads more intuitively to players than resistance percentages.
- **Skip** — It is five unrelated scraps rather than one system: the Monolith share is species-specific body and organ prototypes that are useless without those species, and the deflection thresholds and retuned modifier sets only matter once you attach them to upstream wall, window, machine and mob prototypes, which is a balance pass across the whole content tree rather than a file copy.
- **Touches** — all-players, security, medical, engineering
- **Needs** — [extra-playable-species](#extra-playable-species)
- **Verified** — partly supported. I cloned all three relevant forks (ephemeral-space, Monolith, SerbiaStrong-220) and grepped for actual usage. The core Ephemeral Space mechanics check out precisely: ESDamageDeflectionComponent exists as described, and the ESWall/ESWindow/ESReinforcedWindow/ESWeakBiological modifier-set numbers, when run against the actual FireAxe (Blunt3/Slash7/Structural10, +Slash5/Structural40 when wielded) and the ESWeakBiological comment ('increases effectiveness of weak flammable weapons like lighters'), genuinely produce the claimed player-facing effects (fireaxe nets ~30 structural/hit through the wall's reduction while slash-only weapons like a knife net ~0; windows get an 8x piercing coefficient vs 2x for reinforced). But the graft_shape reasoning is wrong in its specifics even though its conclusion (needs-upstream-edits) is right: I found ephemeral-space directly edits canonical upstream files (Entities/Structures/Walls/walls.yml, Windows/base_window.yml, Furniture/chairs.yml, beds.yml, Machines/base_structuremachines.yml, Doors/Airlocks/base_structureairlocks.yml, Decoration/cobwebs.yml, Objects/Misc/spaceshroom.yml) to attach the new modifier sets, Monolith edits upstream Reagents/medicine.yml to attach HealthScaleEffect to Aloxadone, and SS220 edits upstream Entities/Mobs/NPCs/revenant.yml to attach StunsContacts/DamageOnStunContact — so this is 'fork-patches-upstream' in the literal sense, not merely a hypothetical wiring cost. Separately, the skip_because justification for Monolith ('species-specific body and organ prototypes') does not match the two Monolith files actually cited: containers.yml's ShieldHeavy is a generic damage container used by a handheld heavy-shield item, and HealthScaleEffect.cs is a generic reagent-scaling effect wired into the upstream Aloxadone medicine — neither is species-gated. And the EstacaoPirata evidence file (_EstacaoPirata/EmitBuzzOnCrit/EmitBuzzOnCritComponent.cs) appears to be dead code: it is not referenced by any prototype in the repo. The component actually wired to the IPC mob (Entities/Mobs/Player/ipc.yml) is a near-duplicate, differently-named, non-fork-namespaced file (Content.Shared/Silicon/EmitBuzzWhileDamaged/EmitBuzzWhileDamagedComponent.cs) that wasn't in the evidence list at all, so the citation for that sub-claim doesn't point at the live implementation.

### Limb wounds, body-part targeting and surgery

<a id="surgery-and-limb-wounds"></a>

Replaces flat mob damage with per-limb health and wounds, a body-part targeting doll, step-driven surgical procedures with tool and condition requirements, and detachable limbs and organs.

**rmc14**

*loop-change · entangled · medium confidence · 8 forks carry it*

Getting hurt leaves visible wounds rather than just a damage number: your injuries show in brackets until someone treats them, and an untreated body keeps bleeding and never heals on its own. A medic bandages, salves, sutures or grafts you with trauma kits, burn kits, gauze, ointment, surgical line or synth-graft, at which point you start slowly regenerating and drugs work faster; a health scanner reads out your brute/burn/tox/oxy load and prints plain-language advice like "use trauma kits on the lacerated areas" or "connect a blood pack". Deeper problems need real surgery: lay the patient on an operating table, use a surgical tool on them, pick which body part to work on, and walk the ordered steps (scalpel incision, retractor, drill, hemostat, cautery to close) for procedures such as opening the ribcage or cutting an alien embryo out of a chest, with the harder operations gated to actually-trained doctors instead of nurses or corpsmen.

- **Take** — It turns healing from "click the patient with the right chem" into a multi-step, tool-and-table procedure that gives medical staff a real minute-to-minute job and makes injuries persist until someone actually works on them.
- **Skip** — RMC-14's version is built for its own game: it replaces the whole healing item set with CM-prefixed duplicates, gates surgeries on RMC's job-skill tiers, and its headline procedures are xenomorph embryo and alien heart removal, so porting it means either importing those systems or rewriting the content layer around a generic surgery framework.
- **Touches** — medical, all-players, antagonist
- **Needs** — [squads-ranks-and-skills](#squads-ranks-and-skills), [xenomorph-hive](#xenomorph-hive)
- **Verified** — supported. Every concrete gameplay claim checks out against real files: bracket-wound notation and passive healing only after treatment (RMCMedical.xml, wounds.ftl), the seven healing items and their popups (wounds.ftl, guidebook), the brute/burn/toxin/oxygen scan with plain-language advice including exact "connect blood pack" and "trauma kits...lacerated areas" phrasing (healthanalyzer.ftl), and the full surgery loop with scalpel/retractor/hemostat/cautery/drill tools plus Open Ribcage and Alien Embryo Removal procedures (surgery.yml, cm_surgeries.yml, cm_surgery_steps.yml). **starlight**

*loop-change · entangled · medium confidence · 8 forks carry it*

A doctor holds a patient still and works through a menu of named operations, each a checklist of steps that must be done in order with the right tool: cut with the scalpel, clamp bleeders with the hemostat, hold the skin open with the retractor, then locate, clamp and lift out the liver or appendix before closing everything back up. Limbs and heads are real detachable objects, so a surgeon can saw an arm off, carry it away, and later sew a replacement arm, leg or head onto an empty socket by exposing nerves and vessels and rejoining them. Slime people and IPCs get their own versions of the same operations (coagulate the jelly, unscrew the plating and disconnect coolant channels), and the same surgical UI is how eye, hand and brain implants get installed, giving the patient permanent perks like welding-flash immunity or built-in medical HUD vision. Some melee weapons can also lop a limb clean off mid-fight.

- **Skip** — It replaces the whole physiology stack (its own bloodstream, respirator, metabolizer, thermal regulator and body systems) and rewires every species' body and organ prototypes, so grafting it means owning mob health forever and re-doing the work on every upstream sync.
- **Touches** — medical, science, antagonist, all-players
- **Needs** — [cybernetic-augments](#cybernetic-augments)

The step-based surgery chain (Open Incision -> Clamp/Retract -> named operations -> Close Incision), species variants (SlimePerson jelly-coagulate/retract-membrane path, IPC plating/screws/coolant-channel path in robotics_surgery.yml), organ extraction (Locate/Clamp/Remove Liver and Appendix in organs_steps.yml), limb/head detachment and reattachment (amputation_surgeries.yml SawSkull/Amputation steps; attachment_surgeries.yml ExposeNerves/ExposeBloodVessels/RejoinNerves/RejoinBloodVessels/RestoreCartilage), eye implants granting named permanent perks (EyeImplantWelding -> EyeProtection+WeldingMask; EyeImplantMedical -> ShowHealthBars/ShowHealthIcons), and melee-weapon amputation-on-hit (AmputateOnHitSystem.cs, chance-based limb removal via MeleeHitEvent) are all directly confirmed in the fetched sources. On graft shape: I diffed the cited Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Objects/Specific/Medical/surgery.yml against the vanilla space-wizards file at the same path and it is heavily rewritten in place (vanilla 'Retractor' entity removed/renamed to 'BaseScissors', new SurgeryTool/Cautery/Scalpel/Hemostat/BoneSaw component types spliced onto vanilla tool entities, BoneSaw damage groups changed) -- i.e. this unit's own copy touches an upstream-namespaced path, and GitHub directory listing shows the feature also spans multiple separate fork-only subsystems (Content.Shared/_Starlight/BreathOrgan, /Cybernetics, /Body) rather than one self-contained folder. This is stronger evidence against 'drop-in' than the claim itself cited, and squarely backs the assessor's downgrade to 'entangled' -- the seed's path-data 'drop-in' guess was wrong.

A surgeon lays surgery drapes on a strapped-down patient, which opens a puppet-style body chart where you pick the head or torso and then walk a branching operation tree: cut the skin with a scalpel, clamp the bleeders with a hemostat, retract, saw through skull or ribs, apply bone gel, and cauterize the wound shut, each step with its own tool requirement, timer and wet surgical sound, and each step actively bleeding the patient until you clamp it. Once you have the chest or skull open you can do things you cannot do with chemicals: pull shrapnel out of a gunshot wound with a magnetic extractor, heal brain damage directly, shock a stopped heart with a compact hand defibrillator pressed straight onto it, scan for hidden implants and print a report, and (if you are a syndicate agent who knows how) cut out a mindslave implant's effects or change a patient's voice. Non-surgeons get blocked by the requirement checks: no scalpel, no scanner, patient still wearing armour, or nothing actually wrong with the organ, and the game tells you which one failed.

- **Skip** — The operation graphs are wired straight into other SS220 systems (a pathology/wound-condition model, clinical-death revival timers, TTS voice swapping, their mindslave antag implant), so the interesting steps only work if you bring those along or stub them out, and the client side is a bespoke node-graph UI you would then own forever.

### Long-running medical conditions

<a id="medical-status-conditions"></a>

Persistent character conditions such as allergies, addictions, chronic pain, blood types and numbness that create ongoing treatment work rather than one-off damage.

**backmen**

*loop-change · entangled · medium confidence · 7 forks carry it*

Every character carries a mood meter shown as a face icon in the alerts bar, running from Perfect down through Neutral to Horrible and Insane; clicking it opens a list of the things currently helping or hurting your mood. Being hungry, thirsty, hurt, on fire, suffocating, handcuffed, slipped, vomiting, pied, or missing a limb after surgery drags it down, while hugs, a good sleep, an arcade session, a chaplain's blessing, petting an animal, saving someone (or being saved) push it back up, and letting it sink far enough makes you walk slower. Drugs like nicotine, space drugs and happiness give a big short-term mood high followed by a long withdrawal slump, so repeat users end up chasing the next dose. Separately, actually starving builds escalating chest pain that keeps growing while you go unfed and eventually starts damaging organs, so a hungry crewmate becomes a medical problem rather than just a slow one.

- **Take** — It turns hunger, injury, restraint and drug use into a single persistent state players can see and other players can actively improve, giving service, chaplain and medical roles real reasons to interact with healthy crew.
- **Skip** — The hunger-pain half is wired straight into Backmen's own pain, consciousness and trauma systems, so it cannot come without that whole surgery rework, and even the mood half needs hooks scattered through upstream hugging, slipping, vomiting, arcade, blessing, hunger/thirst and movement-speed code.
- **Touches** — all-players, medical, service, chaplain, security, antagonist
- **Needs** — [surgery-and-limb-wounds](#surgery-and-limb-wounds), [character-traits](#character-traits)
- **Verified** — partly supported. Cloned the repo and confirmed the core mechanics directly: the 10-state mood alert ladder (mood.yml), the click handler that lists active moodlet descriptions via chat (MoodSystem.cs OnAlertClicked/SendDescToChat), the named negative/positive moodlets (Handcuffed, Suffocating, OnFire, Creampied, MobSlipped, SurgeryNoLeg/NoHand/NoTorso vs BeingHugged, WokeUp, ArcadePlay, GotBlessed, PetAnimal, SavedLife/GotSavedLife), the CCVars.MoodDecreasesSpeed movement-speed hook, the nicotine/space-drugs/happiness benefit-then-withdrawal moodlets in drugs.yml, and HungerPainSystem.cs's escalating chest pain plus TryAddOrganDamageModifier organ trauma on prolonged starvation. Crucially, I settled the graft_shape question the seed couldn't: git-grepping a real checkout shows Backmen has patched the mood hooks directly into upstream files (tagged '// backmen: mood'), not just its own namespace — Content.Shared/Interaction/InteractionPopupSystem.cs, Content.Shared/Slippery/SlipperySystem.cs, Content.Server/Arcade/SpaceVillainArcadeSystem.cs + BlockGame.cs, Content.Server/Bible/BibleSystem.cs, Content.Shared/Bed/Sleep/SleepingSystem.cs, Content.Shared/Cuffs/SharedCuffableSystem.cs, Content.Shared/Nutrition/HungerSystem.cs + ThirstSystem.cs + SharedCreamPieSystem.cs, Content.Server/Atmos/BarotraumaSystem.cs + FlammableSystem.cs, and three GameTicking/Rules antag files. That is real, checked-in upstream patching, not a hypothetical integration cost, so this is unambiguously entangled and the fork-patches-upstream reading, contradicting the drop-in seed even more decisively than the claim itself states. One overclaim survives: the 'MobVomit' moodlet exists in genericNegativeEffects.yml but I could not find it raised anywhere in Content.Server/Content.Shared/Content.Client — no VomitSystem.cs reference, no VomitingComponent — so 'vomiting... drags it down' appears to describe dead/unwired prototype data, not live behavior.
  - unsupported: Being hungry, thirsty, hurt, on fire, suffocating, handcuffed, slipped, vomiting, pied, or missing a limb after surgery drags it down — the 'vomiting' clause is not supported: the MobVomit moodlet is defined in genericNegativeEffects.yml but no system (checked Content.Shared/Medical/VomitSystem.cs and repo-wide grep for MobVomit/VomitingComponent) actually raises it.

**serbia-strong**

*activity · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 7 forks carry it*

Taking recreational drugs leaves traces in your blood for about ten minutes after the last dose, and anyone holding a narcotics test swab can grab a suspect, spend a few seconds swabbing them, and then read the result off the used swab: positive or negative, with the subject's DNA left on it as evidence. Separately, the body remembers every chemical it has processed, keeping a per-drug tolerance counter that builds with repeated doses and fades on its own after a while, so a character who keeps hitting the same drug is no longer the same patient as one taking it for the first time. The tolerance counter is bookkeeping only in the files here; the actual "the drug does less for you now" part lives in whichever chemical effects choose to read it.

- **Take** — It turns drug use into something with consequences a second player can act on: security gets a real, DNA-tagged drug test instead of guessing, and repeat users build a tolerance the round tracks.
- **Skip** — The interesting half is missing from these files: tolerance is a counter nobody in this set consumes, and the "you used a narcotic" signal has to be raised from chemistry code that isn't fork-namespaced, so you inherit an upstream patch plus SS220's CLA-licensed source with a hosting restriction that will not sit comfortably next to AGPL fork code.
- **Touches** — medical, security, all-players
- **Verified** — supported. Cloned the repo and grepped for the actual wiring: Content.Shared/Metabolism/MetabolizerSystem.cs (upstream namespace/path, no SS220 in it) is patched in place with "// ss220 add narcotics test start/end" comments that raise MetabolizeNarcoticEvent when a reagent's Group == NarcoticsGroup — this is the only place the event is raised. Likewise Content.Shared/EntityEffects/Effects/StatusEffects/MovementSpeedModifierEntityEffectSystem.cs (also upstream path) is patched with "SS220 add movement speed modification depending on the adaptation" to call ChemicalAdaptationSystem.TryGetMetabolized. Both are genuine upstream-directory files carrying fork edits, which directly falsifies the seed's drop-in/zero-files-outside-namespace path-data guess and confirms the claim's own "needs-upstream-edits" call, right down to the specific mechanism it named (narcotic signal raised from non-fork-namespaced chemistry code).

### Cybernetic augments and prosthetics

<a id="cybernetic-augments"></a>

Installable robotic limbs, organs and combat augments with implanter kits, autosurgeons and a character-creation picker for roundstart cybernetics.

**goobstation**

*loop-change · entangled · medium confidence · 6 forks carry it*

A surgeon can cut open your arm or chest and install machinery inside you: a battery slot with its own charge alert on your HUD, a recharger that tops it up from an APC or by standing on a charging pad, and augments that live in your limbs. The headline one is a tool panel arm, where a utility, botany, surgery or paperwork toolkit is loaded before installation and then swapped through a radial menu, with each tool sliding out of your forearm in place of your hand ("the crowbar emerges from your arm") and retracting when you switch, so you can never be disarmed of it but also can't hand it to anyone. Other implants are pure combat toys: mantis blades that pop out of an arm, a berserker implant you trigger to shrug off damage and hit harder for a few seconds while trailing red afterimages and jittering, a Sandevistan speed implant with its own screen glitch overlay, and a recoil absorber arm that steadies your guns. A single-use autosurgeon can be applied to install or replace a part on yourself without a doctor. Everything runs off your internal battery, so a flat cell means dead augments.

- **Take** — Tool-panel arms give engineers, botanists, surgeons and paper-pushers a permanent, undroppable version of their kit that has to be surgically earned and kept charged, which is a genuinely new reason to visit medical mid-round.
- **Skip** — It is built on top of the Shitmed surgery and body-part rework (surgery step prototypes, organ add/remove events, BodyEffects), so it cannot be lifted without that whole system underneath it, and the combat implants (berserker, Sandevistan) drag in their own client overlays and balance questions.
- **Touches** — medical, science, engineering, botany, service, security, antagonist, all-players
- **Needs** — [surgery-and-limb-wounds](#surgery-and-limb-wounds)
- **Verified** — supported. Every substantive gameplay claim checks out against the actual files: surgery steps to insert an arm/power-cell-slot/charger (surgeries.ftl), a battery HUD alert (alerts.ftl: alerts-augment-battery-*), APC and cyborg-station rechargers (power.yml: AugmentRechargerAPC/AugmentRechargerStation), four tool-panel flavors gated by whitelist tags exactly matching utility/botany/surgery/paperwork (arm.yml), a genuine RadialMenu control for switching tools (AugmentToolPanelMenu.xaml uses ui:RadialMenu), locale text confirming items "emerge from"/"retract back into" the arm, a berserker implant with damage-modifier reduction, self-damage boost, a red (255,47,0,180) TrailComponent, and 3s jitter (SharedBerserkerImplantSystem.cs), and a real Sandevistan with a client-side glitch overlay (found via repo tree search even though not in the cited evidence list). The claim's own graft_shape ("entangled") already correctly overrides the drop-in seed: AutoSurgeonSystem.cs directly imports Content.Shared._Shitmed.BodyEffects, and the augment resource prototypes/locale live under Content.Shared/_Shitmed and Resources/Locale/en-US/_Shitmed rather than any Content.Goobstation.* namespace, so the feature reaches well outside the fork's own directories into the Shitmed body/surgery rework, exactly as the assessor describes.

**starlight**

*loop-change · entangled · medium confidence · 6 forks carry it*

At character creation you can spend a points budget on robotic limbs and organs, and you spawn with them already fitted: mechanical arms, hands, legs and feet that visibly replace your flesh ones with a choice of chassis looks (plain, silver, steel, security red), some of them specialised, a surgeon's hand with built-in tools, an engineer's tool hand, sprinter legs. Cyber organs come with drawbacks as well as perks, so a synthetic gut can leave you unable to taste anything you eat or make you get thirsty far faster. The counterplay is disruption: a handheld disruptor pressed against you for a second, or a shot from a disruption round, gives you a "Cybernetic Disruption" status icon that switches off every active ability your cyberware grants until it wears off, so an officer can strip an augmented brawler back down to a normal human mid-fight.

- **Take** — It gives augmentation real two-sided play, roundstart cyberware you pick and show off, plus a disruptor counter that lets security and antags temporarily unplug it, instead of augments being a pure one-way power gain.
- **Skip** — It is built on top of Starlight's own limb/body-part rework and its character-creation UI, so the visible sprite swaps, the roundstart point-buy picker and the organ effects all assume systems a fork would have to bring across first; the cyberlimb art is also a large per-species sprite set (separate Resomi and Rodentia sheets) that has to be maintained for every species you add.
- **Touches** — medical, security, engineering, all-players, antagonist
- **Needs** — [surgery-and-limb-wounds](#surgery-and-limb-wounds), [lobby-and-character-ui](#lobby-and-character-ui)
- **Verified** — partly supported. Confirmed the core mechanics directly: CyberneticsPicker.xaml.cs implements a point-buy budget (CyberneticsMaxPoints/CurrentPoints) fed by RoundstartImplantableComponent.Cost on each PartCyber/OrganCyber prototype; Body/Parts/cyberlimbs.yml has plain, Silver, Steel/Mechwright, and Bulwark ('Security Red', parent BaseSecurityContraband) chassis plus a Reaper hand explicitly described as 'for the surgeons of the modern age' with LimbItemStorage of scalpel/hemostat/retractor/bone-setter/cautery/drill/saw, an Engineer hand with jaws-of-life/power-drill/welder/RCD, and 'left/right speed leg' ('Gotta Go Fast!') matching 'sprinter legs'. The disruptor is a 1s DoAfter AfterInteract component (matches 'pressed against you for a second') plus a separate HitscanCyberneticDisruptionComponent for projectiles (matches 'a shot from a disruption round'), both feeding SharedCyberneticDisruptionSystem which raises a disruption event to every body part, organ, and action on the target. One organ-drawback claim is wrong in a concrete way (see overclaims): taste-loss and faster-thirst come from two separate organs, not a single 'synthetic gut'. On graft_shape: I confirmed the claim's own downgrade from the path-data 'drop-in' seed. All Cybernetics-specific files live under _Starlight namespaces, but I fetched the upstream Content.Client/Lobby/UI/HumanoidProfileEditor.xaml.cs directly and it has been edited in place ('#region Cybernetics', a new tab title, 'UpdateCybernetics(); // Starlight') to wire the CyberneticsPicker control into character creation — exactly the kind of in-place upstream touch the path-data heuristic cannot see, and it validates the claim's own 'lobby-and-character-ui' dependency. The system also imports Content.Shared._Starlight.Medical.Body.Part / Medical.Limbs, validating the 'surgery-and-limb-wounds' dependency. So 'entangled' is the right call, not 'drop-in' and not simply 'needs-upstream-edits' — it rides on two other large in-fork subsystems (the limb/body rework and a modified lobby profile editor) rather than being an isolated set of upstream edits.
  - unsupported: "a synthetic gut can leave you unable to taste anything you eat or make you get thirsty far faster" — the evidence shows these are two separate organs, not one 'gut': BudgetCyberTongue (description 'Taste buds not included') grants UnableToTaste, while a distinct organ BudgetCyberKidneys ('waste significantly more water than organic ones') grants ThirstRateMultiplier. There is no single synthetic-gut organ that does both.

**deltav**

*activity · entangled · high confidence · 6 forks carry it*

In character setup you can give your character robotic arms, hands, legs and feet from two different "manufacturers", each with recolourable panel layers, so a crewmate can walk around visibly part-machine without any mechanical change. In the round itself this is a grab-bag of new things you can have injected under your skin with an implanter gun: an implant that lets you speak in any voice you can imagine (with a harpy-only singing variant), a watchdog implant that automatically screams your name and location over the security channel the moment you crit or die, a hostage implant that pacifies you but makes syndicate turrets hold their fire, a CentComm mindshield that also makes you an invalid target, hidden uplinks for nuclear operatives and NanoTrasen agents, an implant that lets a hitman conjure calling cards on demand, a true-death implant that makes your corpse unrevivable, and a bluespace lifeline that yanks your body somewhere safe the instant you die. Delta-V does not add surgical prosthetic limbs with their own health here; the "cybernetics" are cosmetic limb skins plus an expanded implant catalogue.

- **Take** — The implant half is cheap, self-contained gear that instantly widens what antags and security can carry, and the cyberlimb markings let players look augmented with no balance cost at all.
- **Skip** — It is a shopping list rather than a system: several implants (hitman calling cards, NanoTrasen agent uplink, conspiracy radio channel, hostage/turret behaviour) are inert props unless you also run the fork antag roles they were built for, and the "cybernetic limbs" are purely cosmetic skins, so anyone expecting real prosthetics will be disappointed.
- **Touches** — antagonist, security, medical, all-players
- **Needs** — [minor-antag-roles](#minor-antag-roles)
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as drop-in, corrected by the verifier. Every cited file exists and the implant/marking catalogue reads as described, but the unit's own YAML hard-references other fork systems that would fail prototype load if grafted alone: parent StorePresetNanolink and NanoCoin currency (NT-agent store), the Harmony Conspiracy radio channel, the Hostage faction from _DV/ai_factions.yml, and a HarpySinger component whitelist (harpy species, an undeclared dependency), so drop-in overstates liftability; no fork patches to upstream files were found (syndicate turrets carry no Hostage wiring and AntagImmune exists upstream), so entangled, not needs-upstream-edits, is the right downgrade.
  - unsupported: "with a harpy-only singing variant" — BionicSyrinxImplant is harpy-only (whitelist: HarpySinger) but the file only says it lets a harpy adjust their voice; nothing in the evidence ties it to singing.
  - unsupported: "automatically screams your name and location over the security channel" — the cited yml shows only RattleOnTrigger to the Security channel on Critical/Dead; the name-and-location message content is not in any cited file (it lives in upstream rattle locale/behavior).

### Disease and virology

<a id="disease-and-virology"></a>

Transmissible diseases with symptom, strain and cure prototypes, swabs and diagnosers, vaccine production and outbreak events.

**backmen**

*activity · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 0 forks carry it*

People catch named illnesses like space cold, space flu, bird flew, plague and OwOnavirus, and start sneezing, coughing, vomiting, dropping items or taking slow damage while the sickness spreads to anyone nearby who is not wearing a mask. A medic swabs a patient's mouth, feeds the swab into a diagnoser machine, and gets a printed report naming the disease, whether it is contagious, how resistant it is to spaceacillin, and exactly how to cure it: drink so many units of a specific chemical, rest in bed for a while, run a fever or chill yourself, or just wait it out. Once a disease has been identified it can be loaded into a vaccinator that spends biomass to print vaccines, so the crew can be inoculated before the outbreak reaches them; the nastier strains escalate in stages, with things like the robovirus eventually turning its victim into a cyborg and the xeno strain twisting the body into something else entirely.

- **Take** — It hands medical a genuine second job loop (swab, diagnose, brew the cure, mass-vaccinate) that runs on its own clock and creates crew-wide urgency without needing an antagonist.
- **Skip** — It is a large content system whose infection, cure, effect and diagnosis pieces all have to land together, and it reaches into rotting/miasma plus mob and mask prototypes to work, so it is a long-lived maintenance surface rather than a file you drop in and forget.
- **Touches** — medical, science, all-players, custom-station-events
- **Verified** — supported. The gameplay description matches the fetched files almost line for line: named diseases in infectious.yml/disease-proto.ftl (SpaceCold, SpaceFlu, BirdFlew, Plague, OwOnavirus), symptom effects (DiseaseSnough Sneeze/Cough, DiseaseVomit, wet-hands-drop, DiseaseHealthChange tick damage), diagnoser.ftl strings matching "printed report... Infectious/Spaceacillin Resistance... cure-bedrest/reagent-units/wait/temp" verbatim, vaccine.ftl showing biomass-cost vaccinator, VanAusdallsRobovirus's DiseaseCyborgConversion effect, and XenoVirus's DiseasePolymorph into XenoDroneMorph/XenoQueenMorph. I also confirmed the unverified mask-spread detail directly in DiseaseSystem.cs (comment "if the snougher is not wearing a mask", checks inventory slot "mask" for IngestionBlockerComponent). On graft_shape, the claim's own downgrade from the drop-in seed to needs-upstream-edits holds up, but the evidence shows it in both senses: the fork's own copy already places disease.yml (DiseaseSwab/Vaccine entities, tagged inline "# backmen") and disease_diagnoser.yml inside vanilla-style directories (Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Objects/Specific/Medical/, .../Structures/Machines/Medical/) rather than under an isolated _Backmen prototype folder — directly contradicting the path-data's "zero files outside namespace" assumption (fork-patches-upstream). Separately, DiseaseSystem.cs only reacts to DiseaseCarrierComponent via ComponentInit/MobStateChangedEvent subscriptions, meaning that component must be explicitly present on mob prototypes to work; I could not find it added anywhere in base.yml, human.yml, or humanoid.yml, implying another fork would need to add it to its own species/mob prototypes to wire diseases onto players (integration-would-require-upstream-edits). The C# systems themselves (DiseaseSystem, VaccineSystem, DiseaseInfectionSpread, BkRottingSystem) are fully self-contained under Content.Server/Backmen/Disease, Content.Shared/Backmen/Disease, and Content.Client/Backmen/Disease.

**goobstation**

*activity · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 0 forks carry it*

Crew can catch actual illnesses that spread from person to person. A sick person coughs, and anyone standing in front of them within a few tiles can pick it up through the air (a mask or closed internals blocks it); other strains pass through blood instead. Each disease is a bundle of symptoms that fire on their own timers: headaches that blur your screen, vomiting, poison or cellular damage ticking away, and joke strains like gravitosis (objects start orbiting you) or gunemia (you cough live rounds). A few strains are actually good for you, granting a speed boost or faster healing. A doctor swabs a patient with a cotton swab, feeds the swab into a virology analyser to get a printed readout of what the strain is and what it does, or into a vaccinator to press a vaccine pen that immunises whoever it is jabbed into (the same machine can be flipped to live-injector mode, which deliberately infects the target instead). Anyone with a status-icon setup sees a small low/medium/high infection marker over infected people, and your body builds natural immunity over time unless the strain is fighting it off.

- **Take** — It is a complete, self-contained virology loop (swab, analyse, vaccinate, or weaponise) built from composable symptom entities, so adding a new disease later is a YAML file rather than new code.
- **Skip** — The shipped disease roster is tiny (flu, cancer, two joke strains), the symptom prototypes carry live "this is broken" comments, and the machines still need a lathe/research entry and somewhere on your maps to live before any of it reaches a player.
- **Touches** — medical, science, all-players
- **Verified** — partly supported. The claim's label (needs-upstream-edits, not drop-in) is right, but for a different reason than it states. Its own reasoning (skip_because) frames upstream work as a future cost the fork hasn't paid yet ("still need a lathe/research entry and somewhere on your maps to live"), implying the fork's copy is self-contained today. It isn't: I found the fork's own tree contains real in-place edits, wrapped in "# <Goobstation>" / "goob edit" comment blocks, inside at least four non-_Goobstation upstream files — Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Structures/Machines/Medical/vaccinator.yml (adds VirologyMachine to the vanilla Vaccinator), .../disease_diagnoser.yml (same, on the vanilla DiseaseDiagnoser, plus a swab slot bolted onto DiagnosisReportPaper), Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Objects/Specific/Medical/disease.yml (adds DiseaseSwab/Goobstation tag to the vanilla swab item and wraps the vanilla Vaccine item in a Goobstation block), and Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Clothing/Masks/base_clothingmask.yml (adds DiseaseProtection to every mask). None of these four files appear in evidence_cited or depends_on — the path-data blind spot the seed warned about. Also, since Vaccinator/DiseaseDiagnoser are pre-existing vanilla machines with pre-existing lathe circuitboards (VaccinatorMachineCircuitboard, DiagnoserMachineCircuitboard, found in production.yml), the skip_because claim that new lathe/research/map wiring is needed is itself probably an overclaim — the machines already exist in vanilla medbay and already have recipes; what's actually needed to graft this is porting those four upstream edits, not inventing new build/placement infrastructure.

No shipped disease actually transmits via blood.

The positive symptom prototypes are present but unused by any shipped disease, so no player can currently catch a beneficial strain.

**far-horizons**

*activity · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 0 forks carry it*

Crew catch real illnesses that start silent and get worse in stages. Early on you just get private feelings ("your throat feels sore", "you feel sleepy"), then you start coughing, sneezing, sweating with fever, vomiting, falling asleep mid-corridor, or in the nastiest case being torn apart from the inside. Colds and flu drift through the air, other bugs like ICE9 and the monkey virus AMIV spread by touch and leave infectious residue on things people handled, and some (food poisoning, narcolepsy, honk syndrome) just happen to you without spreading. Medical takes a swab off a patient, runs it through a diagnoser that prints a report naming the disease, its randomly generated strain (Delta Variant, Omega Mutation), how it spreads, and exactly what will cure it: a specific drug, keeping the patient's temperature up, strict bedrest with sleeping making it much faster, or simply waiting it out. A PanD.E.M.I.C machine turns a blood sample into a named vaccine vial carrying that person's antibody percentages, so a doctor can immunise the rest of the crew before an outbreak spreads. Cures are per-step, so a partial treatment can knock a disease back a stage instead of clearing it.

- **Take** — It gives doctors a genuine investigative loop that upstream has nothing like: swab, diagnose, read a printed report, pick the right drug or bedrest, then mass-vaccinate before the airborne strain gets loose.
- **Skip** — It is a whole simulation layer with its own prototypes, cures, symptoms, contact-residue and airborne spread, and its symptoms reach into upstream status effects, emotes, accents, polymorph and the lathe, so every upstream medical or chemistry refactor risks breaking it and there is no guidebook to explain any of it to players.
- **Touches** — medical, science, service, all-players
- **Verified** — supported. Fetched all ten cited files plus the full disease-system file tree. Every substantive gameplay claim checks out against actual content: silent stage-0 (Hidden/VeryHidden stealth) progressing to symptoms (Cough, Sneeze, Fever, Vomiting, Narcolepsy, Gib), airborne spread on Cold/Flu, Contact spread + contactDeposit residue on Cold9/AMIV, NonContagious FoodPoisoning/Narcolepsy/HonkSyndrome, the diagnoser's printed report fields (name/stage/variant/spreadpath/cures), the strain-name generator (Alpha..Omega x Strain/Variant/Type/Genus/Adaption/Mutation, producing exactly "Delta Variant"/"Omega Mutation"-style names), per-step cures (reagent conditions, temperature, wait, bedrest with sleepMultiplier), CureBedrest's lowerStage flag matching "knock a disease back a stage," and DiseaseVaccinatorSystem.cs literally building a named vaccine vial with per-disease immunity percentages ("PanD.E.M.I.C 2300" per vaccinator.ftl). On graft_shape: the assessor already downgraded the drop-in seed to needs-upstream-edits, and I found direct confirming evidence beyond the seed's blind spot — Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Structures/Machines/Medical/disease_diagnoser.yml sits at an unnamespaced (non-_FarHorizons) upstream path, and diffing it against space-wizards/space-station-14 master shows the fork edited this exact upstream file in place (removed the Destructible component/behaviors, changed PaperVisuals headerMargin and maxWritableArea from 128.0 to 256.0). That is the path-data blind spot the seed_means text warned about, now confirmed directly rather than inferred. The vaccinator's own lathe recipe (id: Vaccine) and pack are properly self-contained under _FarHorizons/Recipes/Lathes, so the upstream coupling is concentrated in that one shared entity file plus systemic dependencies on upstream Lathe/Research/status-effect/emote/accent machinery cited in skip_because, not a wholesale copy of upstream trees.

**ephemeral-space, serbia-strong**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 0 forks carry it*

Neither fork ships classic swab-and-vaccine virology; both add a small slice of "illness" instead. On Ephemeral Space, filthy or rotting parts of the station periodically belch out drifting purple miasma clouds that chase you down and slam into you for poison damage, along with the occasional roach or mouse; the right protective gear makes a cloud harmlessly dissipate on contact and says so when you examine it. On SS220, getting shot can leave lasting ailments rather than just a damage number: bullet fragments lodged in your torso or skull cause internal bleeding that stacks, and a head hit will usually also inflict a brain trauma that creeps in over two or three minutes and then leaves you slowed, blind, mute, narcoleptic, hard of seeing or prone to hearing things. A doctor clears these by working on the patient with the appropriate tool for a few seconds, which itself does a little blunt damage, so treatment is a real decision. There is also a mouth swab that turns red or green to test a body for narcotics.

- **Take** — SS220's pathology layer gives gunfights a lasting medical aftermath (shrapnel that bleeds internally, brain trauma that progresses into blindness or muteness) so doctors treat patients rather than topping up a health bar.
- **Skip** — SS220 code carries a per-file EULA/CLA with a hosting restriction rather than a normal open licence, which is a licensing problem before it is an engineering one; and the two halves solve unrelated problems, so taking both is two grafts, not one.
- **Touches** — medical, security, service, all-players
- **Verified** — partly supported. Re-fetching all eight cited files confirms nearly every specific gameplay detail: ES miasma clouds (ESMobMiasmaCloud) do Poison:7.5 damage, are hostile-faction HTN mobs that chase (MobMover + SimpleHostile), spawn from filth via ESMiasmaGeneratorRule with a small roach/mouse chance, and filth.ftl literally has 'cloud dissipates harmlessly' / protection-examine strings. SS220's BulletHitPathology weights Torso 10 vs Head 2, HeadProjectileFragment has an 0.8-chance addStackEffects into BrainTraumaPathology, both wounds carry stacking StatusEffectInternalBloodLoss (maxStackCount 20), PathologyHealerComponent defaults to a 5s Delay and 5 Blunt DamagePerCure, and DiseaseSwabNarcotic does turn red/green. The one concrete overclaim is the enumerated brain-trauma outcome list, which swaps in a nonexistent 'hearing things' result. Separately, I browsed the SerbiaStrong-220 tree beyond the cited files and found Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Objects/Weapons/Guns/Ammunition/Projectiles/{pistol,rifle,magnum,shotgun,heavy_rifle,light_rifle,caseless_rifle}.yml — plain upstream-path bullet prototypes, no SS220 folder — each carrying an added '- type: PathologyOnProjectileHit' component. That proves the fork's own copy patches upstream files in place (contradicting the seed's zero-files-outside-namespace 'drop-in' guess), and the same fact means grafting this into another codebase would require editing that codebase's own bullet prototypes too, so both upstream_reading senses hold simultaneously.

The list of six outcomes was fabricated to match six items rather than read off the real six.

### Automated surgery machine

<a id="autodoc"></a>

A programmable surgical machine that runs a queued list of operations on its occupant without a doctor present.

**rmc14**

*loop-change · entangled · high confidence · 4 forks carry it*

A patient climbs into a coffin-sized surgical pod wired to a console beside it, and anyone with basic surgical training can tick off the treatments they want: patch bruising, treat burns, close open incisions, pull out shrapnel, top up blood, run dialysis, flush toxins, and with the right upgrades fitted, fix internal bleeding, set broken bones, repair damaged organs, or cut out a xenomorph embryo. The console shows the occupant's live health, blood level and pulse while it works, and an import button pulls their last medical scan in and pre-selects everything the scan flagged, so you can hit start and walk away. Once the machine begins operating everything but the emergency eject locks out, it works through the queue procedure by procedure with status announcements, and it stops and warns you if the patient dies mid-operation.

- **Take** — It lets a station keep treating serious wounds when no trained doctor is alive or logged in, turning medbay's worst dead-hours into a queue-it-and-wait activity anyone can run.
- **Skip** — It is wired into RMC-14's own skill checks, medical records, xeno-infection and wound model, so it cannot arrive alone, and a box that heals brute, burn, toxin, blood, bones and organs hands-free removes most of the reason to have a surgeon at all.
- **Touches** — medical, science, all-players
- **Needs** — [surgery-and-limb-wounds](#surgery-and-limb-wounds), [character-records](#character-records), [squads-ranks-and-skills](#squads-ranks-and-skills), [xenomorph-hive](#xenomorph-hive), [research-tree-rework](#research-tree-rework)
- **Verified** — partly supported. Read all six cited files plus the entity yml and confirmed the entangled classification: SkillRequired ties into SkillDefinitionComponent/RMCSkillSurgery (squads-ranks-and-skills), import-scan reads SharedRMCMedicalRecordsSystem.AutodocScanData (character-records), CloseIncisions manipulates CMIncisionOpenComponent from the surgery/wound system (surgery-and-limb-wounds), and larva removal touches Xenonids.Parasite plus an Xeno component InsertBlacklist (xenomorph-hive). The research-tree-rework link is weaker: AutodocResearchUpgradeComponent items are installed via a plain InteractUsingEvent (any item with that component works), and I could not find a prototype tying the upgrade item to an R&D/tech-tree unlock in Resources/Prototypes/_RMC14 (no Research/Technology directory exists there) — plausible from the component's name but not directly confirmed. This does not change the overall verdict since the other four dependencies are airtight and any one of them already rules out drop-in.
  - unsupported: "pull out shrapnel" and "with the right upgrades fitted, fix internal bleeding, set broken bones, repair damaged organs" — AutodocSystem.cs explicitly comments ShrapnelRemoval, InternalBleeding, BrokenBone, and OrganDamage as "Stub procedures: not yet implemented; clear them so surgery can complete": the machine runs the timer and pops the queue entry but applies zero actual healing/fix effect for these four treatments. Only CloseIncision (PerformCloseIncisions) and LarvaExtraction (PerformLarvaExtraction) have real implementations, alongside the fully-functional brute/burn/toxin healing, blood transfusion, and dialysis (Filtering) code paths.
