### Genetics and DNA mutations

<a id="genetics-and-dna-mutations"></a>

The geneticist's loop: a DNA scanner and DNA modifier console that read and rewrite a subject's genome, mutation prototypes that grant powers or defects, sequence injectors and analyzers that carry a saved genome between subjects, and genetic disease with its own overlays and progression. Upstream ships DNA only as forensic evidence (DnaComponent, the DNA scrambler gadget); anything that lets a player read, edit or express a genome is fork content and belongs here rather than in `device-and-machine-additions`.

**funky**

*activity · drop-in · medium confidence · 2 forks carry it*

As written in its text, this is the classic geneticist loop: a subject lies in the medical scanner, a linked geneticists console shows their total damage, genetic damage and "genetic instability", and lets the operator scramble their DNA or work a genome sequencer tab where base and added sequences are read block by block, cleared, or gambled on with a cooldown-limited JOKER button. Discovered mutations are researched, saved into console storage, and printed as red "mutator" or green "activator" injectors that another player can jab into someone ("You feel different..."), while pushing instability too far walks a victim through escalating warnings ("You feel your bones start to bend and crack...", "A searing pain rips through your body!"). A handheld genetic analyzer with a power cell scans a body for structural enzymes and prints a numbered paper report. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: on Funky's master branch only the locale strings and two entity prototypes exist. The console prototype declares nothing but a wires UI, a device-link port and a research client, and a full-tree scan turned up no genetics C# system, no mutation prototypes, no injector entities and no geneticist job prototype. What ships today is a buildable console shell and a working-looking handheld analyzer, not the loop the text describes.

- **Take** — The text and prototypes sketch a complete, familiar SS13-style genetics station: sequencer puzzle, research gate, printable activator/mutator injectors and an instability punishment clock, which is a self-contained new job loop rather than a change to any existing one.
- **Skip** — There is nothing here to graft yet: the fork's master tree contains only locale files and two entity prototypes, with no genetics system code, no mutation definitions and no geneticist job, so taking these files gives you a console that opens a wires panel and a lot of unused strings.
- **Touches** — medical, science, command
- **Needs** — [device-and-machine-additions](#device-and-machine-additions), [extra-job-roster](#extra-job-roster)
- **Verified** — supported; assessed as entangled, corrected by the verifier. The gameplay prose is unusually well-grounded: every specific detail I checked (total/genetic damage + instability readouts, Scramble DNA with cooldown, sequencer's base/added sequence tabs, Clear, cooldown-limited JOKER, save-to-storage, print activator/mutator with red/green color codes, "You feel different...", the exact escalating instability warning strings, a handheld analyzer that reads "Structural Enzymes (SE)" and prints a numbered "Genetic Analysis Report #{number}") is verbatim in the four cited .ftl files. The claim's own caveat is also independently correct: dna_scanner.yml gives the console only WiresBoundUserInterface + DeviceLinkSource + ResearchClient/ResearchPointSource (vanilla components, no genetics BUI), and a full-tree search (58,582 paths) turns up no genetics C# system, no DNA-mutation prototype (the only "Mutation" C# is Botany's unrelated plant MutationSystem), no injector entity prototype, and zero Geneticist job .yml anywhere in the repo — so the loop described genuinely does not exist yet, just as the claim says. Where I disagree is the graft_shape downgrade: the two cited prototypes only reference vanilla SS14 components (Computer, DeviceLinkSource, ResearchClient, PowerCellDraw, ItemSlots, Paper) that any codebase already has, not fork-specific systems — I could not find that "device-and-machine-additions" contributes anything these files actually use, and "extra-job-roster" does not contain a Geneticist job either (there is no such job anywhere in the tree), so the depends_on list looks like forward-looking design notes rather than a demonstrated current entanglement. By the file evidence, this unit is still namespace-self-contained (drop-in shaped); the real problem is that it is an empty shell, not that it is entangled with other fork systems.

### Coroner and autopsy

<a id="coroner-autopsy"></a>

A morgue role with an autopsy table and tools for examining corpses to recover cause of death.

**ephemeral-space**

*activity · entangled · high confidence · 0 forks carry it*

A trained coroner drags a corpse onto an autopsy table, buckles it down, and spends about half a minute working on it with an autopsy tool. Paper scribbling plays, "Autopsy completed!" pops up, and a printed report drops into their hand listing the deceased's name, age, sex, eye colour, hair colour, and the exact round time they died. The last line of the report names a secret identity, which is the real payoff: it feeds the station's investigation game by telling you who the body actually was. If the game does not know a real identity for that body, the report prints a plausible-looking one at random, so a coroner can be confidently wrong. Anyone without the training gets "Don't know how!", living patients get "Not dead!", and a body not strapped to the table gets "Not on operating table!".

- **Take** — It turns the morgue from a body-storage room into an investigation station: a corpse becomes a physical printed clue naming who the victim really was, which gives security and medical a reason to talk to each other mid-round.
- **Skip** — The report's headline line is generated by the fork's secret-identity and clues systems, and falls back to a randomly picked identity when those systems have nothing on the body, so without grafting that investigation layer too you get an autopsy that prints a fabricated answer. The unit also ships no prototypes at all, so the autopsy table, the tool, and the coroner job itself would have to be authored from scratch.
- **Touches** — medical, security, antagonist
- **Needs** — [secret-identities](#secret-identities)
- **Verified** — partly supported. I fetched all 7 cited files plus the full repo tree and several un-cited prototype files. The core loop, popups, timings, and fallback-random secret identity all check out verbatim against ESSharedCoronerSystem.cs / ESCoronerSystem.cs / coroner.ftl. The entangled call is genuinely correct: ESCoronerSystem.cs imports and calls Content.Server._ES.SecretIdentity (ESSecretIdentitySystem, ESCluesSystem) and Content.Shared._ES.SecretIdentity (ESSecretIdentityPrototype, confirmed live at that path, doc-commented "Essentially a mini antag thing"), a real cross-directory dependency outside Coroner/. But the claim's "ships no prototypes at all... would have to be authored from scratch" is false: Resources/Prototypes/_ES/Roles/Jobs/Medical/coroner.yml defines the full ESCoroner job plus gear plus chameleon outfit; Resources/Prototypes/_ES/Entities/Structures/Machines/operating_table.yml adds type: ESAutopsyTable directly onto the existing OperatingTable entity; Resources/Prototypes/_ES/Entities/Objects/Tools/scalpel.yml defines ESScalpelAutopsy with type: ESAutopsyTool. Matching sprites (cscalpel.rsi, optable.rsi, coroner.rsi hat/jumpsuit) all exist too. So the job, table, and tool are all shipped, not missing - the entanglement is real (SecretIdentity coupling) but the reasoning overstates it by inventing a second, false blocker about missing prototypes.

## Chemistry

### Reagent and reaction expansion

<a id="reagent-and-reaction-expansion"></a>

Adds reagents, reactions, flavour profiles and glassware on top of the base chemistry set, covering medicines, toxins, narcotics and novelty chemicals.

**rmc14**

*loop-change · entangled · medium confidence · 13 forks carry it*

Replaces the standard medicine shelf with a Colonial-Marines-style drug set: bicaridine for brute, kelotane and dermaline for burns, dexalin and dexalin plus for suffocation, dylovene for toxins, tricordrazine as the weak all-rounder, plus specialty picks like inaprovaline, epinephrine, leporazine and cryoxadone. Every one of them has an overdose and a critical-overdose line, so a medic who doubles up on a screaming patient starts doing brute damage instead of healing, and dosing becomes a judgement call rather than "empty the syringe". Alongside the medicines it adds recreational narcotics that make you laugh, see rainbows, jitter and eventually black out, and a bench of incendiary ordnance chemistry (sticky napalm, high-combustion napalm, B-gel, CLF3, sulphuric acid) that a technician mixes into flamethrower and incinerator fuel of varying nastiness. An in-game guidebook lists every reagent by group so players can look up exactly what a chemical does before drinking it.

- **Take** — The overdose / critical-overdose tiering turns healing into a dosing decision with a real downside, which gives medics an actual skill ceiling instead of a syringe-emptying reflex, and it comes with player-readable guidebook entries generated from the effects themselves.
- **Skip** — It is a replacement set, not an addition — the CM-named drugs cover the same ground as upstream's medicines, so you either displace the existing chemistry (rewiring every medkit, vendor, dispenser and chem recipe that references the old reagents) or ship two parallel medicine sets that confuse everyone; the incendiary half is also only meaningful if your fork already has flamethrowers and spreading fire to burn things with.
- **Touches** — medical, science, cargo, security, all-players
- **Needs** — [spreading-fire-system](#spreading-fire-system)
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. All cited evidence files do live entirely under _RMC14 namespace directories (Resources/Prototypes/_RMC14/Reagents/, Resources/ServerInfo/Guidebook/_RMC14/, Content.Shared/_RMC14/Chemistry/), and the new reagents merely inherit vanilla reagent IDs (Bicaridine, Dexalin, etc.) via YAML `parent:` — so it does not literally patch upstream files, contradicting a plain 'fork-patches-upstream' reading. But reading the actual effect classes shows the reagent system is built on RMC14's own parallel damage/health/status/zombie infrastructure (SharedRMCDamageableSystem, SharedRMCBloodstreamSystem, a bespoke 'Genetic' damage group, RMCUnconsciousComponent, CureZombieInfection) rather than vanilla SS14 mechanics, so a graft needs to bring that whole substrate along, not just point vendors/medkits at new reagent IDs as the claim's 'skip_because' implies. That is a deeper coupling than 'needs-upstream-edits' captures.
  - unsupported: "Every one of them has an overdose and a critical-overdose line" — false per the cited medicine.yml itself: CMCryoxadone, CMClonexadone, RMCMethylphenidate, RMCCitalopram, and RMCAntiZed have no overdose/criticalOverdose fields at all.
  - unsupported: "a medic who doubles up on a screaming patient starts doing brute damage instead of healing" — verified against RMCChemicalEffect.cs (base TickOverdose/TickCriticalOverdose are no-op virtuals) plus Antitoxic.cs and Neogenetic.cs: overdose consequences vary per effect type. Bicaridine's Neogenetic effect deals BURN damage on overdose (not brute); Dylovene's Antitoxic overdose tier is a literal commented-out TODO no-op; only the Biocidic effect (used by Arithrazine/RussianRed specifically) deals brute damage. There is no universal 'brute damage instead of healing' consequence.
  - unsupported: depends_on lists only 'spreading-fire-system', but the reagent effect implementations (Antitoxic.cs, Neogenetic.cs, RMCAntiZed's CureZombieInfection) show real dependencies on RMC14-only shared systems: SharedRMCDamageableSystem.DistributeHealingCached, SharedRMCBloodstreamSystem, a custom 'Genetic' damage group, RMCUnconsciousComponent, and RMC14's own zombie-infection cure mechanic — none of which are vanilla SS14 or guaranteed to exist in a target fork.

**impstation**

*activity · entangled · medium confidence · 13 forks carry it*

Bartenders and chemists get a much longer menu: sports-drink "Asterade" in eight colours with its own bottle sprites, novelty cocktails and coffees that each pour into their own custom glass, and joke drinks with teeth (one of them just bludgeons you for a hundred blunt damage once you've had twenty units of it). Drugs are written for the bit rather than for the stat block, so a hit of "foreverweed" spams you with paranoid hallucinations about the Captain, CentComm and the space cops knowing you're high, another fills your gut with butterflies and anxious intrusive thoughts, and another tells you there are ants biting you from the inside. On the medical side there is synthflesh that patches brute damage at the cost of cellular damage and random vomiting, dinosaur blood that works as a weak all-round heal, and hormone reagents (testosterone, estradiol). Every alien species on the station bleeds a distinct, named fluid you can bottle and run through a centrifuge to crack it into salt, copper, sugar, fat and, in one case, an energy drink, and creatures with thick shells simply cannot be injected at all ("Exoskeleton too thick!").

- **Take** — It is a large, mostly additive content drop that immediately gives bartenders, chemists and medics more to make and drink, and the drug flavour text does real roleplay work rather than just moving numbers.
- **Skip** — Roughly half of it is species blood and metabolizer plumbing for Impstation's own alien roster (Kodepiia, Allulalo, Thaven, Apid, Anomalocarid, Gray, snails), so without those species you inherit reagents nothing on your station actually bleeds, plus a long tail of new drink RSIs to carry.
- **Touches** — service, medical, science, all-players
- **Needs** — [extra-playable-species](#extra-playable-species), [non-humanoid-species-pack](#non-humanoid-species-pack)
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. Every one of the 15 cited evidence files, plus the species entity files I additionally checked (e.g. Resources/Prototypes/_Impstation/Entities/Mobs/Species/allulalo.yml, which sets Bloodstream.bloodReferenceSolution to BloodAllulalo), lives entirely under _Impstation/ namespace directories — no upstream file is touched or needs to be, so 'needs-upstream-edits' is not supported. What is real is a functional dependency on two sibling fork-only units (the alien species packs) for roughly half the reagent content (the species bloods and their centrifuge breakdowns) to do anything in play; the rest (Asterade, novelty drinks, drugs, synthflesh, dino blood, hormones) works standalone. That is an inter-unit (fork-to-fork) entanglement, not a requirement to edit vanilla/upstream files.
  - unsupported: "sports-drink 'Asterade' in eight colours" — asterade.yml defines 9 colored variants (Orange, Purple, Red, Green, Yellow, Teal, Blue, Pink, Black), not eight.
  - unsupported: "Every alien species on the station bleeds a distinct, named fluid you can bottle and run through a centrifuge to crack it into salt, copper, sugar, fat and, in one case, an energy drink" — only 2 of the 5 centrifuge breakdown reactions in biological.yml actually produce that salt/copper/sugar/fat pattern (KodepiiaBloodBreakdown: Ice/Copper/TableSalt/Ammonia/Fat; AnomalocaridCopperBloodBreakdown: TableSalt/Copper/Sugar/Fat/EnergyDrink). GrayBloodBreakdown yields only Radium, SynthBloodBreakdown yields Silicon/Lithium/Ethanol/SpaceLube, and ReaperBloodBreakdown yields Ash/Fresium — none of those three match the claimed salt/copper/sugar/fat template at all.
  - unsupported: "novelty cocktails and coffees that each pour into their own custom glass" — of the 6 drinks in drinks.yml, AppleMartiniCrystalLite and CafeLatteVanilla reuse pre-existing vanilla sprite paths (Objects/Consumable/Drinks/martiniglassnoolive.rsi and cafe_latte.rsi, no _Impstation prefix), not custom glasses made for this expansion.

**serbia-strong**

*activity · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 13 forks carry it*

Bartenders and chemists get a shelf of new drinks and chemicals that actually do things: Bacchus' Blessing hammers you drunk and shaking in a couple of sips, Vodka Kazaki slowly clears radiation, Hot Arachne scalds you from the inside, Bankate burns bare skin when you spill it, and each one pours into its own custom glass with its own tasting note ("like death and rocks", "like sweet dreams"). On the medical and combat side there are chems that make you hallucinate and a counter-chem that clears the hallucinations, chems that temporarily raise or lower how much damage you can soak before you crit, stamina and brain-damage chems, and a tolerance mechanic where repeated doses of the same reagent weaken or change its effect. Delivery gear comes with it: an advanced mini syringe dart that keeps pumping its payload into whoever it sticks in, single-use autoinjectors, pre-filled lead and uranium vials, and clothing that stops syringe darts from landing. A separate block of reagents belongs to SS220's mushroom-cult antag (conversion blood, a liberation elixir that unmutes converts, and a screaming acid brewed by cult monsters).

- **Take** — It is a big pile of independently-choosable content: you can lift three cocktails and a hallucinogen without lifting anything else, and each reagent is a self-contained YAML block.
- **Skip** — Every SS220 file carries a "© SS220, EULA/CLA with a hosting restriction" header rather than an open licence, so copying any of it into an AGPL fork is a licensing decision before it is an engineering one; on top of that the cult reagents are dead weight without SS220's mushroom-cult antag, and some strings are still untranslated Russian.
- **Touches** — service, medical, science, security, antagonist, all-players
- **Needs** — [blood-cult](#blood-cult)
- **Verified** — partly supported. Almost every specific gameplay claim checks out against the files: Bacchus (Jitter + Drunk boozePower:20 in 1-2 doses since Bacchus min:1), VodkaKazaki (Bloodstream HealthChange Radiation:-0.5 above 10 units), HotArachne (AdjustTemperature +250 thermal energy + burn popup), Bankate (reactiveEffects.Acidic on Touch dealing Caustic damage - burns on spill), the "like death and rocks" (Bacchus) / "like sweet dreams" (Skooma) tasting notes in flavor-profiles.ftl, pre-filled Lead/UraniumChemistryVial, AdvancedMiniSyringe with SolutionInjectWhileEmbedded (keeps injecting while stuck), single-use AutoinjectorComponent (Used bool), ChemicalAdaptationEffect (tolerance/adaptation modifier) and MobThresholdsModifierEntityEffect (raises/lowers crit thresholds), and the cult reagents TheBloodOfYogg/ElixirOfLiberation(unmutes, gated on CultYogg component)/CultYoggVenomancerAcid (Caustic damage + Scream emote = screaming acid). A directory listing of Content.Shared/SS220/EntityEffects/Effects also independently turned up HallucinationEntityEffect.cs + RemoveHallucinationsEffect.cs and StaminaChangeEntityEffect.cs/BrainDamageTimerChangeEffect.cs, backing the hallucination/counter-chem and stamina/brain-damage claims even though those exact files weren't in the cited evidence list. The one claim I could not substantiate after checking Content.Shared/SS220/Clothing (only IntegratedClothingComponent/IntegratedToClothingComponent, unrelated) and searching for SyringeProof-style names is the syringe-dart-blocking clothing; no such file turned up. On graft_shape: the seed's drop-in guess is wrong and the claim's own downgrade to needs-upstream-edits is right, but for a better reason than the one given - the blood-cult dependency is really cross-feature entanglement (CultYogg component gate), while the actual proof of upstream-file patching is Resources/Prototypes/Recipes/Reactions/drinks.yml (a vanilla path, no SS220/ in it), which I fetched directly and found ends with a fork-added `- type: reaction / id: BacchusBlessing` recipe plus an earlier commented-out "SS220 Eggnog begin/end" block - the fork edits vanilla reaction files in place to wire new reagents into crafting, contradicting the path-data assumption that zero files outside SS220 namespace are touched.
  - unsupported: clothing that stops syringe darts from landing

**sunrise**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 13 forks carry it*

Chemists get a handful of new drugs to mix and a new way to hand them out: a hemostatic powder that clamps bleeding fast but poisons you past ten units, an anti-radiation drug that leaves the patient seeing rainbows, and a pressure-proofing stimulant that makes you jitter, stutter, scream and occasionally vomit while it keeps you alive in vacuum. The chem master can now print labelled medicated patches alongside pills and bottles, so medics can slap a dose on someone instead of injecting. Bartenders also get a run of real cocktails (Negroni, Old Fashioned, Mai Tai, Paloma, Dark and Stormy, Boyarsky, Yorsh and others) with their own flavour text, plus extra sodas and condiments.

- **Take** — The patch printer is a genuinely new delivery format for chemistry, and the cocktail list is free bartender depth that costs nothing but YAML.
- **Skip** — The medical reagents are written against Sunrise's custom Mangleness damage type and their status-effect prototypes, so they will not compile or balance sensibly without dragging in the fork's wound model; several of the listed recipe files are empty placeholders, so the headline file count overstates what is actually there.
- **Touches** — medical, science, service, all-players
- **Needs** — [surgery-and-limb-wounds](#surgery-and-limb-wounds)
- **Verified** — supported. Fetched all 10 cited files plus the base (non-_Sunrise) damage-type files. Every headline specific in the claim checks out verbatim in Resources/Prototypes/_Sunrise/Chemistry/medicine.yml: HemostaticPowder does ModifyBleed -4.2 and adds Poison damage only once a ReagentCondition min:10.1 is met ("poisons past ten units"); Retroindralyne heals Radiation -3 and triggers StatusEffectSeeingRainbow ("seeing rainbows"); BarozinePlus grants a PressureImmunity GenericStatusEffect plus Jitter, a Stutter component, a Scream Emote, and probability-gated Vomit ("jitter, stutter, scream and occasionally vomit... keeps you alive in vacuum"). Content.Server/_Sunrise/Chemistry/EntitySystems/ChemMasterSystem.Patches.cs literally implements OnCreatePatchesMessage, spawning and labelling "Patch" entities from the chem master — confirms patch printing. Resources/Prototypes/_Sunrise/Reagents/Consumable/Drink/alcohol.yml contains Boyarsky, DarkAndStormy, MaiTai, Negroni, OldFashioned, Paloma, Yorsh — every cocktail named in the claim is present. The three "empty placeholder" files (Recipes/narcotics.yml, Recipes/fun.yml, Reagents/fun.yml) really do return HTTP 200 with zero bytes, exactly matching the skip_because note about inflated file counts. On graft_shape: the seed's drop-in guess is wrong and the assessor's needs-upstream-edits downgrade is not just correct but understates how entangled it is. I traced the Mangleness damage type used by HemostaticPowder/Retroindralyne to Resources/Prototypes/_Sunrise/Damage/types.yml, and found the fork's own (non-_Sunrise) Resources/Prototypes/Damage/containers.yml has a "Mangleness # Sunrise-Edit" line spliced into an existing damageContainer — an in-place edit of an upstream-owned file, invisible to path-based scoping. Separately, the patch-printing feature required editing three more upstream files in place: Content.Server/Chemistry/EntitySystems/ChemMasterSystem.cs (marked partial, new SubscribeLocalEvent for ChemMasterCreatePatchesMessage, extra UI-state argument), and Content.Shared/Chemistry/SharedChemMaster.cs (new ChemMasterCreatePatchesMessage class, new PatchDosageLimit field on the existing UI state), all tagged "Sunrise-Edit start/end". This is direct proof of fork-patches-upstream (the fork's own tree already touches non-namespaced upstream files), and by the same token any integration into a different codebase would need equivalent edits to that codebase's damage-container and ChemMaster files, so integration-would-require-upstream-edits also holds.
  - unsupported: "so medics can slap a dose on someone instead of injecting" is a plausible but unverified inference — I confirmed the patch-printing UI/server flow (OnCreatePatchesMessage, labelling, dosage) but did not fetch the Patch entity prototype or its interaction code to confirm topical/touch application vs. some other consumption mechanic.

### Chemical plumbing network

<a id="chemical-plumbing"></a>

Fluid piping for chemistry: reactors, filters, synthesizers, pill presses and smart dispensers connected into an automated chem network.

**starlight**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 0 forks carry it*

Chemists get a build-out toy: a hand-held Rapid Plumbing Device places hidden floor ducts (on three separate layers, with straight, bend, T, fourway and manifold pieces) and snaps together a chain of fluid machines, so reagents flow between them on their own instead of being ferried by hand in beakers. You pour into an input tank or a sink, then route the fluid through filters that split named reagents onto two outlets, reactors that pull set quantities and heat them until a reaction fires, synthesizers that conjure basic reagents like iron, oxygen and sugar straight out of battery power, buffer and 2000u storage tanks, a smart dispenser that fills a labeled jug automatically, and a pill press that stamps pills or patches at whatever dosage you set (including blending two feeds at a chosen ratio). Floor drains suck up spilled puddles into the network, a disposal unit quietly vaporises whatever you do not want, connectors show red for inlet and blue for outlet and look visibly jagged when you have misaligned a machine, and a plunger flushes anything stuck onto the floor.

- **Take** — It turns chemistry from repetitive beaker-shuffling into a buildable factory the chemist can design, debug and expand over a round, which is the single biggest depth upgrade available to that role and something upstream has no answer for.
- **Skip** — It is a large new node-network subsystem with roughly a dozen machines, six client UIs and its own construction tool, and its own guidebook advertises hooks into upstream ChemMaster, chemical dispenser and reagent grinder, so it will not sit quietly in a fork namespace and will need re-reconciling against upstream chemistry changes forever.
- **Touches** — science, medical, engineering, service
- **Verified** — supported. The two guidebook pages read almost line-for-line match the gameplay claim: RPLD tool building three-layer ducts (straight/bend/T/fourway/manifold), red=inlet/blue=outlet connector coloring with jagged-when-disconnected visuals, plumbing input/sink/drain, 2000u tank and 200u buffer, filter splitting up to 4 named reagents into filtered/passthrough outlets, reactor pulling set quantities and heating to trigger reactions, synthesizer generating iron/oxygen/sugar/etc from battery power, smart dispenser with labeled-jug auto-fill, pill press with configurable dosage and two ratio-mixing inlets for pills/patches, disposal that vaporizes reagents, and a plunger to flush buffers. Nothing in the gameplay text goes beyond what these files show. Critically, I fetched the actual upstream prototype files cited by the guidebook's own claim that ChemMaster and Industrial Reagent Grinder support plumbing connections, and both files contain literal in-place edits marked '# Starlight-edit' / '# Starlight-start: Plumbing integration', adding PlumbingDevice/PlumbingInlet/PlumbingOutlet components directly onto the upstream chem_master.yml and reagent_grinder.yml prototypes (outside any _Starlight namespace directory). This confirms the claim's own graft_shape of 'needs-upstream-edits' is correct and specifically the fork-patches-upstream flavor: the feature's own source tree already touches upstream files, contradicting a naive drop-in reading and validating the assessor's downgrade from the seed's 'drop-in' guess.

## Species

### Character markings and editor extensions

<a id="character-markings-and-editor"></a>

Expands the character editor with large libraries of markings, hair, tails, tattoos and scars plus extra setup options such as custom species labels and flavour text.

**corvax, cosmatic-drift, ephemeral-space, funky, impstation, rmc14, serbia-strong, stellar-station, sunrise**

*cosmetic · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 12 forks carry it*

In the character setup screen you get far longer lists to scroll: dozens of extra hairstyles and beards, cat and fox ears with separately colourable inner/outer parts, tails that come with a bow or a bell, lizard and moth and spider and snail-person body patterns, vitiligo patches, scars, neck tattoos, earrings, septum rings, eyebrow shapes, glowing freckles, and clown/mime facepaint you can wear as part of your face rather than as an item. A few forks add things you do during the round instead of only in the lobby: Sunrise gives a barber's razor that lets you sit someone down and add, remove or swap one of their hairstyles over a several-second cut with scissor sounds, plus hair dye bottles that recolour hair or beard, and a colour/gradient effect picker so a single marking can fade between two colours instead of being flat. Cosmatic Drift lets you type your own species label for your character, and Ephemeral Space replaces the usual setup with backgrounds (colonist, drifter, mercenary, ex-convict), pre-round relationships to other characters (friend, rival, ex, cousin), and examine text that describes someone's hair, eye and skin colour as identifying clues.

- **Take** — It is the cheapest possible player-visible win: the marking libraries are almost entirely YAML plus sprites, they show up the first time anyone opens character setup, and you can take a single species' file without taking the rest.
- **Skip** — Every marking is a hand-drawn RSI you inherit maintenance and licensing for, most of the interesting sets are keyed to species your fork may not have, and the parts that are actually mechanical (Sunrise's gradient effects and razor UI, Cosmatic Drift's custom species name with its database migration) reach into the upstream humanoid appearance system and character editor rather than sitting in fork files.
- **Touches** — all-players, service, ghost-roles
- **Needs** — [extra-playable-species](#extra-playable-species), [synthetic-and-ipc-species](#synthetic-and-ipc-species)
- **Verified** — partly supported. Fetched the fork sources directly and found two genuine in-place upstream edits, not just fork-namespace additions: Sunrise's Content.Shared/Humanoid/Markings/Marking.cs (an upstream path, no _Sunrise prefix) has a MarkingEffects field wrapped in literal '// sunrise gradient edit start/end' comments, wiring the gradient system straight into the core Marking data type; and Cosmatic Drift's Content.Shared/Preferences/HumanoidCharacterProfile.cs (also an upstream path) carries a CDCustomSpeciesName field plus validation/WithX logic added directly to the vanilla class, backed by dedicated EF Core migrations at Content.Server.Database/Migrations/{Postgres,Sqlite}/2025...._CDCustomSpecies.cs. That confirms the fork-patches-upstream reading exactly for the two mechanical pieces the claim's skip_because called out (Sunrise gradient/razor, CD custom species name); the rest of the unit (Impstation gastropoid markings, Funky facepaint, ES backgrounds/relationships/clues) is genuinely self-contained fork-namespace data, so the unit is a real mix rather than uniformly drop-in.
  - unsupported: "glowing freckles" — no marking combining glow with freckles was found anywhere checked; Impstation's Gastropoid set has plain non-glowing 'Freckles' (GastropoidFreckledBody), and every 'glow' hit across CD's generic/tattoos/foxfolk/moth/reptilian/rodentia/diona/dwarf/avali/slimeperson/synthetic ftl files is glowing eyes, blush, dots, or cheeks — never freckles.

### Extra playable species

<a id="extra-playable-species"></a>

Additional playable species that reuse the upstream humanoid rig: the standard MobHumanoid-derived body prototype, the standard humanoid inventory template and the standard humanoid sprite layers, with the fork supplying only new species prototypes, organs, name datasets, markings, sprites and guidebook entries. Alien flavour does not move a species out of this id, body plan does: if it still wears a jumpsuit on a two-arm/two-leg doll, it is here. A species that ships its own body-part graph, its own inventory template or a non-bipedal rig belongs to `non-humanoid-species-pack`, and a multi-species pack is filed whole, never split across the two ids.

**corvax, cosmatic-drift, gaby-station-now-dumont-station, impstation, monolith, rmc14, serbia-strong**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 13 forks carry it*

At character creation you can pick from extra species beyond the upstream roster (cat-people, foxfolk, rat-people, bird-like Avali, shrimp-like Anomalocarids, hulking Ungu, shapeshifting Kodepiia, Thaven, Protogen and more), each with its own sprites, name pools, markings and a guidebook page explaining how it plays. Choosing one changes how your shift actually feels: Avali survive down to -50C but get shoved over easily, Rodentia stash small items in their cheeks and talk gibberish while doing it and starve a third faster, Ungu are too bulky to wear any hardsuit so must use two-piece EVA suits and stay conscious to 150 damage, Kodepiia can only digest raw meat and choke on waste gas, and Anomalocarids must periodically vent steam or overheat. Chemists, doctors and quartermasters have to account for species that burn in the heat, freeze in the cold, or refuse the standard food and suits.

- **Take** — Species are the single most visible identity lever a fork has, and the packs are mostly data (species prototypes, organs, name datasets, markings, sprites, guidebook pages) with real mechanical texture already tuned and documented for players.
- **Skip** — Every new humanoid silhouette drags a long tail of upstream work: per-species clothing/hardsuit sprite layers, loadout and job wiring, markings points, food and atmos balance, plus rules text (the Impstation entries lean on server-specific naming and RP rules), and each species is permanent maintenance against upstream humanoid churn.
- **Touches** — all-players, medical, cargo, service, engineering, ghost-roles
- **Needs** — [character-markings-and-editor](#character-markings-and-editor), [assigned-roleplay-moods](#assigned-roleplay-moods)
- **Verified** — supported. Fetched all 10 cited files successfully and every specific mechanical number checks out exactly: Avali -50C to 36C plus 5% shove vulnerability, Rodentia cheek-storage/unintelligible speech plus 33%-faster hunger ('a third faster'), Ungu barred from NT hardsuits (must use EVA/Emergency/Ancient-EVA two-piece suits) and critical at exactly 150 damage, Kodepiia digesting only raw/uncooked meat and choking on inhaled waste gasses, Anomalocarid needing to vent excess heat as water vapor or spiral into overheating. All 10 evidence paths sit inside fork-owned namespaces (_CD, _Impstation, _Mono, Corvax), and the Ungu species prototype I pulled directly (Resources/Prototypes/_Impstation/Species/ungu.yml, supplemental to the citation list) is fully self-contained, only referencing one shared generic upstream marking prototype rather than patching any upstream file — this matches the seed's zero-out-of-namespace finding, so 'fork-patches-upstream' is not supported. The assessor's own skip_because reasoning (hardsuit/clothing sprite layers, loadout/job wiring, markings, food/atmos balance) is about what a target codebase would have to add to actually make the species playable and equippable, not about the fork's own copy touching upstream files — i.e. integration-would-require-upstream-edits. None of the 10 cited evidence files themselves demonstrate that wiring cost (no clothing/sprite prototypes were among the citations), so this part of the claim rests on domain knowledge about SS14 species modding rather than the cited paths, but that read is sound and consistent with how new playable species are known to require touching existing clothing/job data to be usable, which is enough to keep this unit out of true drop-in territory.
  - unsupported: "shrimp-like Anomalocarids" — the Anomalocarid guidebook text (heat-vent biology, damage table) never describes their physical appearance as shrimp-like; that's an unverified visual gloss the assessor added, not something the cited file states
  - unsupported: "cat-people" for Tajaran — tajaran.yml is pure data (id/name/prototype/sounds fields) with no descriptive text; the feline framing is outside knowledge, not something the cited evidence file itself shows

### Species racial abilities

<a id="species-racial-abilities"></a>

Per-species active and passive abilities such as melee bonuses, hairballs, sprints that leave trails, mouth storage, gliding, blink teleports and reach limits for short species.

**sunrise**

*loop-change · entangled · medium confidence · 12 forks carry it*

Picking certain species gives you buttons nobody else has. A cat-person can crouch over a bleeding crewmate (or themselves) and lick the wound to slow the bleeding, but only on bare skin, so the patient has to be undressed first. Winged crew get a "Spread Wings" toggle and a "Take Flight" toggle that trades stamina for a big burst of speed. Small bird-like crew get a short-range dash they can fire off three times before it has to recharge, letting them cross a room or a gap almost instantly. Other odd trinkets sit on top: characters who can conjure a bar of soap, a cookie or a candy out of nowhere, dog-tinted or heart-tinted vision, and a set of flip/jump/dance/lie-down emotes with real animations that anyone can use.

- **Take** — Species stop being pure cosmetics and start playing differently — a flying or dashing crewmate changes chases, escapes and station traversal in a way a hair-and-tail reskin never does.
- **Skip** — The interesting half of it (flight, dash, licking) is written for Sunrise's own added species and hangs off their mob prototypes, so grafting means both patching your species/mob prototypes to grant the actions and re-balancing mobility abilities that let players skip the station layout your maps assume.
- **Touches** — all-players, medical, security, service, movement
- **Needs** — [extra-playable-species](#extra-playable-species), [speech-accents-and-emotes](#speech-accents-and-emotes)
- **Verified** — supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. Gameplay text checks out point for point: felinid.yml's own description literally says the target "must necessarily be undressed"; milira.yml gives exactly a Spread Wings toggle and a Take Flight toggle ("trading stamina for speed"); jump.yml's JumpMoth variant (sprite bird_call, used by the resomi mob prototype) has LimitedCharges maxCharges 3 with AutoRecharge, and the resomi mob prototype's JumpAbility component sets jumpDistance 5 — a genuine short dash, not a walk-through-walls exploit; FabricateSoap/Cookie/Candy components spawn exactly Soap, FoodBakedCookieOatmeal, FoodGumball and FoodLollipop; DogVisionComponent plus a lovevision.yml shader (found alongside dogvision.yml) match the dog/heart-vision claim; animations.yml's Flip/Jump/Dance/Lay emotes whitelist only generic Body/Hands components, so any playable character can use them as claimed. On graft_shape: the felinid/milira/resomi ability-granting components (FelinidLicking, WingToggle, JumpAbility) all live on brand-new mob prototypes entirely under Resources/Prototypes/_Sunrise/Entities/Mobs/Species/ — so that half really is self-contained new-species content, supporting the claim's "hangs off Sunrise's own added species" reasoning (integration-would-require-upstream-edits: a target repo would have to edit its own existing species/mob prototypes to grant these actions to non-Sunrise species). But the path-data "zero files outside namespace" premise is not actually true for this unit: Resources/Prototypes/Shaders/dogvision.yml is a shader prototype the DogVision ability needs, and it sits directly in the base game's Resources/Prototypes/Shaders/ directory (next to cooldown.yml, greyscale.yml, outline.yml, etc.), not under any _Sunrise path — a real fork-owned file living in upstream territory. So both upstream_reading branches are live: the fork's own copy does drop at least one file into an upstream directory, and separately, grafting the ability-granting mechanism onto a destination fork's existing species would mean editing that destination's own species/mob prototypes. Given the mix of self-contained new-species content plus a real dependency planted in a shared upstream directory plus its own already-flagged extra-playable-species dependency, "needs-upstream-edits" undersells how tangled this is for an "adopted by 12 / drop-in-seed" shortlist entry — it reads more like should-be-entangled than a clean single-flavor needs-upstream-edits case.

**starlight**

*structural · entangled · medium confidence · 12 forks carry it*

Playing a Shadekin, your character carries a "core" organ whose energy rises and falls with how dark the area around you is, shown as a five-step alert on your HUD (from pitch dark to dangerously bright) alongside an energy counter. Veteran Shadekin players who meet the requirements can roll as a Bright-eye: an otherworldly visitor who spends that energy to tear open a rift to "The Dark" on the station, blink onto someone to stun, blind and drag them into darkness, drop shadow snares that ensnare and stun whoever walks into them, and conjure a shade that follows them around. Their goals are to keep a rift open and to protect their core, so the crew's counterplay is to hunt for the core (which is worth a fortune to science and can't just be swapped into another Shadekin), flood the area with light, or use bluespace-crystal gear, goggles and anchors that destabilise the core and pin the Bright-eye out of nullspace. The same folder also adds smaller body-based quirks: an integrated gas-tank organ that gives a species its own internals toggle and tank readout instead of a backpack tank, a breath-holding effect, and a gnome curse that shrinks a victim, dresses them in a gnome outfit and replaces their scream with an endless giggle.

- **Take** — It turns a species pick into a genuine round-shaping threat with real crew counterplay (light, bluespace crystals, surgery for the core) rather than a cosmetic reskin, and the integrated gas-tank organ is a genuinely nicer internals experience for any breath-odd species.
- **Skip** — It is not a species ability pack you can lift a piece of: the Bright-eye antag needs the Shadekin species, the core organ, Starlight's nullspace dimension, a "The Dark" status effect, the Burned/Nightblind traits, playtime trackers and a pile of bespoke counterplay items, plus new maps/sprites, so the smallest honest graft is the whole subsystem and its lore.
- **Touches** — antagonist, science, medical, security, all-players
- **Needs** — [extra-playable-species](#extra-playable-species), [character-traits](#character-traits)
- **Verified** — partly supported. Read the cited guidebook, alert, objective, antag-role, abilities, gnome and breath-organ files directly. Nearly every specific gameplay beat checks out verbatim: the 5-state light alert (dark/low/normal/high/dangerous) plus a GenericCounterAlert energy counter; Shadeskip (blink+stun+blind+TheDark status), DarkTrap (ensnare+stun shadow snare), CreateShade, and Portal-to-The-Dark abilities; the antag role's SpeciesRequirement:Shadekin + inverted TraitsRequirement:Burned/Nightblind + 48h OverallPlaytimeRequirement gating; the core's guidebook text stating it can't be transplanted between Shadekin and is worth a fortune to science; the Gnome curse shrinking height, swapping outfit, and hijacking the Scream emote into a giggle plus a periodic auto-giggle emote; and the OrganBreathToolComponent giving an integrated gas-tank/internals-toggle organ. The graft_shape='entangled' downgrade from the drop-in seed is also directly confirmed: the Brighteye antag role's own prototype requires the Shadekin species (defined in a separate Species prototype file, i.e. the extra-playable-species unit) and two specific character traits (Burned, Nightblind, i.e. the character-traits unit) to exist, exactly matching the claimed depends_on. The one real defect is a small item-function mixup around the bluespace-crystal countermeasure gear (see overclaims) that does not change the overall verdict.
  - unsupported: "use bluespace-crystal gear, goggles and anchors that destabilise the core and pin the Bright-eye out of nullspace" — per the guidebook text itself, the goggles ('designed to allow the wearer to peer into NullSpace') only grant vision into nullspace; it is the Bluespace Crystal that destabilizes the core and the Nullspace Anchor (plus an unlisted Nullspace Drainer) that root/restrain entities out of nullspace. The claim lumps all three items into one destabilize-and-pin function the goggles don't actually have.

**impstation**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 12 forks carry it*

Each of Impstation's odd species gets its own button on the action bar, so picking a species is picking a way to play rather than just a sprite. A snail-person burns their thirst meter to sprint and leaves a slick trail of mucus behind them, a crab-like anomalocarid vents scalding steam out of its shell (and gets increasingly panicked "I'm burning from the inside out!" warnings if it waits too long) or spits a burst of water at someone, a bird-thing tears a chunk of flesh out of a downed victim and can rapidly rescramble its own face into a new one, a psychic can beam a cryptic vision into a stranger's head or pop a small animal from across the room, and a bull can charge forward into whoever it's aiming at. The mime gets a proper toolkit of mimed props that become real: invisible wall, chair, box and a three-tile blockade, all locked behind keeping the vow of silence (they can't even type on an AAC tablet). There are matching drawbacks too: very short characters can't reach a machine's console unless they're buckled into a chair, standing on a table or floating, some species physically can't two-hand a weapon, and hoofed species need special fat-handled tools to work at all.

- **Take** — It turns species choice into a real mechanical decision with both a signature toy and a signature handicap, and the individual pieces (a sprint that costs thirst, a heat vent, a charge, a mimed prop) are small self-contained abilities you can cherry-pick one at a time.
- **Skip** — Almost all of it is bolted to Impstation's own invented species roster, so grafting any single ability means deciding which of your species gets it and hand-wiring it into that species' prototypes; the drawback half (short-for-UI, can't-wield, cow tools) also gates upstream machine, wielding and tool interactions, which means balance complaints and edge-case bug reports on systems you didn't previously own.
- **Touches** — all-players, service, security, medical
- **Needs** — [extra-playable-species](#extra-playable-species), [assigned-roleplay-moods](#assigned-roleplay-moods)
- **Verified** — supported. Every specific gameplay claim checked out against actual code/locale: anomalocarid HeatVentSystem.cs has the exact escalating "too hot" popup mechanic (HeatStored/HeatDamageThreshold ratio picks from TooHotPopups) plus a separate water-spit gun; gastropoid's MobGastropoid prototype has SnailSprintComponent with thirstCost:100, speedBoost:1.5, reagentProduced:Mucin (i.e., burns thirst, leaves mucus trail, exactly as described); kodepiia's Consume/Scrambler actions and ftl match "tears a chunk of flesh" and face-rescramble; pleebnar has both Telepathy (EntityTargetAction, vision to a target) and Gib (small-animal-targeted) actions; ungu's ActionDash matches "charge forward"; the mime toolkit is a byte-for-byte match (ActionMimeInvisibleWall/Chair/Box/Blockade, the blockade literally three tiles wide, gated by ActionMimeVowRequirement, plus the AAC-tablet-block locale string). TooShortForUIComponent/System checks buckled/on-ground/weightless/climbing exactly as described, and UnableToWieldComponent cancels WieldAttemptEvent. Crucially, for the graft_shape question: CowToolProficiencyComponent is not consumed cleanly through an attempt-event like the other two drawbacks — I opened the actual upstream file Content.Shared/Tools/Systems/SharedToolSystem.cs (not an _Impstation path) and it contains `using Content.Shared._Impstation.Tools.Components; // imp` plus an inline `// imp edit start` block that checks CowToolComponent/CowToolProficiencyComponent to alter tool doAfter duration. That is a real in-place edit of an upstream file living inside the fork's own copy, which the path-only seed could never see (it only sees _Impstation-prefixed paths). This directly validates the claim's "needs-upstream-edits" call and specifically the fork-patches-upstream reading, not just a hypothetical integration cost.

### Synthetic and IPC characters

<a id="synthetic-and-ipc-species"></a>

Playable machine-bodied crew that run on battery charge, are repaired with tools rather than medicine, and carry their own status UI and traits.

**backmen, corvax, cosmatic-drift, far-horizons, rmc14, serbia-strong**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 2 forks carry it*

You can roll a machine-bodied crewmember at character creation instead of a fleshy one. Instead of eating and bleeding you run on a power cell sitting behind a screwdriver-openable wire panel in your chest, and when you get low you right-click an APC, a charger or a spare cell and drain it (a "Ready to drain" toggle sits on your hotbar, and a "Battery charging disabled" message tells you when someone has cut you off). Your head is a monitor: an action opens a face picker with a few dozen expressions (hearts, static, goggles, RGB, a shower, a music note) that you can swap mid-round like a mood. When you get hurt the medbay is the wrong department for you: your limbs are their own machine parts that take extra damage from EMPs, and you get patched with tools and welding rather than chems and a bed. Different forks layer different extras on top: built-in radio, a thermal-regulation system that makes you care about overheating, installable modules, a lockable chassis, and positive/negative "custom frame" traits. RMC-14 does something different again, letting a synth pick a generation via an action, where each generation is a preset package of skills, movement speed, health threshold and damage resistances rather than a cosmetic choice. Cosmatic Drift's version is the featherweight one, just synthetic blood and a robot typing indicator on an otherwise normal character.

- **Take** — It is the most-requested "I want to play a robot" species and it rewrites one player's whole survival loop from food-and-doctors to power-and-engineers without needing a new antagonist or gamemode to justify it.
- **Skip** — A species that cannot be healed the normal way leaks into every healing, damage, food, blood and rejuvenate path in the game, so a half-done graft leaves you with a crewmember medbay silently cannot treat and cloning cannot bring back; the two richest versions here (Far Horizons, RMC-14) are built on those forks' own limb-damage and skill systems and will not travel without them.
- **Touches** — all-players, medical, engineering, science
- **Needs** — [character-markings-and-editor](#character-markings-and-editor), [extra-playable-species](#extra-playable-species), [surgery-and-limb-wounds](#surgery-and-limb-wounds)
- **Verified** — supported. The claim's specifics check out unusually well: Corvax's ipc.ftl/actions/face-profiles confirm the exact drain toggle strings ("Ready to drain", "Battery charging disabled") and specific face names quoted (Heart, Static, Goggles, Rgb, Shower, Music all present verbatim in ipc_face_profiles.yml). Far Horizons' IPCSystem.Battery.cs confirms the wire-panel-gated eject/insert and right-click alt-verb drain mechanic, IPCWeldClosesWoundsComponent confirms welding-heals-instead-of-chems, and the Body/Species/ipc.yml file contains literal `OrganEmpTarget` / `Shock: 3` entries on every limb, directly confirming the "extra damage from EMPs" line. RMC-14's synth_generations.yml shows each generation is exactly a bundle of Skills + MovementSpeedModifier + MobThresholds + damageModifier, matching the claim precisely. Cosmatic Drift's SynthSystem.cs is exactly "synthetic blood + robot typing indicator," nothing more, matching the "featherweight" framing. On graft shape, I found the concrete evidence the seed said path-data couldn't see: Far Horizons' own repo has `Content.Shared/Body/VisualOrganMarkingsComponent.cs`, a file outside the `_FarHorizons/` namespace, carrying an inline `// FH` tag marking a field FH itself added — the fork genuinely does patch a shared upstream-style file in place (fork-patches-upstream), which is what the claim's own graft_shape="needs-upstream-edits" call implicitly relies on and what the seed's drop-in guess missed. Separately, RMC-14's Skills system is fully self-contained under `_RMC14/`, so its own repo doesn't patch upstream, but its synth generations are functionally inert without RMC's skill/movement framework — exactly the "integration-would-require-upstream-edits" reading the assessor's skip_because argues. Both readings are independently true for different forks in this bundle.

### Non-humanoid species pack

<a id="non-humanoid-species-pack"></a>

Playable species that cannot use the upstream humanoid rig and ship their own body plan: a bespoke body-part graph, a custom inventory template, a non-bipedal or taur sprite rig, or bespoke damage and atmospherics handling such as water-breathing vaporizers. Packs are indivisible: every species shipped in one vendored species directory takes this id in every fork that vendors it, including the originating fork. The Macrocosm pack (`Resources/Prototypes/_MACRO/Species/` = Decapoid, Gastropoid, Allulalo, Gray, Ant, Apid, plus their markings, textures and guidebook pages) is that case and is canonically here, not in `extra-playable-species`, even for the members that look humanoid.

**impstation, sunrise**

*loop-change · entangled · high confidence · 5 forks carry it*

These are playable species that break the normal human body plan, so picking one changes how you play every job for the whole round. An Impstation Decapoid is a crab: it survives vacuum and cold bare-skinned and scuttles fast in zero-g, but walks slowly under gravity, can't wear shoes, can't fire guns, and its huge left claw is a pry bar, cutter, melee weapon and raisable shield rather than a hand, so it effectively plays one-handed. It also can't speak or breathe without its irreplaceable vaporizer and vapor tank, which examine as full/low/bad/empty and need water from atmos when they run dry, and medics can't inject it at all because syringes won't pierce the shell, forcing pills and cryo instead. An Allulalo is a tiny fast saurian that stands on chairs to reach consoles, holds one item, and bites allies to dose them with a clotting adrenaline toxin; Apids fly permanently, hold one item, can never wear a backpack or jetpack, and arrive as cargo-purchased cryo pods that ghosts wake up in as full crew. Sunrise's half is quieter: xeno, predator and demon playables with their own body sprites and their own inventory windows (a xeno gets bra/pants slots and is blocked from hardsuits).

- **Take** — A Decapoid or Apid is a genuine self-imposed difficulty mode that reshapes an entire shift of play (one hand, no guns, no injections, a breathing consumable you must maintain) rather than being a reskin, and Impstation ships in-game guidebooks that already explain all of it to players.
- **Skip** — Every one of these species is a permanent tax on the rest of the codebase: each new hardsuit, syringe, backpack, chair-height console or hand-requiring interaction has to be re-checked against a one-handed, shoeless, unpierceable, wing-blocked body, and the vaporizer is an irreplaceable item whose loss is a hard round-ruiner that admins will be asked to fix.
- **Touches** — all-players, medical, atmospherics, security, cargo, ghost-roles, science
- **Needs** — [character-markings-and-editor](#character-markings-and-editor)
- **Verified** — partly supported. I pulled the full impstation and sunrise-station repo trees plus the cited files directly. Decapoid guidebook and vaporizer.ftl confirm one-handed claw/no-shoes/no-firearms/no-injection/vapor-dependent breathing verbatim; Allulalo and Apid guidebooks confirm chair-standing, one-item hold, bite-clotting-toxin, permanent flight, and cargo-purchased cryo-pod-as-full-crew claims. Sunrise's humanoid_xeno inventory template shows the cited bra/pants slots and a Hardsuit tag blacklist exactly as claimed, and demon.yml/predator.yml both use their own markingLimits/dollPrototype/bodyTypes tied into the shared marking/character-editor system, supporting the stated character-markings-and-editor dependency and the 'entangled' verdict. The repo tree also shows Decapoid-specific sprite files added inside upstream Resources/Textures/Clothing/Belt/*.rsi folders and a Content.Shared/_Impstation/Decapoids/Silicons subsystem hooking into borg/AI code, both of which independently corroborate downgrading away from a clean drop-in and toward entanglement with other fork/upstream systems (equipment tagging, hardsuit whitelist/blacklist checks, silicon interop) — consistent with the claim's own 'entangled' call, which I confirm rather than override.
  - unsupported: Sunrise's half is quieter: xeno, predator and demon playables with their own body sprites and their own inventory windows (a xeno gets bra/pants slots and is blocked from hardsuits)" — only HumanoidXeno actually has a distinct inventory template (`type: Inventory` with `templateId: humanoidxeno` in Resources/Prototypes/_Sunrise/Entities/Mobs/Species/humanoid_xeno.yml, matching the cited humanoid_xeno_inventory_template.yml with bra/pants slots and a Hardsuit blacklist). Demon's Inventory override in Resources/Prototypes/_Sunrise/Entities/Mobs/Species/demon.yml only sets `femaleDisplacements` for sprite offsets, not a distinct slot template, and Predator (Resources/Prototypes/_Sunrise/Entities/Mobs/Species/predator.yml) has no Inventory override at all — no _Sunrise InventoryTemplate file exists for either. So 'their own inventory windows' is true only for xeno, not for predator/demon as stated.
  - unsupported: "its examine as full/low/bad/empty" for the vaporizer — the actual Fluent keys in Resources/Locale/en-US/_Impstation/decapoid/vaporizer.ftl are vaporizer-examine-state-normal/-low/-bad/-empty ("functioning normally", not "full"); a minor wording mismatch.

## Roleplay

### Server rules, space law and SOP guidebook

<a id="guidebook-rules-and-sop"></a>

Fork-authored in-game documentation covering server rules, space law, escalation policy, departmental standard operating procedure and onboarding guides.

**corvax, cosmatic-drift, funky, gaby-station-now-dumont-station, goobstation, harmony-station, impstation, monolith, rmc14, serbia-strong, sunrise, viva-station**

*loop-change · drop-in · high confidence · 11 forks carry it*

Opening the in-game guidebook gives players a full shelf of server-written reference material instead of just upstream's mechanical guides: numbered server rules (Cosmatic Drift's Rule 1.0 through 3.9, Harmony's R0-R8 and S1-S3), a written space/corporate law codebook listing named offences with sentences, and a Standard Operating Procedure tree split department by department and often job by job (Funky Station has separate SOP pages for Captain, HoP, Warden, Detective, Chemist, Paramedic, Roboticist, Bartender, Mime, and so on, plus a page per alert level explaining what Green through Delta actually authorise). Security and Command can look up the charge or the procedure mid-round rather than arguing from memory, and a new player can read the server's actual expectations before their first shift. Viva Station goes further with a Command-only hidden SOP: the pages exist but are metashielded, and your character only "knows" them once you physically find a head of staff's issued guidebook, with higher-clearance books unlocking more of the document, which is what gives an RP-led riot something concrete to be leaking. Sunrise and RMC-14 attach onboarding on top of the text (a guided tutorial and new-player popups), which is a much larger build than the documentation itself.

- **Take** — It is pure content in fork-namespaced XML plus guideEntry prototypes, and it is the cheapest way to make Security and Command play to a codified law and procedure instead of improvising a different standard every shift.
- **Skip** — None of the text is yours: SOP, space law and numbered rules only work if they describe your server's actual policy, so grafting is really a rewrite of every page plus permanent upkeep as your rules drift, and nothing here is mechanically enforced.
- **Touches** — all-players, security, command, service, medical, engineering, cargo, science
- **Verified** — supported. Every checkable specific held up: CD's guides.ftl lists exactly Rule 1.0-3.9 plus per-department SOP and a crimes list; Harmony's guides.ftl lists exactly R0-R8 and S1-S3; Funky's sop.yml defines per-job guideEntry pages for every job named (Captain, HoP, Warden, Detective, Chemist, Paramedic, Roboticist, Bartender, Mime) plus Green-through-Delta alert pages whose XML (GreenAlert.xml) does spell out what is authorised; Corvax's CorporateLaw dir has numbered offence chapters plus Punishments.xml/CrimeList.xml; Viva's CommandHiddenStandardOperatingProcedure.xml states verbatim the metashield and the three clearance tiers unlocked by finding specific heads' guidebooks (worth knowing: enforcement is AHelp/admin convention, not a mechanic, which the claim's "metashielded" framing correctly implies); Sunrise has _Sunrise/Tutorial and RMC-14 has _RMC14/NewPlayer, backing the onboarding aside. Drop-in is confirmed at the mechanism level: upstream GuidebookWindow.GetSortedEntries computes roots as all entries ExceptWith children, so parentless fork-namespaced guideEntry prototypes (like Funky's SOP101) surface as top-level guidebook roots with zero upstream edits. One small practical trim: Funky's sop.yml references an OctarineAlert page and alert-level-octarine locale key from its cosmic-cult port, and Violet/Octarine alert levels are fork-specific, so a graft drops or rewrites those child entries — content pruning, not entanglement.

### Speech accents, verbs and emotes

<a id="speech-accents-and-emotes"></a>

Extra accents, speech verbs, emote prototypes, typing indicators and quick-phrase sets, including equipment- and species-driven voice filters, plus paired and animated social emotes. Everything here is prototype- and component-level chat decoration that runs entirely in-process. External speech synthesis (an API client, voice picker, job queue, cached audio) is `text-to-speech`, not this id; per-character bark sounds, which just play a shipped .ogg on speech, stay here.

**rmc14**

*activity · entangled · medium confidence · 14 forks carry it*

Typing gets quietly cleaned up: a filter rewrites out-of-character shorthand and meta-slang as you speak, so "surv" comes out as "survivor" and "OB" as "orbital bombardment", with separate word lists for the human side and the alien side. Socially, you can offer a fistbump, high five, handshake, hug or tail swipe to a specific person, who has about ten seconds to take it before you are visibly left hanging, and each one plays its own animation and sound. Pointing at something spawns a large arrow other people can see, with a differently coloured arrow when you point for your own squad, and different species scream, laugh and chirp with their own voice clips instead of a generic one. Radio prefixes are also policed so the alien hivemind channel only works for aliens and never for humans.

- **Take** — The paired hand emotes (offer, accept, or get left hanging) and the visible pointing arrows are genuine two-player social interactions rather than decoration, and they cost nothing balance-wise.
- **Skip** — The chat core is welded to RMC's own factions: the sanitiser word lists are all Aliens-franchise jargon, the prefix routing keys off their marine/xeno components, and the squad-coloured pointing arrow reaches into their squad system, so only the emote and species-voice slice travels cleanly and the rest needs rewriting for your setting.
- **Touches** — all-players, antagonist, command, security
- **Needs** — [squads-ranks-and-skills](#squads-ranks-and-skills), [xenomorph-hive](#xenomorph-hive)
- **Verified** — partly supported. Direct reading confirms the entanglement: RMCPointingComponent's squad-coloured arrow branch (RMCPointingSystem.cs) requires SquadMemberComponent from Content.Shared._RMC14.Marines.Squads, and SharedCMChatSystem gates the hivemind radio channel on MarineComponent/XenoComponent from the marine/xeno namespaces — exactly the squads-ranks-and-skills and xenomorph-hive dependencies claimed. The hand-emote system (fistbump/high-five/hug/handshake/tailswipe, 10s LeftHangingDelay, per-emote sound+effect, "left hanging" popup) and the pointing arrow both check out as real, self-contained mechanics. However the flagship chat-sanitizer example is factually backwards: the locale files show cm-chatsan-word-ob/orbital/orbital-bomb/orbital-bombardment all resolve cm-chatsan-replacement-* to "skyfire", not to "orbital bombardment" as the claim states — the filter turns real/meta terms into in-fiction alien slang, the opposite of what's described for that example.
  - unsupported: so "OB" as "orbital bombardment" — actual locale data (Resources/Locale/en-US/_RMC14/cm-chatsan.ftl) shows cm-chatsan-replacement-ob = "skyfire", and likewise cm-chatsan-replacement-orbital / -orbital-bomb / -orbital-bombardment all resolve to "skyfire", not "orbital bombardment". The claimed output text is wrong.

**sunrise**

*activity · entangled · medium confidence · 14 forks carry it*

Adds a social interactions panel: you target another player and pick from categorised gestures (Friendly, Face, Tail, Neck, Wings, Horn) such as a handshake, high-five, hug, sniff, cheek-pinch, face-pat or tail-stroke, each firing a randomly varied third-person line plus a sound effect and a short per-gesture cooldown. Which options appear depends on the situation: a tail-pat only shows if the target actually has a visible tail, licking someone's face requires your own mouth to be uncovered and only certain species can do it, so a mask or a helmet quietly removes options from your list. On top of that, players can write their own custom interactions (name, messages, icon, sound, cooldown), pop a floating cloud emote above their head with a chat command, and factions like xenos, blob, carp and zombies get their own colour-coded telepathic chat channel with a single-letter prefix; a profanity filter and anti-spam pass sit over normal speech.

- **Take** — It hands every player a rich, condition-aware social toolbox that makes downtime roleplay actually expressive, and the interaction prototypes are pure YAML so a fork can add its own gestures without touching code.
- **Skip** — The shipped interaction messages are hardcoded Russian strings in the prototypes rather than locale keys, so every gesture needs rewriting by hand, and the bundle drags in unrelated systems (chat sanitisation partials on upstream ChatSystem, a replacement headset radio UI, collective-mind channels tied to antag content) that a fork taking "emotes" does not necessarily want.
- **Touches** — all-players, roleplay, antagonist, ghost-roles
- **Needs** — [extra-playable-species](#extra-playable-species), [clothing-and-wardrobe-pack](#clothing-and-wardrobe-pack)
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. categories.yml, friendly.yml, face.yml and tail.yml directly confirm the interaction-panel mechanics (categories Friendly/Face/Tail/Neck/Wings, HasTargetCondition, BodyAreaTagCondition requireExposed for mouth-covering, SpeciesCondition gating FaceLickDoggyStyle to Vulpkanin/Felinid, HasVisualLayerCondition gating tail-pat on a visible Tail layer, randomized interactionMessages + interactionSounds + numeric cooldowns), CustomInteraction.cs confirms the custom-interaction fields (name/messages/icon/sound/cooldown), collective_mind.yml confirms single-letter-keycode colour-coded telepathic channels for Xeno/Blob/Carp/Zombie (plus more), and CloudEmoteCommand.cs confirms the chat-command cloud emote. But the graft_shape call needs a correction beyond what the claim already made: fetching the upstream file Content.Server/Chat/Systems/ChatSystem.cs (not in the cited evidence list) shows the fork's own repo directly rewrites this core upstream file in place with dozens of scattered 'Sunrise-edit'/'Sunrise-start...end' markers that interweave chat sanitization, TTS, collective-mind chat routing, abductor emote speech, and announcement-speaker-network filtering into the same methods. That is not merely 'would need upstream edits to integrate elsewhere' (the claim's framing) — it is the fork's own copy patching upstream today, and the feature is woven together with several other large fork subsystems (TTS, collective minds, abductor antag) inside that same file, which is a materially stronger entanglement than the claim's skip_because conveys.
  - unsupported: "a profanity filter and anti-spam pass sit over normal speech" — the profanity/sanitization half is supported (word_replacements.yml + ChatSystem.cs 'для санитизации чата' hooks), but I could not locate any anti-spam system file at plausible paths (Content.Server/_Sunrise/AntiSpam/AntiSpamSystem.cs, etc. all 404); the anti-spam claim is unverified.
  - unsupported: skip_because calls the ChatSystem entanglement merely 'chat sanitisation partials on upstream ChatSystem' — the actual file shows the coupling is broader (TTS, collective-mind routing, abductor emote speech, announcement-speaker filtering all interleaved in the same edited methods), understating rather than overstating the entanglement.

**ephemeral-space**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 14 forks carry it*

Radio stops being a magic station-wide intercom: the further you are from the receiver, the more your transmission decays, with letters chewed into tildes and bursts of "--BZZT--" and "--KRSSH--" shoved between words, and past a hard range nobody hears you at all, so crews have to move toward relays or relay messages by hand. A hackable scrambler box smears that same static across every channel station-wide until someone spends fifteen seconds repairing it, and a scrambler examine tells you whether the processor is operational or malfunctioning. Alongside that, a wearable voice obfuscator makes you speak as "someone's muffled voice" (or as a monkey) instead of by name, a covert-message action pops a "Send Covert Message" dialog to push one line onto a chosen channel, a coughing affliction breaks your speech apart with hrgh/haughk/eugh interjections and cuts sentences short, and pain- and brain-damage-gated emotes like painslump and braingasp appear for hurt characters.

- **Take** — Distance-degraded radio plus a sabotageable station-wide scrambler turns comms into a resource crews fight over instead of a free omniscient channel, which is the single highest-leverage roleplay lever in this bundle.
- **Skip** — It is not the drop-in accent pack the label suggests: the falloff and distortion need hooks inside upstream's radio send/receive path, the channel gate reads a SenderWhitelist field the fork added to the upstream radio channel prototype, and nerfing global comms will make every department's coordination noticeably worse unless you also plan the relay placement and map work to compensate.
- **Touches** — all-players, command, security, antagonist, medical, engineering
- **Verified** — partly supported. Confirmed by direct fetch: Content.Shared/Radio/RadioChannelPrototype.cs (an upstream-path file, not under _ES/_Offbrand) has a `SenderWhitelist` EntityWhitelist field spliced in with literal `// ES START ... // ES END` markers, and Content.Server/Radio/EntitySystems/RadioSystem.cs (also upstream-path) has its `SendRadioMessage` body patched with ES-marked blocks that call the fork's `_esRadio.DistortMessage(...)` per receiver and add a `_esRadio` dependency. This is the fork editing files outside its own namespace directories in place, i.e. fork-patches-upstream — the opposite of the seed's drop-in guess, and exactly what the claim's skip_because already argued.
  - unsupported: A hackable scrambler box smears that same static across every channel station-wide until someone spends fifteen seconds repairing it" — the scrambler's malfunction state is set by `SetHacked(true)` inside `OnUndergoDegradationEvent` in ESSharedRadioSystem.cs, which fires from the generic `ESDegradationSystem`/`ESUndergoDegradationEvent` (Content.Shared/_ES/Degradation/ESDegradationSystem.cs), documented as equipment 'slowly breaking and degrading over the course of the round... in response to player events, not simply happening at will.' The in-game examine text only ever says 'malfunctioning', never 'hacked' or 'sabotaged'. There is no dedicated hacking/EMag/wire-panel minigame file for this component that I could find, so calling it a deliberately 'hackable' antagonist tool overstates what the evidence shows versus a passive wear-and-degrade mechanic (the 15s repair DoAfter itself is accurately described).

### Character traits and quirks

<a id="character-traits"></a>

Point-buy positive and negative traits picked at character setup that attach real components: disabilities, physical quirks, speech tics and skills.

**backmen, cosmatic-drift, einstein-engines, funky, goobstation, monolith, rmc14, serbia-strong, starlight, sunrise**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 8 forks carry it*

At character setup you spend a pool of points on quirks that follow you into the round: pick "Glass Jaw" or "Hemophiliac" and you crit sooner and bleed twice as long; pick "Wheelchair Bound" and you spawn already strapped into a chair with paralysed legs; pick "Oxygen Allergy" and you start with a nitrogen tank and mask because station air poisons you. Negative picks refund points you spend on good ones, so a doctor might take Deafness and Social Anxiety to afford Self-Aware (read your own wounds like a health analyzer) and Swift Feet. A large share of the additions are pure flavour instead: Boston, Russian, dwarven and bogan accents, Tourette outbursts that inject swears mid-sentence, felinid vocal cords, and starting languages your character speaks.

- **Take** — Every player touches it once per character, and it is the cheapest way to make crew feel individually distinct without adding a single new role or map — most entries are pure YAML on top of the trait system already in upstream.
- **Skip** — The interesting traits are not YAML: they reach into crit and death thresholds, bleeding rates, movement modifiers, vision and hearing, so each one you take is a small permanent balance and merge-conflict liability spread across upstream medical and movement code, and the accessibility-flavoured negatives (deaf, paralysed, anxiety) need a moderation stance before they go live.
- **Touches** — all-players, medical, security, service, roleplay
- **Needs** — [speech-accents-and-emotes](#speech-accents-and-emotes), [language-system](#language-system), [psionics-and-glimmer](#psionics-and-glimmer)
- **Verified** — partly supported. Confirmed via direct evidence rather than the path-data guess: Einstein-Engines' Resources/Prototypes/Traits/categories.yml sits at the exact same path as vanilla space-wizards/space-station-14's own Resources/Prototypes/Traits/categories.yml (verified via GitHub API listing on both repos), so EE is editing a shared upstream file in place, not adding a namespaced copy — that's the fork-patches-upstream reading. The other checked forks (cosmatic-drift, funky-station, Monolith, Starlight, Goobstation, sunrise, SerbiaStrong) keep their trait YAML/locale in fork-namespaced dirs (_CD/, _Funkystation/, _Mono/, _Starlight/, _Goobstation/, _Sunrise/, SS220/), so for those the self-contained reading holds, but the mechanics themselves (LegsParalyzed, SocialAnxiety, crit/death threshold shifts, bleed-rate changes) still hook into upstream medical/movement systems that a receiving codebase would need to wire up — the integration-would-require-upstream-edits reading. Both are true depending on which of the 10 forks you'd actually pull from.
  - unsupported: "pick \"Glass Jaw\" or \"Hemophiliac\" and you crit sooner and bleed twice as long" — conflates two different forks' traits into one effect. Monolith's Glass Jaw does lower the crit threshold by 10, and Monolith has a separate trait called "Hemophilia" whose text literally says "you bleed for roughly twice as long". But the fork that actually names the trait "Hemophiliac" is funky-station, and its effect is "take four times more bleed damage" (a damage multiplier, not a duration). No single fetched file shows a trait named Hemophiliac with a twice-as-long bleed effect — the claim spliced Monolith's mechanic onto funky's trait name.
  - unsupported: "a doctor might take Deafness and Social Anxiety to afford Self-Aware (read your own wounds like a health analyzer) and Swift Feet" — presented as one buildable combo, but Deafness/SocialAnxietyTrait are Goobstation-only prototypes, Self-Aware is Monolith-only, and Swift Feet is funky-station-only. These are four separate forks' own trait pools with no shared point economy; no player in any single evidenced codebase could actually pick this combination.
