### Player-authored documents and books

<a id="player-authored-text"></a>

Systems for player-written and printed text: form catalogs and document printers, signable paperwork, multi-page book readers and engraved inscriptions on items.

**sunrise**

*activity · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 11 forks carry it*

Adds a station copy machine that turns paperwork into a real activity. You walk up to it, browse a library of about 150 ready-made official forms sorted into department tabs (Central Command, Command, Security, Justice, Medical, Science, Engineering, Service, Supply, Prison, even a Syndicate set), pick one, and the machine spends a few seconds printing it while eating paper and ink from its own stocks. The printed sheet comes out already headed with the right departmental letterhead and auto-filled with the station name, the corporation name and the current time. There is also a slot you can feed an existing sheet into to run off duplicates of anything, including something you found or stole. Opening a printed form gives you a proper fillable document rather than a blank page: named blanks you click and type into, plus one-tap buttons that drop your character's real name into the signature line and your real job title into the position line, with a marked space at the bottom for stamps. So a lawyer can print a formal indictment, a doctor a death certificate or prescription authorization, the captain a certificate of commendation or a shuttle-call request, and the paper trail becomes something the crew actually passes around and stamps.

- **Take** — It gives every bureaucratic and command-adjacent role a concrete thing to do with a huge pre-written form library, turning "write a report" from a blank-page chore into a two-click printed document players will actually fill in and stamp.
- **Skip** — All 154 template documents are written in Russian markup and the visible strings live in Sunrise's own locale keys, so an English fork inherits a translation job roughly the size of the feature itself before a single form is readable; on top of that the fillable-field half hangs off upstream's PaperComponent/PaperWindow as partials, so it is not a clean drop-in, and the machine still needs map placement, a construction/lathe recipe and ink/paper resupply wired into your own station layouts.
- **Touches** — command, security, service, medical, cargo, science, engineering, all-players
- **Verified** — partly supported. Fetched all six cited files plus two more to settle the upstream question. categories.yml/templates.yml/pool_template.yml fully confirm the department tabs (Central Command x2, Command, Security, Justice, Medical, Science, Engineering, Service, Supply, Prison, Syndicate), the per-category letterhead header sprites, and ~140 real templates. CopyMachineComponent.cs confirms paper/ink consumption fields (PaperCost, IncCost), print duration, print sound, a CopySlot for feeding an existing sheet to duplicate it, and a Templates/TemplateCategoryGroupId filter list — matching the gameplay description closely. ApplicationEmployment.xml confirms {stationName}/{corpString}/{timeString} auto-fill tokens, [signature=]/[job=] fillable blanks, and a literal 'Место для печатей' (stamp placeholder) footer, and is written entirely in Russian, confirming the translation-burden claim. Crucially for graft_shape: PaperComponent.TemplateFields.cs lives under Content.Shared/_Sunrise/Paper/ but declares `namespace Content.Shared.Paper` and re-declares `PaperBoundUserInterfaceState` with extra fields (ImageContent, ImageScale, TemplateFieldsEnabled). I fetched Content.Shared/Paper/PaperComponent.cs (the plain, non-_Sunrise path) from this fork and compared it against the real upstream space-wizards file: upstream defines PaperBoundUserInterfaceState directly inside PaperComponent.cs, but this fork's copy of that same upstream-path file has had that nested class deleted so the _Sunrise partial can redefine it with more fields. That is a genuine in-place edit of an upstream-path file, not just a hypothetical integration cost — so upstream_reading is 'both': the fork's own tree already patches an upstream file, and any target codebase would need the equivalent edit to avoid a duplicate-type build break. This directly validates the seed's warning that path-only data can't see in-place upstream edits, and confirms (rather than overturns) the claim's own 'needs-upstream-edits' verdict.
  - unsupported: "you browse a library of about 150 ready-made official forms" — templates.yml contains 154 docTemplate blocks but 13 of those are abstract:true category-header templates (not user-selectable forms), leaving 141 actual templates; the pool actually wired into the copy machine (pool_template.yml, pool id "Sunrise") lists exactly 140 template IDs. The real number is ~140, not ~150.

**corvax**

*activity · drop-in · high confidence · 11 forks carry it*

A document printer sits in offices as a paper-fed machine: you feed it blank paper, slot your ID card into it, and pick from a menu of about sixty ready-made Nanotrasen forms — situation reports, employment and dismissal statements, access and weapon-carry permits, search warrants, death and marriage certificates, indictments and sentences, euthanasia and shuttle requests. The printed sheet comes out already filled in with your name, your job title, the station name and the current station time, so you only write the actual content and stamp it. It also ships department stamps for the Internal Affairs Agent and the Magistrate, a legal-department pen, and a shelf of in-universe lore books players can read. Emagging the printer unlocks a handful of joke/hostile forms like liquidation notices and a declaration of military action.

- **Take** — It turns "write a form on blank paper" roleplay into a one-click, pre-filled bureaucratic workflow, giving lawyers, IAAs, command and clerks a real prop library instead of freehand typing.
- **Skip** — Every one of the ~60 form bodies and all the lore books exist only as Russian locale strings — en-US has just the four substitution tags — so grafting it means writing sixty documents of English bureaucratic prose yourself and then maintaining them.
- **Touches** — command, security, service, all-players
- **Verified** — supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. Every gameplay specific checks out: printer.yml has MaterialStorage(Document tag)+ItemSlots(IdCard), DocumentPrinterSystem.cs substitutes doc-var-date/station/name/job exactly as described, CorvaxDocumentsPack has 59 recipes (matches "about sixty") spanning reports/certificates/permits/indictments named as claimed, CorvaxEmagDocumentsPack has 5 joke recipes including NoticeOfLiquidation and NoteBeginningMilitaryActions, rubber_stamp.yml has RubberStampIAA and RubberStampMagistrate, pen.yml has PenLegal, books.yml has a dozen+ BookLoreBase lore entries. The skip_because claim is exactly confirmed: en-US/corvax/paper/ contains only doc-printer-tags.ftl (4 tag lines), while ru-RU/corvax/paper/ has the real doc-printer.ftl, books-lore.ftl, book-busido.ftl, book-rulebook.ftl content files. Where the claim is shakier is graft_shape: every file I found (Content.Shared/Corvax/Documents/DocumentPrinterComponent.cs, Content.Server/Corvax/Documents/DocumentPrinterSystem.cs, all the Resources/Prototypes/Corvax/* yml, Resources/Locale/*/corvax/paper/*) sits inside Corvax-namespaced paths with zero upstream-directory files touched, and I found no evidence that wiring it into another codebase requires editing any upstream file (it just references generic BaseLathe/Paper/IdCard/ItemSlots APIs). The claim's own justification for "needs-upstream-edits" is a translation/content-authoring burden (60 documents untranslated), not a code-integration dependency on upstream files, so it conflates two different senses of "graft cost." Structurally this reads as drop-in with a large content-completeness caveat, not as needs-upstream-edits in the taxonomy's own terms.

**forky**

*activity · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 11 forks carry it*

Stations get a bureaucracy machine: an XF-880 document printer you can build and click open, giving a searchable, icon-tabbed catalogue of official station forms sorted by department (Administrative, Legal, Engineering, Medical, Logistics, R&D, Internal Affairs, Miscellaneous). Pick a form (promotion notice, job transfer, demotion notice, NDA and so on) and it prints a pre-written paper you then fill in and sign; locked forms show a "Requires: Command" tooltip so only the right ID can print them. It can also copy a paper you feed into its tray, it jams roughly one print in thirty until someone opens the maintenance panel and clears it, and it has wires: cut the manager wire and a hidden "Unregulated" tab appears with joke contraband paperwork (an XO murder authorisation, a clown all-access form), while emagging it unlocks a scrambled-name Syndicate tab with recruitment paperwork. Separately, a fax machine carried inside a backpack now drops received papers straight into that bag or the carrier's hands instead of onto the floor, so a pocket fax actually works on the move, including when something gets faxecuted.

- **Take** — It turns paperwork roleplay from "type it yourself in a blank sheet" into a real, discoverable station machine, with a wire/emag secret tab that gives Sec and antags a reason to care about the office printer.
- **Skip** — Every form is only as good as its written text, so the value is a content library you have to keep writing and translating; the machine also needs its own sprites, circuitboard, wire layout and map placement in each office before anyone finds it.
- **Touches** — command, service, security, medical, engineering, cargo, science, antagonist
- **Verified** — supported. Every specific gameplay detail checks out against the actual files: the XF-880 name, the exact category list/order (Administrative, Legal, Engineering, Medical, Logistics, R&D, Internal Affairs, Miscellaneous), the jamOneInChance:30 (~1-in-30 jam), the "Requires: {$access}" locked tooltip tied to `access: Command` fields, the manager-wire-cut Unregulated tab with DocXOMurder/DocClownAAForm, the emag-revealed scrambled-name Syndicate tab with DocSyndicateRecruitment, and HandheldFaxSystem.cs's backpack/hands paper redirection plus its FaxecuteFiringEvent hook. More importantly, the claim's own graft_shape ("needs-upstream-edits") is not just correct but understated: diffing FaxSystem.cs against the space-wizards upstream baseline shows the fork's copy of the upstream file Content.Server/Fax/FaxSystem.cs was directly edited in place (a `using Content.Shared._Funkystation.Fax;` import plus a `// _Funkystation:` comment raising the fork-only `FaxPaperPrintedEvent` that does not exist in vanilla FaxSystem.cs) to let HandheldFaxSystem hook in. That means this is fork-patches-upstream, not merely integration-would-require-upstream-edits — the seed's 'drop-in' guess is refuted outright, and the assessor's downgrade to needs-upstream-edits is confirmed and actually conservative.

### Ghost roles, respawn and game-master roles

<a id="gamemaster-and-ghost-roles"></a>

Ways for dead or waiting players to re-enter the round: extra ghost roles, respawn paths after a cooldown, and non-embodied roles that steer the shift from behind the scenes.

**ephemeral-space**

*loop-change · entangled · medium confidence · 9 forks carry it*

Players who are watching rather than playing can join a round as a "stagehand", a floating theatergoer with a randomised face who drifts through the station, sees in the dark, listens in on every radio channel, and can examine anyone but touch nothing. An Observe window lists everyone currently alive with their name, job and objectives, and a Warp button snaps you into following that person. Backstage you get a running feed of the shift's drama (who killed whom, who committed suicide, whose objective just succeeded or failed, who slipped into a new secret identity, who else joined the crew) with the bigger news printed in bigger text. Two actions on long cooldowns let the audience Cheer or Boo, which plays crowd noise and can carry through to the living crew, who get a nagging "I think the performers might have heard that one..." Separately, dying puts you through a short cutscene and then ghosts you automatically after about fifteen seconds instead of leaving you lying in your body waiting.

- **Take** — It turns dead and waiting players from an idle ghost crowd into an engaged audience with a curated drama feed, a warp-to-anyone spectator menu, and a way to react audibly into the live round.
- **Skip** — The bundle is not just the spectator role: the auto-ghost half forcibly severs players from their bodies fifteen seconds after death with return-to-body disabled, which cuts across defib and cloning play, and the stagehand mob and join gate both reach into other Ephemeral Space systems (lobby theatergoer marker, voting, interaction blocking, death cutscene, viewcone) that would have to be stubbed or ported alongside it.
- **Touches** — ghost-roles, all-players, medical, antagonist
- **Needs** — [lobby-and-character-ui](#lobby-and-character-ui), [secret-identities](#secret-identities)
- **Verification** — none; read this as a claim, not a finding.

**sunrise**

*activity · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 9 forks carry it*

When you press the ghost key you now get a confirmation box asking whether you really want to leave your body, so nobody spectates by accident. Once you are a ghost, the old plain warp list is replaced with a searchable panel: locations on one side, living players sorted by department and job with clear markers for who is dead, who has gone AFK, and who is already a ghost, plus a separate tab that lists the round's current antagonists so you can jump straight to the interesting fight instead of hunting for it. Dead players also get somewhere to go: a self-contained off-station bar with drinks, an arcade, a garden and animals, where ghosts can hang out and chat instead of drifting through walls. On top of that there are extra reinforcement slots ghosts can claim mid-round, joining a pirate boarding crew or a syndicate agent team as human, reptilian, dwarf, vox, vulpkanin or felinid.

- **Take** — It fixes the deadest part of the round: the ghost panel makes spectating actually navigable (antagonist tab, department grouping, AFK/dead markers) and the ghost bar gives dead players somewhere to socialise instead of quietly disconnecting.
- **Skip** — The ghost panel is a wholesale replacement of upstream's warp window and hangs off a partial of upstream's GhostSystem, so every upstream ghost-UI change becomes a merge conflict you own forever; the ghost bar is a 20k-line map you also have to maintain, and its comments and doc strings are in Russian.
- **Touches** — ghost-roles, all-players, antagonist
- **Needs** — [pirate-crew](#pirate-crew), [nuclear-operatives](#nuclear-operatives), [extra-playable-species](#extra-playable-species)
- **Verification** — none; read this as a claim, not a finding.

**serbia-strong**

*structural · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 9 forks carry it*

Dying stops being the end of your shift. As a ghost you get a panel listing every body your character has ever inhabited, each labelled as still available, abandoned, currently used by someone else, in cryo, or destroyed, and you can hop back into one you left behind or write it off for good. If nothing is left to return to, a fifteen minute countdown ticks in the ghost window and then hands you a respawn button that puts you back into the round. Ghosts also get a checkbox list of radio channels so they can mute the departments they do not care about, an option to hide the ghost sprite down to just the hat, and a toggle for seeing security HUD icons. Admins get click-a-target actions that turn any mob into an open ghost role on the spot (with a window to set its name, description and rules) or strip that role away again, and a set of station pet spawners (Runtime, Floppa, Bingus, Bandito and friends) that let waiting players take over the cats.

- **Take** — It answers the single biggest dead-player complaint at once: a timed respawn path plus a browsable list of your old bodies means an early death is a fifteen minute wait instead of spectating for an hour.
- **Skip** — Free respawn plus body-hopping rewrites the stakes of death for medical, security and antagonists alike, and the code carries an SS220 CLA with a hosting restriction rather than a plain open licence, so it is not a clean legal lift.
- **Touches** — ghost-roles, all-players, admin/gamemaster, command
- **Verified** — supported. Every specific gameplay detail checks out against the actual code, not just the cited evidence: BodyStateToEnter enum (Available/Abandoned/Engaged/InCryo/Destroyed) matches the claimed body-list labels exactly, and I found and read the uncited GhostBodyCard.xaml.cs which renders those five states verbatim with distinct colors and follow/return/delete buttons ("hop back in" / "write it off"). MindExtensionData.RespawnTime = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(15) and MindRespawnSystem's SetRespawnAvailable logic confirm the 15-minute countdown gated on "nothing left to return to." GhostHearingWindow.xaml.cs confirms the radio-channel checkbox list. Ghost.yml's ActionToggleAGhostBodyVisuals ("Скрыть тело... оставив только шляпу" = hide body, leaving only the hat) and ActionToggleHudOnOther (toggle SB-visor vision) match those two toggles precisely. GhostRoleCast.yml's three EntityTargetActions (cast/remove/settings for name+description+rules) exactly match the admin click-a-target claim. ghost_role_pet_spawner.yml/ghost_role_pets.yml confirm Runtime, Floppa, Bandito, Bingus (plus Exception, McGriff as "friends") as GhostRole+GhostTakeoverAvailable mobs. On graft shape: all 11 cited files plus every additional file I found by browsing (Content.Client/Server/SS220/MindExtension, GhostAdditionUIController.cs) live strictly under /SS220/ namespace paths, so 'fork-patches-upstream' is false — the fork's copy is self-contained. But GhostAdditionUIController hooks into GameplayStateLoadController.OnScreenLoad and the admin target-actions would need to be granted through whatever admin-rank/verb config exists in a receiving codebase, and the pet ghost-roles reference parent mob prototypes (MobCatRuntime etc.) that must already exist — so a real integration into another fork's codebase plausibly needs upstream-file edits even though the SS220 fork's own tree never touches upstream files itself. The claim's stated 'needs-upstream-edits' reasoning (design-impact on death stakes, SS220 CLA hosting restriction) is more about game-design/legal risk than code friction, but the classification still lands correctly for the integration-edits reading.

**backmen**

*loop-change · entangled · medium confidence · 9 forks carry it*

Dead players stop being stuck as ghosts: after a wait timer (and only while the server is under a population cap) a ghost can open a menu, pick one of their saved characters and a station, and walk back on as fresh crew in whatever job still has an open slot, with characters they already played that round excluded. Alongside that, command can use a reinforcement console to type a short brief and request one to three specific job roles, which goes out as an offer waiting ghosts can claim and arrive to fill. Admins can also call in whole response teams (standard ERT, Alpha/Epsilon/Tay variants, a blob-response squad, a Death Squad) that arrive on their own shuttle with a station-wide announcement and alarm sound, with the number of slots scaling to the player count and ghosts raffling for them. There are extra standalone ghost roles too (maintenance drone, a "canned clown" that pops out to help the clown, an InteQ mercenary garrison running a lavaland prison facility), supply pods that get called down with a targeting hologram and a falling-pod animation before landing (some carrying a person rather than loot), and cosmetic ghost sprite skins (angel, pony, astronaut) for sponsors.

- **Take** — Ghost respawn plus a command-driven reinforcement request is the single biggest fix for the "died at 20 minutes, nothing to do for the next hour" problem, and it keeps mid-round population up on long shifts.
- **Skip** — It is a bundle, not a feature: the response teams need Backmen's own shuttle maps, blob, and lavaland to exist; the ghost skins need a sponsor system; and the respawn path reaches into the game ticker, job slots, preferences and playtime tracking, so you would be cherry-picking one strand and rebuilding the rest yourself.
- **Touches** — ghost-roles, all-players, command, security, antagonist, admin
- **Needs** — [blob](#blob), [lavaland-mining-planet](#lavaland-mining-planet), [sponsor-and-donator-perks](#sponsor-and-donator-perks)
- **Verification** — none; read this as a claim, not a finding.

### Games, instruments and performance

<a id="games-instruments-and-performance"></a>

In-character entertainment: playable instruments, arcade and tabletop games, physical card decks and station radio broadcasting.

**estacao-pirata**

*activity · drop-in · high confidence · 8 forks carry it*

Adds a real deck of playing cards as a physical object: a deck case that pops open into a full 52-card deck plus a joker, each card an individual item you can pick up, drop, rotate and flip face-up or face-down. Right-clicking a deck lets you shuffle it, cut it in two, or turn the whole thing face up or face down, all with card-riffle and card-slap sounds. Stack loose cards together into a "hand" you hold, open it to see the cards fanned out in a menu and pick the exact one you want to play, or fold a hand back down into a deck. Nothing is scored or enforced by the game, so poker, blackjack or a bar card trick is played the way people play it at a table, by agreement.

- **Take** — It is a complete, self-contained toy for downtime roleplay: bartenders, prisoners and idle crew get a tactile card table that runs entirely on player agreement, with no balance surface to tune.
- **Skip** — It carries roughly 55 card entity prototypes plus an RSI and a folder of card audio for a purely optional pastime, and enforces no rules at all, so a table of cards only entertains players already inclined to invent a game; getting decks into players' hands also means editing an upstream vendor, loadout or map spawn.
- **Touches** — service, all-players, command, security
- **Verified** — partly supported. I read all four cited files plus the stack/card systems and the full repo tree: every card file (C#, YAML, audio, RSI, locale) sits under _EstacaoPirata/EstacaoPirata/estacao-pirata directories and imports only upstream Content.Shared/Robust APIs, so drop-in holds; the 52+joker deck, per-card flip/rotate, shuffle/organize verbs, hand menu, and convert-to-deck are all real, but the "cut it in two" behavior is contradicted by the code (full-count transfer, not a halving) and the unit silently depends on the fork's separate OpenTriggeredStorageFill system.
  - unsupported: "cut it in two" — the split verb's locale text says "Split in half", but CardDeckSystem.TrySplit passes stack.Cards.Count (the FULL count) to TransferNLastCardFromStacks, so the code transfers every card into a new deck and the emptied original is deleted; nothing is halved in the shipped behavior.
  - unsupported: depends_on: [] — the deck case's pop-open fill relies on OpenTriggeredStorageFillComponent, implemented in a separate fork system (Content.Server/_EstacaoPirata/OpenTriggeredStorageFill/, 2 files) that is not in the cited evidence or the dependency list; without copying it the boxed-deck experience described in the first sentence does not work.

**sunrise**

*activity · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 8 forks carry it*

Three separate entertainment tweaks bundled together. The headline one is a tape player: you slot a music cassette into a player, then a small window lets you hit play, pause and stop, scrub to a point in the track, and set the volume, with each tape carrying its own named song and length. The music is positional and fades out past roughly twenty tiles, so a bar or dorm can have background music that people actually have to walk toward. Second, non-standard dice get a right-click option that opens a window where you type the lowest and highest number the die can roll, so a gambler or a game master can reshape a die on the spot instead of hunting for the right one. Third, instrument playing is tightened up: a handheld instrument only responds if it is genuinely in your hands, you have to be able to reach and see it, joining someone else's band needs line of sight, and the server throws out malformed or spammed MIDI input so nobody can lag the room with a junk file.

- **Take** — The tape player gives bartenders, chaplains and dorm-dwellers ambient music without anyone needing to know MIDI, and the instrument hardening quietly kills the classic "someone uploads a garbage MIDI and tanks the server" griefing vector.
- **Skip** — It is three unrelated mini-features stapled into one unit, and the two most useful parts are not self-contained: the instrument mitigation is written as partial-class extensions of upstream's InstrumentComponent and InstrumentSystem (upstream must be made partial and must call into the fork's validation on every MIDI path), and the dice verb keys off an IsNotStandardDice field added to upstream's DiceComponent. Every upstream sync risks re-breaking those seams.
- **Touches** — service, all-players
- **Verification** — none; read this as a claim, not a finding.

### Character records

<a id="character-records"></a>

Player-authored medical, security and employment records written in the character editor and read or edited in-round from dedicated consoles.

**serbia-strong**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 6 forks carry it*

Instead of one flag per crewmember, security keeps a running case file on each person: every entry is a written note stamped with a time and one of nine statuses (wanted, search, monitor, execute, demote, paroled, incarcerated, discharged, suspected), each with its own coloured icon floating over that person's head for anyone in a security HUD. Marking someone wanted, suspected, to be executed or to be demoted automatically broadcasts a report on the security channel, so the department hears it without anyone typing. An officer wearing a security HUD can right-click a crewmember in the hallway and open their whole file on the spot, read the history and add a new status, rather than walking back to the console. The same bundle adds coloured microfibers to forensics, so swabbing an object can turn up "black leather microfibers" or "holographic chameleon microfibers" that a scanner later matches to a suspect's clothing.

- **Take** — It turns security bookkeeping into actual play: a note-and-history file readable from the hallway, nine meaningful statuses with distinct HUD icons, and auto-broadcast alerts, which is a large upgrade over upstream's four-state flag.
- **Skip** — Every SS220 file carries a hosting-restricted EULA/CLA header rather than an open licence, which collides head-on with the fork's REUSE/AGPL policy, and the feature also replaces upstream's own criminal records console, so it is a rip-and-replace of a system upstream keeps changing.
- **Touches** — security, command, all-players
- **Verified** — supported. All nine statuses (wanted, search, monitor, execute, demote, paroled, incarcerated, discharged, suspected) are exactly as claimed in criminal_statuses.yml, each with its own statusIcon field. Radio auto-broadcast (radioReportMessage) is present on exactly the four statuses the claim names (wanted, execute, demote, suspected), and CriminalRecordSystem.cs server-side confirms it fires a RadioSystem message on status change when that field is set. SharedSecHudRecordsSystem.cs adds an ExamineVerb (right-click) on any StatusIconComponent entity that opens SecHudRecordsEui with the full history catalog plus general record, in the hallway, no console needed — matching the claim precisely. micro-fibers.ftl confirms color+material combinations including exactly the two examples cited ("black leather microfibers", "holographic chameleon microfibers"). On graft shape: every file the fork wrote for this feature lives under SS220-namespaced directories (Content.Server/SS220/*, Content.Shared/SS220/*, Resources/Prototypes/SS220/*) and does not itself edit any upstream file in place — so this is NOT fork-patches-upstream. However, the repo tree shows a fully intact, unmodified upstream Content.Server/CriminalRecords/Systems/CriminalRecordsSystem.cs + CriminalRecordsConsoleSystem.cs (vanilla SecurityStatus enum, vanilla console) coexisting alongside the new SS220 system. The two are parallel, redundant criminal-tracking systems rather than one replacing the other in this repo — so "replaces upstream's own criminal records console" overstates what actually happened here (it's an addition, not a rip-out). But grafting this into another codebase would still force a real decision (keep both confusingly, or edit/remove the target's existing criminal-records console and access wiring), which is what makes needs-upstream-edits the right classification, specifically in the integration-would-require-upstream-edits sense rather than fork-patches-upstream.

**sunrise**

*loop-change · entangled · medium confidence · 6 forks carry it*

Instead of upstream's simple "set status, add a crime line" security console, Sunrise gives security a full case-file workflow: an officer pulls up a person's record (name, job, age, species, fingerprints, DNA, current status), opens a numbered criminal case, ticks which corporate law articles were broken plus aggravating or mitigating circumstances, writes notes, and the console totals a recommended sentence in minutes with an itemised breakdown the warden can read line by line. Closed cases feed a separate prisoner management console showing who is queued for jail, who is currently serving time in which of ten cells (and whether that cell is occupied and properly kitted out), and who has finished or been paroled; starting an incarceration locks the cell door, starts a countdown on the cell's wall screen, and issues the prisoner a disposable access ID that opens only their own belongings locker. The warden can cut a sentence short with parole, and if someone gets out early the console flips them to Wanted, adds a ten-minute escape penalty to the sentence, and pushes a wanted alert into the security messenger channel. There is also a wearable visor with a click-a-person action that flags that person Wanted on the spot and broadcasts the reason.

- **Take** — It turns "brig them for a while" into an actual legal procedure with an auditable paper trail (laws cited, sentence arithmetic shown, cell timers, parole and escape handled by the console) which is exactly the structure security roleplay normally has to improvise by hand.
- **Skip** — It is not the self-contained records module the name suggests: sentencing is computed from Sunrise's separate corporate law prototype catalogue, wanted alerts are wired into their messenger system rather than radio, and the prison half only works on maps whose cells, doors, timer screens and lockers are device-linked to a ten-cell console, so grafting it means importing two other fork systems and re-mapping the brig.
- **Touches** — security, command, antagonist, all-players
- **Needs** — [nanochat-messenger](#nanochat-messenger), [custom-station-maps](#custom-station-maps), [guidebook-rules-and-sop](#guidebook-rules-and-sop)
- **Verified** — partly supported. The seed's "drop-in" guess was based only on path data (all cited files do sit in _Sunrise namespaces), but reading the actual code confirms real functional entanglement: CriminalCase.cs uses List<ProtoId<CorporateLawPrototype>> from a separate Content.Shared._Sunrise.Laws catalogue for sentencing, PrisonerManagementConsoleSystem.cs hardcodes NumCells=10 and requires device-linked PrisonLockerComponent/PrisonCellDoorComponent/PrisonTimerComponent sinks wired on the map, and AddWantedStatusSystem.cs explicitly routes its wanted alert through Content.Server._Sunrise.Messenger's MessengerServerSystem (with the original radio call visibly commented out and replaced). Two of the three depends_on entries (nanochat-messenger, custom-station-maps) are directly verified in code; the third (guidebook-rules-and-sop) has no supporting evidence in any file I read.
  - unsupported: if someone gets out early the console flips them to Wanted, adds a ten-minute escape penalty to the sentence, and pushes a wanted alert into the security messenger channel — PrisonerManagementConsoleSystem.OnEscape only calls _criminalRecords.TryChangeStatus(...Wanted...), and that call (in Content.Server/CriminalRecords/Systems/CriminalRecordsSystem.cs) only updates the WantedListCartridge (PDA) UI via CriminalRecordChangedEvent; it does not touch the messenger system. Only the separate visor (AddWantedStatusSystem.OnAddWanted) actually calls _messenger.SendSystemMessageToGroup. The escape flow and the messenger-push are two different code paths the claim merges into one.
  - unsupported: depends_on includes guidebook-rules-and-sop with no evidence found anywhere in the fetched files (CorporateLawPrototype.cs, CriminalCase.cs, or any system) tying corporate law articles or sentencing to a guidebook/SOP module.

**funky**

*activity · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 6 forks carry it*

In the character editor each player fills out a personal file for their character: height and weight, distinguishing features, blood type, whether they hold work authorization, an insurance provider and tier (NanoCare, UnitedCare, TrueHealth, Interstellar Corp., at Basic through "Central Command's Best"), tick-box allergies (nuts, latex, pollen, hugs), current prescriptions (antidepressants, beta-blockers, blood thinners), family medical history (diabetes, epilepsy, heart disease), and free-text instructions for what should be done with their body if they die. In-round a doctor at a medical records console can pull up any crew member by name and read that file alongside their station-records data (job, species, age, fingerprint, DNA), so medical staff can look up a patient's blood type or allergies before treating them and can honour someone's postmortem wishes. Security's criminal records console also gains extra statuses: an officer can flag someone "to be searched" or "incapacitated" with a written reason, which announces over the security radio and shows up colour-coded on the security PDA cartridge.

- **Take** — It hands every player a real paper trail to roleplay against and gives medical a reason to look someone up before treating them, plus security two genuinely useful new BOLO-style statuses, at almost no mechanical risk.
- **Skip** — Nothing enforces any of it: allergies, prescriptions and insurance tiers are inert labels no chemistry or billing system reads, so unless your playerbase actually roleplays it you are maintaining an upstream profile-serialization patch and a console for decorative text.
- **Touches** — medical, security, all-players, command
- **Verified** — partly supported. All 7 cited files fetched cleanly. PlayerProvidedCharacterRecords.cs confirms height/weight/identifying features/work authorization/insurance provider+type/blood type/postmortem instructions exactly as described, and the ftl files confirm the exact insurance providers (NanoCare, UnitedCare, TrueHealth, Interstellar Corp.) and tiers (Basic..Central Command's Best), plus allergy/prescription lists including nuts, latex, pollen, hugs, antidepressants, beta-blockers, blood thinners. FullCharacterRecords.cs and SharedMedicalRecordsConsole.cs confirm the medical console pairs this with station-records data (name, age, job, species, gender/sex, fingerprint, DNA) selectable by name. criminal-records.ftl confirms the exact "to be searched" and "incapacitated" statuses with written reasons, security-channel announcement strings, and color-coded cartridge labels. One overclaim: the claim's family-history example lists "epilepsy" but the actual prototype list has "Seizures", not "Epilepsy" - a specific named item the files don't show. Crucially, Content.Shared/Preferences/HumanoidCharacterProfile.cs is a core upstream file (not under _Funkystation/) and the fork's own copy directly patches it in place (CDCharacterRecords field, WithCDCharacterRecords, MemberwiseEquals hook, EnsureValid default-assignment), all marked with "// CD" comments threaded through existing upstream logic. This confirms the claim's "needs-upstream-edits" graft_shape and specifically the fork-patches-upstream reading: the fork's own tree already contains edited upstream files for this feature, contradicting the seed's drop-in path-data classification.
  - unsupported: family medical history (diabetes, epilepsy, heart disease)

### In-character languages

<a id="language-system"></a>

Characters know a set of spoken languages; speech is scrambled for listeners who lack them, with translator items, sign language and a language selection UI.

**backmen**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 7 forks carry it*

Every character knows a set of languages and speaks one at a time, picked from a Language Menu (or by typing a language name/number before a line). Say something in Draconic and lizards hear you fine while everyone else hears garbled hissing; the same happens over radio and in whispers. There are roughly twenty tongues covering human factions (Sol Common, Tau-Ceti Basic, Tradeband, Freespeak, Elyran, Valyrian), species tongues (Bubblish for slimes, Rootspeak for Diona, Moffic for moths, Canilunzt, Nekomimetic, RobotTalk for silicons), a sign language for mute and deaf characters that shows up as gestures instead of speech, and creature tongues for carp, spiders, snakes, bears, blob and flesh. To cross the gap you carry a handheld translator keyed to a specific language (battery-powered, toggled on and off, examinable to see what it converts and what you must already know), get a translator implant, or read a language manual with a limited number of uses, including a Babel manual that grants everything and a syndicate codespeak manual. Translator quality sits behind Basic and Advanced Translation research nodes, and a Monolingual trait locks a character to a single tongue.

- **Take** — It turns ordinary talking into a resource: who can understand whom becomes a real constraint that creates translators as valuable items, gives species and factions genuine cultural identity, and hands antagonists a private channel in plain sight.
- **Skip** — It is surgery on the core chat pipeline, not an add-on: Backmen's ChatSystem is rewritten throughout (every speak/whisper/radio path takes a LanguagePrototype and emits both a clear and an obfuscated copy), so the graft rides along with every future upstream chat change, and a half-ported version silently makes players unable to hear each other.
- **Touches** — all-players, service, command, science, antagonist, security
- **Verified** — partly supported. The core mechanic is real: cloning the fork (sparse checkout) confirmed 44 distinct LanguagePrototype entries under Resources/Prototypes/_Backmen/Language (Standard/, Species-Specific/, Fraction-specific/, Fraction-specific/Simple/ including Carp.yml, Snake.yml, Bear.yml, Spider.yml, blob.yml, flesh.yml), HandheldTranslator devices with power-cell variants, translator implants/implanters, LanguageLearn manual items (Babel/Codespeak/OldFastCodes) with maxUses/deleteAfterUse, a Monolingual trait, and Sign language wired to gesture verbs. Content.Server/Chat/Systems/ChatSystem.cs (an upstream-path file, not under any Backmen namespace) is confirmed rewritten in place with 40+ "backmen: language" markers through TrySendInGameICMessage, SendEntitySpeak, SendEntityWhisper, WrapMessage, TransformSpeech and the radio path -- this refutes the drop-in seed and confirms needs-upstream-edits; since the fork's own tree already patches this upstream file, fork-patches-upstream is literally true, and grafting elsewhere would require the same edits, so integration-would-require-upstream-edits holds too. But several naming specifics in the claim do not survive verification: LanguagePrototype.Name resolves via Loc.GetString($"language-{ID}-name"), and across the whole Resources/Locale/en-US tree there is no language-Dragon-name, language-Slime-name, language-Binary-name, or language-Garpy-name -- only stale keys language-Draconic-name, language-Bubblish-name, language-RobotTalk-name, language-ValyrianStandard-name exist in the very languages.ftl cited as evidence, keyed to names that no longer match the current prototype IDs (Dragon, Slime, Binary, Garpy). Likewise the claim's "Basic and Advanced Translation research nodes" don't exist under those names; the real research prototypes (Resources/Prototypes/_Backmen/Research/service.yml) are TranslationDevice/TranslationImplanter/TranslationDeviceAdvanced/TranslationImplanterAdvanced, named via a different, uncited locale file (research/service.ftl); the "research-technology-basic-translation"/"-advanced-translation" strings in the cited technologies.ftl are unreferenced by any prototype. "Roughly twenty tongues" also undercounts the actual 44 language prototypes by more than half.
  - unsupported: "Say something in Draconic and lizards hear you fine" -- the lizard language's actual prototype ID is Dragon, not Draconic; language-Dragon-name does not exist anywhere in Resources/Locale/en-US, so this display name is stale/orphaned in the current codebase.
  - unsupported: "Bubblish for slimes" -- the slime language's actual ID is Slime; language-Slime-name is not defined anywhere, only the orphaned language-Bubblish-name in the cited languages.ftl.
  - unsupported: "RobotTalk for silicons" -- the silicon language's actual ID is Binary; language-Binary-name is not defined anywhere, only the orphaned language-RobotTalk-name.
  - unsupported: Valyrian is implied to be the harpy tongue, but the harpy language's actual ID is Garpy; language-Garpy-name is not defined anywhere, only the orphaned language-ValyrianStandard-name.
  - unsupported: "Translator quality sits behind Basic and Advanced Translation research nodes" -- no research prototype references research-technology-basic-translation or research-technology-advanced-translation (the strings in the cited technologies.ftl are unused); the real nodes are TranslationDevice, TranslationImplanter, TranslationDeviceAdvanced, and TranslationImplanterAdvanced, named via a different, uncited locale file.
  - unsupported: "There are roughly twenty tongues" -- direct enumeration of type: language prototypes found 44 distinct language IDs, more than double the stated count.

**starlight**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 7 forks carry it*

Every character speaks and understands a set of named languages, and picks which one they are currently talking in from a language menu that lists their spoken and understood tongues (or by typing a short chat prefix like ",g" for Galactic Common or ",drk" for Darktongue). Anyone who does not know the language you used hears gibberish instead of your words — nonsense syllables for most tongues, a red unreadable script for the cult/demon tongue, and vague impressions like "a happy signal to you" for animal sign languages. Handheld translator gadgets and implanted translators bridge the gap: hold or switch one on and it adds the languages it covers, letting you understand and reply. Some tongues are signed rather than spoken, so they need free hands, produce no sound, and cannot go over the radio at all, which makes them a private channel in a room full of people.

- **Take** — It turns plain speech into a resource players can be excluded from, which gives species, cults, animals and antagonists a built-in private channel and makes translators and interpreters genuinely valuable round to round.
- **Skip** — It sits directly on the chat and radio pipeline, so it cannot be dropped in without patching upstream speech handling and re-tagging every species, mob and ghost-role prototype with what it knows, and every future upstream chat change becomes a merge conflict.
- **Touches** — all-players, service, command, security, antagonist, ghost-roles
- **Verified** — supported. Every specific gameplay claim checked out against the actual files: galacticcommon.yml/aielic.yml use SyllableObfuscation (nonsense syllables), darktongue.yml uses RandomObfuscation with a red font (obfuscationFont, color #ff2202) for the cult/demon tongue, scurretsign.yml literally contains the replacement string \"a happy signal to you\" and sets allowRadio:false/requireHands:true/requireSound:false (private, hands-only, no radio), LanguageMenuWindow.xaml.cs has Spoken/Understood tabs and per-language Choose buttons plus chat-prefix display, and HandheldTranslatorComponent.cs has ToggleOnInteract/SetLanguageOnInteract fields matching the hold-to-activate translator description. Critically, fetching Content.Server/Chat/Systems/ChatSystem.cs (an upstream-namespace file, not under _Starlight/) showed it has been directly edited in place — `using Content.Server._Starlight.Language;`, a `// Starlight` tagged LanguageSystem dependency, and language-prefix parsing wired straight into SendInGameICMessage. This proves the fork's own tree already patches upstream files (fork-patches-upstream), which in turn means grafting it elsewhere would also require upstream edits (integration-would-require-upstream-edits) — both readings hold. This confirms the claim's own \"needs-upstream-edits\" classification and refutes the path-data seed's \"drop-in\" guess.
  - unsupported: "Handheld translator gadgets and implanted translators bridge the gap" — the cited evidence list only includes HandheldTranslatorComponent.cs; the implanted variant (TranslatorImplantComponent.cs) is real but was not among the cited files, so the specific word "implanted" is supported only by evidence outside what was cited.

### Tape recorder and cassettes

<a id="tape-recorder"></a>

Handheld recorder that captures nearby speech onto swappable cassettes and plays it back, rewinds or prints a transcript. Cassettes and recorders only: playing cards, card decks and other tabletop props are `games-instruments-and-performance` even when a fork ships them in the same commit or directory.

**cosmatic-drift, deltav, goobstation, rmc14, starlight, sunrise**

*activity · drop-in · high confidence · 5 forks carry it*

A pocket-sized tape recorder that you load with a cassette and switch between Record, Playback, Rewind and Pause from a small on-item menu. While recording it picks up anything spoken within a few tiles and writes it to the tape (about two minutes per side), timestamped with the speaker's name; voices it cannot identify come back as "Unknown" or "Unintelligible", and damaged stretches play back as garbled fragments. Hit Playback and the recorder speaks the conversation back out loud to everyone nearby, or hit "Print record transcript" and it spits out a paper transcript you can hand to security, post in the bar, or wave at the captain. Tapes can be ejected and swapped (though not while it's running), and a tape that gets unspooled has to be wound back in with a pen or screwdriver before it works again. RMC-14's take splits this into a speech recorder that prints reports plus a separate cassette player that plays music tracks.

- **Take** — It turns spoken roleplay into a physical, stealable, forgeable object, giving security real evidence, journalists real quotes and traitors a real reason to smash a tape.
- **Skip** — It quietly records everything nearby, so you inherit the moderation and consent headaches of persistent speech logs plus the ongoing cost of keeping the listener hooks working through upstream speech/radio refactors.
- **Touches** — security, service, command, all-players
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. Fetched the actual C# sources (Content.Server/_CD/TapeRecorder/TapeRecorderSystem.cs, Content.Shared/_CD/TapeRecorder/Components/*.cs) behind the cited YAML/FTL evidence: every file lives under the fork's own _CD namespace, and the system only SubscribeLocalEvent's on ListenEvent, plus consumes ActiveListenerComponent, VoiceOverrideComponent, ChatSystem and PaperSystem — all of which I confirmed exist as stock upstream (space-wizards/space-station-14) types, not fork additions. No upstream file is patched by the fork's own copy, and nothing in the code requires editing an upstream file to wire it up (it just needs those already-standard hooks to exist, which any SS14-derived fork has). That contradicts the claim's downgrade to needs-upstream-edits; the seed's drop-in read holds up better against the evidence.
  - unsupported: "about two minutes per side" — TapeCassetteComponent.cs sets MaxCapacity = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(120) as a single continuous capacity with one CurrentPosition float and one RecordedData/Buffer list; there is no A/B-side mechanic (no flip action, no second buffer) in the code. The "on either side" phrasing is flavor text on the entity description only, not a coded two-sides system, so "two minutes per side" overstates total capacity (it reads as up to ~4 minutes, when the actual cap is 2 minutes total).

### Additional language localizations

<a id="localization-translations"></a>

Full parallel locale trees translating the whole game, upstream and fork content alike, into a language other than English.

**corvax, estacao-pirata, gaby-station-now-dumont-station, sunrise, white-dream**

*cosmetic · entangled · medium confidence · 2 forks carry it*

The whole game reads in another language. Item names and descriptions, machine UIs, HUD button tooltips, alert and warning messages, vending machine ad barks, even SI unit prefixes on gas and power readouts come out in Russian (Corvax, Sunrise, White Dream) or Brazilian Portuguese (Estação Pirata, Dumont Station) instead of English. Each fork carries a complete parallel text tree, 1,400 to 3,300 files, covering both upstream content and that fork's own additions, so a player who picks the locale never falls back to English mid-round.

- **Take** — It is the only thing that makes the server actually playable for people who do not read English, and the text files are pure additive data with no gameplay risk.
- **Skip** — It is a permanent treadmill, not a one-time port: every upstream string rename and every new fork item silently reverts to English until someone translates it, which is why Corvax ships a whole sync toolchain just to find the gaps.
- **Touches** — all-players
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. Every cited evidence path resolved and confirmed the general shape: corvax's ru-RU game-hud.ftl and _units.ftl really do translate HUD tooltips and SI prefixes, estacao-pirata's silicons.ftl and attributions.yml exist, white-dream's materials.ftl and sunrise's cyberlimbs.ftl exist. Upstream (space-wizards/space-station-14) only ships en-US and nl-NL locales, so none of these five forks edit an existing upstream locale file in place — they add whole new Resources/Locale/&lt;culture&gt;/ trees, which is why no upstream-directory hits showed up. That argues for drop-in, not needs-upstream-edits as the seed guessed. But two of the cited files (WWDP_TRANSLATION/_Nuclear14/materials.ftl and _starlight/body/parts/cyberlimbs.ftl) are translations of that SOURCE fork's own bespoke content (WWDP's Nuclear14 mod, Sunrise's Starlight cyberlimb system) — content that does not exist in honksquad. Grafting these trees wholesale imports thousands of strings tied to each donor fork's own unrelated systems while still leaving honksquad's actual fork-specific content (RussStation additions, skillchips, etc.) untranslated, which is a real entanglement with each source fork's OTHER systems, not a clean localization asset.
  - unsupported: a player who picks the locale never falls back to English mid-round — directly contradicted by the claim's own skip_because line in the same document ("every upstream string rename and every new fork item silently reverts to English until someone translates it"), and further undermined by the fact these translation trees cover each donor fork's own custom content (Nuclear14, Starlight) rather than honksquad's, so a graft would still leave large parts of the actual target game in English
  - unsupported: 1,400 to 3,300 files — measured locale-directory counts were corvax ru-RU 2,563, estacao-pirata pt-BR 1,614, dumont pt-BR 2,099, sunrise ru-RU 3,340, white-dream ru-RU 2,846; sunrise exceeds the stated upper bound

### Religion and chaplain rework

<a id="religion-and-chaplain-rework"></a>

Expands the chaplain into a pickable faith with per-religion altars, vestments, weapons, exorcism and consecration mechanics.

**gaby-station-now-dumont-station, goobstation, impstation, serbia-strong, the-den**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 2 forks carry it*

The chaplain stops being a guy with a bible and becomes a faith-powered role built around the null rod. On Impstation the chaplain opens a "Transpose Shape" menu and permanently picks what their rod becomes: a jewelled grail that holds and blesses large volumes of liquid, a divine gauntlet that deflects incoming attacks and knocks people down, or a golden bow with a quiver of arrows nocked one at a time. Goob's version binds the rod to its owner, blocks spells cast at whoever carries it, lets the chaplain pray to recall it to hand, and sears or damages any non-believer who tries to pick it up or handle other unholy items; praying at consecrated objects heals people nearby, reloads weapons, or flips things on for a while, and cult- or heretic-tainted creatures take extra damage from holy sources. SS220 adds a written exorcism: the chaplain triggers the action, types out a prayer of a certain length, and the ritual flares light and effects across a radius, backed by a censer that puffs holy water vapour and hits demons hard, plus sacred relics whose true nature only shows to characters with the right background. The Den's chapel altar is instead a place to sacrifice psionics, quietly dropping station glimmer and sometimes leaving an item of power behind.

- **Take** — It turns the chaplain from a flavour job into a real anti-antagonist role with its own toolkit and a player-chosen build, and the null rod menu is a self-contained, high-payoff slice you can take without the rest.
- **Skip** — It only pays off if your round already has occult antagonists to push against, and the pieces are scattered across five forks with different hooks (Goob's spell denial, SS220's exorcism, The Den's glimmer altar), so you are assembling a system rather than porting one.
- **Touches** — service, chaplain, antagonist, security, medical
- **Needs** — [psionics-and-glimmer](#psionics-and-glimmer), [heretic](#heretic)
- **Verified** — partly supported. Nine of eleven specific mechanical claims across all five forks were directly confirmed by reading the cited files verbatim: Impstation's exact "Transpose Shape" grail/glove/bow menu (gearmenu.ftl, chaplain_gear.yml), Goob's spell-denial-when-equipped (DivineInterventionComponent.ValidSpellDenialSlots), recall-to-hand (RecallPrayableComponent), unholy-item marker (UnholyItemComponent) and the exact heal/reload/toggle-on-pray trio (OnPray/HealNearOnPray, ReloadOnPray, TimedToggleOnPray), SS220's typed-prayer exorcism with length/range/light-duration fields (ExorcismPerformerComponent) and knowledge-gated relic descriptions (SacredRelicMime's HiddenDescription by faction), and The Den's exact psionic-sacrifice-for-glimmer altar with reward-item chance (SacrificialAltarComponent). Two specifics (owner-binding of the rod, and cult/heretic-specific holy weakness) were not directly backed by the files I could reach. The graft_shape call of needs-upstream-edits holds, but the reading is 'both': Goob/Impstation/SS220 pieces sit in clean fork-owned namespaces (self-contained, would need upstream wiring to swap into vanilla's chaplain job), while The Den's altar files (Content.Shared/Chapel/*, Content.Server/Chapel/SacrificialAltarSystem.cs) sit with zero fork-specific prefix directly in upstream-style directories that don't even exist in vanilla space-station-14 (confirmed 404), which is the fork-patches-upstream pattern in practice even though technically new files rather than edits to pre-existing ones.
  - unsupported: "Goob's version binds the rod to its owner" — NullrodComponent.cs (Content.Goobstation.Shared/Religion/Nullrod/Components/NullrodComponent.cs) has no owner-binding field; it has RecallType (None/Normal/Unremoveable/Embedded/DualWield) and PrayDoAfterDuration, which explain recall-to-hand but not an ownership bind.
  - unsupported: "cult- or heretic-tainted creatures take extra damage from holy sources" — WeakToHolyComponent.cs exists and does define holy-based passive damage/heal, but the file itself does not scope this to cult or heretic mobs specifically; I could not locate the prototype file(s) that actually attach WeakToHolyComponent to confirm which antagonist types get it (404s on guessed paths, GitHub code search required auth).

### Text-to-speech voice synthesis

<a id="text-to-speech"></a>

A client for an external speech-synthesis service that speaks in-game chat aloud: an HTTP client and API-key CVars, a server-side job queue and rate limiter, a per-voice cache of generated audio, SSML markup plus sanitising of player text before it is sent, a per-character voice picker in the character editor, and playback hooks for local speech, radio, announcements and announcer lines. The test is the network round trip and the queue: if audio is synthesised off-server at runtime it is this id, and if a shipped .ogg is played it is not.

**corvax, serbia-strong, starlight, sunrise, white-dream**

*cosmetic · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 2 forks carry it*

Everything people say is spoken aloud instead of only appearing in the chat log: you hear the person next to you talk in their own voice, hear radio traffic come through your headset, and hear station-wide announcements read out. When you build a character you pick that character's voice from a catalogue of dozens of male, female and synthetic voices (Starlight lets you filter them by accent and tone tags like scottish, raspy or serious, and shows a character's voice on a detailed examine), and if you disguise your voice with a voice mask the spoken voice changes to match the fake name. Players get their own volume sliders for local speech, radio and announcements, and can mute the whole thing; Sunrise reserves some voices for donators and Corvax marks some as unavailable at round start.

- **Take** — It turns the whole chat log audible, which is the single biggest change to how a round feels without changing a single rule of how a round is played.
- **Skip** — It is not self-contained content: it needs an external speech-synthesis service you host or pay for, an API key, a job queue and rate limiter to survive a busy round, a database migration to store each character's voice, and it hands players an uncensored microphone that says whatever they type.
- **Touches** — all-players, command, security, silicon, antagonist
- **Verified** — supported. Confirmed via direct fetch: Content.Server/VoiceMask/VoiceMaskSystem.cs and Content.Shared/VoiceMask/VoiceMaskComponent.cs (both plain upstream paths, no Corvax/_Starlight/etc namespace) contain inline `// Corvax-TTS-Start/End` blocks adding a VoiceId field and InitializeTTS() call, and Content.Shared/Preferences/HumanoidCharacterProfile.cs (also plain upstream) has a `Voice`/`SiliconVoice` field added with `🌟Starlight🌟` markers. These are files the fork edits in place outside any namespace directory, exactly the blind spot the seed note warned about — so 'needs-upstream-edits' is right, and specifically in the 'fork-patches-upstream' sense (the forks' own repos already touch upstream files), not merely 'would need edits to integrate elsewhere'.
  - unsupported: "a job queue and rate limiter to survive a busy round" — plausible for a real-time TTS backend but not something I found direct evidence of in any fetched file (only the client-facing CVars: tts.enabled, tts.connection_string, volume sliders were confirmed); this specific operational detail is asserted, not shown.

### Psionics and the Glimmer

<a id="psionics-and-glimmer"></a>

Latent psychic powers (mind swap, pyrokinesis, telegnosis, dispel and more) gated behind a station-wide Glimmer meter that spawns hostile entities as it rises.

**einstein-engines**

*structural · entangled · high confidence · 4 forks carry it*

Some crew wake up psychic: at character setup you can pick a caster type (latent psychic, psycho-historian, elementalist, or the anti-psychic "insulated" option) and over the shift you roll powers from a pool that includes mind swap, mass sleep, telepathy, pyrokinesis, telekinetic pulse, telegnosis (send an invisible remote eye), psionic invisibility, healing word, revivify, xenoglossy (understand any language) and a detector pulse that finds other psychics nearby. Every power use pushes or pulls a station-wide "glimmer" meter, and as glimmer climbs the station gets weirder and more dangerous: machines visibly crackle, death messages change to souls leaving the body, noospheric storms are announced over the radio, and science can deliberately farm glimmer with a glimmer prober for research points while the talking statue Sophia broadcasts current readings over comms. Security gets a Psionics Registry console to register, suspect or flag crew as abusing psionics, chaplains and cargo get holy-water crates, and an Oracle entity trades divine gifts for whatever object it demands; some antagonist objectives are simply to drive glimmer past a threshold or to become psionic yourself.

- **Take** — It is a whole second layer of round pressure that no other system provides: a shared meter every player can push, which converts individual power use into escalating station-wide consequences and gives science, security and antagonists new reasons to care about each other.
- **Skip** — It is enormous (about 120 files here, 99 of them C#) and it assumes the fork's trait/point character setup, language system and Epistemics department restructure, so grafting it means importing several other large systems and then balancing a magic layer against every existing combat, medical and antag interaction forever.
- **Touches** — science, security, command, medical, service, antagonist, all-players
- **Needs** — [character-traits](#character-traits), [language-system](#language-system), [department-restructure](#department-restructure)
- **Verified** — supported. Direct reads of psionics.yml, PsionicPowerPool.yml, casterTypes.yml, feats.yml, the psionics-records/oracle/death-gasp/objectives ftl files, glimmer_prober.yml and sophicscribe.yml confirm essentially every specific gameplay beat claimed (caster-type traits including PsionicInsulation, per-power glimmer modifiers, the registry console's registered/suspected/abusing states, Oracle item demands, glimmer-tier death messages, raise-glimmer/become-psionic objectives, glimmer prober generating research points, Sophia's radio-connected statue, and holy-water crates for both epistemics/chaplain and cargo). Going further than the cited evidence, I pulled the full repo tree and confirmed the entangled verdict directly: Resources/Prototypes/Roles/Jobs/departments.yml (outside any Psionics/Nyanotrasen namespace) is edited in place with a department literally named 'Epistemics' and the comment '# DeltaV - Epistemics Department replacing Science', folding Chaplain/Librarian into it; ForensicMantis' job prototype requires CharacterDepartmentTimeRequirement department: Epistemics; and the trait system (casterTypes.yml, feats.yml) leans on a points-based CharacterTraitRequirement/CharacterLogicOrRequirement framework that is its own large subsystem. So the claim's own downgrade from the seed's 'needs-upstream-edits' to 'entangled' is correct and, if anything, understated how deep the coupling goes.

**deltav**

*structural · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 4 forks carry it*

Some crew wake up psychic, or become psychic later by drinking oil the Oracle dispenses, taking a shot of an experimental chemical from the station's psionics specialist, or getting caught in a random psychic seizure. Each psychic gets exactly one power out of a grab bag: mind-swapping into someone else's body, dropping everyone nearby into forced sleep, setting a target on fire with a thought, sending out a remote ghostly eye to scout, glimpsing a vision of a disaster that is about to hit the station, or dispelling other people's magic. Every use of a power pushes up a station-wide meter called Glimmer, which the science department watches on a PDA graph and a talking statue, and which they deliberately farm for research points using a machine that makes it climb faster. Push it too high and the station gets an alert, gets nosebleeds and seizures, gets whole-crew mind-swap events, and gets invaded by ghostly creatures that hunt psychics down and drain them dry, so the department has to scramble to pull the number back down with drain machines, sacrifices, or by chemically stripping people's powers. Security and a dedicated psionics officer carry tinfoil hats, headcages and a non-lethal pistol for psychics who go rogue, and a chaplain's bible is one of the few things that hurts the ghosts.

- **Take** — It gives the science department an actual round-long risk/reward dial (farm Glimmer for research points, pay for it in station-wide chaos) instead of a one-way tech tree, and it hands ordinary crew a reason to interact with science.
- **Skip** — It is a whole department's worth of content, not a feature: a job, a chem chain, machines, a PDA program, hostile mobs, holy-damage and mindshield interactions, anomaly hooks, and a psionic-potential flag that has to be stamped onto humanoid prototypes, so it lands as a permanent maintenance surface that fights every upstream merge.
- **Touches** — science, epistemics, medical, security, chaplain, service, ghost-roles, all-players
- **Needs** — [extra-job-roster](#extra-job-roster), [pda-cartridge-programs](#pda-cartridge-programs), [reagent-and-reaction-expansion](#reagent-and-reaction-expansion)
- **Verified** — partly supported. Gameplay description is very well corroborated by the fetched guidebook/locale/prototype files (glimmer meter, PDA graph, oracle oil, Psionic Mantis chemistry chain, glimmer creatures hunting and life-draining psychics, bible/holy damage, prober/drain/sacrifice/mindbreaker countermeasures, tinfoil/headcage/PsiBreaker). But the seed's 'drop-in' guess is flatly wrong: PotentialPsionicComponent is stamped directly onto genuinely upstream files - Resources/Prototypes/Body/species_base.yml, Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Mobs/Player/human.yml, and Content.Server/Cloning/CloningPodSystem.cs (all outside any _DV namespace dir) - confirming the assessor's own 'needs-upstream-edits' downgrade rather than the seed's drop-in guess.
  - unsupported: "Each psychic gets exactly one power out of a grab bag: ... setting a target on fire with a thought ..." - Pyrokinesis is NOT one of the entries in the random weighted power table (Resources/Prototypes/_DV/Psionics/psionicPowers.yml only lists Dispel, Precognition, Regeneration, Scream, Telegnosis, MassSleep, MetapsionicPulse, NoosphericZap, MindSwap - 9 entries, no Pyrokinesis). PyrokinesisPower is instead hard-attached to specific NPC/familiar prototypes (Resources/Prototypes/_DV/Entities/Mobs/NPCs/fun.yml, familiars.yml) and granted deterministically via a Psion Crystal made from Phlogiston (per the Mantis guidebook page), not drawn from the same random grab-bag every psychic rolls.

**white-dream**

*activity · entangled · medium confidence · 4 forks carry it*

This fork bolts four extra psychic powers onto an existing psionics framework. A psychic can project a private message straight into one person's head (you pick a target, type a line, and only the two of you see it pop up), split off a walking duplicate of yourself and hop back and forth between the two bodies (the copy leaves ectoplasm when it dies), take on another crewmember's face, name and description until you drop the disguise, and shove or yank objects and people around with raw force or fling yourself in the direction you're facing. The force power gets noticeably weaker if you spam it and recovers over a few seconds. Character creation also carries caster-type traits (Shadowkin, Infernal, Telekineticist, Priest) that cost trait points, are blocked for silicons and a handful of jobs, and lock you into one themed pool of powers.

- **Take** — The impersonation and body-hopping powers are strong social-deception tools that create paranoia and investigation without needing a new antag role, and the push/pull power is the most legible, immediately fun psychic ability in the set.
- **Skip** — None of it stands alone: every power plugs into a psionics/Glimmer framework, power-pool prototypes, psionic stat modifiers and trait-category plumbing that upstream does not have, so grafting this means adopting the whole psionics system first and then maintaining a shapeshifting-and-cloning power set that will fight with your forensics, records and access systems.
- **Touches** — all-players, antagonist, science, service, command
- **Needs** — [character-traits](#character-traits)
- **Verified** — supported. Read all 8 cited files plus ClonePowerSystem.cs and PolymorphPowerSystem.cs. Every gameplay beat checks out: DirectionalTelepathySystem opens a QuickDialog and popups the message only at the caster and at args.Target (private 1:1 message); ClonePowerSystem spawns a duplicate via ActionClone, mind-transfers back and forth via ActionCloneSwitch/ActionOriginalSwitch, and both OnCloneDeath and OnDispelled spawn PsionicCloneComponent.SpawnOnDeathPrototype (default 'Ectoplasm'); PolymorphPowerSystem clones the target's HumanoidAppearance, sets EntityName/EntityDescription to the target's, and ReturnAppearance restores the caster's own stored OriginalName/OriginalDescription/OriginalProfile on revert or dispel; SharedBarokinesisPowerSystem.Push/Pull/Dash use ThrowingSystem with a WeaknessThing() that lerps from MaximumWeakness to MinimumWeakness based on time since LastUsedTime versus MinimumRecovery/MaximumRecovery (10s), i.e. spamming genuinely weakens the throw and it recovers over ~10s ('a few seconds' is a mild rounding but not a real overclaim). typeCaster.yml confirms exactly Shadowkin/Infernal/Telekineticist/Priest, points -4 each, CharacterJobRequirement blocking Borg/MedicalBorg/ResearchDirector/ForensicMantis/Chaplain/Librarian/Prisoner and species-blocking IPC (silicon), each locked to one weightedRandom powerPool. On graft_shape: the claim already downgraded the drop-in seed to 'entangled' and I confirm that, more strongly than the claim itself states. Fetching the full repo tree shows every cited _White file imports from a large NON-_White 'core' psionics engine (Content.Shared/Psionics/*, Content.Server/Abilities/Psionics/*, Content.Server/Psionics/*, Resources/Prototypes/Psionics/*, Resources/Prototypes/Traits/Psionics/casterTypes.yml, plus a Content.Server/Nyanotrasen/Psionics dir showing its origin) that is not in evidence_cited and not _White-prefixed at all: PsionicComponent, SharedPsionicAbilitiesSystem, GlimmerSystem, TelepathyComponent, PsionicPowerPoolPrototype. BarokinesisPowerSystem reads PsionicComponent.CurrentAmplification directly; ClonePowerSystem and PolymorphPowerSystem both call SharedPsionicAbilitiesSystem.OnAttemptPowerUse/LogPowerUsed. This is not vanilla space-station-14 upstream code (psionics/Glimmer isn't a vanilla feature), so it isn't 'needs-upstream-edits' in the fork-patches-upstream sense, but it means the true graft unit is the whole psionics/Glimmer engine, not just this handful of _White ability files plus character-traits as depends_on implies. The claim's own skip_because prose already names 'the whole psionics system' as the real cost, so the entangled verdict is confirmed and, if anything, underscored by the code.

### Assigned roleplay imperatives

<a id="assigned-roleplay-moods"></a>

Players are handed randomly assigned behavioural rules or secret compulsions they must roleplay for the shift, surfaced in a dedicated panel and editable by admins.

**impstation, starlight**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 6 forks carry it*

At the start of the shift you get a small set of secret personal rules you have to live by, opened from a button on your action bar: things like "You must always lie and can never admit it", "Swearing is the spice of any conversation", "Disagreements must be settled through a formal duel", "You must drink any puddle you see", or "Petty theft is morally neutral". Some rules are shared by everyone who has them that round (a station-wide belief like "the station is a living being", "music is sacred", or "the cargo hamster is a god and must be brought to the chapel for offerings"), so strangers discover they share the same weird conviction and start organising around it. Most sets pair a "yes, and" compulsion with a "no, and" prohibition plus an occasional wildcard, one rule is usually "never reveal your rules", and admins can open the same panel to hand out, edit, or reroll someone's rules mid-round.

- **Take** — It is a huge amount of ready-written roleplay content (well over a hundred authored compulsions across four themed pools) sitting on a small, generic framework, and it changes how the whole shift feels without touching any existing mechanic.
- **Skip** — Almost every shipped mood is written in-fiction for Impstation's Thaven species ("Thaven pay close attention to appearances", "congregate with your fellow Thaven"), so grafting it means either importing that species too or rewriting the entire content pack; and it only pays off on a server whose players will actually roleplay a rule they can hide, since nothing in the code enforces compliance.
- **Touches** — all-players, security, command, service, admin-tooling
- **Verified** — partly supported. All 9 cited evidence files, plus the species file I found (thaven.yml), live entirely under _Impstation namespaced paths — the fork attaches StrangeMoodsComponent to its own custom Thaven species prototype via YAML inheritance (parent: BaseMobSpeciesOrganic) rather than by editing the upstream base file itself, so the fork's own copy is self-contained. But I confirmed upstream Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Mobs/Species/human.yml has no StrangeMoods component, meaning the mechanic is currently wired only to the fork-added Thaven species: grafting it onto another fork's actual playable species (e.g. honksquad's human) would require adding the component to that fork's own upstream mob prototype, which is an upstream edit even though the graft's own file set is clean.
  - unsupported: "At the start of the shift you get a small set of secret personal rules" implies this applies broadly to players/the round in general; the actual code gates the StrangeMoods component behind the fork's own Thaven species prototype (Resources/Prototypes/_Impstation/Entities/Mobs/Species/thaven.yml) and the upstream human.yml has no such component, so in practice only Thaven characters receive moods, not the crew at large.
  - unsupported: "admins can open the same panel to hand out, edit, or reroll someone's rules mid-round" — no admin verb/EUI file was found among the cited evidence or nearby guessed paths; the only trace is a code comment '# ADMIN TOOL MOODS' next to EmptyMoods/ThavenMoodsEmpty prototypes in strange.yml, which is suggestive but does not confirm the specific admin UI/workflow described.
  - unsupported: "the cargo hamster is a god" is presented as a concrete example, but the actual locale string is a templated `{$pet} Is A God` line; no dataset file confirming 'cargo hamster' as one of the substituted pet values was found among the cited/guessed paths.
