### Player factions and corporations

<a id="player-corporations"></a>

Players belong to a company or faction prototype that gates access, equipment and radio channels, with faction-aware readers and admin tooling.

**monolith**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 1 forks carry it*

At character setup you pick which company or faction your character works for, from a roster of roughly thirty: industrial giants, medical suppliers, arms dealers, mercenary outfits, religious cults and outright criminal syndicates, each with its own logo, name colour and a page of in-fiction background. Your company follows you into the round: it shows on your ID and in examine text, and company-locked doors, lockers and machines slam shut with "Access Denied: invalid company biometrics" if you are not on the list, while some companies spend their own currency at uplinks instead of the standard one. Some jobs force a company on you automatically, and prestigious or lore-heavy factions are locked behind an admin whitelist, so an admin has to add you to a company before you can play as one.

- **Take** — It gives every player a persistent chosen allegiance that actually does something mechanically (access gating, ID/examine identity, per-faction uplink currency) rather than being pure flavour text, and the whitelist commands make it usable for admin-curated lore factions on day one.
- **Skip** — The roster is almost entirely Monolith's own Colossus Sector setting (TSF, PDV, USSP Remnants, dozens of named PMCs), so you get an empty framework unless you write your own faction fiction, and the company field lives on the character profile and reads a company off the upstream job prototype, so it cannot land without touching character creation, profile save/load and job prototypes.
- **Touches** — all-players, security, command, antagonist, ghost-roles
- **Verified** — partly supported. Core mechanics check out against the actual code: CompanyPrototype has Color/Description/Image/Disabled/Whitelisted/CompanyUplinkCurrency fields, CompanySystem.cs writes the company onto the player's ID card and JobPrototype.AssignedCompany force-assigns a company per job, whitelist-commands.ftl and companies.yml's `whitelisted: true` entries (Winter Solstice, Cerberus, Viper Group, RedSail, PLXCOR) confirm admin-gated lore factions, and TSF/PDV each have their own companyUplinkCurrency (FederationMilitaryCredit/Doubloon). Crucially, I confirmed the fork edits Content.Shared/Preferences/HumanoidCharacterProfile.cs and Content.Shared/Roles/JobPrototype.cs in place to add the Company field/AssignedCompany property — real upstream-directory files carrying this feature's logic that were NOT in evidence_cited, which directly validates the claim's graft_shape downgrade to needs-upstream-edits over the seed's drop-in guess. But several specifics overclaim: companies.yml has ~26 live entries (not ~30), and 7 of those are disabled/admin-only (TSF, PDV, MD, Colonial, TSFHighComm, USSP, MMC), leaving only ~19 a player can actually pick at character creation; the two explicitly cult-named companies (Zealots of Balaam, Cult of the Machine God) are commented out of the prototype file entirely, leaving "religious cults" represented by a single ambiguous entry (The Hive); and per-company lore is a one-paragraph .ftl description plus an optional Image field (several entries like AetherionDynamics, CivilDefenseMilita, TheHive, paycheckbratva have no image at all) rather than each company getting "a page" — only the top-level factions (PDV, TSF, Minor Factions) get dedicated guidebook XML pages.
  - unsupported: from a roster of roughly thirty
  - unsupported: religious cults and outright criminal syndicates
  - unsupported: each with its own logo, name colour and a page of in-fiction background

## Jobs

### Extra jobs and roles

<a id="extra-job-roster"></a>

Additional crew job entries with their own gear, icons, access and playtime trackers, from senior variants to wildcard and CentComm roles.

**rmc14**

*structural · entangled · high confidence · 7 forks carry it*

Instead of a station crew list, you pick from a marine unit's roster: commanding officer, executive and staff officers, senior enlisted advisor, intelligence officer, dropship and gunship pilots, crew chiefs and support crew, each slotted into a military chain of command with a stated supervisor and an authority level that decides who can lawfully give you orders. Your character joins with a rank tied to how many hours you have logged in that role (a dropship pilot starts as a warrant officer and works up to second lieutenant), wears a rank prefix in front of their name, spawns in role-specific uniform and kit, and gets a point budget to spend at the unit's supply vendors. Senior roles unlock only after long playtime across other departments, and command roles announce themselves to the whole crew on arrival, hand out commendations, see intel objectives, and show up as their own labelled blip on the tactical map.

- **Take** — It is a fully worked example of a rank-and-chain-of-command roster: playtime gates that ladder across departments, in-name rank prefixes, per-role authority levels and supervisors, and role-specific spawn kits, all expressed in readable per-job files.
- **Skip** — These jobs are not crew jobs at all, they are USCM marine roles that only make sense on RMC-14's dropship-and-planet round; every single one leans on that fork's skills, ranks, squads, marine vendors and tactical map, so grafting one job means grafting several large systems and then rewriting the job itself to mean anything on a space station.
- **Touches** — command, security, cargo, engineering, medical, all-players
- **Needs** — [squads-ranks-and-skills](#squads-ranks-and-skills), [vending-and-loot-catalogs](#vending-and-loot-catalogs), [access-control-rework](#access-control-rework)
- **Verified** — supported. Fetched all 5 cited files plus 4 more (gunship_pilot.yml, dropship_crew_chief.yml, staff_officer.yml, executive_officer.yml, all HTTP 200) to check the roster claim. Every specific mechanic the claim describes is directly present in the YAML: JobPrefix (rank prefix), ranks: blocks with RoleTimeRequirement hour thresholds (dropship pilot literally starts at RMCRankWarrantOfficer: [] and ladders to RMCRankChiefWarrantOfficer at 25h then RMCRankSecondLT at 70h, matching 'starts as warrant officer, works up to second lieutenant' exactly), CMVendorUser with a points value (supply-vendor budget), multi-department DepartmentTimeRequirement/TotalJobsTimeRequirement gating for senior roles (commanding_officer.yml spans CMSquad/CMMilitaryPolice/CMMedical/CMCommand/CMRequisitions/CMEngineering), joinNotifyCrew: true plus CommendationGiver/RMCAwardRecommendation on command roles, ViewIntelObjectives, TacticalMapIcon per-job blips, marineAuthorityLevel and supervisors fields (chain of command). The claim's downgrade from the seed's 'drop-in' to 'entangled' is itself well-founded: the same files show heavy component-level coupling to other fork subsystems (Skills/ranks, CMVendorUser vending, AssignSquad/SquadArmorWearer squads, accessGroups access control) that the depends_on list names correctly, even though those dependent files may live inside the same _RMC14 namespace (so the narrow 'zero files outside namespace' path signal was technically true but misleading about actual graftability).

**starlight**

*activity · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 7 forks carry it*

Adds a long list of extra jobs you can pick at the lobby screen, each with its own title, outfit, ID access and a one-line "here is your job" blurb. Station-side additions include a Magistrate and Internal Affairs Agent who put crew on trial, a Blueshield Officer who bodyguards the heads instead of doing normal security work, a Duty Officer who runs the prison wing under the Warden, a Mail Technician who delivers packages for cargo cash, a Mining Specialist who works the salvage magnet without leaving the station, a Salvage Lead who runs the salvage team, a Surgeon, Roboticist, Zookeeper, Performer and Boxer. On top of that sit CentComm and military roles (NanoTrasen Representative, Greenshield and Navy Corps bodyguards, NTSF and Decimus operatives, CentComm chef/bartender/janitor/service worker), most of which are locked out of the normal roster and spawned in by admins, arrive in heavy gear with mindshield implants, and are told in their briefing that they serve NanoTrasen or Central Command rather than the crew. Many roles are gated behind playtime in a related job or department, so the lobby screen tells you how many hours you still need before you can pick one.

- **Take** — It is the cheapest way to add roster variety: each job is a self-contained YAML file with gear, access and playtime gates, and you can cherry-pick just the two or three roles you want without taking the rest.
- **Skip** — The roles only exist if the station map has spawn points and job slots for them, so every map you run needs editing, and the CentComm/military half drags in a large pile of custom uniforms, hardsuits, PDAs, weapons and job icons that do not come from upstream.
- **Touches** — cargo, security, command, service, medical, science, ghost-roles, all-players
- **Needs** — [clothing-and-wardrobe-pack](#clothing-and-wardrobe-pack), [department-restructure](#department-restructure)
- **Verified** — partly supported. All nine cited files check out and the specific gameplay claims (Blueshield 'not a security officer', Duty Officer under the Warden, Mining Specialist staying station-side, playtime-gated requirements with hour displays, cc-aligned briefing text 'you do NOT serve the crew') are near-verbatim matches to the fetched .ftl/.yml content. Critically, I went beyond the cited evidence and fetched Resources/Prototypes/Roles/Jobs/departments.yml (NOT under _Starlight/) — it is directly edited in place with new job IDs (MailTech, MiningSpecialist, Performer, Zookeeper, CentralCommandGreenShield, Magistrate, NanoTrasenRepresentative, Surgeon, DutyOfficer, Roboticist) each tagged with comments like '# Starlight Addition' / '# Starlight-edit'. This proves the unit genuinely touches a shared upstream-path file to become playable, confirming the claim's downgrade from the seed's 'drop-in' to 'needs-upstream-edits' — and if anything the claim understates it, since the fork itself (not just a future integration) already patches that file.
  - unsupported: "most of which are locked out of the normal roster and spawned in by admins... arrive in heavy gear with mindshield implants" generalizes across the whole CentComm/military role list, but only one of those job files (greenshield.yml) was actually fetched and confirmed (setPreference: false, AddImplantSpecial MindShieldImplant, SMG/energy-magnum gear). NanoTrasen Representative, IAA, Decimus, NTSF, ntncblueshield, and the CentComm chef/bartender/janitor/service-worker jobs were not individually checked for the same setPreference/implant/gear pattern.

### Character loadouts

<a id="loadout-system"></a>

Per-job character loadout groups letting players pick starting clothing and items at setup, with item groups capping how many picks come from each pool.

**frontier**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 9 forks carry it*

In character setup, each job gets its own slot-by-slot wardrobe menu: jumpsuit or jumpskirt, hat, coat, badge, gloves, shoes, mask, glasses, backpack, belt, plus functional picks like PDA cartridges, encryption keys, a survival box, a wallet, implanters, in-hand items and even an emotional support pet. Picks are drawn against a spending budget shown as "Total Loadout Cost" and "Available Balance", so a player trades a fancy coat against a useful gadget rather than taking everything. The menu quietly hides options your character cannot use ("That item is not permitted for your role", "not permitted for your sex"), and species-aware filtering means a Diona is never offered shoes and a Vox is never offered the wrong breathing gear, while mandatory items like your job PDA and ID badge are auto-assigned without cluttering the list.

- **Take** — It turns the loadout screen from cosmetic dress-up into a real pre-round choice: a budget plus role/species/sex filters means players pick starting kit they will actually use, and every job can be given a curated wardrobe without handing out free gear.
- **Skip** — Nearly all 192 prototype files are wardrobes for Frontier-only jobs (Bailiff, Brigmedic, Contractor, Mercenary, Pilot, Mail Carrier, Traffic Controller, Valet, Sheriff) wearing Frontier-only clothing, so what actually ports is the effects-and-price framework, and you then write every job's wardrobe yourself and re-curate it each time a job or an item set changes.
- **Touches** — all-players, security, medical, service, command, cargo
- **Needs** — [extra-job-roster](#extra-job-roster), [clothing-and-wardrobe-pack](#clothing-and-wardrobe-pack), [extra-playable-species](#extra-playable-species)
- **Verified** — supported. The gameplay description is well supported: loadouts.ftl confirms the "Total Loadout Cost"/"Available Balance" budget strings, loadout-effects.ftl confirms the exact role/sex rejection messages quoted, loadout-groups.ftl lists the same slot vocabulary (backpack items, hand items, encryption keys, survival box, cartridges, wallet, implanters, emotional-support animals), loadout_effects.yml shows real species-gated groups (ShoesCapableNF excludes Diona, NFNitrogenBreather/NFOxygenBreather gate Vox/SlimePerson), and bailiff_loadout_groups.yml shows a PDA group marked hidden with "gets auto-selected" — matching the auto-assigned-badge/PDA claim. But the graft_shape claim is more right than the assessor even argued: fetching Content.Shared/Clothing/LoadoutSystem.cs and Content.Shared/Preferences/Loadouts/RoleLoadout.cs (both outside any _NF directory, i.e. shared/upstream namespace) shows explicit "// Frontier: ..." / "// End Frontier" edit markers wrapping extra fields, hidden-loadout/fallback logic, and subgroup checks — meaning Frontier's own repo copy patches the core loadout engine files in place, not just adds _NF prototype data on top of an untouched upstream system. None of these non-_NF core files were in the cited evidence list, so the claim under-cited the strongest reason this is needs-upstream-edits (it undersold its own case) while still landing on the correct verdict via a different, weaker argument (mostly-Frontier-only wardrobe prototypes).
  - unsupported: Evidence citation issue (not a gameplay overclaim): Resources/Locale/en-US/_NF/preferences/ui/humanoid-profile-editor.ftl was cited as evidence but its full content is only 'humanoid-profile-editor-preference-messenger = Messenger' and 'trait-category-height = Body' — it contains nothing about loadouts and does not back any claim in the text.

**serbia-strong**

*cosmetic · entangled · high confidence · 9 forks carry it*

At character setup each job gets its own list of wardrobe slots to fill in: a captain picks between two headset styles and white or black gloves, a salvager chooses which hard hat and jumpsuit to spawn in, a clown picks a classic suit, a Pennywise outfit or a gold one. Some of the fancier options stay greyed out until you have logged enough hours in that specific role (30, 50, 70 hours for salvage variants; 5 or 50 hours for clown outfits), and a large slice of them are reserved for donators, so the setup screen doubles as a visible progression ladder. Separately, every character spawns with cash tucked in their bag scaled to how senior the job is, roughly 250 spesos for a civilian job, 500 for a technical one and 700 for command, so people have spending money for vendors from the first minute of the round.

- **Take** — It is a huge, ready-made per-job wardrobe catalogue that makes the character setup screen feel personal without touching a single round mechanic, and the playtime-gated variants give returning players something to unlock.
- **Skip** — Almost every entry hangs a sponsor-tier effect off itself and points at fork-only clothing entities, so grafting it means importing SS220's donator system and its whole sprite wardrobe first; the loadout files also have to be wired into upstream job prototypes, and the SS220 files carry a CLA with a hosting restriction rather than a plain permissive licence.

- **Needs** — [sponsor-and-donator-perks](#sponsor-and-donator-perks), [clothing-and-wardrobe-pack](#clothing-and-wardrobe-pack)
- **Verified** — supported. Every substantive detail checks out against the raw files: clown.yml has RoleTimeRequirement gates at exactly 18000s (5h) and 180000s (50h) for the Pennywise/Classic clown variants; salvage_specialist.yml has RoleTimeRequirement gates at 108000/180000/252000 (30/50/70h) exactly as claimed; cash_loadouts.yml defines SpaceCash250/500/700 tied to CivilianCash/WorkerCash/SeniorStaffCash loadout groups matching the civilian/technical/command tiers described; loadout_groups.yml shows CaptainGloves (CaptainGloves + CaptainWhiteGloves) and CAPHeadset (CaptainHeadset + CaptainHeadsetAlt), matching "two headset styles and white or black gloves"; the touches list (command, security, cargo, service, medical, engineering) all appear in loadout_groups.yml. The CLA.txt I fetched directly confirms "hosting restriction" language (prohibits commercial use and public hosting without SS220's permission) so that specific claim is accurate, not embellishment. On graft_shape: the seed's "drop-in" was a raw path-containment signal, and the assessor correctly downgraded it. Sponsor-tier group definitions (BigShlopaSponsorTier, GoldenShlopaSponsorTier, SeniorDevTeamTier, etc.) do live in a sibling file in the same Loadouts folder (sponsor_tier_requirements.yml), so namespace containment holds narrowly, but nearly every job file (clown, mime, lawyer, salvage) hangs multiple loadout entries off these sponsor-tier requirements and off entity IDs (ClothingSponsorGoldClownSuit, ClothingUniformJumpsuitMoryak, etc.) that are not among the cited evidence and are almost certainly defined in a separate SS220 clothing/entities tree, plus the underlying SponsorTierRequirementLoadoutEffect mechanism implies a live donator/account-status backend, not just static YAML. That is a real, verifiable in-practice entanglement even though it doesn't show up as "files outside the namespace directory" in a naive path scan, which is exactly the gap the assessor's downgrade is describing.

**starlight**

*cosmetic · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 9 forks carry it*

At character setup every job gets a long list of wardrobe and kit slots, and you pick what you spawn wearing: jumpsuit or jumpskirt variant, hat, cloak or mantle, shoes, gloves, scarf, tie, mask, pen, backpack, instrument and a pocket trinket. A lot of the nicer options are locked behind hours played in that specific role, so a clown who has put in six hours unlocks the spotted and performer suits and a fifteen-hour clown unlocks the formal ones, while assistants earn a grey mantle at ten hours and the "head of assistants" mantle at twenty. A handful of slots hand out working gear rather than looks, so security officers choose their starting sidearm and non-lethal, engineers choose which insulated gloves they carry, and brigmedics choose their beaker; the same picker also dresses fork-only roles like Blueshield, Magistrate, NT Representative and Duty Officer, and even the Brighteye antag chooses its rags and cloak.

- **Take** — Upstream already ships the loadout engine, so this is almost pure content: dozens of per-job wardrobe groups plus playtime-gated unlocks that give veterans something visible to earn without adding a single new system.
- **Skip** — It is roughly 53 YAML files whose options point at Starlight's own clothing prototypes and its own job roster (Blueshield, Magistrate, NCT, Duty Officer, Mining Specialist, Salvage Lead), so most of it will not resolve unless you take that wardrobe and those jobs too, and the shared-job files still need the upstream roleLoadout entries edited to list the new groups.
- **Touches** — all-players, security, cargo, medical, science, engineering, command, service, antagonist
- **Needs** — [extra-job-roster](#extra-job-roster), [clothing-and-wardrobe-pack](#clothing-and-wardrobe-pack)

But I also pulled the actual vanilla file Resources/Prototypes/Loadouts/RoleLoadouts/role_loadouts.yml (693 lines, no _Starlight in path) and found it directly edited in place with dozens of scattered '# Starlight' tagged additions (SecuritySidearm/SecurityNonLethalWeapon on JobSecurityOfficer, Insuls on JobChiefEngineer, Scarves/Pins/Pens on nearly every job in the game). This proves the needs-upstream-edits classification is right, and specifically it is fork-patches-upstream, not merely a hypothetical integration cost as the claim's skip_because implies ('the shared-job files still need the upstream roleLoadout entries edited') — the fork's own tree already carries this entanglement pervasively across almost the entire vanilla loadout file, which is a larger and messier footprint than the claim's framing of 'a handful of shared-job files' suggests.

### Silicon lawsets and AI appearance

<a id="ai-lawsets-and-appearance"></a>

Extra silicon lawsets, per-job or per-module law assignment, physical lawboard swapping and selectable AI hologram and core-screen appearances.

**cosmatic-drift**

*cosmetic · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 5 forks carry it*

The station AI gets a much bigger wardrobe: 10 extra hologram bodies it can project when it talks to the crew (an alien, a swarm of bees, an oversized moth, a ghost, a shapeless horror, drifting leaves, Nar'Sie, Ratvar, and a couple of abstract forms) and 27 extra faces for the display on its core and its cameras (thinking, database, firewall, matrix, rainbow, monochrome, static, a cat, the Nanotrasen logo, a "not malf" smiley, a presidential face, an evil red dot, and so on). Each core face has a matching cracked/dead version, so when the AI is destroyed the crew sees its chosen face go dark rather than a generic broken screen. It is purely a look: the AI still picks its appearance the same way it already does, there are just far more options in the list.

- **Take** — The AI is one of the most visible characters on the station and upstream ships only a handful of appearances, so 37 extra holograms and core faces is a large amount of player-facing personality for zero mechanical risk.
- **Skip** — The prototypes are just pointers: the value lives in two RSI sprite sheets and a locale file that must come with them, several designs are lifted from other codebases (Nar'Sie, Ratvar, Goon, Hades), so you inherit an attribution and licensing chore for art that changes nothing about how a round plays.
- **Touches** — silicon, command, all-players
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as drop-in, corrected by the verifier. I fetched both cited prototype files and confirmed 10 holograms + 27 icons with the claimed names, and CD's StationAiCustomization C# files are byte-identical to upstream so the system itself is not forked. But StationAiCustomizationGroupPrototype requires an explicit ProtoIds list, and CD registers its prototypes by patching upstream Resources/Prototypes/AppearanceCustomization/station_ai.yml (diff shows a "# CD changes from here" block appending all 37 IDs), so the unit is not drop-in: the fork copy itself patches an upstream file, and a graft needs the same small upstream YAML edit. The dead-face claim is also wrong for roughly half the icons, which fall back to the generic ai_dead sprite.
  - unsupported: "Each core face has a matching cracked/dead version, so when the AI is destroyed the crew sees its chosen face go dark rather than a generic broken screen." — false for 13 of the 27 icons (Firewall, Fuzzy, Helios, Inverted, Matrix, NanoTrasen, NotMalf, President, Red, Meow, Text, TooDeep, Triumvirate): their Dead layer points at upstream Mobs/Silicon/station_ai.rsi state ai_dead, i.e. the generic broken screen.
  - unsupported: "27 extra faces for the display on its core and its cameras" — the prototypes define only Occupied/Dead layer data for the AI core; nothing in the cited files shows the faces appearing on cameras.
  - unsupported: "there are just far more options in the list" implies the options simply exist as new files; in reality they only enter the list because the fork edits the upstream group file Resources/Prototypes/AppearanceCustomization/station_ai.yml to append all 37 prototype IDs.

**goobstation**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 5 forks carry it*

Adds a programmable law board: you click it open, type your own laws into a list (up to 15 laws, 512 characters each), then slot it into the AI upload console to overwrite the station AI's or a borg's entire lawset with text you wrote yourself. There are two versions: a freeform NanoTrasen board that command can buy and fill with anything, and a Syndicate "experimental" board sold in the traitor uplink that comes pre-loaded with Antimov and plays an ominous upload jingle. It also adds joke and role-flavoured lawsets to the pool, such as Helpimov (the first person who talks to the AI becomes "the courier" and the AI must agree with and obey them) and Gambamov (the AI must gamble constantly, protect its gambling, and insist it is not an addiction), plus short "you must heal the crew" / "repair the station" / "clean the station" / "mine materials" style law lines for department-themed lawsets.

- **Take** — A freeform law board turns the AI from a fixed-lawset NPC-ish role into whatever the crew (or a traitor) writes that shift, which is the single biggest lever on how an AI round plays, and the joke lawsets give the same payoff cheaply.
- **Skip** — Player-authored law text goes straight into everyone's chat and law screen with only newline stripping and a length clamp, so it is an unmoderated free-text broadcast channel your admins now have to police; the "AI appearance" half of the catalogue feature is not in this fork's files at all.
- **Touches** — silicon, command, antagonist, science, all-players
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as drop-in, corrected by the verifier. The custom-lawboard upload path is a Goob edit inside the upstream file Content.Server/Silicons/Laws/SiliconLawSystem.cs (OnUpdaterInsert branches on CustomLawboardComponent), and the Helpimov/Gambamov pool weights live in the upstream-path Resources/Prototypes/silicon-laws.yml, so the fork's own copy patches upstream files and a graft would need equivalent edits; without them the board uploads its dummy Crewsimov lawset and the joke lawsets never enter the random pool.
  - unsupported: "a freeform NanoTrasen board that command can buy" — NTCustomLawboard is referenced in no cargo product, store, or catalog file anywhere in the repo (code search hits only its own prototype file); it has a StaticPrice of 5000 and BaseCommandContraband parentage, which makes it legal for command to possess, but no purchase route is shown
  - unsupported: "comes pre-loaded with Antimov and plays an ominous upload jingle" (attributed to the Syndicate board) — the upload sound (/Audio/Ambience/Antag/emagged_borg.ogg) is set on the shared abstract BaseCustomLawboard, so the NT freeform board plays the same jingle; it is not a Syndicate-board feature

**harmony-station**

*cosmetic · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 5 forks carry it*

A player taking the Station AI gets extra looks to pick from: the face on the AI core screen can be a house, a lizard, a xeno queen or a creeping blob, and the hologram it projects into holopads can be a xenomorph instead of the default. It also adds an eight-law "Orwellian" lawset in which the Captain is Big Brother, Command is the Inner Party and Security is the Thought Police, the AI is told to report "thought criminals" for re-education in perma, to insist Big Brother has never been wrong about anything, and to ignore orders from anyone outside the Inner Party. The files here only define the lawset and the skins, so how a round actually hands the AI those laws (ion storm, a lawboard, an admin) is not shown.

- **Take** — Very small, self-contained flavour: a handful of AI skins plus one genuinely fun roleplay lawset that turns a normal AI round into a paranoid surveillance state without touching any mechanics.
- **Skip** — It is content with no delivery mechanism in these files, so the Orwellian lawset only ever appears if your fork already has ion storms or a lawboard that can roll it, and the appearance entries are useless without also copying Harmony's AI sprite sheets.
- **Touches** — silicon, command, security, all-players
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as drop-in, corrected by the verifier. I fetched all five cited files and they match the described skins and eight Orwellian laws nearly verbatim, but I also fetched Harmony's copy of upstream Resources/Prototypes/AppearanceCustomization/station_ai.yml and found the fork's own '# Harmony Addition' edits wiring the skins into the customization groups — required for them to show in the UI — so the unit both patches upstream in the fork and would need the same upstream edit to integrate elsewhere. The Orwellian lawset is additionally inert without the OrwellianCircuitBoard lawboard defined in a _Harmony file outside this unit (and it is not in Harmony's IonStormLawsets pool).

Upstream only shows skins listed in those groups, so grafting the _Harmony files alone produces skins that never appear in the picker.

### Role slot management and join queue

<a id="role-slots-and-join-queue"></a>

Runtime control over who can take which role: opening and closing job slots mid-round, whitelist and playtime gating, a readied-jobs manifest and a queue for full servers.

**rmc14**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 6 forks carry it*

On a busy server more of the roles that matter scale up: the number of open slots for medics, doctors, military police, staff officers, cargo techs, intel officers, weapons and smartgun specialists, cooks and vehicle crew is recalculated from the live player count, clamped between a per-role floor and ceiling (for example medics run 3 to 5 per squad, MPs 4 to 8 station-wide), and squad-tagged roles get their allowance per squad rather than once for the whole station. Players also get a playtime window that lists every role they have played, broken out by department with department and overall totals, sortable by role or hours, and awards a tiered medal icon next to each role once you cross the hour thresholds (bronze up through prismatic, with xeno roles using their own upgrade icons instead). Admins can hand-wave a specific player past the playtime requirement for a specific role.

- **Take** — Population-scaled job slots fix the two ends of the curve at once: a 20-player round is not drowning in command staff, and a 100-player round is not stuck with two doctors, and the whole rule set is one YAML block of factor/min/max per job.
- **Skip** — The shipped tuning is entirely CM-specific job ids and the per-squad multiplier assumes a squad system, so you inherit an empty config you must re-derive for your own roster; the playtime medal half is a separate cosmetic feature bolted into the same unit and drags in a fork medal field on the job prototype.
- **Touches** — all-players, command, medical, security, cargo, service, admin
- **Needs** — [squads-ranks-and-skills](#squads-ranks-and-skills)
- **Verified** — supported. Every specific in the gameplay text checks out against the fetched files: rmc_job_slot_scaling.yml has exactly the roles named with the exact numbers claimed (CMHospitalCorpsman min:3/max:5/squad:true = "medics 3 to 5 per squad"; CMMilitaryPolice min:4/max:8 with no squad flag = "MPs 4 to 8 station-wide"); JobSlotScaling.cs/RMCStationJobsSystem.cs implement the clamp(marines/factor+c, min, max) curve; CMDistressSignalRuleSystem.Spawning.cs applies per-squad allowances via SquadTeamComponent/_squad.SetSquadMaxRole, confirming the squads-ranks-and-skills dependency the claim already lists; RMCPlaytimeStatsWindow.cs implements department/general tabs, per-department and overall totals, role/playtime sortable headers, and an 8-tier bronze-to-prismatic medal lookup with a separate xeno icon branch exactly as described; ExcludeRoleTimerCommand.cs is the admin toolshed command that lets an admin exclude one player from one job's playtime requirement. On graft_shape: the seed's 'drop-in' is refuted, and the claim's own downgrade to needs-upstream-edits is correct — I found Content.Server/Station/Components/StationJobsComponent.cs (a real upstream-namespace file, not under _RMC14) carrying an added `JobSlotScaling` field that references the RMC prototype, and confirmed against vanilla space-wizards/space-station-14's copy of the same file that this field does not exist upstream. A second instance, Content.Client/Players/PlayTimeTracking/JobRequirementsManager.cs (also upstream-namespaced), has an RMC14-tagged method (`FetchPlaytimeJobIdByRoles`) added directly into it. Both are genuine in-place edits of upstream files living in the fork's own tree, not merely a theoretical integration cost.

**cosmatic-drift**

*loop-change · drop-in · medium confidence · 6 forks carry it*

Command gets a "Job Slots Console" they can walk up to and use mid-round: a searchable list of every job on the station, each row showing the job's icon, its name and how many slots are still open, with plus and minus buttons to open another seat or close one off. So the Head of Personnel can add a second engineer slot when the department is drowning, or shut the last security slot so no more latejoiners can take it. Certain jobs are locked and just show a "this job's slots cannot be adjusted" tooltip, and using the console without the right ID access gets you a rejection buzz instead. Separately, on the join side the server can reserve seats for whitelisted players: once the general (non-whitelist) slots are all taken, an unwhitelisted player trying to connect is told the open slots are currently full and to try rejoining later.

- **Take** — Gives command a real in-world lever over station staffing instead of leaving the latejoin roster fixed at round start, and the whitelist-slot condition lets a busy server keep seats for its regulars without hard-closing the door.
- **Skip** — The unit ships no prototypes at all, so the console entity, its machine board and its placement in an office have to be authored and mapped in yourself before a player ever sees it, and handing HoP the power to close job slots invites round-souring griefing that you then have to write policy for.
- **Touches** — command, all-players, server-operators
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. Every file touched by this feature — C# (Server/Client/Shared), locale, prototypes, and even the maps that place the console — lives under _CD namespaces/directories; nothing outside the fork's own tree was found for it. The whitelist half plugs into an upstream extension point (WhitelistCondition is `[ImplicitDataDefinitionForInheritors]` in vanilla space-wizards/space-station-14, confirmed by fetching the same path from upstream) rather than editing an upstream file. The claim's downgrade to needs-upstream-edits rested on the false premise that no prototypes ship; a git tree/grep of the actual repo shows a full entity+board+flatpack+map chain already exists, so the seed's drop-in path-data read was actually correct here.
  - unsupported: "The unit ships no prototypes at all, so the console entity, its machine board and its placement in an office have to be authored and mapped in yourself before a player ever sees it" — false. The fork ships a complete, wired entity prototype (Resources/Prototypes/_CD/Entities/Structures/Machines/Computers/computers.yml, id ComputerJobSlots, parent BaseComputerAiAccess, AccessReader restricted to HeadOfPersonnel, JobSlotsConsole component with a real blacklist), a matching circuitboard (Resources/Prototypes/_CD/Entities/Objects/Devices/Circuitboards/computer.yml, id JobSlotsComputerCircuitboard), a portable flatpack variant (Resources/Prototypes/_CD/Entities/Objects/Devices/flatpack.yml, id JobSlotsComputerFlatpack) and a tabletop variant (tabletopcomputer.yml, ComputerTabletopJobSlots) — and it is already placed on three of the fork's live station maps (Resources/Maps/_CD/cluster.yml, gemini.yml, aspid.yml).

**harmony-station**

*cosmetic · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 6 forks carry it*

When the server is already at its player cap, you are no longer bounced with a "server full" rejection. Instead you connect and land on a dedicated Server Queue screen showing the station's logo and name, your position in line, and how many people are waiting, with a Disconnect button if you would rather not wait. When a slot frees up you are pulled in automatically and a ping sound plays as the game loads. Admins and whitelisted/privileged players skip the line entirely, and admins in-game see a chat notice each time someone joins the queue.

- **Take** — Turns a hard "server full" bounce into a waiting room that fills empty slots the instant someone leaves, so a popular server stops leaking players who would have come back if they could just hold a spot.
- **Skip** — It only matters on a server that regularly hits its soft cap; below that it is dead code, and it still needs upstream connection-handling and client state-switching patches plus ongoing maintenance through every upstream connection-flow change.
- **Touches** — all-players, admins
- **Verified** — partly supported. Fetched all five cited files plus Content.Server/Entry/EntryPoint.cs and Content.Client/Entry/EntryPoint.cs. Content.Server/Connection/ConnectionManager.cs (an upstream directory, not _Harmony) is directly patched in three places with '// Harmony Queue Start/End' markers (interface method, soft-cap gating logic, HasPrivilegedJoin implementation), and both EntryPoint.cs files are patched with '// Harmony' lines to construct/Initialize the queue manager. This is the fork's own committed copy already containing edited upstream files, which is exactly why the claim correctly downgraded the seed's 'drop-in' to 'needs-upstream-edits' rather than accepting the seed at face value.
  - unsupported: "Admins and whitelisted/privileged players skip the line entirely" — the code only shows two bypass paths in HasPrivilegedJoin(): an admin with the queue.enable-independent AdminBypassMaxPlayers CVar set, or a session that was already PlayerGameStatus.JoinedGame (a reconnect). There is no whitelist-status check anywhere in the queue-skip path; the only whitelist-related CVar found (BypassBunkerWhitelist) belongs to the separate panic-bunker system, not the join queue.

**impstation**

*activity · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 6 forks carry it*

While sitting in the lobby waiting for the round to start, you can open a "ready manifest" window that lists every job by department alongside how many readied players have picked it as a top choice, with unpicked jobs highlighted in red and the counts ticking up and down live as people ready and unready. It lets you see that nobody has taken a doctor or an engineer this round and switch your own pick to cover the gap before roll time. Separately, antagonist roles can be grouped so that time played in any one of them counts toward unlocking the others: hours as a nuclear operative also count toward the operative medic and commander, and if you are still short the game tells you exactly how many more minutes you need in that colour-coded group.

- **Take** — The ready manifest is a cheap, self-contained fix for the classic "round starts with zero medics" problem, letting players self-organise staffing before the shift instead of discovering the gap ten minutes in.
- **Skip** — It is not purely additive: the manifest needs a button wired into the upstream lobby UI and a ready-toggle event the upstream game ticker does not raise, and the antag-group timers only do anything once you edit your existing antag role prototypes to use them, so the useful half of the feature is upstream patching plus per-role balance decisions you then have to maintain across every upstream sync.
- **Touches** — all-players, antagonist, command, medical, security, engineering, cargo, science, service
- **Verified** — partly supported. Sparse-cloned the impstation repo and read the actual upstream files, not just the fork-namespaced ones. Content.Server/GameTicking/GameTicker.Lobby.cs (an upstream file) has `RaiseLocalEvent(new PlayerToggleReadyEvent(player)); //imp edit, for preround ready manifest` inserted into the existing ToggleReady/ToggleReadyAll methods, and the PlayerToggleReadyEvent class itself is nested inside that same upstream file — it does not exist in vanilla space-station-14 (confirmed via Sourcegraph: 0 matches). Content.Client/Lobby/LobbyState.cs (upstream) is edited with `//imp` markers to hold a ReadyManifestSystem field, wire `Lobby!.ManifestButton.OnPressed += OnManifestPressed`, and call `_readyManifest.RequestReadyManifest()`. Content.Client/Lobby/UI/LobbyGui.xaml (upstream) has a new `<Button Name=\"ManifestButton\" ... Text=\"Manifest\">` added to the existing lobby layout. This is unambiguous: the fork's own tree contains modified upstream files (fork-patches-upstream), and grafting this feature into a different codebase would require the identical edits (integration-would-require-upstream-edits) — both readings hold simultaneously. This directly falsifies the path-data \"drop-in\" seed and matches the claim's own \"needs-upstream-edits\" / skip_because reasoning almost exactly. The antag-group half (antag_groups.yml Nukies group + AntagGroupTimeRequirement.cs summing playtime across grouped roles, with a color-coded shortfall message) is also fully corroborated and is genuinely additive (no upstream edits needed there), matching the claim.
  - unsupported: "alongside how many readied players have picked it as a top choice" — FilterPlayerJobs in ReadyManifestSystem.cs actually counts a job if priority == High, OR (job.Weight >= 10 AND priority > Never). So a Medium/Low pick on a high-weight job is counted too, not only "top choice" (High) picks; the description overstates the precision of what's being counted.
  - unsupported: "unpicked jobs highlighted in red" — only the numeric count label is recolored red when the count is 0 (readyCount.SetMessage(..., Color.Red)); there is no row/job highlighting, just a colored digit.

### Latejoin spawn flow and cryosleep

<a id="latejoin-spawn-and-cryo"></a>

Reworks how players enter and leave a round in progress: spawn region selection, arrivals markers, personal lockers, cryosleep pods and lost-and-found for stored gear. When a fork ships cryosleep inside a larger medical rework, only the cryosleep and arrivals subtree lands here; the wounds, surgery, cloning and life-support subtrees take their own medical ids.

**ephemeral-space**

*structural · entangled · medium confidence · 1 forks carry it*

Instead of the usual latejoin list, joining players get a "Spawning" window that groups jobs by department, shows how many slots are still open (or infinity for uncapped ones), and lets you pick which station or ship you want to arrive on before riding in on an arrivals shuttle. Once you arrive, a locker in your department already has your name printed on it and only opens for your ID. If you leave the round, your body freezes into a nameless, sluggish "Cryohusk" with a frozen ID card that other players can find and loot, and dying puts you on a countdown ("Respawn available in N seconds") before you can come back as someone new. The same package scatters the station's loot differently every round: armory, cargo and tech caches hand out a randomised split of guns, armour and gear across marked rooms, and maintenance fills with random crates, closets, posters, magazines and trash.

- **Take** — It replaces the whole "how do I get into and out of a round" flow at once — slot-aware job picking across multiple stations, a body left behind when you leave, timed respawns, and per-round loot scatter that stops veterans from memorising where every gun lives.
- **Skip** — It is not a feature you can drop next to your existing latejoin — it assumes multi-station/ship spawning, its own item and loot-table catalogue, and hand-placed region and spawner markers on every map, so adopting it means re-mapping your stations and replacing upstream arrivals rather than adding to it.
- **Touches** — all-players, security, cargo, science, command, ghost-roles, admin
- **Needs** — [custom-station-maps](#custom-station-maps), [vending-and-loot-catalogs](#vending-and-loot-catalogs)
- **Verified** — supported. Re-fetched every cited file plus several the claim didn't cite. spawn-menu.ftl literally has department-grouped headers, "(N open)"/"(∞ open)" slot strings, and a "Ships" heading confirming multi-station/ship selection; ESSharedSpawningSystem.Stations (List<NetEntity>) backs the multi-station picker. ESPersonalLockerSystem ties a locker's name label and AccessReader key to the joining player's StationRecordKey/job, matching "name printed on it / opens for your ID". ESSharedCryohuskSystem + species.ftl confirm the nameless "???" cryohusk, frozen ID card strings, and a movement-speed modifier (sluggish); ESSharedSpawningSystem's RespawnTimes/CVars back the countdown, matching es-respawn-ghost-gui-button. Distributed/armory.yml, cargo.yml and tech.yml (I found the latter two myself, not in the cited evidence) all use randomized EntityTable/DistributedSpawner tables with fork-only weapon/armor prototype IDs (ESWeaponPistol9mm, ESClothingOuterArmorSecurity, etc.), and Random/ has dedicated posters.yml, periodicals.yml and trash.yml alongside maintenance.yml — all matching the loot-scatter description exactly. On graft shape: I confirmed the fork's Resources/Maps directory contains ONLY _ES and Test subfolders — every standard upstream map (meta.yml, box.yml, omega.yml) 404s, meaning this fork fully replaced the station roster with its own maps (toast.yml, syndiebase.yml, singularity_world.yml). toast.yml itself contains dozens of hand-placed ES spawner/wardrobe/locker prototype instances. That's real structural entanglement beyond what path-based "zero files outside fork namespace" scanning could see: the feature is stitched into a bespoke map set and a bespoke item/weapon catalogue, not just self-contained code. This directly validates the assessor's downgrade from the seed's "drop-in" to "entangled" — the depends_on (custom-station-maps, vending-and-loot-catalogs) is exactly right and I found corroborating evidence for it myself.

**frontier**

*structural · entangled · high confidence · 1 forks carry it*

Joining late opens a picker that first asks whether you want a job on a station or a berth on another player's ship, then lists the specific ships and their open slots. Taking a crew slot drops you in as a translucent "Applicant" hologram: you and the ship's deed-holder negotiate terms in character, both press Approve, and only then do you spawn as your real character (anyone can dismiss the hologram back to the lobby, optionally closing the slot). Leaving works the same way in reverse: stepping into a cryosleep pod pops a confirmation that warns you about anything you're walking off with (ship deeds in your bag, an unsold ship on your PDA, an uplink and its balance, other important items and which pocket they're in), tells you how long your body will be kept, then puts you under and reopens your job slot. Later in the same shift you can request to wake up and return to your body at any free cryopod, with the explicit rule that you remember nothing that happened while you slept.

- **Take** — It turns joining and leaving a shift into an in-character transaction, hiring interviews on the way in and a checked, reversible cryo exit on the way out, instead of a menu click and a vanished body.
- **Skip** — The whole flow is built around player-owned ships: the picker's second tab is "which ship's crew", Approve requires holding a shuttle deed, and the cryo warnings are largely about deeds and unsold ships, so on a single-station fork most of it has nothing to point at.
- **Touches** — all-players, command, ghost-roles, service, medical
- **Needs** — [shipyard-player-ships](#shipyard-player-ships)
- **Verified** — supported. Every deed/ship reference in the evidence ties this feature to NF's separate shipyard-player-ships system: Interviews.xml states outright \"You need to have the deed to a shuttle to Approve a hologram\", and the cryosleep .ftl file's warning strings are almost entirely about ship deeds (accept-cryo-window-prompt-shuttle-bag-warning, -shuttle-pda-warning, -shuttle-pda-and-bag-warning) and an \"unsold ship\" on the PDA. The path-data seed of drop-in only reflects that no upstream files were edited in place; it can't see that the feature's core gating logic (who may Approve) and its main warning content are meaningless without the shipyard/deed economy. That is a real functional entanglement, not just co-location in the same fork namespace, so the assessor's downgrade from drop-in to entangled is correct.
  - unsupported: "drops you in as a translucent \"Applicant\" hologram" — the fetched evidence (Interviews.xml, cryosleep locale) confirms the "Applicant" hologram label and the Approve/Dismiss mechanics, but none of the six evidence files say anything about the hologram being rendered translucent; that specific visual detail is not backed by what was cited.

**cosmatic-drift**

*loop-change · entangled · high confidence · 1 forks carry it*

A player who is done with their shift can ride the arrivals shuttle back to Central Command, follow the "Cryo" signs, and climb into a cryosleep casket; a confirmation prompt asks whether they want to finish the shift as this character, and a station-wide announcement names them and their job as they go under. The casket locks away everything they were carrying, and anything the station still needs turns up in a Lost and Found locker that anyone can open, browse slot by slot (helmet, ID, backpack, pockets, even what was in each hand), and pull individual items back out of. After five minutes in cryo the player can rejoin the round as a fresh character. Alongside this, latejoiners no longer all appear at the same station spot: they are placed at arrivals markers, with per-job markers preferred and some jobs excluded, plus mapped spawn points for the fork's own roles such as Senior Engineer, Senior Physician and Private Investigator.

- **Take** — It closes the "player logs off wearing the only RCD" hole: gear gets recovered into a Lost and Found anyone can search by name and slot, and the departing player is announced instead of silently vanishing.
- **Skip** — The code is self-contained but the payoff is not: every station map needs cryo caskets, Lost and Found lockers, signage and arrivals spawn markers placed by hand, and giving players a sanctioned five-minute route to abandon a character mid-shift is a policy call, not just a feature.
- **Touches** — all-players, command, service, cargo
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. The claim already downgraded the drop-in seed to needs-upstream-edits, but understated why. Beyond map wiring, the C# actually has a real compile-time dependency on the fork's own Character Records subsystem (Content.Server._CD.Records.CharacterRecordsSystem, used to delete records on cryo-entry) — a separate, sizeable _CD feature not listed in depends_on. On top of that, the mechanism that actually places Lost-and-Found lockers and cryo pods onto stations is a third fork subsystem (CDMapPatch), and one of its files, Content.Shared/Maps/GameMapPrototype.CDMapPatch.cs, physically lives in the upstream Content.Shared/Maps/ directory alongside vanilla GameMapPrototype.cs, not under any _CD path — which the path-data's 'zero files outside fork namespace' signal would have missed entirely. Two hidden fork-system dependencies plus a stray file in an upstream directory push this past plain 'needs upstream edits to wire in' into genuinely entangled.
  - unsupported: "The casket locks away everything they were carrying, and anything the station still needs turns up in a Lost and Found locker" — CryoSleepSystem.CryoStoreBody() unconditionally moves ALL inventory items and held items into the Lost and Found container (StorePlayerItems inserts every foundItems entry); nothing stays locked in the casket itself. There is no two-tier split between casket-retained items and station-needed items surfacing in L&F — the casket only ever holds the now-empty body.
  - unsupported: "depends_on": [] — false. Content.Server/_CD/CryoSleep/CryoSleepSystem.cs directly imports and injects Content.Server._CD.Records.CharacterRecordsSystem and calls _characterRecords.DeleteAllRecords(body, recordKey) on cryo-entry. That is a hard compile-time dependency on the fork's separate Character Records subsystem (Content.Server/_CD/Records/*, Content.Shared/_CD/Records/*), not disclosed anywhere in the claim.
  - unsupported: skip_because framing ("every station map needs cryo caskets, Lost and Found lockers, signage and arrivals spawn markers placed by hand") undersells what actually exists and misses what actually integrates it: the fork ships a CDMapPatch overlay system (Content.Server/_CD/MapPatch/*, Resources/CDMapPatches/*.yml) that injects entities like LockerLostAndFound onto the ORIGINAL, otherwise-untouched vanilla station map files (e.g. Resources/Maps/bagel.yml has zero cryo/L&F entities baked in — they're added via Resources/CDMapPatches/bagel.yml at load time). That patch system itself is a third undisclosed fork subsystem this unit depends on, and one of its files (Content.Shared/Maps/GameMapPrototype.CDMapPatch.cs) sits directly in the upstream Content.Shared/Maps/ directory, not under any _CD path — contradicting the path-data premise that zero fork files exist outside namespace directories.

**sunrise**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 1 forks carry it*

Joining mid-round starts with picking a station from a searchable list (the server runs several, sorted so the one with a Station Representative comes first) and only then picking a job on it, with free slots shown per station; certain roles then arrive at spawn points reserved for their job instead of generic arrivals. If you go SSD or disconnect while alive and stay gone past a set number of minutes, your character is swallowed by a blue portal with a whoosh and wakes up stored in the station's cryosleep locker, gear and all, so the crew can pull your kit out of storage instead of stepping over a sleeping body forever (zombies, borgs, polymorphed people and anyone mid brain-transplant are left alone). Ghosts can also open a respawn menu and re-enter the round as a completely different character from their save slots, choosing station and job, limited by a cooldown and by only being able to spend each saved character once per round.

- **Take** — It fixes the two chronic population leaks in one package: SSD bodies clear themselves into cryo with their gear recoverable, and dead players can rejoin as a fresh character instead of spectating a two-hour round out.
- **Skip** — Respawning as a new character is a roleplay-policy decision as much as a code one (death stops costing you the round), and the package ships a replacement late-join window plus a sponsor-perks interface hook, so you inherit UI you must re-sync every time upstream touches the lobby.
- **Touches** — all-players, ghost-roles, command, medical
- **Needs** — [sponsor-and-donator-perks](#sponsor-and-donator-perks)
- **Verified** — supported. Cloned the repo and confirmed every mechanical claim in code: SRLateJoinGui/StationsListControl.cs has a FilterLineEdit search box and DefaultComparison that puts StationRepresentative (then Sheriff, then PirateCaptain) first; PreferredSpawnComponent/System gives reserved spawn points to certain jobs; CryoTeleportSystem exactly matches the SSD/disconnect timer, portal-blue sprite, and exclusion list (ZombieComponent, BorgChassisComponent — borgs never even get the tracking component, PolymorphedEntityComponent, and a live GetBodyOrgans/BrainComponent check that explicitly comments it's for mid-brain-transplant bodies); NewLifeSystem confirms ghost-only respawn, station/job/character picking, NextAllowRespawn cooldown, UsedCharactersForRespawn cleared only at round end, and a nullable ISharedSponsorsManager (Content.Sunrise.Interfaces.Shared) gating sponsor-only mode — exactly the 'sponsor-perks interface hook' the skip_because names. Critically, `rg -l SRLateJoinGui` turned up Content.Client/Lobby/LobbyState.cs — an upstream file (no _Sunrise in its path) saturated with 'Sunrise-Edit'/'Sunrise-Start' comments, including the literal wiring line `new SRLateJoinGui().OpenCentered(); // Sunrise-Edit`. That means the path-data 'drop-in' seed was wrong (contradicted, not just unproven), and the claim's own downgrade to needs-upstream-edits was correct and, if anything, understated: the fork's own copy already patches an upstream file for this feature's entry point (fork-patches-upstream), and grafting the same UI into a different fork would still require finding and editing that same hook elsewhere (integration-would-require-upstream-edits) — hence 'both'.
  - unsupported: "swallowed by a blue portal with a whoosh" — the portal-blue sprite and a teleport_departure.ogg sound are confirmed in code, but the specific word "whoosh" is an unverifiable stylistic gloss on an audio file, not something readable from source.

**backmen, rmc14, serbia-strong, starlight, stellar-station**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 1 forks carry it*

These forks each bolt something small onto the standard cryosleep pod. Stellar Station makes the cryo pod itself the spawn point, so you wake up inside a lime-lit pod (behind Cryogenics access) at both roundstart and latejoin, and its "wakeup station" can put the whole crew to sleep and rouse them with flickering lights and a shudder when the station finishes an FTL jump. SS220 quietly walks idle or disconnected players into cryo through a bluespace portal after a configurable timeout, and gives ghosts a button to cryo themselves out. Starlight keeps the belongings of anyone who cryos out and hands them to the next person who latejoins into that vacated job slot, who spawns at cryo holding a duffel of the previous holder's kit; RMC-14 does the equivalent through a requisitions console that lets you pull gear out of hypersleep chambers for marines who left, with Military Police and whitelisted roles blocked from recovery. Backmen adds arrivals-grid protection so nobody can dismantle or damage the arrivals shuttle while people are still coming in.

- **Take** — The gear-handoff piece is the real prize: latejoiners inheriting the cryo'd player's kit removes the "someone left with the only pair of insuls" problem that quietly bleeds equipment out of every department across a long round.
- **Skip** — These are five separate small hacks around one upstream system rather than one coherent feature, and the shared prerequisite (extra events fired when a player enters, leaves, or is deleted from cryostorage) means patching upstream's cryostorage system before any of them work; the auto-cryo-on-AFK piece in particular is a policy decision that will annoy players who step away mid-round.
- **Touches** — all-players, ghost-roles, cargo, command
- **Verified** — partly supported. Confirmed directly: RMC-14's own repo copy of the upstream file Content.Server/Bed/Cryostorage/CryostorageSystem.cs (not under any _RMC14/ namespace directory) has been edited in place to construct and raise `new EnteredCryostorageEvent()` and `new LeftCryostorageEvent()` (lines 245 and 304), which the fork's own sidecar recovery console then subscribes to. This proves the seed's path-data 'drop-in' guess was wrong for RMC-14 — the fork's copy really does contain edits to an upstream-namespace file, which is the 'fork-patches-upstream' reading, not merely a hypothetical integration cost. The claim's own graft_shape ('needs-upstream-edits') and its stated reasoning (shared cryostorage-event prerequisite) hold up. However roughly two of the five per-fork gameplay claims (Backmen arrivals protection, RMC-14 hypersleep-chamber gear recovery) are not supported by their cited evidence and one citation (RMCSurvivor.xml) is wholly irrelevant, while SS220 (AFK/disconnect teleport-to-cryo via bluespace portal, ghost cryo button), Starlight (belongings queued and handed to latejoiner who is force-spawned at the pod), and Stellar Station (cryo-pod-as-spawnpoint with Cryogenics access, FTL-triggered wake/sleep of the whole crew) are all solidly confirmed by the actual source.
  - unsupported: "Backmen adds arrivals-grid protection so nobody can dismantle or damage the arrivals shuttle while people are still coming in." — the cited evidence (Resources/Locale/en-US/_backmen/connection_messages.ftl) is a single-line ban-appeal message, entirely unrelated to arrivals or shuttles; no arrivals-protection system was found at any plausible path in the Backmen (Rxup) fork.
  - unsupported: "RMC-14 does the equivalent through a requisitions console that lets you pull gear out of hypersleep chambers for marines who left" — the actual RMCCryoRecoverySystem.cs only reads from vanilla Content.Shared.Bed.Cryostorage.CryostorageComponent.StoredPlayers, never HyperSleepChamberComponent. HyperSleepChamberComponent/SharedHyperSleepChamberSystem is an unrelated system that just blocks Xenos from entering a container and ejects the occupant on movement input — it has no gear-recovery logic and is not read by the recovery console anywhere.
  - unsupported: The evidence file Resources/ServerInfo/Guidebook/_RMC14/Guides/RMCSurvivor.xml is a combat/looting guide for the Survivor role against Xenomorphs — it contains no mention of cryo, hypersleep, or latejoin, and does not support any part of this claim.

### Cyborg and station AI overhaul

<a id="silicon-borg-overhaul"></a>

Reworks silicon play with selectable borg chassis and subtypes, extra modules and actions, borg PDAs and access, drones and remote-controlled shells.

**backmen**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 7 forks carry it*

The station AI stops being a static camera-hopper: it flies a free-roaming eye around the station, opens a camera list with a station nav-map to jump straight to any working camera, and can fire a destabilising stun shot from a camera at a spot on the floor (on a cooldown). The AI can also right-click a crew member to flag them as a hostile, and any cyborg tied to that AI sees the mark when examining them, so the AI can point its borgs at a target instead of just talking about it. The AI's holographic avatar gets a long list of alternate looks (Matrix, rainbow, static, a xenomorph queen, a horror form, and many more). Separately there are remote drone shells that run on a power charge shown as a suit-power alert and spend that charge on buttons that fabricate supplies in the field, a full stack of brutepacks, ointment or blood packs for the medical drone, or cable coils, steel, plasteel, glass, reinforced glass and plastic for the engineering one. Cyborgs also gain a storage module that gives them a very large satchel to haul things in, and malfunctioning hostile robots and saw-wielding drones exist as station threats to fight.

- **Take** — It turns the AI from a passive camera observer into an active player: free-flying eye, map-driven camera jumping, a stun shot, and a target-marking channel that finally gives AI and borgs a shared command loop.
- **Skip** — It is a reimplementation of a system upstream now ships its own version of, so grafting it means owning a permanent divergence from upstream station AI, and much of the shipped content (drone crafting actions, several prototypes) is written in Russian and would need full retranslation.
- **Touches** — silicon, command, science, medical, engineering, security, ghost-roles
- **Verified** — supported. All 9 cited files fetched and confirmed the specific claims (free-roaming eye via AiEyeMover async camera-range job, cooldown stun shot via AIEyeCamShootAction/WorldTargetAction useDelay:3, Russian-language drone-crafting actions producing full stacks of brutepack/ointment/bloodpack and cable/steel/plasteel/glass/rglass/plastic, a SuitPower AlertPrototype on BSSDroneComponent, a Huge-grid borg satchel module, ~28 alternate AI hologram looks including Matrix/Rainbow/Static/xenomorph-queen/horror, and a saw-wielding MobMalfunctioningRobotCutter on a hostile NPC faction). I also browsed the live tree beyond the cited evidence and found Content.Client/Backmen/StationAI/UI/CameraNavMapControl.cs, confirming the nav-map claim that wasn't directly evidenced. Vanilla Content.Server/Silicons/StationAi/StationAiSystem.cs already implements its own AI eye attach/clear logic and contains zero Backmen references, proving this is a fully parallel, self-contained system under Backmen/_Backmen namespaces rather than an in-place patch of upstream files — so the claim's own skip_because reasoning (owning a permanent divergence from upstream station AI) is accurate, and the correct reading is that grafting requires disabling/rewiring the vanilla system rather than the fork itself touching upstream files.
  - unsupported: "point its borgs at a target instead of just talking about it" is interpretive framing, not a directly-verifiable mechanic — the examine markup (AIEnemyNTComponent + ExaminedEvent) is visible to anyone examining the target, not gated specifically to cyborgs tied to that AI, so the borg-targeting benefit is inferred rather than shown in code.

**monolith**

*structural · entangled · medium confidence · 7 forks carry it*

Cyborgs are picked by faction and role: a PDV or marine-corps borg chooses an assault, engineer or medical chassis and spawns with that kit already fitted (built-in gun and jetpack for assault, RCD, cabling and construction tools for engineer, surgery kit and defibrillator plus health-bar vision for medical), with two or three empty slots left for modules the crew installs later. The bigger addition is the Xenoborg faction: a ghost-role Mothership Core sits immobile aboard its own ship, takes bodies its borgs drag back through a crusher, and prints fresh borg shells and type-specific upgrades from delivered materials, while four xenoborg types raid the sector for brains (an engineer that bolts doors open to make entry points, a slow armoured heavy with a laser and a radio jammer to stop victims calling for help, a fast scout that hauls corpses home and rescues borgs lost in space, and a stealth borg with a cloak, a disguise projector and a self-refilling sleep hypo). Every xenoborg carries a pinpointer to the core, so the crew's counterplay is finding and destroying it, which kills the whole faction at once; the xenoborgs win outright only if the entire sector has been converted.

- **Take** — It turns silicon play into a real role choice at spawn and bolts on a complete team antagonist with its own base, production loop, counterplay target and stated win/loss conditions.
- **Skip** — The xenoborg half is welded to Monolith's ship-sector setting, the mothership is a mapped FTL-capable grid with an IFF toggle and the crew borgs are named and equipped for factions (PDV, TSFMC, ADS) that mean nothing elsewhere, so a station fork faces a rename-and-remap job plus ongoing balance ownership of a whole antag faction before any of it plays.
- **Touches** — silicon, antagonist, ghost-roles, science, security, engineering, medical, command
- **Needs** — [ai-lawsets-and-appearance](#ai-lawsets-and-appearance), [gamemaster-and-ghost-roles](#gamemaster-and-ghost-roles), [warp-drive](#warp-drive), [custom-station-maps](#custom-station-maps)
- **Verified** — partly supported. I fetched all five cited files and they back nearly every specific claim: borg_types.yml shows pdv/tsf assault-engineer-medical chassis with pre-fitted defaultModules (weapon+jetpack for assault; RCD/cable/construction for engineer; surgery/defibrillator/ShowHealthBars for medical) and extraModuleCount of 2 or 3; Xenoborgs.xml guidebook confirms the immobile ghost-role Mothership Core, body-crusher intake, material-lathe printing, all four xenoborg types' abilities (access-breaker engineer, slow tanky laser+jammer heavy, fast corpse-hauling/rescue scout, cloak+chameleon-projector+regenerating-hypopen stealth), universal pinpointers, FTL/IFF prep text, and the exact win/loss conditions. This is strong evidence for 'entangled': the guidebook itself instructs players to check IFF before FTLing near stations, and silicon.ftl/xenoborg.ftl show custom per-faction lawsets and ghost-role wiring, matching the claimed dependencies on warp-drive, ai-lawsets-and-appearance and gamemaster-and-ghost-roles — a real reason to override the path-data 'drop-in' seed. One specific overclaim survives: the skip_because text lists 'ADS' alongside PDV/TSFMC as a named crew-borg faction, but borg_types.yml has no ads-prefixed borg chassis at all — ADS only appears in silicon.ftl as the shared underlying AI-core designation across vessel/PDV/TSFMC cores, not a third borg faction with its own assault/engineer/medical kit.
  - unsupported: "the crew borgs are named and equipped for factions (PDV, TSFMC, ADS)" — borg_types.yml only defines pdv* and tsf* borg chassis factions; ADS appears solely as the shared AI-core designation ("An ADS AI core that has been reprogrammed and put onto...") used across vessel/PDV/TSFMC AI cores, not as a distinct crew-borg faction with its own chassis kit.

**sunrise**

*loop-change · entangled · medium confidence · 7 forks carry it*

A player who becomes a cyborg picks from a much wider set of bodies than usual: peace, clown and security models alongside the standard ones, each with its own look, footstep sounds, radio channels, door access and built-in gadgets summoned as actions (pocket station map, camera feed, criminal-records HUD, forensic scanner). The flavour is baked in: the clown borg prints soap on demand, the peace borg bakes cookies and physically cannot attack anyone, the security borg sees warrants and mindshields overlaid on people. Borgs can also open a menu and choose the synthesised voice they speak with. Separately, a batch of non-crew chassis exists for antagonists and ghost roles: pirate boarding borgs that raid the station, ERT combat borgs with night vision, syndicate reaper and heavy combat units, and self-replicating xenoborgs whose whole goal is harvesting brains to build more of themselves. A special emag variant loads a specific lawset into a silicon instead of the generic subversion.

- **Take** — It turns "playing a borg" from one flat role into a menu of distinct characters with their own toys, voice, access and comedy, and throws in a stack of ready-made silicon antagonist and ghost-role bodies for free.
- **Skip** — The chassis definitions lean on fork-extended borg-type prototype fields (extra module counts, injected components, per-type radio and footstep sets) that upstream's borg type does not accept, the voice picker is wired straight into the fork's TTS stack and its sponsor-only voice gating, and the xenoborg line is vendored from another fork, so nothing here lands as a clean copy of a few YAML files.

- **Needs** — [text-to-speech](#text-to-speech), [sponsor-and-donator-perks](#sponsor-and-donator-perks), [pirate-crew](#pirate-crew), [cross-fork-vendored-bundles](#cross-fork-vendored-bundles)

Pirate, ERT, syndicate-heavy, and xenoborg-reaper antagonist/ghost-role chassis were all independently confirmed in borg_chassis.yml, pirate.yml and xenoborgs.yml, and LawsetEmagComponent.cs confirms the emag-lawset variant. Only the specific 'vendored from another fork' claim about xenoborgs did not hold up.
  - unsupported: "the xenoborg line is vendored from another fork" (and the depends_on entry "cross-fork-vendored-bundles") — GitHub commit history for xenoborgs.yml shows only a single commit ("Ксеноборг жнец для Рыбьей Станции" / "Xenoborg reaper for Fish Station", PR #4164) adding this file from scratch inside sunrise-station itself, with sprites in the fork's own _Sunrise/Mobs/Silicon/ namespace. **deltav**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 7 forks carry it*

A newly built cyborg picks its body at activation, and Delta-V adds a Security chassis to the list: it comes flash-immune, sees mindshield and criminal-record icons over people's heads, talks on the security and science channels, carries handcuffs and de-escalation gear, and runs on the Silicon Police lawset. Every borg now carries a built-in PDA it can pop open, plus an ID chip slot that grants its door access, and its maintenance panel gains extra wires roboticists can cut to hide it from the robotics console, pop its power cell, yank its ID chip, or sever a hidden "slave" link. That slave link is a permanent Law 0 that survives lawset changes and chassis swaps, which is how a Syndicate-built brain ends up as a "Syndicate Neuroling" serving whoever assembled it. The station AI gets a shop action to unlock powers it spends the round using at range, recoloring light fixtures with RGB, regrowing broken bulbs and tubes, honking bike horns and playing sounds through the station, spraying smoke, and spawning things, and it gets its own fax interface where it can read, copy, send, and shred paperwork like any crew member. Borgs also gain a long list of specialist item slots (organs and pills, patient transport, spraypaint, forensic supplies, seeds and swabs, kitchenware and drink bottles, fishing rods and fish, pies and slipping tools) and a candy fabricator with randomized flavors.

- **Skip** — It is a broad bundle rather than one feature: security borgs raise obvious balance questions for your security roster, and the AI shop pulls in a whole action catalogue plus sprites and UI you then own forever.

A candy fabricator with FabricateCandyActionEvent was also found in the fork's _DV tree. On graft_shape: I sparse-cloned the DeltaV repo and confirmed Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Mobs/Player/silicon.yml and .../Cyborgs/base_borg_chassis.yml are genuine upstream (space-wizards) files that DeltaV has extensively edited in place with '# DeltaV' comments — attaching StationAiShop, StationAiFax, FaxMachine, WiresPanel additions, IdChipSlot, and SlavedBorg directly onto vanilla entity prototypes. These files were not in evidence_cited, so the original path-data seed ('drop-in') missed real in-place upstream edits; the claim's 'needs-upstream-edits' downgrade is correct and specifically means the fork's own copy patches upstream files, not merely that a future graft would need new edits.

**cosmatic-drift**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 7 forks carry it*

Robotics can print a "B.O.R.I.S. AI-Cyborg Remote Control" brain at any exosuit fabricator (no research needed, same cost as a positronic brain) and slot it into a normal cyborg frame instead of a posibrain or MMI. The finished shell is a permanently-named, empty robot body that the station AI can take over on demand: the AI gets an "AI Shell" action that opens a list of every connected shell, letting it jump its camera eye to one or fully possess it and then walk around and use borg modules like any cyborg, keeping its radio channels and still receiving law changes, but losing its core actions, its station-wide camera vision and holopad call alerts until it exits back to the core. - **Skip** — A mobile AI is a much stronger AI: an unbound or subverted one can now personally open doors, fight, and haul things instead of having to talk crew into it, so silicon balance and your lawset culture both need re-tuning; the cosmetic subtypes also need bespoke RSI art per body and hook into the upstream borg type-selection menu, which is re-merge maintenance every upstream sync.

Every substantive gameplay claim checks out against the actual files: AIShells.xml guidebook literally states the B.O.R.I.S. brain prints at any exosuit fabricator "without the need for any research, requiring the same cost in resources that a positronic brain would require," and spells out the jump/possess mechanic, radio-channel retention, law updates, and the loss of core actions/vision/holopad alerts almost verbatim to the claim. ai_holograms.ftl and ai_screens.ftl confirm the hologram/icon pool (Bees, Matrix, Hades, Rainbow, President, etc.), and borg_subtypes.yml/base_borg_subtypes.yml confirm cosmetic subtypes (spider miner, qualified doctor) override both spritePath and footstepCollection.
