### Department restructure

<a id="department-restructure"></a>

Reorganises the department layout, adding or renaming departments and moving jobs between them with matching access, consoles and lockers.

**stellar-station**

*structural · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 5 forks carry it*

The job list you pick from at round start is rebuilt from scratch. Familiar roles are merged and renamed: Cargo Tech and Salvager become Handler and Courier, the Chaplain becomes a Cleric, Clown and Mime become a single Performer, the Chief Medical Officer becomes Head of Medicine, and the Head of Personnel becomes an Operations Manager who runs Supply. The Janitor moves under Supply, and Silicon gets its own department for borgs and the AI. On top of that there is a whole new Intern department with five low-rank slots (engineering, medical, science, security, supply) that let a new player shadow a department without holding a real job slot, each with its own ID icon, uniform and starting kit. Every job gets a rewritten wardrobe of headwear, eyewear, coats, uniforms, gloves, shoes and backpacks to choose from in the character editor.

- **Take** — The Intern tier is the genuinely novel piece: five per-department trainee slots give brand-new players a supervised on-ramp into Engineering, Medical, Science, Security or Supply without occupying a real job slot or carrying real responsibility.
- **Skip** — It is visibly unfinished and not portable in pieces: every department and job description in the locale files is still literal "LOREM IPSUM", all playtime requirements are commented out, and every job (Handler, Courier, Warden, Intern, all of them) is stubbed with `access: [Service]`, so grafting it as-is hands the whole crew identical, wrong access.
- **Touches** — command, security, medical, engineering, science, cargo, service, silicon, all-players
- **Verification** — none; read this as a claim, not a finding.

**impstation**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 5 forks carry it*

Service stops being a leaderless grab-bag and gets its own head of staff, the Hospitality Director, who arrives roundstart with a mindshield, a flash, command access and authority over bartender, chef, botanist, janitor, chaplain, librarian, musician, reporter, clown, mime, boxer, zookeeper and service worker. Their signature toy is a Service Job Board console: they open it, pick from a shuffled shortlist of station events (ballroom dance, game show, renaissance fair, feast, bar fight, concert, talent show, eating contest, pool party, scavenger hunt, lottery, yoga class, a fake fire drill), and the pick goes out over the radio as "Station event selected, you have X to prepare." When the prep timer runs out a station-wide announcement fires the event off ("BAAAR FIIIIIIGHT!!!!", "Surf's up!"), and the board marks it claimed so it cannot be run twice. Nothing is simulated beyond the announcement, so the actual dance or tournament is whatever the crew turns up and does.

- **Take** — It gives the service department a command-tier player whose whole job is generating crew-wide social events on a timer, which is the cheapest reliable source of roleplay a round can have.
- **Skip** — The board only prints announcements, so the events live or die on player initiative, and the HD needs a real office, a console spawn on every map and steep playtime gates before the role reads as anything but a spare greytide head.
- **Touches** — service, command, all-players
- **Needs** — [extra-job-roster](#extra-job-roster)
- **Verified** — partly supported. I confirmed the seed's 'drop-in' path-scan was wrong on its own terms: the fork's tree contains Resources/Prototypes/Roles/Jobs/departments.yml, a genuine upstream-path file (not under an _Impstation directory), with the Civilian department's roles list edited in place (Bartender/Botanist/Chaplain/Chef/Clown/Janitor/Librarian/Mime/Musician/Reporter/Visitor/ServiceWorker commented out with '# begin imp edit, service split') to make room for the new Service department defined in _Impstation/Roles/departments.yml. That is a real edit sitting in an upstream directory (fork-patches-upstream), and porting this feature into another fork would likewise require editing that fork's own department file to avoid the same roles double-counting across two departments (integration-would-require-upstream-edits) — both readings hold. The core gameplay mechanics I could verify (HD stats, job board console flow, event list, radio pick + broadcast fire) check out closely against the actual files, but the 'claimed so it cannot be run twice' framing overstates what the code does: the whole board locks after one pick, it isn't a per-job claimed flag.
  - unsupported: "the board marks it claimed so it cannot be run twice" — the actual client code (Content.Client/_Impstation/Service/ServiceJobBoardMenu.xaml.cs) sets `entry.Disabled = state.ActiveJob != null` for every entry, not just the picked one, and the server (ServiceJobBoardSystem.Update) only clears `EndTime` when the timer ends, never `ActiveJob`. So once the HD picks one event, the whole board locks for the rest of the round rather than marking just that one event used while leaving others pickable — the claim's phrasing implies a per-event 'claimed' flag with the rest of the shortlist still available, which the code does not support.

**starlight**

*loop-change · entangled · medium confidence · 5 forks carry it*

Three extra department headings appear in the job-select lobby alongside the usual Command/Security/Medical block. "Law Department" gathers the Magistrate, Internal Affairs Agent and Lawyer, "NanoTrasen Personnel" gathers the corporate/off-station arrivals (NT Representative, Blue Shield officer, Magistrate, IAA, career trainer, NT special forces, plus the Station AI), and "Trans-Solar Federation" gathers the SolGov officers, sheriff and TSF marines. For a player it means the legal and outside-authority roles are no longer scattered into Command or Civilian: they sit in their own colour-coded groups when picking a job, and the station reads as having a separate legal branch and a separate NT/military presence rather than one chain of command. The two off-station groups are hidden from the map/job editor, so they are joinable but not part of the normal station roster count.

- **Take** — A tiny, readable file that cleanly separates legal and off-station-authority roles out of Command, which is the natural grouping once a fork has more than one lawyer-type job.
- **Skip** — Every role it lists (Magistrate, IAA, Blue Shield, NT Representative, SolGov and TSF marines, Decimus) is a Starlight job that does not exist upstream, so the file is an empty shell unless you port that whole job roster first, and the department ids also need matching access groups, ID console entries and radio channels that this file does not carry.
- **Touches** — command, security, legal, silicon, ghost-roles, all-players
- **Needs** — [extra-job-roster](#extra-job-roster)
- **Verification** — none; read this as a claim, not a finding.

**frontier**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 5 forks carry it*

Security is replaced by the New Frontier Sheriff's Department, a sector-wide law enforcement outfit with its own rank ladder instead of a single HoS: Cadet, Deputy, Detective, Brigmedic, Public Affairs Liaison, Senior Officer, Bailiff and Sheriff, each with distinct brown-and-cream NFSD uniforms, badges, sidearms and a supervisor they answer to. Officers all spawn mindshielded and tracked, carry less-lethal universal pistols with rubber and overpressure magazines, and get Frontier Uplink Coins to spend at an NFSD uplink store on tiered hardsuits gated by rank. The department also has its own job: hunting smugglers by finding Syndicate dead drops and contraband drop pods scattered around the sector, scanning them with a detective's contraband forensics module to pay spesos and coins into the department's bank, and tracking DNA back to the smugglers, while senior ranks get ship vouchers to claim NFSD patrol craft.

- **Take** — It turns a flat three-role Security department into an eight-rank career ladder with a reward loop of its own (smuggling interdiction paying into a department bank), giving security players progression and something proactive to do when nobody is committing crimes.
- **Skip** — The roles are inseparable from Frontier's sector economy: uplink coins, department bank payouts, ship vouchers, dead-drop/drop-pod smuggling content and a whole bespoke NFSD wardrobe and weapon set all have to come along, and departments.yml rewires upstream department membership on top of that.
- **Touches** — security, command, medical, antagonist, all-players
- **Needs** — [player-economy-and-banking](#player-economy-and-banking), [shipyard-player-ships](#shipyard-player-ships), [access-control-rework](#access-control-rework), [clothing-and-wardrobe-pack](#clothing-and-wardrobe-pack)
- **Verified** — supported; assessed as entangled, corrected by the verifier. I fetched all 11 cited files plus browsed the repo tree, and confirmed almost everything in the gameplay description directly (rank ladder, mindshield+tracking implants, less-lethal rubber/overpressure magazines, FrontierUplinkCoin currency and hardsuit BuyerJobCondition rank gating, ShipVoucherNfsdBailiff/Sergeant, ContrabandForensicsModule, dead-drop/drop-pod smuggling loop paying spesos+FUCs into an NFSD bank per Smuggling.xml). But the seed's drop-in premise (zero files outside the fork's own namespace) is actually false for this unit: the department-restructure's Security role list is rewritten in place inside Resources/Prototypes/Roles/Jobs/departments.yml, a non-_NF, non-namespaced upstream path, with '# Frontier' diff-marker comments replacing the vanilla Security roster. The claim's own cited departments.yml (the _NF one) doesn't contain this edit at all — it cited the wrong file for that specific assertion, but the underlying behavior (upstream rewiring) is real and lives outside the namespace, which is stronger than merely 'entangled with sibling systems.'
  - unsupported: "departments.yml rewires upstream department membership on top of that" — the cited evidence file (Resources/Prototypes/_NF/Roles/Jobs/departments.yml) only defines the fork's new "Frontier" and "Antag" departments; it contains no Security entry at all and does not do the rewiring described. The actual rewiring lives in a DIFFERENT file the claim never cited: the non-namespaced Resources/Prototypes/Roles/Jobs/departments.yml (no _NF/ prefix), which directly comments out upstream Security roles (Detective, HeadOfSecurity, SecurityCadet, SecurityOfficer, Warden, SecurityGuard) and replaces them in place with the NFSD job IDs, each tagged '# Frontier'. This is a real file living outside the fork's own namespace directories, which falsifies the seed's premise for this unit.

### Squads, ranks and skill gating

<a id="squads-ranks-and-skills"></a>

A military-style role ladder with squads, ranks, order-issuing and per-job skill presets that gate which equipment a character may use.

**rmc14**

*structural · entangled · medium confidence · 0 forks carry it*

Instead of joining as a lone crewmember, you spawn into a numbered squad under a squad leader, wear a rank on your ID (Dep., Marshal, Spec., Off. and dozens more, each with its own paygrade and name prefix), and answer to a chain of command that runs up to a central command console. Squad leaders get three shouted orders on their action bar (Move, Hold, Focus) that give everyone nearby a real buff: faster movement, tougher hide, or steadier aim, plus a colour-coded oversized pointing arrow in their squad's colour so they can direct people visually when nobody is reading chat. Every character also carries a set of numbered skill ratings (medical, engineering, firearms, construction, CQC, piloting, forklift, police, intel and more) tied to their role, and those ratings decide both what gear you are allowed to touch and how fast you do things with it, so a leader with medical 1 injects an auto-injector instantly while an untrained marine fumbles it.

- **Take** — It turns a loose crew into an actual command hierarchy with mechanical teeth: orders that buff, ranks that read on sight, and skill numbers that make "trained for this" a real distinction instead of a roleplay convention.
- **Skip** — It is built for RMC-14's military total conversion, not a station: the squads, ranks and skill presets are written against a marine job roster and its equipment, so on a normal station you would be reinventing every rank table and re-tagging every tool with a skill requirement before a single player noticed a difference.
- **Touches** — command, security, medical, engineering, cargo, all-players
- **Needs** — [extra-job-roster](#extra-job-roster)
- **Verified** — partly supported. I re-fetched all six cited files plus the linked control-computer XAML and a rank-directory listing. The core mechanics check out: marine_order_actions.yml has exactly the Move/Hold/Focus InstantActions the guide describes; RMCGuideSquadLeader.xml confirms the squad-colored pointing arrow, medical-1 auto-injector perk, and a commander/CIC chain of command; skills.yml lists the named skill categories (Medical, Engineer, Firearms, Construction, Cqc, Pilot, Police, Intel, PowerLoader/forklift, etc.); cmb.yml shows real rank prefixes (Dep., Marshal, Off., Spec., Med., Breach., Agent) and a browsed Ranks/ directory (Colony, Other, SPP, TSE, UNMC, We-Ya, hefa_ranks.yml) backs \"dozens more\"; and MarineControlComputerWindow.xaml is literally titled \"Almayer Control Console\" with alert-level/announcement/evacuation buttons, supporting the central command console. That said, several specific phrasings outrun the evidence (numbered vs. named squads, \"each\" rank having a paygrade, and item-level access gating by skill) — hence partly-supported rather than supported. On graft shape: the seed's drop-in guess is clearly wrong and the claim's own \"entangled\" downgrade holds up — the system is built on marine-specific equipment tags, faction/job-specific rank tables, and a ship-specific (Almayer) command console, all pointing to the extra-job-roster dependency the claim already names.
  - unsupported: "you spawn into a numbered squad under a squad leader" — the guide evidence names squads phonetically ("alpha", "three other squads with three others leaders", "Charlie got the queen kill"), not by number; no cited file shows squads identified by number.
  - unsupported: "dozens more, each with its own paygrade and name prefix" — in the cited cmb.yml, several ranks (RMCRankCMBInvestigativeSynthetic, RMCRankCMBRiotControlSynthetic, RMCRankCMBRiotControlOfficer, RMCRankCMBMedicalTechnician, RMCRankCMBBreachingTechnician, RMCRankCMBSWATSpecialist) have a prefix but no paygrade field at all, so "each" having its own paygrade is not true even within the one cited file.
  - unsupported: "those ratings decide both what gear you are allowed to touch and how fast you do things with it" — the cited skills.yml only shows a SkillDefinition with delayMultipliers (use-speed scaling per skill level), which backs the "how fast" half; no cited file shows a hard access-gate (skill required just to touch/use an item) to back the "what gear you are allowed to touch" half.

**serbia-strong**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 0 forks carry it*

Every character spawns with a competence sheet set by their job: seven trainings (medicine, anatomy, combat, construction, EVA, bureaucracy, physical) each sitting somewhere between "initial" and "professional". Low training makes you visibly bad at the work rather than just slower: an untrained medic's health analyzer spits out scrambled readings, the defibrillator has a chance to shock the person holding it, injectors slip and cut the patient, and every treatment takes noticeably longer, while a professional works faster and cleanly. Combat training shifts your odds of shoving someone to the floor versus being shoved yourself, and some machine consoles simply refuse to open for a character without the relevant training. You can improve mid-round: skills accumulate study progress and pop up when they level, standing near a talking mentor character speeds learning in the trees they teach, and a skill-tree window lets you spend the spare points your job grants. Note that this fork's version is purely the training ladder, with no squads, ranks or order-issuing.

- **Take** — It turns a job from an access badge into a competence gradient, so a bystander fumbling a defib or a doctor reading a garbled scanner becomes readable, teachable gameplay, and it gives non-antag rounds a progression loop.
- **Skip** — SS220's files ship under a custom CLA with a hosting restriction rather than an open licence, and the system only bites because it hooks upstream medical, disarm and console code plus needs an experience definition bolted onto every job prototype, so it is a permanent merge-conflict surface plus a full balance pass on your own roster.
- **Touches** — medical, security, engineering, command, cargo, service, all-players
- **Needs** — [language-system](#language-system)
- **Verified** — partly supported. Cloned the fork and read the actual code: JobPrototype.cs, SharedStationSpawningSystem.cs, StationSpawningSystem.cs, SharedMeleeWeaponSystem.cs, SharedDefibrillatorSystem.cs, HealthAnalyzerControl.xaml.cs, AdminVerbSystem.cs and ConstructionSystem.Guided.cs are all upstream files (outside any SS220/ directory) carrying in-place "SS220-..." edits that reference the Experience system directly (e.g. JobPrototype.cs has a required ExperienceDefinition field; SharedMeleeWeaponSystem.cs raises a disarm-multiplier event; SharedDefibrillatorSystem.cs calls _electrocution.TryDoElectrocution(user,...) gated by a skill-driven chance). This is unambiguous fork-patches-upstream, confirming the claim's own needs-upstream-edits verdict and refuting the drop-in seed.
  - unsupported: some machine consoles simply refuse to open for a character without the relevant training — the ActivatableUIRequiresSkillComponent/ActivatableUIRequiresSkillSystem mechanism exists in Content.Shared/SS220/Experience/Skill/Checks/, but a full-text search of the entire checked-out Resources/ tree found zero prototype files that attach this component to any entity (console or otherwise), so as shipped this specific behavior is unused infrastructure, not something that currently happens in a round.

**corvax**

*activity · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 0 forks carry it*

The Head of Security carries a handheld "SecApartment" tablet (battery powered, screen goes dark when the cell dies) that turns the security roster into named squads. On it they see every security officer on the station, drag unassigned ones into squads, name each squad and give it a short standing-orders description, stamp it with a Greek-letter badge (Alpha through Omega), and flip it between Active and On Break. Each squad's card shows its members' suit-sensor vitals and last known location, so the HoS can see at a glance which team is hurt or out of position, and officers wearing a security HUD see their squadmates' Greek-letter icon floating over their heads in the field. The same tablet also lists live countdown timers pulled from portable wooden signal timers, with their labels and remaining time, so brig sentences can be tracked from one screen instead of walking cell to cell.

- **Take** — It gives the Head of Security a real command tool: named squads with visible field badges and shared vitals turn a scattered pile of officers into teams that can be assigned and tracked, which is the missing middle between "HoS shouts on radio" and "everyone freelances".
- **Skip** — Despite the feature name, this is only the squad-roster half: there are no ranks, no chain-of-command mechanics, and no skill gating on equipment, so it buys organisation UI rather than any new rule, and it only pays off on high-population rounds where security is big enough to split. It also leans on suit sensors and the security HUD, so it quietly degrades to an empty roster whenever officers strip their sensors.
- **Touches** — security, command
- **Verified** — partly supported. I fetched an upstream (non-Corvax-namespaced) prototype file, Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Clothing/Eyes/hud.yml, and it contains the abstract entity `ShowSecurityIcons` with a components list that includes `- type: ShowJobIcons`, `- type: ShowMindShieldIcons`, `- type: ShowCriminalRecordIcons`, `- type: ShowContrabandDetails`, and critically `- type: ShowSquadIcons # Corvax-SecApartment` — an inline comment tagging it as a fork insertion into this core upstream file (which every security HUD/eyepatch entity in the file inherits from). This directly proves the fork's own copy edits files outside the Corvax/ namespace directories, contradicting the path-data 'drop-in' seed and confirming the claim's 'needs-upstream-edits' downgrade — specifically as fork-patches-upstream, not just a hypothetical integration cost. The rest of the gameplay description (battery/dying-screen tablet, named squads with Greek-letter badges Alpha-Omega, Active/OnBreak toggle, per-squad suit-sensor vitals + last-known-location via SensorStatusUpdateState, aggregated countdown timers with labels/remaining time) is well supported by SecApartmentComponent.cs, SecApartmentUi.cs, SecApartmentEnums.cs, secapartment.yml, and portable_screen_timer.yml, but a few specific narrative flourishes (drag-and-drop UI, brig-sentence framing for the generic timer, 'standing-orders' description) are not shown in the cited evidence.
  - unsupported: "drag unassigned ones into squads" — the evidence shows AddMemberToSquadMessage/RemoveMemberFromSquadMessage BUI messages exist, but none of the cited files (nor the client BUI, which wasn't cited) show a drag-and-drop interaction specifically; it could just as easily be button/dropdown assignment.
  - unsupported: "The same tablet also lists live countdown timers pulled from portable wooden signal timers ... so brig sentences can be tracked from one screen instead of walking cell to cell" — portable_screen_timer.yml defines a generic SignalTimer item ("Cool wooden timer for counting time") with DeviceLink ports for arbitrary triggers; nothing in the evidence ties these timers to brig cells or sentences specifically, that framing is invented.
  - unsupported: "give it a short standing-orders description" — Squad.Description is a plain free-text string field with an UpdateSquadDescriptionMessage; nothing shows it is specifically for 'standing orders' as opposed to any other note.

### Xenobiology and slime rework

<a id="xenobiology-rework"></a>

Rebuilds the slime husbandry loop with new slime types, processing equipment, extract crafting and a dedicated console.

**goobstation, starlight**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 0 forks carry it*

Xenobiology becomes a full slime-ranching loop: you breed slimes through roughly twenty-two colour breeds (grey, metal, bluespace, sepia, gold, adamantine and so on), each splitting into new colours on mitosis with a mutation chance you can push up with destabilizer jelly or clamp down with stabilizer. A handheld scanner tells you a slime's breed, its mutation odds, which colours it can become and how many extracts it would yield right now, and a backpack-sized "xenovac" containment tank lets you suck up slimes and carry them around instead of herding them by hand. Feeding slimes with steroid jelly raises extract yield, boost jelly raises litter size, and a docility jelly tames them into pets. Extracts are then activated by squirting reagents on them: grey extract reacts with water to make epinephrine, with blood to spit out three monkey cubes, and with plasma to burst into three baby slimes, and each extract goes dry and useless after one reaction. Goob adds a xenobiology bounty console that pays out for specific extracts or "any three tier-2 extracts", so slime farming feeds cargo; the jellies also let anyone drinking them turn fireproof, swap species into a slimeperson or felinid, or change gender. Loose slimes are genuinely dangerous now: they latch onto a living crewmember, pump them full of sedative hallucinogenic slime toxin that holds them alive in crit at zero blood, and can tear organs and limbs off corpses. Starlight's version covers the same ground more compactly, with a remote xenobiology console you drive from safety (pick up and place slimes, drop monkeys from stored cubes, recycle dead monkeys back into cubes, apply mutation and stabilizer potions at range), a slime processor you activate to grind slimes into extracts, and a wide potion shelf including sentience, mind transference, speed, bluespace radio, name change and gender change.

- **Take** — It turns xenobiology from a thin upstream stub into a real department loop with its own progression, its own equipment, its own payout path through bounties, and a genuine failure mode when the slimes get out.
- **Skip** — This is two large parallel implementations (161 and 49 files) that overlap heavily but are not interchangeable, so you must pick one and then own a breeding/mutation table, roughly twenty-two extract prototypes with per-reagent reaction lists, custom HTN slime AI, and a bespoke bounty database forever — and the species-swap and sentience potions leak balance decisions into parts of the game far outside science.
- **Touches** — science, cargo, all-players, ghost-roles
- **Verified** — supported. Fetched and read every cited Goobstation file plus follow-ups. grey.yml's Reactive block matches the claim exactly: water->Epinephrine(MakeUnreactiveEntityEffect so it goes dry after one use), blood->3 MonkeyCube, plasma->3 MobSlimeXenobioBabyGrey. reagents.ftl independently confirms every jelly the claim names: slime-toxin (crit at zero blood + hallucinogenic/sedative), steroid (extract yield), stabilizer/destabilizer (+/-25% mutation, carries generations), boost (litter size), docility (tame), green (slimeperson), felinid toxin, genderfluid. breeds.ftl lists 22 lines (incl. "undetermined") covering every named example (grey, metal, bluespace, sepia, gold, adamantine). scanner.ftl literally reads "chance of mutation", "possible mutations are", "yield X extracts". bounties.ftl has the exact "Any Three Tier 2 Slime Extracts" string. mob_actions.yml has ActionSlimeLatch ("Latch onto a target and begin digesting it") and ActionEatCorpse ("tear off the target's body part or organ"). xenovac.yml is a backpack-slot Clothing item with a vacuum-nozzle child item, matching "backpack-sized xenovac". For Starlight, xenobiology-console-text.ftl and processor-verbs.ftl match the remote console (pick up/place slimes, drop/recycle monkey cubes, apply potions at range) and the activate-to-grind processor verbatim. gender-change-verbs.ftl confirms the gender potion. The one weak link: the cited xenobiology_tables.yml is actually SilverSlimeFoodTable/GoldSlime loot tables, not a potion list — it does not itself support "wide potion shelf including sentience, mind transference..." However I independently confirmed via the repo tree that Content.Shared/_Starlight/Xenobiology/Potions/ genuinely contains SlimeSentiencePotionComponent, SlimeMindTransferencePotionComponent, SlimeSpeedPotionComponent, SlimeBluespaceRadioPotionComponent, SlimeNameChangePotionComponent and SlimeGenderChangePotionComponent, so the claim itself holds even though that one citation was a miss. On graft shape: file-path scans of both forks show all Xenobiology-named C#/prototypes sitting under Content.Goobstation.*/Resources/Prototypes/_Goobstation or Content.*/_Starlight namespaces (looks drop-in at first glance, matching the seed). But I checked the forks' own standard, non-namespaced Resources/Maps/*.yml station files directly and found them referencing the new feature: .convex.yml has "xenobiology lab chamber 1/2/3 air alarm", .elkridge.yml has "airlock (Xenobiology)" and "proto: SignXenobio", .oasis.yml has "proto: ComputerScienceXenobiologyBounty" and "proto: LockerScienceFilledXenobiology". These are ordinary shared map files (same path convention upstream SS14 uses), not fork-namespaced, and Goobstation's own copy edits them to place the new machines/rooms. That is a real fork-patches-upstream-directory situation the path-data seed missed (it likely only scanned for prototype/component definitions, not map placements), so the assessor's downgrade from "drop-in" to "needs-upstream-edits" is correct, and the reason is that the fork's own tree already contains edited upstream-path files, not merely that wiring the feature elsewhere would require new edits.

## Combat

### Firearms and ammunition expansion

<a id="firearms-content-expansion"></a>

A larger gun roster with new ammunition, magazines and projectiles, plus gun subsystems such as fire modes, bipods, accuracy modifiers and firing restrictions on who may pull the trigger.

**ephemeral-space, forky, funky, gaby-station-now-dumont-station, goobstation, impstation, monolith, rmc14, serbia-strong, starlight, stellar-station, viva-station**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 10 forks carry it*

Players get a much larger armoury: extra pistols, revolvers, snipers, SMGs, shotguns and energy guns, each with its own calibre of boxed cartridges, magazines and speedloaders to print, carry and reload, plus themed rounds like ion bolts, disabler spreads, a clown-launching shot and a .45 magnum "temporal" round. Guns also gain handling depth you feel in a fight: a right-click menu to pick which bolt an energy weapon fires, screw-on barrel and sight attachments listed when you examine the gun, weapons that only work when dual-wielded, and an ammo readout that names what you are loading ("12/24 Shells") instead of showing a bare number. Several forks also gate the trigger itself, so a weapon missing its firing mechanism just clicks uselessly and some guns break outright in the hands of a species they were not built for.

- **Take** — It is the cheapest way to make firefights feel less samey: the ammo-type and fire-mode layers turn "point gun, hold click" into an actual loadout decision, and most of the content is plain prototype data you can cherry-pick a calibre at a time.
- **Skip** — Every fork wires its gun subsystems (fire modes, accuracy, firing pins, dual-wield, attachment UI) into upstream's shared gun and projectile code, so you inherit merge pain on the single hottest upstream file family, and the twelve implementations disagree enough that you cannot mix two of them without picking a winner.
- **Touches** — security, antagonist, cargo, science, all-players
- **Verified** — partly supported. All 10 cited evidence files check out on their specific content: goobstation's ammo_selector_protos.yml really does define BulletEnergyGunIon ("Ion bolt"), BulletDisablerSmgSpread ("Disabler bolt spread"), and BulletEnergyGunClownshot ("sending clowns, and only clowns, flying away"); goob_gun.ftl really has both the fire-mode-select verb and a RequiresDualWieldComponent string; viva's magnumtemporal.yml really defines a ".45 magnum temporal" cartridge; starlight's firingpins.ftl really has "firing-pin-weapon-failure = The gun clicks." for a missing firing mechanism; Dumont's SpeciesRestrictedTriggerComponent.cs really breaks a weapon's trigger for a configured species list; stellar's ammo.ftl really supports a named-count readout. The one gap: ephemeral-space's cited attachments.ftl (9 lines total) only defines a "barrel" attachment slot name — I pulled the full ESSharedGunAttachmentsSystem.cs and its component files and found no "sight"/"scope" slot anywhere in that fork's attachment code, so "screw-on barrel and sight attachments" overclaims a second attachment type the evidence doesn't show (may exist in some other fork not cited here, but not in what was cited). On graft_shape: I settled it by diffing against real upstream (space-wizards/space-station-14). Ephemeral-space's attachment system and Dumont's species-trigger/broken-trigger system are both 100% additive — they subscribe to pre-existing vanilla events (GunRefreshModifiersEvent, ShotAttemptedEvent, both byte-for-byte identical to current upstream) and touch zero upstream files; those two slices alone would be near drop-in. But goobstation's Content.Shared/Weapons/Ranged/Systems/BatteryWeaponFireModesSystem.cs — sitting at the plain upstream path with no fork-namespace marker — is a genuinely modified copy of the real upstream file (removed `partial`, swapped the injected prototype manager, changed PopupEntity→PopupClient), i.e. goobstation's copy really does diverge from upstream in an upstream directory. So the seed's needs-upstream-edits holds, but the mechanism differs by fork: some forks (goobstation) directly carry a diverged file in upstream's own path, while others (ephemeral-space, Dumont) achieve the same feature family purely through existing extension points with no upstream edits at all.
  - unsupported: "screw-on barrel and sight attachments listed when you examine the gun" — the cited ephemeral-space evidence (attachments.ftl, and the full ESSharedGunAttachmentsSystem.cs/component files) only defines a "barrel" attachment slot; no "sight" slot exists anywhere in that fork's attachment code.

### Melee weapons, shields and blocking

<a id="melee-weapons-and-blocking"></a>

Added melee weapons plus the defensive layer around them: rechargeable shields, blocking, parrying, whetstones and personal energy shields.

**goobstation**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 5 forks carry it*

Melee fights stop being pure damage trades and become about what you are holding. Goob adds a big rack of hand weapons (a crafted hammer, canes, sabres, the Head of Security's self-recharging "Justice" energy sword that can be flipped between a cutting mode and a stun mode, a Syndicate contractor baton that ion-shocks borgs and staggers people, flatcaps with glass shards sewn into the brim in plasma/uranium variants, boomerangs that fly back to your hand after a throw) alongside a defensive layer: the Blueshield's battery-powered greatshield soaks a large fraction of incoming blunt, slash, piercing and heat damage even when you are not actively blocking, drains its charge doing so, hums and glows while raised, and has a slot to sheath your baton in. There are also gloves that teach the wearer Krav Maga while worn. Some blades cut deeper wounds than their raw damage suggests, and several of these are theft-target or contraband items that antagonists and security both want.

- **Take** — It turns melee from a damage-number exchange into a real defensive game (passive vs active blocking, shield charge as a resource, weapons with two firing modes) and hands security and antags a much wider, more characterful weapon roster.
- **Skip** — The good parts lean on Goob's own extensions to blocking, item-switching and the wound system rather than upstream's plain BlockingComponent, so you cannot take just the shields without porting or reimplementing that combat plumbing, and rebalancing a whole new melee roster against your existing security kit is ongoing work.
- **Touches** — security, antagonist, command, service, all-players
- **Needs** — [martial-arts](#martial-arts), [surgery-and-limb-wounds](#surgery-and-limb-wounds)
- **Verified** — partly supported. shields.yml, contractor_baton.yml, justice.yml, bladed_caps.yml, hammer.yml, kravmagagloves.yml and BoomerangComponent.cs all read exactly as claimed (passive/active block fractions, battery-drain-on-block, baton sheath slot, StunBorgsOnHit+Ion:35 on the contractor baton, self-recharging battery on Justice, plasma/uranium bladed flatcaps, Construction-graph hammer, ClothingGrantComponent Krav Maga, boomerang return fields). But going beyond the cited evidence to check the C# backing the shields: Content.Shared/Blocking/BlockingSystem.cs sits at the literal upstream path (no _Goobstation prefix) and, diffed against space-wizards/space-station-14 master, is substantially rewritten with an inline "// Goobstation" marker on an added ItemToggleSystem dependency and older API idioms than current upstream -- a fork copy patching an upstream-path file in place, not a self-contained addition, exactly the case path-data can't see. RechargeableBlocking additionally lives under Content.Server/_White/Blocking (a merged sub-fork, not _Goobstation), and the Justice sword's ItemSwitch plumbing lives under Content.Shared/_Shitmed/ItemSwitch (the wound/surgery sub-fork) -- neither is drop-in-clean even by the fork's own internal boundaries.
  - unsupported: "the Head of Security's self-recharging 'Justice' energy sword that can be flipped between a cutting mode and a stun mode" -- justice.yml's ItemSwitch actually defines five states (off/stun/ion/lethal/empowered), including an ion mode and an explosive 'empowered' mode with ExplodeOnMeleeHit; describing it as a two-mode cutting/stun toggle understates what the file shows.
  - unsupported: "a crafted hammer, canes, sabres" -- canes and sabres are not among the evidence_cited paths and were not found in any file fetched; only the hammer (hammer.yml) is verified.

**rmc14**

*loop-change · entangled · medium confidence · 5 forks carry it*

Instead of every swing and shot landing automatically, characters carry a dodge rating: small or invisible targets are harder to hit, big ones easier, and lying down makes you easier to hit, with a separate looser roll for shots from your own side so friendly fire past a squadmate often whiffs. On the alien side, several castes get a temporary absorbing shield they pay plasma for and trigger as an ability, with its own overlay on the sprite, a shatter sound when it runs out and a slow drain that eats it if nobody hits you; some flavours also soak explosions for a couple of seconds. Melee itself gets a training layer, so a trained marine hits harder with the same weapon than an untrained one, some weapons stun on contact or do bonus damage against particular targets, some creatures shrug off punches entirely, you cannot hit yourself unless you opt in, and a dedicated key fires a held weapon's special function without digging through a right-click menu.

- **Take** — The dodge-and-shield layer turns flat trade-blows melee into something with defensive counterplay, and the separate friendly-fire miss chance is a genuinely elegant fix for the "my own team shot me in the back" problem.
- **Skip** — It is built for a Colonial Marines round, not a station one: the shields are alien caste powers keyed to a hive and plasma economy, and the melee damage scaling reads from a marine skills/rank system, so grafting it means bringing those systems or gutting the parts that make it interesting.
- **Touches** — security, antagonist, all-players, command
- **Needs** — [xenomorph-hive](#xenomorph-hive), [squads-ranks-and-skills](#squads-ranks-and-skills)
- **Verified** — partly supported. All cited files are RMC-14's own _RMC14 namespace files (self-contained, no upstream-directory edits in this unit's evidence), but SharedRMCMeleeWeaponSystem.cs directly imports and calls into Content.Shared._RMC14.Marines.Skills (_skills.ApplyMeleeSkillModifier, _skills.GetSkill for RMCMeleeDamageSkillComponent) and Content.Shared._RMC14.Xenonids (_xenoQuery checks in ImmuneToUnarmed and MeleeReceivedMultiplier logic), and the shield system's ShieldType enum and components (VanguardShieldComponent, CrusherShieldComponent) are named for specific Xenomorph castes with plasma costs — confirming genuine functional entanglement with the fork's separate skills/rank system and hive/xenomorph system, exactly as the claim states, even though file-locality alone (path data) would read as drop-in.
  - unsupported: "lying down makes you easier to hit" as part of the dodge-rating system: EvasionComponent's only extra modifiers found in EvasionSystem.cs are size (SizeSmall +10, SizeBig -10) and Rest (-15); DownedEvent/StoodEvent only trigger a recompute with no downed-specific evasion penalty visible anywhere in the evasion code. The only prone-related combat effect actually found is a flat damage multiplier (gun.Comp.ProneDamageMult) applied to point-blank ammo shots on downed targets in CMGunSystem.cs — a damage bonus, not a hit-chance/evasion mechanic, and scoped to point-blank shots rather than general ranged combat.

**sunrise**

*loop-change · entangled · medium confidence · 5 forks carry it*

Sunrise fills out the melee shelf with weapons that each change a fight in a specific way: a pocketable energy shield you flick open to soak hits and bounce lasers until its battery runs dry (it recharges itself after a lull), a two-handed double energy sword that only lights up when wielded and blocks well while held, a wieldable double stun baton that knocks the wind out of two people at once, a switchblade that flicks from pocket-lint to stabbing knife, a heavy breaching hammer that pries airlocks open and caves in structures when swung two-handed, a shock-cane, and an exotic scythe that flings molten projectiles while wielded. A whetstone-style sharpener puts a temporary edge on any slashing or piercing weapon for a limited number of swings, then the blade visibly dulls and the stone wears out. Some syndicate weapons are biocoded, so a crewmember who loots an energy sword off a dead traitor cannot swing it at all.

- **Take** — Rechargeable pocket shields, sharpening and biocoded antag weapons give melee fights a defensive and upkeep layer instead of pure damage trading, and most of it is item prototypes rather than new mechanics.
- **Skip** — It is a grab bag, not a coherent system: 155 files where individual pieces quietly reach into the fork's other content (the abductor silencer needs the abductor tag and mute toxin, the double energy sword doubles as a Sunrise surgery scalpel, the sharpening component lives in their blood cult namespace), and nothing reaches players until you also edit upstream uplink, vendor and loadout catalogs to stock it.
- **Touches** — security, antagonist, all-players, cargo, salvage
- **Needs** — [abductors](#abductors), [surgery-and-limb-wounds](#surgery-and-limb-wounds)
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. All 11 cited files and the catalog file I found live under fork-owned _Sunrise/ (or shared _Starlight) paths, none patch an upstream-named file, so "fork-patches-upstream" is not shown. But the claim's core "needs-upstream-edits" premise (must edit upstream uplink/vendor catalogs) is directly contradicted for the uplink path by Resources/Prototypes/_Sunrise/Catalog/uplink_catalog.yml, a fork-owned catalog that already stocks the switchblade, biocoded e-sword, and a breaching-hammer variant. What is real and confirmed is entanglement with the fork's OTHER systems: silencer.yml requires the Abductor tag + MuteToxinAbductor reagent, e_sword.yml's double energy sword carries Scalpel/SurgeryTool components tying it to Sunrise's surgery system, and SharpeningSystem.cs imports Content.Shared._Sunrise.BloodCult.Items for SharpenerComponent/SharpenedComponent (used but not defined in the cited file), meaning the sharpening mechanic actually lives in the blood-cult namespace. That is sibling-feature entanglement, not proven upstream-file dependency, so the unit is better classified as entangled with the fork's own other content than as strictly needing upstream edits.
  - unsupported: "nothing reaches players until you also edit upstream uplink, vendor and loadout catalogs to stock it" — refuted for the uplink channel: Resources/Prototypes/_Sunrise/Catalog/uplink_catalog.yml is itself a fork-owned file (under _Sunrise/) that already stocks WeaponMeleeSwitchblade (as UplinkSwitchblade) and EnergySwordBiocode (as UplinkEswordNuke) and a breaching-hammer variant (UplinkWeaponBreachingHammer -> SyndieBreachingHammer). Wiring these into the traitor shop did not require touching any upstream file; the fork simply added its own catalog file.
  - unsupported: "a wieldable double stun baton that knocks the wind out of two people at once" — doublestunbaton.yml shows MeleeWeapon angle:180 (a wide swing arc) plus StaminaDamageOnHit:40, which is consistent with hitting multiple targets in one swing, but nothing in the file states or limits it to exactly two people; this is the assessor's inference from angle, not a directly evidenced mechanic.

**serbia-strong**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 5 forks carry it*

Shields stop being passive luck and become something you actively hold up: a dedicated keybind raises the shield, an "Active Blocking" indicator appears on your HUD, your character visibly changes stance, and your chance to stop incoming melee and gunfire jumps (a riot shield goes from roughly a coin-flip to blocking about three attacks in four), at the cost of not being able to throw anything while braced. Shields now have their own condition you can examine and they wear down under fire, eventually shattering into steel, glass, planks or webbing depending on what they were made of, and there is a full ladder of them: cardboard, wooden buckler, makeshift steel, web, riot, laser-dissipating, heavy ballistic (which slows you down), collapsible telescopic, mirror, clockwork, and toggleable energy shields including a syndicate red variant. Armour and shields also work by threshold rather than percentage, so a weak hit bounces off entirely while a heavy one punches through, holding a raised shield resists the instant stun from batons, and some armour converts part of a stunbaton's stamina hit into shock damage instead of dropping you outright.

- **Take** — It turns melee and close-range fights from a stat-check into an active exchange, and specifically defangs the stunbaton-into-cuffs instant-win that dominates security versus antagonist encounters.
- **Skip** — It replaces the whole armour and stun pipeline, not just shields: threshold armour, stamina conversion and instastun resistance rebalance every existing weapon, armour set and antagonist kit at once, and it needs a new keybind wired into upstream input handling, so you inherit a permanent balance-tuning job.
- **Touches** — security, antagonist, all-players, cargo
- **Verified** — supported. I found direct edits to three genuinely-upstream, non-SS220 files: Content.Shared/Input/ContentKeyFunctions.cs (a vanilla file listing dozens of engine key functions) has 'ToggleActiveBlocking' spliced in at line 11 among stock entries like Drop/ExamineEntity/FocusChat; Resources/keybinds.yml has a block literally fenced '#SS220 shield rework begin' binding ToggleActiveBlocking to key B; and Content.Client/Input/ContentContexts.cs adds 'human.AddFunction(ContentKeyFunctions.ToggleActiveBlocking); //SS220 shield rework'. That settles needs-upstream-edits as fork-patches-upstream, not just integration-would-require-upstream-edits. The gameplay claim itself checks out in fine detail: shields.yml shows 11 named shield prototypes (Riot, RiotLaser, RiotBullet, WoodenBuckler, Card/cardboard, Makeshift/steel, Web, Clockwork, Mirror, Energy, Telescopic) each with AltArmor tresholdDict/durabilityTresholdDict (threshold not percentage) and Destructible behaviors spawning SheetSteel/SheetGlass, MaterialWoodPlank, or MaterialWebSilk on break; RiotBulletShieldAlt has ClothingSpeedModifier/HeldSpeedModifier 0.9 (the slow-you-down heavy ballistic shield); EnergyShieldAlt is ItemToggle-based and syndi.yml adds a red-lit EnergyShieldSyndi variant; BaseShieldAlt carries InstastunResist/InstastunResistOnActiveBlocking (baton-stun resistance while blocking); StaminaConvertArmorComponent.cs literally converts a DamageCoefficient of stamina damage into a configured DamageType (e.g. Shock); blocking.yml is the 'Active Blocking' HUD alert; and SharedAltBlockingSystem.User.cs wires the toggle to ContentKeyFunctions.ToggleActiveBlocking and cancels ThrowAttemptEvent while blocking (can't throw while braced). Only minor imprecisions found, noted in overclaims.
  - unsupported: "your chance to stop incoming melee and gunfire jumps (a riot shield goes from roughly a coin-flip to blocking about three attacks in four)" blends two different stats: RiotShieldAlt's actual AltBlocking values are rangeBlockProb 0.50 -> activeRangeBlockProb 0.60 (ranged/gunfire), and meleeBlockProb 0.65 -> activeMeleeBlockProb 0.75 (melee). No single stat goes from 0.50 to 0.75; the claim cherry-picks the passive number from one axis (ranged) and the active number from the other (melee) to build a punchier 'coin-flip to 3-in-4' line.
  - unsupported: "there is a full ladder of them" implies an exhaustive list, but the fork also ships a Dagon's Scale cult shield (Resources/Prototypes/SS220/Entities/Objects/Shields/dagots_scale.yml, parent BaseShieldAlt) that isn't in the enumerated ladder.

### Explosion rework and effects

<a id="explosion-rework"></a>

Changes how explosions propagate and how they read on screen: directional obstruction-aware blasts, shockwave overlays, explosion effect entities and shrapnel projectiles.

**stellar-station**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 9 forks carry it*

Explosions hit harder to look at and to stand near. A blast throws a red-orange flash and a rippling shockwave that visibly warps the screen, shakes your camera (harder the closer you are), and plays a different, muffled boom for people far enough away to only hear it. Small blasts no longer just chew tiles: they knock you off your feet, stun you, and fling you away from the centre, but only if you actually had line of sight to it, so ducking behind a wall or a locker genuinely protects you. Some bombs also spray shrapnel outward in all directions as real flying projectiles, and different explosive types (standard, fire, demolition, EMP, and several unique device blasts) each get their own coloured flash, light, and shockwave feel.

- **Take** — Cover suddenly matters in a firefight: obstruction-checked knockback, knockdown and stun turn grenades from a damage number into a positional threat, and the shockwave/screenshake presentation makes every explosion read instantly.
- **Skip** — It is a second explosion system living alongside upstream's, so every grenade, bomb and explosive device you want it on needs its prototype rewired, and the screenshake half pulls in a separate camera-effects system vendored from another fork.
- **Touches** — security, antagonist, engineering, salvage, all-players
- **Needs** — [visual-feedback-effects](#visual-feedback-effects)
- **Verified** — partly supported. The fork's own explosion-rework files (explosions.yml, StellarExplosiveComponent.cs, SharedStellarExplosionSystem.cs) are self-contained under _ST/Content.Stellar.Shared and do not edit any upstream/vanilla prototype file in place — grenades.yml and Bombs/*.yml still carry only the plain vanilla Explosive component, unmodified. But SharedStellarExplosionSystem.cs has a real compile-time dependency on Content.Shared/_ES/Camera/ESScreenshakeSystem.cs, a separately-authored (SPDX 'Mirrorcult', MIT-licensed) subsystem outside the _ST namespace that the evidence_cited list omits entirely, confirming the claim's own depends_on: visual-feedback-effects. Giving the new system the game-wide reach the gameplay text implies would require editing a target codebase's own upstream grenade/bomb prototypes, since as-is only a couple of fork-specific ForkFiltered antagonist grenades use it.
  - unsupported: "only if you actually had line of sight to it, so ducking behind a wall or a locker genuinely protects you" — in SharedStellarExplosionSystem.cs the obstruction check (_interaction.InRangeUnobstructed) gates ONLY the physical knockback throw. Knockdown and Stun are applied in a separate loop over all entities in range with no obstruction check whatsoever (only a whitelist filter), so cover does not protect you from being knocked down or stunned, only (sometimes) from being physically flung. One shipped prototype (StellarGrenadeGorlexC4) even sets `ignoreObstruction: true`, explicitly disabling the one check that does exist.
  - unsupported: "Small blasts no longer just chew tiles: they knock you off your feet, stun you, and fling you away" reads as a description of explosions in general, but as actually wired in the repo the StellarExplosive/StellarShockwave system is applied only to a handful of new fork-specific antagonist grenades (StellarGrenadeCybersunEmp/Flash, StellarGrenadeGorlexExplosive/C4 — all tagged `categories: [ForkFiltered]`). The vanilla frag grenade, flashbang, minibomb and all the Bombs/*.yml prototypes (Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Objects/Weapons/Throwable/grenades.yml, .../Bombs/*.yml) are untouched and still use only the plain upstream `Explosive` component with no knockback/knockdown/stun/shrapnel/shockwave at all.

**rmc14**

*loop-change · entangled · medium confidence · 9 forks carry it*

Explosions stop being a flat circle of damage and become a thing you read and react to: a nearby blast punches a visible shockwave ripple across your screen, throws shrapnel streaks outward, and burns scorch marks into the floor around it (darker at the centre, lighter at the edges, and moppable afterwards). A blast happening far away plays a distant rumble instead of the same close-up bang, so you can tell roughly how far off the boom was, and heavy ordnance like mortar and orbital-strike blasts is tuned to chew through walls rather than just hurt people. On the throwing end, priming a grenade makes your character shout a warning that everyone nearby sees and hears, and grenades gain new ways to go off: on landing after a throw, after flying a set distance, when the round is shot out of a launcher, or on a sword impact. Cluster and shrapnel grenades scatter their payload in a configurable arc (including backwards when they bounce off something). Separately you can plant a claymore mine, which takes a few seconds to place and arm, ignores your own side, blows up if someone shoots it twice, and can be carefully disarmed with a pulsing tool. Some explosives implode instead, dragging everything nearby into the centre before they go off.

- **Take** — It makes every explosion in the game legible: screen shockwave, shrapnel, floor scorching and near-vs-far blast audio give players real feedback about where a bomb went off and how close it was, and the trigger variants (throw-end, distance, shot-to-arm, claymores) turn explosives from one-shot timers into placeable, plannable tools.
- **Skip** — It is built for a Colonial Marines game, not a station one: claymores and cluster payloads key off RMC-14's own IFF faction system, the explosion presets are tuned around mortars and orbital bombardment, and the trigger layer hooks upstream TriggerEvent and extends the upstream ProjectileGrenadeComponent as a partial, so you cannot take the pretty half (shockwave, shrapnel, scorch, far-sound) without either untangling it from the marine content or accepting the whole 150-file block and its upstream-touching edges.
- **Touches** — security, antagonist, all-players, cargo
- **Needs** — [firearms-content-expansion](#firearms-content-expansion)
- **Verified** — supported. Claim's graft_shape is "entangled" and this held up under direct inspection — in fact the entanglement is worse than the claim states. The claim says the trigger layer "extends the upstream ProjectileGrenadeComponent as a partial," implying a self-contained fork-side partial; but I fetched Content.Server/Explosion/Components/ProjectileGrenadeComponent.cs (an upstream-namespace path, NOT under any _RMC14 directory) and diffed it against space-wizards/space-station-14's copy of the same file: the fork's copy adds `using Content.Server._RMC14.Explosion;` and `Access(typeof(RMCProjectileGrenadeSystem))` directly into the upstream file. That is a genuine in-place edit to an upstream file outside the fork's namespace directories, which the evidence_cited list didn't even surface (it only cited the fork's own RMCProjectileGrenadeComponent.cs partial). Combined with RMCExplosionSystem.cs hooking upstream TriggerEvent/ActiveTimerTriggerEvent/ExplosionSystem, and RMCLandmineComponent depending on the fork's own IFF faction system, "entangled" is the right call — if anything the claim undersold how the fork touches upstream-owned files.
  - unsupported: "burns scorch marks into the floor... (darker at the centre, lighter at the edges...)" — code only shows two decal tags, CenterDecalTag="RMCScorch" and EdgeDecalTag="RMCScorchSmall" (RMCScorchEffectComponent.cs); this distinguishes decal size/position, not a confirmed color/darkness gradient — the actual decal sprite/color prototypes were not reachable to verify "darker/lighter"
  - unsupported: "a nearby blast punches a visible shockwave ripple across your screen" — RMCExplosionShockWaveComponent.cs confirms a shockwave effect exists with FalloffPower/Sharpness/Width fields (consistent with a radial distortion), but no client-side rendering/shader file was found to directly confirm it renders as a full-screen effect specifically (component is server/shared only in what was checked)

**goobstation**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 9 forks carry it*

Blasts stop being one generic orange boom: a supermatter breach throws a green, radiation-laced shockwave, a tesla arc detonates in cyan sparks, a rigged pizza box makes a tight thump that scorches people without tearing the floor open, and a molotov you build and light by hand shatters into a spreading pool of fire that clings to anyone who runs through it. Flashbangs now knock you flat and stun you on a sliding scale by how close you were standing, so hugging the grenade is far worse than being across the room, and wearing earmuffs or a helmet with hearing protection shrinks the radius that can floor you (examining the gear tells you how much it protects). Bombs can also be wired to go off on a spoken code phrase, on being punched, or on being dropped, so an antagonist can hand someone a "gift" that only detonates when the right person says the right word.

- **Take** — Flashbang knockdown that scales with distance and is reduced by hearing protection turns "throw bang, everyone falls" into a positioning-and-gear fight, and the extra explosion types make each hazard read distinctly on screen instead of every boom looking the same.
- **Skip** — The flashbang half hooks into upstream's flash system (AreaFlashEvent, FlashSystem resistance tags) and a fork-side Common/Shared flash layer, so it is not a clean drop-in and will need re-patching every time upstream touches flashes or stuns; several explosion prototypes also assume fork content (supermatter, thermobaric launcher, molotov construction graph and RSI) that would arrive as dead entries otherwise.
- **Touches** — security, antagonist, all-players, engineering, service
- **Verified** — partly supported. Fetched Goob-Station's own Content.Shared/Flash/SharedFlashSystem.cs (an upstream-namespaced path, not under _Goobstation/) and found it directly edited in place with \"// Goob edit\" / \"// Goobstation\" markers adding `AreaFlashEvent` and the `IgnoreResistancesTag` ProtoId that Content.Goobstation.Server/Flashbang/FlashbangSystem.cs subscribes to and checks. Diffing against vanilla space-wizards/space-station-14's Content.Shared/Flash/SharedFlashSystem.cs confirms these symbols do not exist upstream — they were added by Goob-Station directly inside the upstream file/namespace, which the path-data evidence (limited to _Goobstation-prefixed paths) could not see. This confirms the claim's own skip_because reasoning and downgrades the seed's \"drop-in\" guess to needs-upstream-edits, specifically the fork-patches-upstream variant.
  - unsupported: "Bombs can also be wired to go off on a spoken code phrase, on being punched, or on being dropped" — the "on being dropped" trigger is not backed by the cited evidence or by anything found in Content.Goobstation.Server/Explosion/Components/: the only similarly-named component, OnTrigger/DropOnTriggerComponent.cs, does the opposite (it drops the entity's held items when the bomb triggers, it is not a trigger fired by the bomb itself being dropped). "Spoken code phrase" (TriggerOnVoiceIdLockedComponent) and "on being punched" (TriggerOnMeleeComponent.cs, confirmed to exist) both check out; the drop-trigger claim does not.

### Barricades, sentries and field fortification

<a id="field-deployables-and-fortification"></a>

Deployable cover and automated defences built mid-round: barricade kits, sandbags, entrenching tools, sentry turrets and heavy weapon emplacements with IFF.

**rmc14**

*loop-change · entangled · high confidence · 3 forks carry it*

Players can turn any patch of open ground into a defended position mid-fight. You dig with an entrenching tool to fill sandbags and stack them into walls, unfold portable metal, plasteel, wood or snow barricades (with a hint that you should stand flush against cover or more than four tiles back for it to help you), link folding barricades together into a continuous line, string barbed wire across the top so anyone climbing over gets cut, and repair the battered ones with a blowtorch or nailgun as they crumble through visible damage stages. On top of that you can bolt down automated sentry guns that hum to life, track and shoot intruders, need their magazines swapped when dry, can be rotated with a screwdriver, upgraded with kits, and monitored or controlled remotely from a ruggedized sentry laptop once you link them with an access tuner. Heavy machine guns like the M2C come as folded tripod kits you screwdriver into place and then man with both hands free, complete with an overheating penalty that punishes holding the trigger down.

- **Take** — It gives combat a spatial, buildable dimension: fights become about who fortified the corridor first rather than who clicked faster, and it hands non-combat players a meaningful job during a siege.
- **Skip** — RMC-14 built this for a planetside marines-vs-xenos war, so it leans on that fork's skill gating (RMCSkillConstruction), its acid and planet-surface deploy checks, and its own ammo and repair systems; stripping those out of ~190 files is most of the work, and a station with sentry turrets and barbed barricades is a very different balance problem from one without.
- **Touches** — security, engineering, cargo, antagonist, all-players
- **Needs** — [squads-ranks-and-skills](#squads-ranks-and-skills), [firearms-content-expansion](#firearms-content-expansion), [construction-and-crafting](#construction-and-crafting)
- **Verified** — supported. Fetched all 7 cited files plus the barricade directory listing. Every concrete gameplay beat checks out: entrenching.ftl confirms digging/filling sandbags; barricade.ftl confirms damage stages 1-4, folding-barricade linking, and barbed-wire examine text; barricade_metal.yml confirms RMCRepairable (blowtorch/welder) + NailgunRepairable components, the Barbed component, and — critically — a hard `skill: RMCSkillConstruction` gate on repair, directly substantiating the skip_because's RMCSkillConstruction claim; the barricade directory listing confirms metal/plasteel/wood/snow variants exist as claimed; rmc-sentry.ftl confirms hum-to-life, magazine swap, screwdriver rotation, and upgrade-kit text; sentry_laptop.yml confirms remote monitoring/control via a security access tuner AND carries `RequiresSkill: RMCSkillEngineer: 2`, independently confirming the skills-system entanglement; emplacements.ftl confirms the M2C/ML66D fold-mount-screwdriver-both-hands-free-overheat mechanics. The claim already downgraded the path-data seed from drop-in to entangled, and the RMCSkillConstruction/RMCSkillEngineer component gates I found are direct code-level proof of that entanglement with the fork's own skill system, not just a plausible inference — so the entangled call is confirmed, not merely unrefuted.
  - unsupported: "an overheating penalty that punishes holding the trigger down" — the emplacements.ftl only confirms an overheat mechanic exists (emplacement-mounted-weapon-overheated) and that overheating causes damage to the weapon; nothing in the fetched locale text specifies the trigger must be held down continuously to trigger it, so this causal detail is asserted beyond what was read.

**serbia-strong**

*loop-change · entangled · medium confidence · 3 forks carry it*

Fights stop being open-floor shootouts because you can put things between you and the bullets. Barricades and similar cover give incoming shots a real chance to be stopped, and that chance grows the further away the shooter is, so ducking behind sandbags actually punishes long-range fire while doing little against someone standing on top of you; friendly or designated entities can be set to shoot past it. Engineers can set up a generator that projects a curved or circular energy barrier in front of it, humming while it burns power to stay up and draining faster the harder it gets hit, and it can be wired to a switch or button to drop and raise on command. Alongside that there are bear-trap style leg traps you spend a few seconds arming on the floor (and a few seconds carefully defusing), which snap onto whoever steps in and can stun them, and a battery-powered point-defence emplacement that swats down incoming projectiles that stray into its radius, though it misses sometimes. Certain armour and equipment also carries a personal shield emitter that soaks a set number of hits before recharging; examining tells you how many charges are left, you can only wear one such piece at a time, and an EMP jams it locked onto your body so you cannot take it off.

- **Take** — Distance-scaled cover plus deployable energy barriers turns SS14 gunfights into something with positioning and terrain, which is the cheapest available fix for how flat ranged combat currently feels.
- **Skip** — It is four loosely related mechanics (barricade cover, forcefield generators, traps, point defence) bundled under one name, each hooking into projectile and damage flow, so you inherit four balance surfaces and a permanent maintenance tax on the hottest upstream code path; the SS220 files also carry a hosting-restricted EULA/CLA header rather than a plain permissive licence, which needs checking before anything is copied.
- **Touches** — security, engineering, antagonist, cargo, all-players
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. The four subsystems are individually well-evidenced (BarricadeComponent's MinHitChance/MaxHitChance/MinDistance/MaxDistance confirm distance-scaled cover plus a Whitelist for friendlies; ForcefieldGeneratorComponent confirms EnergyUpkeep/DamageToEnergyCoefficient/idle-hum sound/DeviceLinking toggle port; TrapComponent confirms 5s SetTrapDelay/DefuseTrapDelay plus DurationStun; AirDefenseComponent+SharedAirDefenseSystem confirm PowerCell-driven battery power, a circular fixture radius check, and MissProbability=0.25f; FieldShieldProviderComponent + force-field-ui.ftl confirm charge-count examine text, one-shield-at-a-time, and LockOnEmp). But I fetched SharedBarricadeSystem.cs myself (not in the cited evidence) and it subscribes only to pre-existing engine event types (PreventCollideEvent, AttemptHitscanRaycastHitEvent, ProjectileHitEvent, StartCollide), and the AirDefenseTarget tag is defined in the fork's own SS220-namespaced tags.yml -- i.e. no upstream FILES appear to be patched, which weighs against a literal 'fork-patches-upstream' reading. The claim's own skip_because reasoning (four mechanics 'hooking into projectile and damage flow' on 'the hottest upstream code path') is really an entanglement argument, not an upstream-file-edit argument, and it overgeneralizes: the bear-trap subsystem has nothing to do with projectile/damage flow at all (it's a DoAfter-armed floor trap with a stun, triggered by stepping on it). Wiring shield emitters onto pre-existing armor items, or adding barricades/traps into construction and loot tables, would plausibly touch existing upstream prototype files even though the fork's C# is self-contained -- that supports 'integration-would-require-upstream-edits' over 'fork-patches-upstream'. Net effect: this reads less like literal upstream edits and more like deep behavioral coupling with the game's live collision/hitscan/power pipeline across four separately-balanced mechanics.
  - unsupported: "the SS220 files also carry a hosting-restricted EULA/CLA header rather than a plain permissive licence" -- false as a blanket statement across the cited evidence: FieldShieldProviderComponent.cs is headed '© SS220, MIT license', the FieldShield audio attributions.yml credits CC-BY-SA-3.0 material from Baystation12, and both AirDefenseComponent.cs and SharedAirDefenseSystem.cs carry no license header at all. Only Barricade, Trap, and Forcefield files show the EULA/CLA-with-hosting-restriction header.
  - unsupported: "each hooking into projectile and damage flow" -- true for Barricade and AirDefense, but the bear-trap subsystem (TrapComponent) is a floor-mounted DoAfter arm/defuse mechanic with a stun, not something that hooks into projectile or damage flow.
  - unsupported: "Engineers can set up a generator that projects a curved or circular energy barrier" -- the specific shape claim ('curved or circular') is not shown in any of the cited evidence; ForcefieldGeneratorComponent.cs only exposes an opaque ForcefieldParams data field with no shape details verified.

**ephemeral-space, far-horizons, starlight, sunrise**

*activity · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 3 forks carry it*

These four forks each add one deployable-cover gadget rather than a fortification system. Ephemeral Space gives you a barricade kit: click it in hand and after a three-second setup you drop a full-tile barricade to crouch behind, or use it on an airlock to board the doorway shut. Far Horizons adds a wall-sized holographic field generator you anchor and wire into medium-voltage power, which projects an airtight, light-blocking shimmering barrier that can be flipped on and off remotely by signal, with lights on the casing showing how charged it is. Starlight and Sunrise both carry the same energy dome: a battery-powered shield bubble you toggle with an action or a linked switch, which visibly parries incoming hits with a sound and drains charge per point of damage absorbed until the battery runs dry and the dome collapses.

- **Take** — Each piece is small and self-contained, and a one-click barricade kit or a rechargeable shield bubble gives fights actual cover and terrain instead of open-corridor trading.
- **Skip** — Four unrelated gadgets that only look like one feature: the barricade kit needs a marker component sprinkled onto upstream airlocks, Sunrise's dome sits in an unnamespaced Content.Server/EnergyDome folder rather than a fork directory, and none of them ship any locale or guidebook text, so you would be writing all the player-facing wording and balance numbers yourself.
- **Touches** — security, engineering, antagonist, cargo, all-players
- **Verified** — partly supported. Cloned all four forks (sparse checkout) and read the actual source. The core mechanics described (3s barricade DoAfter with Tile/Airlock variants, dual-generator holofield with medium-voltage/DeviceLink/GenericVisualizer power lights, battery-drain energy dome with parry sound and DeviceLink toggle) are all real and match the code. Sunrise's dome sits in Content.Server/EnergyDome and Content.Shared/EnergyDome (no _Sunrise prefix), confirming that specific claim.
