### Mech and exosuit overhaul

<a id="mech-overhaul"></a>

Extends piloted exosuits with new chassis, weapon and utility modules, construction graphs, pilot support modules and cargo-handling power loaders.

**goobstation**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 3 forks carry it*

Engineers and roboticists build named exosuits piece by piece — a Ripley MkII, Clarke, Durand or Gygax harness plus its head, arms, legs or treads — then a pilot climbs in and bolts on hardpoints. Miners get drills (including a diamond-tipped upgrade) and a proto-kinetic launcher for tearing through rock; security and hostile pilots get a wall of mounted guns instead: heavy pulse rifles, "Firedart" and "Solaris" lasers, an immolation beam, a Tesla cannon, scattershot and incendiary shotguns, an autocannon, two sizes of missile rack that must be reloaded from outside the suit, a flashbang launcher for riots, non-lethal disablers and tasers, a chainsword, and joke mortars that lob banana peels or mousetraps. Weapons are class-locked so a mining suit cannot mount a pulse rifle, they run off the mech's own battery, and cargo posts bounties asking the station to ship a finished Clarke, Durand, Ripley or Gygax back to a client.

- **Take** — It turns the thin upstream exosuit into a real mid-round escalation object: a buildable, class-differentiated armed vehicle that gives engineering and roboticists a long-horizon project and gives security and antags something to fight over.
- **Skip** — A dozen lethal mounted weapons including missile racks and a Tesla cannon is a large balance surface to own, and the pieces it needs (per-chassis equipment tags, construction graphs, weapon upgrade slots, a pilot-faction hook fired from the upstream mech system) mean it does not land as a clean isolated drop.
- **Touches** — engineering, science, security, cargo, salvage, antagonist
- **Needs** — [gun-attachments-and-upgrades](#gun-attachments-and-upgrades)
- **Verified** — supported. I fetched all 11 cited files plus, to settle the graft-shape question, the actual upstream file Content.Shared/Mech/EntitySystems/SharedMechSystem.cs (not in the cited list). That upstream file is patched in place with dozens of '// Goobstation' / '// Goobstation Change' tagged edits across ~600 lines (new dependencies on EmagSystem/SharedHandsSystem/SharedVirtualItemSystem, a new CVar-gated 'mech gun outside mech' behavior, a mech-lights toggle action, and the very MechInsertedEvent/MechEjectedEvent firing that Content.Goobstation.Shared/Mech/GoobMechSystem.cs subscribes to for the pilot-faction hook). This is a real in-place upstream patch, not a hypothetical one, so the claim's own 'needs-upstream-edits' call is correct and if anything conservative. The gameplay description itself checked out almost line for line: mecha_equipment.yml shows the CombatMech/IndustrialMech/SpecialMech/SmallMech tag scheme (class-lock basis) and per-class StaticPrice; the Gun/*.yml files confirm the named weapons (eZ-14 pulse rifle, Firedart/Solaris lasers, ZFI immolation beam, P-X Tesla Cannon, Scattershot/Hades incendiary shotguns, Ultra AC-2, SRM-8/BRM-6 missile racks, SGL-6 flashbang launcher, CH-PD disabler, PBT taser, banana/mousetrap mortars); Weapons/Melee files confirm the exosuit drill, diamond-tipped drill, and chainsword; BaseMechWeaponRange/BaseMechWeaponMelee show the Battery component comment 'Battery is charged by mech' backing the 'runs off the mech's own battery' claim; mech_construction.yml confirms Ripley MkII, Clarke (with treads), Durand and Gygax harness+part+construction-graph structure; mechs.ftl confirms the exact cargo bounty locale strings for Clarke/Durand/Ripley MkII/Gygax.
  - unsupported: 'two sizes of missile rack that must be reloaded from outside the suit' generalizes a trait to both racks, but only the BRM-6 ('Tubes must be reloaded from the outside') states it in its description -- the SRM-8 ('Launches low-explosive breaching missiles designed to explode only when striking a sturdy target') has no such text, and both use the same BatteryAmmoProvider/Battery mechanism with no distinct external-reload component visible in the cited files.

**sunrise**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 3 forks carry it*

Piloting an exosuit gets a proper gear wheel: hit the equipment key and a radial menu pops up at your cursor showing every weapon and tool bolted into the mech, plus a "bare hands" option, with the currently active one lit green — you pick your drill or gun directly instead of cycling through the list, and a popup confirms the swap. Mechs also stop being immune to electronics warfare: an EMP pulse shocks the chassis for damage on a short cooldown and leaves it visibly sparking for a few seconds afterward, so crew have a way to hurt a rampaging exosuit without a gun. On top of that, anyone holding a can of mech paint can right-click a mech and, after a couple of seconds of spraying, recolour its chassis (open, closed and broken sprites all follow the new paint job).

- **Take** — The radial equipment wheel is a flat quality-of-life win for every mech pilot, and EMP vulnerability hands the crew a real, non-firearm counter to an exosuit that has gone hostile.
- **Skip** — The fork-namespaced files only deliver the selection wheel, EMP damage and a paint verb — not the new chassis and modules the feature name suggests — and the server system is compile-wired into Sunrise's own cryo-teleport and paint systems, so it will not build standalone without stripping those handlers.
- **Touches** — engineering, cargo, science, security, salvage
- **Needs** — [latejoin-spawn-and-cryo](#latejoin-spawn-and-cryo)
- **Verified** — supported. The gameplay description holds up well: SharedMechEquipmentSelectSystem.cs + MechEquipmentSelectBoundUserInterface.cs confirm a radial UI (SimpleRadialMenu) opened at cursor with a "no equipment" option and a green highlight (Palettes.Green) on the active selection, plus a confirmation popup via PopupPredicted. SunriseMechSystem.cs confirms the EMP path (OnEmpPulse -> DamageableSystem.TryChangeDamage with a 6s cooldown, EnsureComp<MechOnEMPPulseComponent> driving a 1s-interval spark effect) and the paint verb (GetVerbsEvent<UtilityVerb>, 2s DoAfter, then SetData on MechVisualLayers.Base/Open/Broken). The "bare hands" framing is directly backed by upstream MechComponent.cs's own doc comment: "If null, the mech is using just its fists." Critically, that same fetch of Content.Shared/Mech/Components/MechComponent.cs (an upstream, non-_Sunrise file) shows CurrentSelectedEquipment and nullable BaseState/OpenState/BrokenState fields living directly in the vanilla component — i.e. this unit really does patch an upstream file in place, which the path data (and even the claim's own evidence_cited list) never surfaced. SunriseMechSystem.cs also confirms real coupling to other _Sunrise systems: it imports Content.Server._Sunrise.CryoTeleport (BeforeCryoTeleportEvent, matching the stated latejoin-spawn-and-cryo dependency) and Content.Shared._Sunrise.Paint.PaintDoAfterEvent for the paint DoAfter. So the claim's needs-upstream-edits verdict is correct, and actually understated: it is both a direct upstream patch (MechComponent.cs) and cross-dependent on sibling _Sunrise features.

**rmc14**

*activity · entangled · high confidence · 3 forks carry it*

You climb into a two-armed walking loader (a buckle-in exosuit rather than a piloted mech) and use its claws to pick up things no person could carry: crated 30mm ammo, missile pods, rocket pods, laser cannons, medevac winches, fulton balloon recovery rigs and paradrop gear. You walk them over to the dropship's hardpoints and spend several seconds bolting each one on, or unbolting it to swap loadouts; empty ammo crates and unwanted parts can be shoved back into a dropship fabricator to recover most of their build cost. The loader itself is slow, stomps loudly, punches hard enough to matter in a brawl, and leaves a wreck behind when destroyed; people trained on it work noticeably faster than people who are not.

- **Take** — It is the clean answer to "heavy object a human should not be able to lift": a buckle-in loader plus grab/attach/detach do-afters that any fork can hang its own bulky cargo, machine parts or weapon mounts onto.
- **Skip** — Almost all of the content here exists to service RMC-14's dropship rearm loop, so the loader arrives welded to dropship weapon/utility hardpoints, a points-based dropship fabricator and RMC's skill-gating system; strip those out and you are left with a forklift with no freight.
- **Touches** — cargo, engineering, shuttle-piloting, command, medical
- **Needs** — [squads-ranks-and-skills](#squads-ranks-and-skills), [shuttle-piloting-extensions](#shuttle-piloting-extensions), [ship-to-ship-combat](#ship-to-ship-combat)
- **Verified** — supported. Fetched all six cited files directly from RMC-14/RMC-14. rmc_power_loader.yml confirms the buckle-in Strap mechanic (not a piloted mech), MobMover/InputMover, MeleeWeapon 30 Blunt damage (punches hard), baseWalkSpeed/Sprint 1 (slow), FootstepModifier with a dedicated powerloader step sound (stomps loudly), and SpawnOnTerminate wreckage entities on destruction. dropship_weapons.yml confirms GAU-21 30mm cannon, guided missile launcher, and rocket pod, each with PowerLoaderAttachable/Detachable attachDelay/detachDelay of 7 seconds (several seconds bolting/unbolting). dropship_utility.yml confirms medevac winch, fulton recovery, and paradrop deployment attachments. dropship_fabricator.yml's own description states "get 80% of your points back" when recycling parts/ammo in a powerloader claw, matching "recover most of their build cost." PowerLoaderComponent.cs shows SpeedSkill=RMCSkillPowerLoader with SpeedPerSkill=1.2, confirming trained pilots work faster, and it imports Content.Shared._RMC14.Marines.Skills, directly tying the loader to RMC14's skill system (squads-ranks-and-skills dependency). Every DropshipWeapon/DropshipUtility entity is gated by RMCSkillPilot and wired only to RMCDropshipWeaponPoint/RMCDropshipUtilityPoint hardpoints defined elsewhere in the dropship system, confirming the claim's own downgrade to entangled: the loader's grab/attach/detach mechanic is real and generic, but essentially every piece of cited content (weapons, utility gear, ammo, the fabricator economy) is welded to RMC14's dropship rearm loop and skill system, exactly as the claim describes. No overclaims found; the claim is notably conservative if anything (it already downgrades the seed's drop-in guess to entangled, and the evidence fully bears that out).

**starlight**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 3 forks carry it*

Building a mech now includes slotting a physical reactor into its battery bay, so a chassis is only as good as the power cell someone welded into it, and conversion kits let you walk an existing frame up into a better one (a Ripley into a Ripley MkII, or a Paddy). Once you are inside, the mech hands you a row of pilot buttons: flip on emergency sirens, blast an air horn at whoever is standing in the doorway, switch to night vision, or fire up thrusters that burn charge for extra speed. Picking which weapon or tool is live is done from a radial wheel instead of blind cycling, with a popup naming what you just selected, and a support module can be fitted that widens who is allowed to climb in (pulling that module out kicks the current pilot straight back out onto the floor).

- **Take** — It turns mechs from a mostly-static vehicle into something with a build path, an upgrade path and a handful of pilot toggles, which is a lot of play value for a system most forks already have half of.
- **Skip** — The construction graphs are fork rewrites of the upstream Ripley/Gygax/Durand/Clarke graphs and the equipment-select system re-handles an upstream mech event, so it fights upstream mech changes on every sync rather than sitting quietly beside them.
- **Touches** — engineering, cargo, science, security, salvage
- **Verified** — supported. Every gameplay beat checks out against files I fetched myself: the reactor-in-battery-bay step is a real construction-graph node (`tag: MechReactor, store: battery-container` in ripleymkii_construction.yml and clarke_construction.yml), the Ripley-to-RipleyMkII and Paddy conversion kits are real graphs (ripleymkii_upgrade_construction.yml, paddy_upgrade_construction.yml with a TransformMech completion), sirens/air-horn/night-vision/thrusters all exist as dedicated components+systems (MechSirenComponent, MechAirHornComponent+System client/server/shared, MechNightVisionComponent, MechThrustersComponent with a charge DrawRate), the radial-select-with-popup replaces blind cycling exactly as described (SharedMechEquipmentSelectSystem opens a UI and pops 'mech-equipment-select-popup'), and PilotSupportModuleSystem does add/remove whitelist entries plus calls `_mech.TryEject` on removal. On graft_shape the claim is not just confirmed but understated: I fetched the actual upstream (non-_Starlight) files Content.Shared/Mech/EntitySystems/SharedMechSystem.cs and Content.Shared/Mech/Components/MechComponent.cs, and both are directly patched in place with dozens of scattered '// Starlight' / '//Starlight Edit' comments (battery-percent movement thresholds, low-power sound thresholds, a commented-out `SubscribeLocalEvent<MechComponent, MechToggleEquipmentEvent>` with a note 'moved to SharedMechEquipmentSelectSystem', pilot container events, sound playback changes). That is real, in-repo evidence of fork-patches-upstream, not just a hypothetical about wiring into a different codebase - the path-data's evidence_cited list only shows the _Starlight-namespace half of this unit and misses these two heavily-edited upstream files entirely, which is exactly the blind spot the seed warned about. Separately, the construction-graph replacement is also a genuine integration concern: the standard upstream path Resources/Prototypes/Recipes/Construction/Graphs/Mechs/ doesn't exist in this repo at all (404), meaning the fork's _Starlight copies are the only Ripley/Clarke/Durand/Gygax graphs left, so grafting this into a codebase that still has the vanilla graphs would require deleting/replacing them (integration-would-require-upstream-edits too). Both readings are true here.

**backmen, frontier, gaby-station-now-dumont-station, monolith, serbia-strong**

*activity · drop-in · medium confidence · 3 forks carry it*

These forks bolt extra hardware onto the mechs the game already has rather than rebuilding piloting. Cargo gets the biggest win: a forklift attachment lets a pilot spend mech power to scoop up to five crates, lockers or vending machines into the suit with a short hydraulic whine and set them back down beside the mech, and one fork adds a wearable powered exosuit with its own control panel and a "Lift cargo" action so a worker can haul heavy objects without climbing into a full chassis. Elsewhere you get a two-seat Space Buoy escape pod that flies well in vacuum and handles badly under gravity, a bolt-on air recycler module that burns mech battery to make oxygen and scrub toxins so a pilot can sit in a breach longer, buildable control and targeting boards for extra combat chassis, and a pilot mech whose mounted guns are driven from a proper "Mech weapons" hands panel instead of the generic equipment list.

- **Take** — The forklift and cargo-lifting exosuit give cargo and salvage a genuinely new physical job loop (moving crates, lockers and vendors around the station) using a chassis the game already ships.
- **Skip** — This is five unrelated bolt-ons from five forks rather than one coherent system, and the listed files are visibly incomplete (the fork equipment entity, its toggle action prototype and the construction graphs consuming the Monolith board tags all live outside this unit), so grafting any one piece means chasing prototypes and sprites the file list does not name.
- **Touches** — cargo, engineering, science, security
- **Needs** — [exotic-gas-expansion](#exotic-gas-expansion)
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. Every file I fetched (backmen's vova-mech.ftl, frontier's MechForkComponent.cs and mech.ftl, dumont's SpaceBuoy pod, monolith's Broadsword/Flail control-and-targeting electronics, serbia-strong's SS220 mech actions) sits inside that fork's own namespaced directory (_backmen, _NF, _Gabystation, _Mono, SS220), matching the seed's path-data drop-in signal. The claim's downgrade to needs-upstream-edits leans on a companion file (the toggle-action prototype) it says 'lives outside this unit' — but when I fetched that exact file it turned out to be Resources/Prototypes/_NF/Actions/mech.yml, still inside frontier's own _NF tree, not an upstream directory. That means the stated reasoning describes an incomplete evidence list within the fork's own namespace, not a genuine fork-patches-upstream or wiring-requires-upstream-edits situation, so I could not confirm either upstream_reading option; the concrete gameplay specifics (forklift MaxContents=5 and hydraulic-whine sound, MechAirRecycler's battery-for-oxygen description, Space Buoy's vacuum-good/gravity-bad text, Broadsword/Flail control+targeting modules, SS220's Control Panel/Lift cargo actions) all check out against the raw files.
  - unsupported: "the fork equipment entity, its toggle action prototype and the construction graphs consuming the Monolith board tags all live outside this unit" (used to justify graft_shape: needs-upstream-edits) — I fetched the toggle action prototype directly at Resources/Prototypes/_NF/Actions/mech.yml (ActionMechForkToggleInsert) and it lives inside frontier's own _NF namespace, not an upstream directory. The files are missing from the cited evidence list, but that's an evidence-completeness gap within the fork's own tree, not proof of an upstream-editing dependency.
  - unsupported: "a pilot mech whose mounted guns are driven from a proper \"Mech weapons\" hands panel instead of the generic equipment list" — the only cited file (vova-mech.ftl) contains a single locale string `bkm-vova-mech-hands-label = Mech weapons`; that confirms the label text but not the specific claim that this replaces/differs from 'the generic equipment list' UI behavior.

### Stains and laundry

<a id="laundry-and-stains"></a>

Spilled reagents and blood leave persistent stains on clothing, walls and floors that must be scrubbed, wrung out or washed in a washing machine.

**forky, gaby-station-now-dumont-station, backmen, goobstation**

*activity · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 5 forks carry it*

Spilled liquids no longer vanish: blood, chemicals and drinks soak into your clothes as visible splatter overlays, smear onto walls, and track behind you as fading footprints wherever you walked through a puddle. You can wring a soaked garment out by hand (a slow, ~15-second job that dumps the liquid on the floor at your feet), scrub a wall stain off with a wetted rag while a dry one just smears it, or stuff up to four items into an industrial washing machine, shut the door and run a cycle — the drum sprays water, thumps loudly, and anyone who climbs in with the laundry gets beaten up by it. Stains stay scannable for DNA, so a bloodstained jumpsuit or a trail of footprints is real evidence a detective can follow, and some outer layers keep the clothing underneath clean. Forky also lets flammable spills soaked into a wall catch fire; other forks ship narrower slices (Backmen adds showers and washing machines, Goob just the footprints).

- **Take** — Turns the station's mess into something that persists and has to be dealt with, giving the janitor real work and giving security a physical evidence trail (bloody footprints, DNA-scannable stains) that survives the moment of the crime.
- **Skip** — Very asset- and hook-heavy for what is mostly flavor: every stainable garment needs per-slot stain overlay layers authored, and the spill/footprint hooks sit in upstream fluid and movement code, so it re-breaks on every upstream sync and adds constant entity churn (a stain entity per splatter) to already busy rounds.
- **Touches** — service, security, medical, all-players, janitorial
- **Verified** — partly supported. Read the actual forky source: Content.Server/Fluids/EntitySystems/PuddleSystem.cs and Content.Shared/Fluids/SharedPuddleSystem.cs are true upstream files (no _Funkystation namespace) that the fork edited in place — they now `using Content.Shared._Funkystation.Fluids/Footprints/WallStains`, raise SpilledOnEvent, and carry an explicit comment about protecting Footprints. That confirms needs-upstream-edits and specifically that the fork itself patches upstream, contradicting the drop-in seed. Most gameplay specifics (wring 15s DoAfter, DNA-scannable stains via a tag, StainBlockerComponent keeping underlayers clean, 4-slot washing machine with bluntDamagePerSecond/selfDamagePerSecond fields, flammable wall stains, footprint entities tracking movement, Backmen showers) check out against the code, but I found one concrete overclaim in the WallStainSystem.cs cleaning logic.
  - unsupported: "scrub a wall stain off with a wetted rag while a dry one just smears it" — WallStainSystem.OnInteractUsing shows a dry absorbent tool just pops "wall-stain-cleaning-dry-rag" ("The rag is too dry! Wet it first.") and returns immediately (args.Handled = true); it does not smear or spread the stain, it simply refuses the clean attempt.
  - unsupported: "fading footprints" — FootprintSystem.cs has no time-based Update() or evaporation logic for footprint entities (unlike WallStainSystem, which explicitly evaporates stain volume every tick); footprints only lose solution via active mechanisms (stepping through them, cleaning), so the claim of passive fading over time is not shown in the code I read.

**ephemeral-space, funky**

*cosmetic · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 5 forks carry it*

Spills on the floor stop looking like one generic coloured blob. Every liquid gets its own mess style: blood lands as scattered droplets that grow into ragged pools, water and shiny liquids look thin and wet, acid looks caustic and irritating, powders look dry and dusty, and vomit, pie filling and broken eggs each have their own hand-drawn look that ignores the usual tinting. Puddles pick randomly from several small, medium and large variants, so a medbay floor after a bad shift or a chem spill in the hallway reads at a glance as blood versus chemicals versus water instead of everyone squinting at colour alone. This is purely how spills look; mopping, slipping and reagent behaviour work exactly as before. Note that despite the catalogue name, nothing here was found for clothing stains, scrubbing or washing machines, and the Funky Station side of this unit lists no files at all.

- **Take** — Cheap, self-contained visual upgrade that makes floor spills instantly readable as blood, chems, water or vomit instead of identical recoloured blobs.
- **Skip** — It needs new fields bolted onto the upstream reagent prototype plus a whole new puddle sprite sheet, and it is mislabelled here: it delivers puddle variety, not the laundry or clothing-stain system the catalogue name promises.
- **Touches** — all-players, medical, service, science, janitorial
- **Verified** — supported. All three cited files check out. puddle_sprites.yml (ephemeral-space) defines esPuddleSpriteSet entries for Default, Blood, Splotchy, Vomit, Water, Shiny, Acid, Powder, Pie, and Egg, each with distinct small/medium/large sprite lists — the Blood comment literally reads "Messy and natural, small puddles are droplets" and Acid reads "Messy and irritating-looking," and Vomit/Pie/Egg explicitly set recolor: false, matching the claim's "ignores the usual tinting" almost verbatim. Critically, Content.Shared/Chemistry/Reagent/ReagentPrototype.cs — an upstream-namespace file, not under _ES/ — has been edited in place to add `PuddleSpriteSet` and `PuddleColor` DataFields, so the fork's own tree already contains a modified upstream file for this feature; that directly falsifies the path-data 'drop-in' seed and confirms the claim's own downgrade to needs-upstream-edits. funky-station returns 404 for both _ES-only files and its copy of ReagentPrototype.cs has no PuddleSpriteSet/PuddleColor/_ES references at all, so 'the Funky Station side lists no files' is accurate. No laundry, clothing-stain, or washing-machine files were found among the evidence or in a broader search (GitHub code search required login so this is not exhaustive), consistent with the claim's own admission that the catalogue name is a mismatch.

### Rideable vehicles

<a id="rideable-vehicles"></a>

Buckle-in vehicles a player drives around the map, from small pods and clown cars to multi-crew armoured vehicles with hardpoints, keys and fuel.

**rmc14**

*loop-change · entangled · high confidence · 3 forks carry it*

You climb into a humvee, van, APC or tank through its doors and end up standing inside a real drivable room: driver's seat, passenger seats, viewports you look out of, wall lockers, and on the medical variants a surgical bed and blood vendor, so a crew can treat wounded while the vehicle is moving. The driver takes the wheel with a key imprinted to that vehicle (blanks can be imprinted or copied, and locks can be broken and repaired), locks the doors, hits the horn and spotlight, and has a short overdrive burst for a speed boost. Other players ride as passengers, sit at port guns, or take a turret and open a weapons panel to pick between mounted cannons, autocannons, flamers, grenade and TOW launchers, watching ammo counts and reload timers; a separate ammo loader panel refills them from ammo boxes. Bolt-on hardpoints let a crew fit armour plating, a snowplow, smoke and flare launchers, a sensor array or an artillery module, and each hardpoint has its own integrity you can examine, damage off, and repair, alongside wheel repairs and a hull that can be destroyed outright. Bigger vehicles must be deployed in place before their turret works, and passengers can be dragged in or refused when the interior is full.

- **Take** — It is by far the most complete crewed-vehicle implementation in any fork: walk-in interiors as real grids, driver/gunner/passenger split, keys and locks, modular hardpoints with per-part integrity, and a full weapons and ammo-loading UI, none of which upstream has in any form.
- **Skip** — It is a 1300-file subsystem wired straight into RMC-14's own world: xeno block/push sizing, RMC night vision, RMC gun and projectile content, RMC medical props and dropship seats, plus a custom grid-based vehicle mover and interior-viewport rendering, so nothing here arrives as a self-contained drop-in and a station fork would be adopting and maintaining a second movement and rendering path.
- **Touches** — all-players, security, engineering, medical, command, cargo
- **Needs** — [xenomorph-hive](#xenomorph-hive), [firearms-content-expansion](#firearms-content-expansion)
- **Verified** — partly supported. Nearly every specific gameplay claim I checked is directly confirmed in the fetched files: driver/passenger seats, viewports, wall lockers, surgical bed + blood vendor on the medical Humvee interior map, keys that can be imprinted/copied with breakable/repairable locks (vehicle.ftl), horn/spotlight/overdrive systems (VehicleHornSystem, VehicleSpotlightSystem, VehicleOverchargeSystem under Content.Shared/_RMC14/Vehicle/Core), port guns, a weapons-select UI with ammo/cooldown display and a separate ammo-loader UI (vehicle.ftl strings), per-hardpoint integrity with repair/examine, wheel repair, hull destruction, deploy-then-turret gating, and drag-in/passenger-full refusal — all confirmed by name in the .ftl and prototype files. The one overclaim is the snowplow hardpoint, which does not appear in any hardpoint file I fetched across Tank, APC, or Van (armor/cannon/launcher/support variants and their SPP counterparts). On graft_shape: every vehicle file I found (Content.Client/Server/Shared/_RMC14/Vehicle, Resources/Prototypes/_RMC14/Vehicles, Resources/Maps/_RMC14/Vehicles) does stay inside the fork's own _RMC14 namespace, technically passing the seed's 'no files outside namespace' drop-in test. But the claim's 'entangled' verdict is about a different, more important kind of coupling that I verified directly: hardpoint guns use RMCWeaponAccuracy and RMCFlamerAmmoProvider (RMC's own firearms system), VehicleXenoPushIgnoreComponent exists specifically to interoperate with xenomorph collision/throw behavior, and the medical Humvee interior reuses CMPortableSurgicalBed (a Colonial-Marines-prefixed prop shared with other RMC medical content, e.g. dropships). That is a real, load-bearing dependency on the fork's own gun, xeno, and medical subsystems that a station fork would also have to graft or stub out, which is exactly what 'entangled' is meant to flag even though the files themselves are self-contained by path.
  - unsupported: Bolt-on hardpoints let a crew fit armour plating, a snowplow, smoke and flare launchers, a sensor array or an artillery module" — I enumerated every hardpoint prototype file for Tank, APC, Van and their SPP variants (hardpoints_armor/cannon/launcher/support/base, spp_hardpoints for all three vehicle types) and found armor plating, smoke launchers, flare modules, sensor/warning arrays, artillery modules, cannons, autocannons, flamers, grenade/TOW launchers — but no snowplow hardpoint anywhere, and a full-tree path search for 'plow'/'snow' turned up nothing.

**far-horizons**

*activity · entangled · high confidence · 3 forks carry it*

You climb into an ATV, segway, secway, janicart, wheelchair or unicycle and drive it around the station, honking a horn, running people down and popping open a trunk to haul cargo. The bigger ones need their keys turned in the ignition before they start (someone can try to steal the keys or drag you out of the driver's seat), burn welding fuel or a power cell as they run, and can be dented until they visibly break down and refuse to start. A maintenance window lets you bolt on parts that actually change how the thing handles: tires, a basic or advanced engine, armour plating, headlights and a wailing security lightbar. Space-rated variants seat two, hold their own air in the cabin, and come with thrusters and a radar screen so you can putter around off-station.

- **Take** — It is a complete, self-contained joyride toy chest: ignition keys, fuel, crashes, breakage and a real upgrade-slot loop, so it gives every department a new thing to do without touching how rounds are won.
- **Skip** — A rider-controlled moving entity leans on exactly the upstream code that churns most (buckle/strap, InputMover, physics, prediction), so each upstream sync risks re-breaking driving in ways that only show up in-game, and 96 files of sprite/key/equipment variants is a lot of surface to keep alive for something purely recreational.
- **Touches** — security, service, cargo, medical, all-players
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. The fork's own C#/prototype/locale files for vehicles are cleanly namespaced under _FarHorizons (confirmed via raw fetch and 404-probing sibling paths), so no pre-existing upstream file is directly patched — supporting 'integration-would-require-upstream-edits' over 'fork-patches-upstream' for the upstream_reading question. But the claim's depends_on:[] is contradicted by a real compile-time and runtime dependency on Content.Shared._Starlight.Actions.Events.JetJumpActionEvent for the space-vehicle jet-jump mechanic — a separate vendored fork subsystem within the same repo, not disclosed anywhere in the claim. That is a genuine cross-system entanglement beyond ordinary upstream composition (Buckle/InputMover/MoverController/physics), which the skip_because text already flags as risk but the depends_on field fails to record, so the shape should be marked entangled rather than plain needs-upstream-edits.
  - unsupported: "depends_on": [] is false. SharedVehicleSystem.cs (Content.Shared/_FarHorizons/Vehicles/SharedVehicleSystem.cs) has `using Content.Shared._Starlight.Actions.Events;` and a live handler `OnJetJumpActionEvent(Entity<TransformComponent> ent, ref JetJumpActionEvent args)` that unbuckles the rider — JetJumpActionEvent is defined in Content.Shared/_Starlight/Actions/Events/JumpActionEvent.cs, a separate vendored fork subsystem (Starlight-Impstation's jump/cybernetics action framework), not part of the vehicles feature's own directories.
  - unsupported: "Space-rated variants seat two" overclaims specificity: the abstract VehicleSpaceshipBase does default to seats: 2, but the only concrete space vehicle actually shipped (VehicleTransport in vehicles_space.yml) overrides it to seats: 1. No 2-seat space vehicle prototype exists in the cited file.

**goobstation**

*activity · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 3 forks carry it*

You buckle onto a vehicle and drive it around the station: a secway, an ATV, a janicart with a headlight, a wheelchair or a plush hoverchair, a cargo forklift, and the clown car. Most need their matching keyset slotted in before the engine will turn over (the key locks in place while someone is driving), you steer with a hand occupied, and you get a horn action plus a looping siren on the security models; wheelchairs and hoverchairs need no keys or hands. The forklift stacks up to four crates on its prongs and carries them visibly across the station, while the clown car only accepts a clumsy driver, uses a bike horn as its key, swallows passengers whole (a huge-capacity syndicate variant scoops up anyone it rams), fires them back out of a cannon, plays jukebox music while it drives, leaks lube when it takes damage, and detonates if you pour an Irish Car Bomb into it.

- **Take** — It hands every department a cheap, self-contained new toy: cargo gets a working forklift, the janitor gets his cart back, medical gets a self-propelled wheelchair, and the clown gets one of the most memorable antag gimmicks in the SS13 lineage.
- **Skip** — The vehicle core is tidy, but the clown car is a second, much heavier feature bolted onto it — it leans on Goob's own container-collision, drag-insert and solution-trigger components, and getting any of it in-game also means adding key tags, uplink and cargo listings, and map spawns in upstream files.
- **Touches** — service, cargo, security, medical, antagonist, all-players
- **Verified** — supported. Every specific gameplay claim checks out against source: BaseVehicle's requiredHands=1 default plus PreventEjectOfKey (SharedVehicleComponent.cs) confirm the key-locks-in / hand-occupied mechanic; VehicleSecway has hornSound+sirenSound; VehicleWheelchair/VehicleHoverchair set requiredHands: 0 with no key ItemSlots; VehicleJanicart carries UnpoweredFlashlight+PointLight (the headlight); VehicleForklift's overlay entity has four crate-count visual states (OneCrate..FourCrates); the clown car (clowncar.yml) uses a BikeHorn-tagged key slot, ExtendedContainer capacity 6 (VehicleClowncarBase) vs capacity 50 for VehicleClowncarAntag (nukie/syndicate uplink variant per uplink_catalog.yml), a Clowncar component with cannon activate/deactivate sounds plus a ClowncarFireModeActionEvent handler, a Jukebox component, SpawnSolutionOnDamage->PuddleSpaceLube, and TriggerOnSolutionInsert on solution IrishCarBomb wired to an Explosive component. That's a supported gameplay description. However the claim's specific justification for needs-upstream-edits is partly wrong: I found the named 'key tags' and 'uplink listings' are already self-contained in the fork's own _Goobstation-namespaced prototype files, not upstream ones. What I did find that genuinely breaks drop-in status (and that the claim didn't cite) is that this feature's own sprite art sits in the shared, non-namespaced Resources/Textures/Objects/Vehicles/ directory tree (atv.rsi, chairs.rsi, janicart.rsi, etc.) rather than under _Goobstation, i.e. the fork's own copy really does include files outside its namespace directories — so needs-upstream-edits is the right bucket, just for a different concrete reason than the one given.
  - unsupported: "getting any of it in-game also means adding key tags, uplink and cargo listings, and map spawns in upstream files" — checked directly and this is wrong for two of the four items named. The vehicle key tags (VehicleKey, SecwayKeys, ATVKeys, JanicartKeys, ForkliftKeys) are already declared in the fork's own Resources/Prototypes/_Goobstation/tags.yml, not the upstream tags.yml (which only has the pre-existing BikeHorn tag, unrelated to this feature). The clown car's uplink listings (UplinkClowncar, UplinkClowncarNukie) are already declared in the fork's own Resources/Prototypes/_Goobstation/Catalog/uplink_catalog.yml, not the upstream Catalog/uplink_catalog.yml. Neither needs an upstream edit to exist; SS14 loads prototypes recursively so a self-contained fork subdirectory is enough.

**serbia-strong**

*activity · drop-in · medium confidence · 3 forks carry it*

You climb onto a vehicle the way you'd strap into a chair, then drive it around the station with a horn you can sound as you go; some vehicles won't move unless a key has been left in them, and the rider is drawn sitting on top of or behind the frame depending on which way it faces. Wheelchairs run on the same handling, with a deliberately slower struggle to get back out of one. The other half is hitching: walk a cart or trailer up to something that tows, right-click to attach it, and after a brief moment it's locked on, so nobody can yank it loose or fold it up until someone spends that same moment unhitching it, and a heavier cart visibly drags on whoever is towing it.

- **Take** — Upstream deleted its vehicle system outright, and this is a still-maintained buckle-based revival plus a hitching mechanic that turns hauling into an actual logistics activity for janitors and cargo instead of dragging crates one at a time.
- **Skip** — The entire cart half carries an "© SS220, An EULA/CLA with a hosting restriction" header, which is a real licensing blocker for an AGPL fork and cannot be waved away; on top of that no vehicle or cart entity prototypes appear in this file set, so you would inherit the machinery and still have to author every actual drivable thing yourself.
- **Touches** — service, cargo, medical, all-players
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. Every file I could find for both halves (VehicleComponent.cs, RiderComponent.cs, SharedVehicleSystem.cs, SharedVehicleSystem.Rider.cs under Content.Shared/SS220/Vehicle/, and the four Cart files under Content.Shared/SS220/Cart/) lives entirely inside the fork's own SS220 namespace and hooks in purely by subscribing to already-existing vanilla SS14 events (StrappedEvent/UnstrappedEvent, MoveEvent, RefreshMovementSpeedModifiersEvent, GetAdditionalAccessEvent, PullAttemptEvent, FoldAttemptEvent, GetVerbsEvent, container-insert/remove messages) rather than editing any upstream file in place. That matches the path-data 'drop-in' seed better than the claim's 'needs-upstream-edits' downgrade; I found no upstream file the fork patches, and the mechanism (subscribing to public events, no core edits) suggests wiring this into another codebase wouldn't need upstream edits either, just the missing entity prototypes the claim itself already flags as absent.
  - unsupported: "with a horn you can sound as you go" — in the current master, the code path that actually grants the rider the honk action (SharedVehicleSystem.OnBuckled: `_actionsSystem.AddAction(args.Buckle, ref component.HornActionEntity, component.HornAction, uid, actions);`) is wrapped in a `// remove vehicle begin ... // remove vehicle end` block and commented out, alongside the HornAction/HornActionEntity fields in VehicleComponent.cs also being commented out under the same marker. The HonkActionEvent handler still exists but nothing in the evidence shows the action ever being granted to a rider, so whether the horn is actually reachable in play is unconfirmed and the surrounding comments read as an in-progress removal, not confirmation of a maintained feature.
  - unsupported: "Wheelchairs run on the same handling, with a deliberately slower struggle to get back out of one." — the only evidence is a nullable `UnbuckleTime` field on VehicleComponent tagged '// SS220 Wheelchair fix begin/end' that can override the default Buckle unbuckle time; no wheelchair entity prototype was in the evidence set (attempts to fetch likely paths 404'd) and no default/override value is shown, so 'deliberately slower' is an inference about direction, not something the cited files demonstrate.

**gaby-station-now-dumont-station**

*activity · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 3 forks carry it*

A small piloted pod you climb into the way you climb into a mech, except it hovers: on station floors it glides above the ground, and once it drifts off the grid into open space it fires its own thrusters so you can fly it around outside instead of being stranded. A second person can right-click the pod and, after a short buckling-in delay, ride along as a passenger; if the pod is sealed, the passenger breathes from its internal air tank rather than the vacuum outside. Wreck the pod and everyone riding inside is dumped out onto the floor with a message.

- **Take** — It turns a mech into a genuine two-seat space runabout, giving crew a cheap way to move a pair of people across open space without EVA gear, which upstream mechs do not offer.
- **Skip** — It is a thin layer welded onto upstream's mech and jetpack systems with no prototype or locale files of its own in this unit, so you inherit the wiring work plus five missing UI strings, and every upstream mech refactor is a chance for it to break.
- **Touches** — all-players, cargo, engineering, science
- **Verified** — supported. All three cited files check out for the gameplay description: OnEntryPod/OnParentChanged switch between CanMoveInAirComponent (grid hover) and a forced JetpackComponent activation (off-grid thrust) exactly as described; OnPassenger uses a GetVerbsEvent<AlternativeVerb> (right-click) plus a DoAfter keyed to mech.EntryDelay for the passenger boarding; OnInhale/OnExhale/OnExpose route to MechAirComponent only when mech.Airtight, matching 'sealed pod -> internal air'; OnDestruction calls EjectAllPassengers with a 'mech-passenger-ejected' popup on Broken/zero integrity, matching the wreck-and-dump behavior. I additionally cloned the repo tree and grepped Content.Shared/Mech/EntitySystems/SharedMechSystem.cs and MechComponent.cs for 'pod' — zero hits, so the fork does not patch those upstream-inherited files in place; the CompactPod code only subscribes to already-existing events (MechEntryEvent exists verbatim in vanilla space-wizards/space-station-14 too). That means the seed's path-data signal (zero files outside own namespace) is technically accurate. But the claim's needs-upstream-edits verdict still holds under the integration-would-require-upstream-edits reading: CompactPodSystem hard-depends on specific fields/shapes of MechComponent (PilotWhitelist/Blacklist, EntryDelay, Airtight, Broken/Integrity), JetpackComponent (Acceleration, WeightlessModifier, Friction), MechAirComponent, and Atmos/DoAfter/Whitelist APIs as this Goobstation-derived fork defines them (its SharedMechSystem.cs differs enormously from vanilla, e.g. added Emag/VirtualItem/StationAi dependencies) — grafting into a differently-shaped Mech/Jetpack implementation would require adapting to (not necessarily editing) those upstream systems, which is exactly the reading the claim's skip_because argues for.
  - unsupported: "with no prototype or locale files of its own in this unit" — false. The fork's own _Gabystation namespace does include a prototype file (Resources/Prototypes/_Gabystation/Entities/Objects/Specific/Mech/mechs.yml, defining BaseCompactPod and the SpaceBuoy entity with the CompactPod/Jetpack/MechAir components and its own SpaceBuoy.rsi sprite) and a locale file (Resources/Locale/pt-BR/_Gabystation/robotics/compact-pod.ftl, containing exactly the 5 Loc.GetString keys used in CompactPodSystem.cs). They just weren't in the evidence_cited list and the locale file is pt-BR only, not en-US — so 'no locale files of its own' overstates it; the real gap is 'no English translation', which is a narrower and different claim than 'no locale files'.

## Ui

### HUD status readouts and alerts

<a id="hud-and-status-readouts"></a>

Reworks the on-screen status layer with new alert widgets, resource bars, ammo counters, job and antag status icons, and richer speech bubbles.

**rmc14**

*loop-change · entangled · high confidence · 8 forks carry it*

Everyone gets a persistent on-screen compass arrow that points toward whoever matters to them: marines track their squad leader (or the captain, the landing zone, the corporate liaison), while xenos track the queen, hive leaders, tunnels and resin markers, with the arrow swinging as you move. A shared tactical map opens from a screen button, showing live blips for your side over the station layout, and leaders can draw coloured lines and drop text labels on it that everyone on their side then sees. Command staff sit at an Overwatch console listing every marine in a squad with their status (conscious, unconscious, dead, SSD), role, location, distance from the squad leader and a saved comment, from which they can broadcast squad-wide messages, set squad objectives, hide or promote people, watch through helmet cameras, and call in supply drops or orbital bombardment. Medics see floating health icons over bodies that distinguish "still defibbable", "nearly too late" and "permanently gone", plus a holocard tag they can set on a patient to flag their treatment status to the next doctor. Senior officers can award named medals with written citations, and anyone can recommend a crewmate for one, with the recommendations queueing up for approval on a medals panel.

- **Take** — It turns "where is everyone and how bad off are they" from radio guesswork into a readable shared picture, which is exactly what command and medical roles lack and the single biggest lever on coordinated play.
- **Skip** — Almost none of it stands alone: the trackers, Overwatch console and medical icons are readouts for RMC-14's squad roster, hive structure and its multi-stage defib window, so grafting the UI without those underlying systems leaves widgets with nothing to display.
- **Touches** — command, medical, security, antagonist, all-players
- **Needs** — [squads-ranks-and-skills](#squads-ranks-and-skills), [xenomorph-hive](#xenomorph-hive), [resuscitation-and-life-support](#resuscitation-and-life-support)
- **Verified** — supported. Every specific in the gameplay text checks out against the raw files. alerts.yml contains the full tracker family: HiveTracker/LeaderTracker/TunnelTracker/HiveCoreTracker/ResinMarkerTracker for xenos, and a long SquadTracker* list (per-squad leaders, CommandingOfficer, ExecutiveOfficer, ChiefMilitaryPolice, LandingZone, CorporateLiaison) for marines, each with directional trackon-north/south/etc. sprite states matching a swinging compass arrow. overwatch.ftl has every named feature: Name/Role/State(conscious/unconscious/dead/SSD)/Location/SL Dist. columns, COMMENT + Save Comment, message-squad, squad-objectives, supply-drop, orbital-bombardment (warhead/crate/cooldown strings), hide/show-marine, promote-squad-leader, and a NO CAMERA string implying camera viewing. tacmap.ftl confirms colored line drawing (7 colors, line width) and a label create/edit/delete dialog. medals.ftl confirms citation prompts, award recommendations, and a medals panel with approve/reject tabs. holocard.ftl gives exact treatment-status states (Surgery/Emergency/Permadead/Xeno Embryo) matching the 'flag treatment status' claim precisely. CMHealthIconsSystem.cs directly imports Content.Shared._RMC14.Medical.Unrevivable and computes DeadDefib/DeadClose/DeadAlmost/DeadDNR/Dead stages, confirming the multi-stage defib dependency the claim's skip_because cites. On graft_shape: all files I fetched (including CMHealthIconsSystem's imports) stay inside _RMC14 namespaces, so the seed's 'zero files outside fork namespace' is literally true, but the claim's 'entangled' verdict is about functional coupling to the fork's OTHER units (squad roster/ranks, hive structure, defib stage system), not about upstream file patching — and that coupling is directly visible in the code (CMHealthIconsSystem depends on RMCUnrevivableSystem; SquadTracker alerts are meaningless without the squad system; HiveTracker alerts are meaningless without hive leadership). That supports downgrading the seed's drop-in to entangled, exactly as the claim argues.

**serbia-strong**

*cosmetic · entangled · medium confidence · 8 forks carry it*

Players wearing the right eyewear see a much denser layer of floating icons above people's heads: a security HUD that distinguishes wanted, under surveillance, to-be-searched, paroled, incarcerated, demoted, discharged and marked-for-execution instead of just a couple of criminal flags, job badges for the fork's extra roles (magistrate, security pilot, Death Squad operative/commander/medic, RedWings pilots and medics) and faction badges that tag people as Nanotrasen, IOT or USSP combatants, medics or officers during faction-war events. On your own screen you also pick up new status alerts and effect icons that tell you when something is happening to your body rather than making you guess: internal bleeding, a combat technique that has slowed you down, a shield/blocking indicator, a temporary boost to how much damage you can take before going critical, and a generic countdown alert slot for timed effects.

- **Take** — It is the readability layer for everything else a fork adds: once you have extra jobs, ghost roles, faction events and custom status effects, players need icons and alerts that name them, and this is a ready-made pattern for all four at once.
- **Skip** — Almost every prototype here is a label for SS220 content you would not have (magistrate, RedWings, IOT/USSP factions, Death Squad, void blocker, the Frontier reagent, their pathology system), so grafting it lands you a pile of icons pointing at nothing plus C# status-effect components pulled in from unrelated fork systems.
- **Touches** — security, medical, command, antagonist, ghost-roles, all-players
- **Needs** — [extra-job-roster](#extra-job-roster), [gamemaster-and-ghost-roles](#gamemaster-and-ghost-roles), [medical-status-conditions](#medical-status-conditions), [martial-arts](#martial-arts), [melee-weapons-and-blocking](#melee-weapons-and-blocking)
- **Verified** — supported. Every specific icon/effect named in the gameplay paragraph traces directly to a fetched file: sechud.yml has exactly wanted/monitor/search/execute/demote/paroled/incarcerated/discharged; job.yml/centcom.yml have magistrate, SecurityPilot, and the three Deathsquad ranks; antag.yml has the NT/IOT/USSP faction icons (Combatant/Medic/Officer variants); movement.yml has the martial-art slowdown; blocking.yml has the shield icon; internal_blood_loss.yml has internal bleeding; mobThresholds.yml has the critical-threshold boost; categories.yml has the CountDown alert slot. On graft shape, the same evidence directly contradicts a plain drop-in reading even though no files sit outside SS220/ dirs: mobThresholds.yml names a 'Frontier' reagent dependency in a code comment, internal_blood_loss.yml wires in PathologyStatusEffectStackable, and every job/faction icon points at roles (magistrate, RedWings, Deathsquad, IOT/USSP combat factions) that only exist in other fork units. The claim's own skip_because and depends_on list match this evidence closely, so the entangled downgrade from the seed's 'drop-in' signal is correct, not an overclaim.

**stellar-station**

*cosmetic · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 8 forks carry it*

Instead of reading your condition from a handful of coarse icons, you get labelled sliding bars stacked around your character: a red Health bar that becomes a darker "Critical Health" bar once you go down and a grey "Dead" one when you die, a yellow Stamina bar for how much sprinting you have left, thin Hunger and Thirst bars on either side, a blue Respiration bar that drains as your air tank empties while internals are on, and a green Battery bar for anything that runs on a cell. Hovering a bar tells you plainly what it does ("If this gets to 0, you go critical", "The amount of gas left in the tank"). Alongside that, being incapacitated is spelled out in words rather than guessed at: a yellow "Stun Buildup" meter warns you that you are about to be knocked down and is already slowing you, and separate red "Stunned", "Slowed" and "Restrained" warnings tell you exactly why you cannot act, with "Restrained" also telling you that anyone dragging you will meet no resistance. Wielding a gun puts a crosshair on your cursor so you can see where you are actually aiming.

- **Take** — It turns the vaguest part of the game (how close am I to crit, how much air is left, why can't I move) into continuous labelled bars every player reads at a glance, and the bar itself is a data-driven prototype so a fork can add its own without touching C#.
- **Skip** — The resource bar files carry an SPDX header of `LicenseRef-Wallening`, a custom non-standard licence rather than MIT or AGPL, so grafting it into an AGPL fork is a licensing question before it is an engineering one; on top of that the Stunned / Stun Buildup / Restrained alerts are the readout for a fork stun-and-grab rework that does not exist upstream, so half the strings would have nothing to display.
- **Touches** — all-players, medical, security, silicons
- **Needs** — [close-quarters-combat-rework](#close-quarters-combat-rework)
- **Verified** — partly supported. Confirmed by direct inspection well beyond the cited evidence: the SPDX LicenseRef-Wallening header on resource_bars.yml and ResourceBarsComponent.cs is real. But the wiring is far more entangled than the claim's own reasoning suggests — Resources/Prototypes/Body/species_base.yml (the shared base every humanoid species inherits from) and Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Mobs/Cyborgs/base_borg_chassis.yml both carry inline `# Begin Stellar - Resource Bars` / `# End Stellar` edits that attach ResourceBars/MobThresholdResourceBars/SatiationResourceBars/InternalsResourceBar directly onto vanilla prototypes. Likewise Resources/Prototypes/Alerts/alerts.yml (vanilla, not under _ST/) has `# Begin Stellar changes` blocks reskinning the existing vanilla `Stun`, `Stamina`, `Handcuffed`, and `Ensnared` alert ids with new icons/text — these are NOT a novel fork-only 'stun-and-grab rework' as claimed, they are upstream SS14 alert mechanics being relabeled. So the claim's specific justification ('half the strings would have nothing to display' because the mechanic doesn't exist upstream) is not supported, but the graft_shape downgrade to needs-upstream-edits is still correct, for a different and stronger reason: this fork edits shared/vanilla files in place rather than overlaying only _ST-namespaced files.
  - unsupported: "separate red \"Stunned\", \"Slowed\" and \"Restrained\" warnings tell you exactly why you cannot act" — the cited status-effects.ftl does define `alerts-stellar-snared-name = [color=red]Slowed[/color]`, but that key is dead code: the only alert with a matching 'slowed' icon (id: Ensnared, in Resources/Prototypes/Alerts/alerts.yml) is wired to the plain vanilla keys `alerts-slowed-name`/`alerts-slowed-desc`, not to `alerts-stellar-snared-name`. So the in-game 'Slowed' alert is not confirmed to render red or use that custom description; the cited evidence string is simply unused.

**backmen**

*loop-change · entangled · medium confidence · 8 forks carry it*

Certain glasses and roles let you see floating health bars over living creatures, so you can read at a glance who is hurt and how badly instead of scanning them one by one. The HUD also gains a pile of new overhead markers: fellow vampires, blob members and flesh cultists recognise each other by an icon over their heads, medical HUDs flag anyone carrying an infection, extra job icons cover the fork's own roles (marines, sergeants, death squad), and the AI can paint a target that security sees. New status alerts sit in your alert tray too: a red "Face blocked!" warning you click to tear a creature off your face before you suffocate, cosmic heart/lung icons telling you that you can survive vacuum, and a power-level meter for shadowkin abilities.

- **Take** — Overhead health bars and faction icons change how fights and rescues are read at a glance, and the health-bar overlay itself is a compact, self-contained client feature.
- **Skip** — Most of the pack is icon and alert prototypes wired to Backmen's own antags, species, organs, jobs, mood and disease systems, so grafted alone it is one health-bar overlay plus a folder of icons that never appear.
- **Touches** — medical, security, command, antagonist, all-players

The alert .ftl/.yml files confirm the "Face blocked!" click-to-remove alert, cosmic heart/lung vacuum-immunity alerts, and the shadowkin "Power Level" alert verbatim. The claim's own skip_because reasoning matches what the files show.

**forky**

*cosmetic · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 8 forks carry it*

Two visible things. First, everyone wearing a job-tracking HUD (security visors, medical glasses, command implants) now sees proper little job badges floating over the fork's extra staff instead of a blank or generic marker: Central Command Intern and Official, Corporate Liaison, Executive Officer, Hospitality Director, Internal Affairs Agent, Magistrate, Deputy, Fitness Instructor, Space Cowboy, Party Maker, Command Maid, Security Clown. Each key chirps a different musical note, the display blinks a cursor, flashes "[ ENJOY ]" or "[ YUM! ]" on a successful vend, buzzes on a bad code, and times out and resets if you dither too long.

- **Take** — The keypad turns a mundane menu click into a small tactile ritual with sound and feedback, and it costs the round nothing: the same items come out.
- **Skip** — The job-icon half is dead weight without the fork jobs it labels (Magistrate, Corporate Liaison, Deputy and friends), and the keypad swaps out the vending machine interface via a client-side interface hook, so it needs upstream vending UI edits and will fight every upstream vending change afterwards.

This proves the fork's own copy edits a real upstream-namespace file (not just _Funkystation dirs), which is exactly what the claim's skip_because already asserted ("swaps out the vending machine interface via a client-side interface hook, so it needs upstream vending UI edits"). Job icon list (Central Command Intern/Official, Corporate Liaison, XO, Hospitality Director, IAA, Magistrate, Deputy, Fitness Instructor, Cowboy, Party Maker, Command Maid, Security Clown) matches job.yml/job-names.ftl exactly. Vending keypad mechanics (letter+number codes via GetCode, SOLD OUT flag, CLR/ENT keys, per-key musical pitch via a blues scale, blinking cursor, "[ ENJOY ]"/"[ YUM! ]" success phrases among a 4-phrase pool, buzz on bad/empty code, 15s inactivity timeout that resets the buffer with a Timeout sound) are all confirmed line-for-line in VendingMachineKeypadMenu.xaml.cs and VendingMachineKeypadSystem.cs.

### Admin and mentor tooling

<a id="admin-and-mentor-tooling"></a>

Extends staff tooling with extra panels and commands, separate mentor or curator help channels, event preference tracking, smites and honeypots.

**serbia-strong, rmc14, corvax, backmen**

*activity · entangled · medium confidence · 9 forks carry it*

Players get a second help channel next to ahelp: a mentor-help line staffed by experienced players rather than admins, with typing indicators, claim-tracking so two mentors do not answer at once, and its own chime and unread badge (and on one fork an AI assistant that drafts a first answer to your ahelp before a human picks it up). Staff get a much deeper toolbox: right-click a player to edit their traits (optionally handing over the matching gear), toggle status effects, change how many lives they have left, resize them, hand an antagonist a brand new objective, or swap the job icon floating over their head for a bespoke event faction icon. Bans get finer-grained too, so someone can be silenced in chat or barred from a specific species or antag role instead of being kicked off the server outright, and event runners get a props locker of admin-only kit: invisible walls and instant invisible portals, faction flags and capture pedestals for team-war events, and calibration knives that deal exactly one damage type on hit.

- **Take** — The mentor-help channel alone is a real quality-of-life win for a new-player-facing fork, and the finer-grained chat/species/role bans let staff correct one behaviour without removing a player from the round.
- **Skip** — It is four forks' staff toolkits piled into one bucket, most of it patches upstream ban managers, bwoink and the admin menu (chat and species bans even ship their own database migrations), and several of the shiniest pieces are welded to systems you would also have to take: the xeno-hive and marine-squad admin tabs, the bank-account commands, the TTS voice switcher.
- **Touches** — admin-staff, all-players, antagonist, ghost-roles
- **Needs** — [character-traits](#character-traits), [discord-and-external-services](#discord-and-external-services), [xenomorph-hive](#xenomorph-hive), [squads-ranks-and-skills](#squads-ranks-and-skills)
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. Every cited file I could fetch (admin-verbs.ftl, add-objective-window.ftl, job-icon-changer-window.ftl, backmen admin/toolshed.ftl, the Corvax invisible-wall/portal YAML, the SS220 debug-knife and capture-flag YAML, and both RMC14 mentor C# files) confirms the core mechanics the claim describes almost line-for-line: typing indicators (OnMentorHelpTypingUpdated/UpdateTypingIndicator), claim-tracking (_claims dict, ClaimButton, 'Claimed by'), unread badges and a chime sound (_unread, _unreadByPlayer, _mHelpSound), trait editing with an item-grant checkbox, status toggles, life counts, X/Y scale, an 'Add objective' dialog, a job-icon picker, invisible walls/portals, faction capture flags, and one-damage-type debug knives. However, browsing SerbiaStrong-220's tree showed the admin-verb piece lives in its own Content.Server/SS220/Administration/Systems/AdminVerbSystem.cs, a self-contained class that hooks in purely via SubscribeLocalEvent<GetVerbsEvent<Verb>> — a non-invasive extension point that needs zero upstream file edits to wire in, which undercuts a blanket 'needs-upstream-edits' read for that piece. I could not verify (GitHub API rate-limited) the skip_because's specific claim that chat/species bans patch the upstream ban manager and ship their own migrations, so I can't confirm fork-patches-upstream for that half of the bucket. Given the bucket mixes at least one genuinely drop-in-style piece (the verb menu, the mentor UIController hooks, the pure-YAML props) with unverified-but-plausible upstream-coupled pieces (bans/bwoink) and explicit cross-dependencies on other catalog units (TTS/Discord, xeno-hive and squad admin tabs), the honest verdict is that this is a heterogeneous 4-fork grab-bag rather than a single unit that uniformly needs upstream edits.
  - unsupported: on one fork an AI assistant that drafts a first answer to your ahelp before a human picks it up — no such feature exists in the cited RMC14 evidence (MentorHelpWindow.xaml.cs, StaffHelpUIController.cs). The only adjacent RMC14 directory, Content.Server/_RMC14/Mentor/ImaginaryFriend, implements an unrelated ghost-companion/advisor roleplay mechanic (a ghost becomes an invisible 'imaginary friend' following a living player), not an AI that drafts ahelp replies.
  - unsupported: Bans get finer-grained too, so someone can be silenced in chat or barred from a specific species or antag role instead of being kicked off the server outright (and the related skip_because detail that 'chat and species bans even ship their own database migrations') — none of the 12 cited evidence files mention bans, mutes, species restrictions, or database migrations at all; this rests on zero cited evidence.

**sunrise, rmc14, backmen**

*activity · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 9 forks carry it*

Pressing the help key no longer goes straight to admins: players first pick "Admin Help" (rule-breaking, player reports, bugs) or "Mentor Help" (how do I do surgery, what does this machine do), so beginner questions reach a separate volunteer mentor team instead of clogging the admin queue. On Sunrise a mentor question becomes a proper ticket with a subject line, and mentors work a two-tab queue (Open / Closed) where they claim a ticket, reply, teleport to the player, unassign, or close it, with per-mentor stats for tickets and messages handled over a week, month, or all time. RMC-14 does the same thing as a live chat instead of a queue, with claim, teleport and typing indicators, plus a "De-Mentor" toggle so a mentor can step out and re-enter the channel. Backmen adds an optional GPT-backed assistant that can auto-answer ahelps when no admin picks them up, plus a pile of staff commands for editing a character's access, faction, sex, voice, bank balance, manifest record or fingerprints mid-round.

- **Take** — A dedicated mentor channel is the single highest-leverage retention tool for a small fork: new players get answers without an admin having to drop what they are doing, and the ticket queue plus per-mentor stats makes it a role trusted regulars can actually be given.
- **Skip** — It only pays off if you actually have people willing to sit as mentors — with no volunteers it is a second empty inbox — and it is not a clean drop-in: the ticket queue needs its own database storage, a new admin-permission flag, a lobby button, a keybind, and a rewrite of the existing help button to fork the choice between ahelp and mhelp.
- **Touches** — all-players, new-players, admin, mentor-staff
- **Verified** — supported. Every concrete gameplay claim checked out against fetched source: Sunrise's mentor-help-ui.ftl and MentorHelpWindow/NewTicketDialog XAML confirm the two-tab Open/Closed queue, ticket subject line, claim/reply/teleport/unassign/close actions, and week/month/all-time per-mentor stats; RMC-14's MentorWindow.xaml/StaffHelpWindow.xaml confirm the live-chat model with TypingIndicator, ClaimIndicator, Claim/Teleport buttons, De-Mentor toggle and a ReMentorButton, plus the Admin Help/Mentor Help choice screen; Backmen's GptAhelpSystem.cs plus CCVars.gpt.cs (including a gpt.no_admin_auto flag) confirm the optional GPT auto-responder, and toolshed.ftl plus AddBankAcсountCommand.cs/SetBankCurrencyCommand.cs confirm the full staff-command list (access, faction, sex/changesex, voice/changetts, bank balance, manifest/stationrecord, fingerprints). On graft shape, I fetched Content.Shared/Input/ContentKeyFunctions.cs from Sunrise directly and found a live "// Sunrise-Start" block adding OpenMentorHelp/OpenHelpChoice key functions inside this upstream (non-_Sunrise-namespaced) file, plus MentorHelp EF Core migrations sitting in Content.Server.Database/Content.Shared.Database (also outside the _Sunrise tree) — direct proof the fork's own copy edits upstream-shared files in place, not just that wiring it elsewhere would require edits.

**serbia-strong, goobstation, corvax**

*activity · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 9 forks carry it*

This is the kit admins use to stage set-piece events, so what players actually see is a round that suddenly has scenery and rules the map never had: invisible walls fencing off an arena, invisible portals a staffer steps through, unseen drop pods that thump down carrying supplies or a strapped-in person, and flag postaments that two factions fight to plant their banner on for a war event. Staff can also flip your job status icon so the crew reads you as a different role, add or strip character traits and statuses mid-round, resize you, hand you a fresh objective, top up your remaining lives, equip an item straight onto a slot, or smite you with a "Thunderstrike". Goob adds a Thunderdome: players get pulled to a separate arena map, pick a weapon loadout from a menu (shotguns, SMGs, rifles, revolvers, e-sword, capoeira manual), and brawl with revival between bouts. On the support side, adminhelp conversations are relayed out to a Discord bot that can answer back in-channel, and there are chat bans and species bans alongside the usual ban types.

- **Take** — Admin-run events are how a fork gets memorable rounds without shipping a whole gamemode, and these props (drop pods, invisible walls and portals, capture-point flags, job-icon swaps, trait and objective editors) are exactly the levers a staffer needs to improvise one live.
- **Skip** — Almost none of it is player-facing on its own, so it only pays off if you have active admins running events; the ban and AHelp-relay half also drags in database migrations and an external bot service you would have to host and maintain yourself.
- **Touches** — all-players, antagonist, ghost-roles, command
- **Needs** — [character-traits](#character-traits), [discord-and-external-services](#discord-and-external-services), [devil-pacts](#devil-pacts)
- **Verified** — supported. Most of the unit (job-icon changer, traits/statuses/scale/lives verbs, add-objective window, EquipTo command, Thunderstrike smite, Thunderdome, drop pods, invisible wall/portal, the AHelp-relay hook) is implemented as new files confined to fork namespaces (SS220/, _Goobstation/, Goobstation/, Corvax/), several of them C# partial-class extensions of upstream classes (AdminVerbSystem, BwoinkSystem) that are already declared partial in vanilla — self-contained, not upstream edits, matching integration-would-require-upstream-edits at most. But the chat-ban/species-ban half genuinely edits the upstream Content.Server.Database/Model.Ban.cs file in place (fetched it directly: fields and an interface cast added with inline `// SS220-add-admin-name`, `// SS220-add-stated-round`, `// SS220-abstract-ban-role` markers) and ships real EF Core migrations (AddSpeciesBans.cs for Postgres and Sqlite) tied to a specific schema-history position — that is unambiguous fork-patches-upstream, exactly the kind of in-place edit path data can't see. So the unit mixes both flavors.

### Lobby and character sheet overhaul

<a id="lobby-and-character-ui"></a>

Replaces the pre-round and in-round player-facing shells: custom lobby screens and flow, job priority pickers, online player lists, in-round character sheets and notification panels.

**cosmatic-drift, ephemeral-space, gaby-station-now-dumont-station, impstation, rmc14, serbia-strong, starfall-drift, stellar-station, the-den**

*cosmetic · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 6 forks carry it*

A grab-bag of pre-round and out-of-round screen dressing rather than one system: custom lobby splash art and lobby music per server, fork-branded colour themes, and reworked character-setup windows. Players get a lobby that tells them how many hours they have played today (Stellar nags you to take a break and can lock you out until tomorrow, Impstation turns the same counter into a random joke line), a job-preference window showing how many slots each job has left and how many people are queued for it plus a "if none of my jobs open, stay in lobby or spawn as an overflow job" toggle, a tabbed character editor split into Identity / Loadouts / Roles with clothing preview and confirm-before-randomise, a movie-credits round-end screen that scrolls the round's cast and antagonists, an in-game server browser for hopping between a community's own servers, and an in-round panel showing your character's name and job. Ephemeral Space goes furthest: instead of a static screen you wait in a physical theatre map as a theatregoer, walk to a door to ready up, hear an in-fiction "the stage is now open" announcement, and can opt into a spectator "stagehand" role that sees everyone's secrets and calls votes to disrupt the round.

- **Take** — The pieces are individually cheap and highly visible: lobby art, lobby music, a round-end credits roll and a job-slot/queue readout are the first things every player sees, and the clearest way to make a server feel like its own place rather than a downstream copy.
- **Skip** — Only the art-and-music half is genuinely drop-in; the stylesheets, profile-editor partials and replacement game screens sit on top of upstream's client UI, which churns constantly, so every upstream sync risks a broken or silently stale character sheet that you then own forever.
- **Touches** — all-players, ghost-roles
- **Verified** — partly supported. Locale-file evidence directly confirms several specific mechanics (job slot/queue readout format, Identity/Loadouts/Roles tabs with overflow-job toggle and preview/confirm-randomize buttons, Stellar's escalating playtime-nag/lockout copy, Impstation's joke playtime lines, Serbia-Strong's Cast/Antagonists round-end-titles screen, Ephemeral Space's stagehand spectator role with vote/secret-sight and open/closed stage announcements). Fetching Starfall-Drift's Content.Client/Lobby/UI/HumanoidProfileEditor.xaml and CharacterSetupGui.xaml (both 200, both at the identical upstream path used by honksquad-ss14's own tracked copy) and diffing shows the fork completely rewrote the upstream file in place rather than adding a separate namespaced file, which directly confirms 'needs-upstream-edits' and specifically the 'fork-patches-upstream' reading for at least this fork's profile-editor piece; the-den's single hub_servers.yml is self-contained data in its own namespace, so the unit as a whole spans both readings. Several specific narrative details in the claim (splash art/music, colour themes, a walkable physical theatre map with a door, calling the character-info window an 'in-round panel') are not shown by any file actually fetched and go beyond the evidence.
  - unsupported: custom lobby splash art and lobby music per server
  - unsupported: fork-branded colour themes
  - unsupported: instead of a static screen you wait in a physical theatre map as a theatregoer, walk to a door to ready up
  - unsupported: an in-game server browser for hopping between a community's own servers
  - unsupported: an in-round panel showing your character's name and job
