### Visual feedback and particle effects

<a id="visual-feedback-effects"></a>

Screen and world feedback for what just happened: pain flashes, screenshake, interaction particles, sparks, a general particle emitter framework and cutscene playback.

**rmc14**

*cosmetic · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 10 forks carry it*

Fights and interactions get visible, readable punctuation: a punch throws up a little impact burst, a grab and a disarm each flash their own icon over the target, and social gestures like a fistbump, high-five, handshake or hug pop a small picture above the pair's heads for a few seconds so bystanders can see what happened without reading chat. Big hits and blasts knock your view around in a short series of jolts, explosions and burning leave scorch marks scattered across the floor afterwards, and creatures under a buff or in a special state glow with a coloured outline around their sprite (green, red or purple depending on what is affecting them). There are also warning markers that flash on the ground, such as a red exclamation over a pipe that is about to blow.

- **Take** — It makes melee, grabs, disarms and explosions legible at a glance, which is exactly the feedback SS14 combat is weakest at, and the coloured aura outline is a reusable way to show "this mob has a status on it" without a new HUD element.
- **Skip** — Almost none of it fires on its own: the effect entities are inert prototypes that RMC's own combat, xeno and emote code spawns, so grafting it means patching upstream melee, disarm and emote handlers to call the spawns, and the shared base effect prototype pulls in RMC's night-vision-visibility component, so you either bring that along or strip it and re-test every effect.
- **Touches** — all-players, security, antagonist, medical
- **Needs** — [screen-overlays-and-visors](#screen-overlays-and-visors)
- **Verified** — partly supported. All 9 cited files exist as described and I traced real consumers (XenoPunchSystem, RMCPullingSystem, SharedRMCEmoteSystem, RMCExplosionSystem, xeno buff systems) entirely within the fork's own _RMC14 namespaces, no upstream file edits found anywhere, which confirms the claim's downgrade from the seed's naive 'drop-in' guess to 'needs-upstream-edits' is correct, and confirms it means integration elsewhere, not that RMC patches its own upstream copy.
  - unsupported: social gestures like a fistbump, high-five, handshake or hug pop a small picture above the pair's heads for a few seconds -- RMCEffectEmoteBase's actual TimedDespawn lifetime is 20 seconds, not 'a few seconds'
  - unsupported: creatures under a buff or in a special state glow with a coloured outline around their sprite (green, red or purple depending on what is affecting them) -- traced every GiveAura() call site across the xeno ability systems (Rage, Tantrum, Empower, Soak, Lifesteal, Crippling Strike, Firewalk, Hedgehog) and the actual default colors are black, white, dark red (#A31010), translucent red (#FF000046/#FF000023), olive/mustard (#6C6F24), Color.Teal, and dark red variants (#421313/#AD1313); no purple appears anywhere, and 'green' is only a stretch via the olive shade

**stellar-station**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 10 forks carry it*

Hitting someone or something makes the world react: a little ghost image of whatever you're holding flings itself from your hand toward the target, tumbles and fades, and the thing you hit visibly flinches backward for a fraction of a second before snapping back. Powered gear, gunshots hitting metal, and things breaking throw off short-lived orange (or blue) sparks that light the area, make a crackling noise, bounce off walls and can set flammable stuff alight. Certain hits and effects also shove the camera around with a decaying shake. Separately, clicking on another player opens a small radial wheel around them instead of doing the default hand interaction, with options like grab/pull, examine, and a timed pat-down to inspect what they're wearing.

- **Take** — It makes every melee swing, tool use and gunshot feel like it landed, with almost none of the effect logic touching upstream game rules: the particle and recoil pieces just listen to interaction and damage-flash events that already fire.
- **Skip** — It arrives as three separate bundles glued together (Ephemeral Space sparks/screenshake, Stellar interaction particles, and a player-on-player radial menu) across two fork-only assembly projects; the sparks only appear once you sprinkle spark components onto upstream weapon and machine prototypes, and the radial menu intercepts the ordinary click-a-person interaction and pulls in the fork's social-interaction system, so taking the visuals without also taking that UI change means unpicking it.
- **Touches** — all-players, security, engineering, medical
- **Verified** — partly supported. Confirmed real upstream-file edits in the fork's own tree: Content.Shared/Interaction/SharedInteractionSystem.cs (core vanilla interaction system) contains a block marked '// End Stellar Additions - Interaction particles' that raises StellarInteractionParticleEvent, and Content.Server/Electrocution/ElectrocutionSystem.cs contains a '// ES START' / '// ES END' block calling ESSparksSystem.DoSparks(). Both are upstream namespaces/files, not _ST/_ES/Content.Stellar.* directories, so the seed's drop-in path-data guess is wrong in the direction the seed itself warned about (it can't see in-place upstream edits). That also means grafting elsewhere requires the same kind of upstream-file surgery.
  - unsupported: Powered gear, gunshots hitting metal, and things breaking throw off short-lived orange (or blue) sparks — verified zero occurrences of ESSparkOnHit/ESSparkOnProjectileHit/ESSparkOnItemToggle/ESSparkOnTrigger across all 2,342 Resources/Prototypes/*.yml files in the repo (git sparse-checkout + rg -i 'esspark'). The only confirmed live call site is a direct DoSparks() invocation hand-patched into Content.Server/Electrocution/ElectrocutionSystem.cs — i.e. 'powered gear' via electrocution is real, but 'gunshots hitting metal' and 'things breaking' triggering sparks is not backed by any wiring in this codebase.
  - unsupported: skip_because: 'the sparks only appear once you sprinkle spark components onto upstream weapon and machine prototypes' — this describes a hypothetical mechanism, not the actual state of the repo: no upstream (or fork) prototype anywhere attaches these components today. The real wiring found is a direct method call embedded in an upstream C# file, not YAML sprinkling.

**serbia-strong**

*cosmetic · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 10 forks carry it*

This is a grab-bag of on-screen feedback rather than one feature. Drugged or supermatter-exposed crew start seeing things that are not there: skeletons, graves, lightning, sparks, portals, gore, stray toolboxes and even a floating balloon, each pulled from a weighted table so no two trips look alike. Cult ritual drugs wash the screen in a pulsing tentacle-and-vignette overlay that fades in and out instead of a flat colour tint. Characters can sprout a thought bubble above their head, a ninja's whistle plants a loud exclamation marker over a target, and a player who dies gets a pop-up window asking them to confirm before their body is handled.

- **Take** — The reusable pieces (a fading/pulsing full-screen texture overlay, a weighted hallucination-spawn table, an animation helper, a thought bubble) are the kind of presentation plumbing every other fork feature ends up wanting, and they are cheap to reuse once present.
- **Skip** — It is not a coherent feature you can port in one go: the effect prototypes reference SS220's own drugs, cult, supermatter and gore entities, so grafting them without those systems leaves you with a framework and a pile of effects nothing ever triggers.
- **Touches** — all-players, medical, engineering, antagonist, science
- **Needs** — [reagent-and-reaction-expansion](#reagent-and-reaction-expansion), [supermatter-engine](#supermatter-engine)
- **Verified** — partly supported. Resources/Prototypes/Reagents/medicine.yml — an upstream vanilla file, not under any SS220/ path — contains a fork-added line `!type:ChemRemoveHallucinationsEffect #SS220` (line 958) that is part of this exact feature's own EntityEffect system (Content.Shared/SS220/EntityEffects/Effects/HallucinationEntityEffect.cs + RemoveHallucinationsEffect.cs). That is a real in-place edit to a shared/upstream prototype file for this unit, which the path-only seed could not see, so 'needs-upstream-edits' holds and specifically as fork-patches-upstream, not merely integration-would-require-upstream-edits.
  - unsupported: "stray toolboxes" — the two fetched weighted tables (Hallucinations/reagents.yml, Hallucinations/supermatter.yml) list individual tools (CrowbarYellow, Wrench, Screwdriver, Wirecutter, Welder, Multitool, WelderExperimental, JawsOfLife, PowerDrill, GasAnalyzer, trayScanner, HolofanProjector) but no 'toolbox' entity anywhere in either table.
  - unsupported: "Cult ritual drugs wash the screen in a pulsing tentacle-and-vignette overlay" — RaveComponent.cs and both RaveSystem.cs files (Shared/Server) show raving tied to an entity that mumbles cult phrases and plays sounds on a timer (with an unused EffectEntity field), not to a reagent/drug metabolism effect; I found no code wiring CultYoggRaveEffect (the actual tentacle/vignette overlay from rave.yml) to anything a player ingests.

**impstation**

*loop-change · entangled · medium confidence · 10 forks carry it*

This is a grab-bag of world-effect systems rather than one feature. The showpiece is a glowing crystal growth that creeps outward tile by tile after a supermatter incident: it lights the area a sickly yellow, cracks and groans as it spawns, replaces the floor plating underneath, and hurts anyone who walks onto it, so the crew has to route around a spreading no-go zone instead of just fleeing a boom. Alongside it: creatures and items that visibly change sprite the moment their holder flicks into combat mode (claws out, weapon raised), objects that puff chemical smoke on a timer or burst into a cloud when they vanish, a cleaning tool that scrubs blood and decals in a small radius while draining its own solution tank, and a set of spell effects (writhing dark tentacles that grab someone in place, plus joke event spells that rain soap or lollipops on the whole station).

- **Take** — The crystal cascade turns a supermatter failure from a single explosion into an ongoing, navigable hazard the whole crew has to work around, and the smaller pieces (combat-mode sprites, timed smoke emitters, radius decal cleaning) are generic building blocks you can hang on your own content.
- **Skip** — It is not one feature but five loosely related ones, and the best part of it does not stand alone: the crystal system compiles against an Einstein Engines supermatter component and a custom floor tile, and the spell effects assume a magic/action stack, so you inherit two large upstream systems to get one visual payoff.
- **Touches** — engineering, service, all-players, antagonist
- **Needs** — [supermatter-engine](#supermatter-engine), [wizard-magic](#wizard-magic)
- **Verified** — partly supported. Fetched all 9 cited files. CrystalMassSystem.cs literally imports Content.Shared._EE.Supermatter.Components and checks SupermatterImmuneComponent, confirming the claim's core assertion that the crystal-cascade showpiece compiles against an Einstein Engines supermatter component — a genuine third-party system, not vanilla SS14. That alone justifies downgrading the drop-in seed to entangled. The other four files (CombatModeVisuals, CleansDecals, CrystalMass client visualizer, EmitSmokePeriodically) are small and self-contained with no unusual dependencies, matching the "generic building blocks" framing. The magic/action stack half of the entanglement claim is weaker than stated though: RandomGlobalSpawnSpellEvent (used by event_spells.yml) is vanilla upstream SS14, not an extra system to port.
  - unsupported: "hurts anyone who walks onto it" — CrystalMassSystem.OnStepTriggered calls EntityManager.QueueDeleteEntity(args.Tripper): stepping on the crystal deletes the entity outright (unless it has SupermatterImmuneComponent/GodmodeComponent/GhostComponent), it does not apply damage-over-time as "hurts" implies.
  - unsupported: "the spell effects assume a magic/action stack, so you inherit two large upstream systems" (paired with depends_on: wizard-magic) — event_spells.yml's RandomGlobalSpawnSpellEvent is a vanilla space-wizards/space-station-14 file (confirmed at Content.Shared/Magic/Events/RandomGlobalSpawnSpellEvent.cs, HTTP 200), already present in any modern SS14 tree; it is not a separate large system this fork adds, unlike the genuinely fork/mod-specific _EE Supermatter dependency.

### Vision overlays and visors

<a id="screen-overlays-and-visors"></a>

Wearable and ambient post-processing that changes what the player can see: tinted goggles and welding visors, night vision, motion detectors, CRT and grain filters, and limited-vision cones.

**rmc14**

*loop-change · entangled · medium confidence · 9 forks carry it*

Players get gear that changes what they can actually see. A powered night-vision visor flips down over the helmet and lifts the darkness (either partially or fully, draining a power cell while it runs, and examining the helmet tells you which visor is down and how much charge is left; a screwdriver pops visors back out). A handheld motion detector is toggled on and pings on a timer, painting moving contacts as blips around you out to about seven tiles on short range or fourteen on long, with an audible sweep tone and a different tone when nothing is out there, and it shuts itself off if you drop it. Binocular-style eyewear has a toggle action that pushes your view slightly further out so you can spot things before they reach you, and a rangefinder window reports coordinates on a target. Squad leaders get a tracker readout listing their fireteam and where each member is, plus a security-camera viewer window for watching remote feeds.

- **Take** — Motion detection, night vision and the visor-swap loop turn darkness and line of sight into things players actively manage with gear, which is a real tactical layer SS14 does not otherwise have.
- **Skip** — It is written for RMC-14's Colonial Marines total conversion: night vision branches on xeno-specific components, the trackers are a table of CM job ids and squad alerts, and the visor logic assumes the fork's helmet-container gear, so almost none of it lands without dragging squads, jobs and the xeno side along.
- **Touches** — security, command, antagonist, all-players
- **Needs** — [squads-ranks-and-skills](#squads-ranks-and-skills), [xenomorph-hive](#xenomorph-hive), [extra-job-roster](#extra-job-roster)
- **Verified** — partly supported. Trackers.yml is wall-to-wall CM-prefixed job ids (CMSquadLeader, CMCommandingOfficer, RMCPMCDirector, etc.) with SquadTracker* alerts, confirming a hard dependency on the fork's own job roster and squad system. Content.Client/_RMC14/Tracker/SquadLeader/* (SquadInfoWindow, SquadFireteamContainer, SquadLeaderTrackerUISystem) confirms the squad-leader fireteam readout is real and job-gated. NightVisionSystem.cs directly imports Content.Shared._RMC14.Xenonids and Xenonids.Burrow and holds a live XenoComponent query, a genuine compile-time coupling to xenomorph-hive even though the two xeno-branching call sites are presently dead code behind an early return. This is real, multi-system entanglement (squads, jobs, xeno), so the 'entangled' classification holds and the drop-in seed is rightly overturned. The core mechanical claims (visor examine text + screwdriver removal + power-cell drain, motion-detector 7/14 tile ranges with distinct sweep/empty sounds and drop-deactivation, FarSight toggle+zoom) all matched the source verbatim.
  - unsupported: "Squad leaders get ... plus a security-camera viewer window for watching remote feeds" — a camera-viewer window does exist (Content.Client/_RMC14/Camera/RMCCameraWindow.xaml, RMCCameraComputerComponent), but it is wired to a console/machine entity with a ProtoIds/Watchers list, not shown anywhere in the cited evidence or the files I checked to be granted specifically as squad-leader personal gear; attributing it to squad leaders alongside the tracker readout is not backed by what I read.
  - unsupported: "night vision branches on xeno-specific components" (skip_because) is true only at the import/compile level: Content.Client/_RMC14/NightVision/NightVisionSystem.cs does import Content.Shared._RMC14.Xenonids and Xenonids.Burrow and query XenoComponent, but both call sites (SetMesons and SetMesonSprites) begin with an unconditional `return; // TODO RMC14 make this not lag horribly` before ever reaching the xeno-specific logic, so the branching is currently dead code, not active runtime behavior.

**serbia-strong**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 9 forks carry it*

This is a grab-bag of things that change what your screen shows you. The heavy hitters are sight modes: a thermal mode (from goggles, worn clothing or an implant) that picks out warm bodies through darkness and walls out to a set radius, a night-vision mode that bathes everything around you in a soft tinted glow so dark maintenance reads clearly, and a Tajaran-style "Activate Keen Hearing" button that briefly outlines your surroundings for about five seconds on a two-minute cooldown. The other half is atmosphere and mischief: lamps and light sources get soft bloom halos, wall corners get smoothed so the vision cone edges look less blocky, and a hallucination effect makes you periodically see creatures and objects that other players cannot, unless you are wearing the item that protects against that particular hallucination. Screen shaders for glitching, blurring and fading are included, plus a small overlay that labels items with their cargo sell price.

- **Take** — Seeing warm bodies through walls and darkness is the single biggest change you can make to how hunting, hiding and searching feel, and this ships it in three flavours (goggle, implant, racial) off one shared overlay stack that other vision effects can plug into later.
- **Skip** — Every file carries the SS220 CLA/EULA with an explicit hosting restriction, and some of it is relicensed downstream of CM-14 and Imperial code, so it is not cleanly compatible with an AGPL fork; on top of that the overlay work reaches into upstream draw-depth ordering and needs its own .swsl shader and mask assets brought along.
- **Touches** — all-players, security, antagonist, cargo, science
- **Verified** — partly supported. Fetched Content.Shared/DrawDepth/DrawDepth.cs directly (an upstream file, not under any SS220/ namespace directory) and it contains inline fork edits: `WallFovOverlay = DrawDepthTag.Default + 9, //SS220 Perpective-wall-fov` and `AboveFovOverlay = ... //SS220 Perpective-wall-fov` spliced into the standard enum. That is the exact upstream draw-depth-ordering dependency the claim's skip_because describes, and it proves the fork's own copy patches an upstream file in place (fork-patches-upstream), not merely that a future port would need upstream edits. All ten cited component/shader files were fetched and match their described roles (thermal vision goggles with radius/closeRadius, keen hearing action, custom FoV corner-smoothing overlay with WallFovOverlay z-index, hallucination with per-slot item protection, bloom light mask, glitch/texture-fade shaders), and the SS220 CLA/EULA-with-hosting-restriction plus CM-14/Imperial provenance is directly visible in file header comments (ThermalVisionComponent.cs cites CM-14 MIT + CLA restriction; glitch.yml cites Imperial CLA). A separate blur shader (Resources/Prototypes/SS220/Shaders/blur.yml, 200 OK) backs the "blurring" shader claim not in the cited list.
  - unsupported: a Tajaran-style "Activate Keen Hearing" button that briefly outlines your surroundings for about five seconds on a two-minute cooldown" — Resources/Prototypes/SS220/Actions/Ignore_light_overlay.yml sets `useDelay: 30`, not 120. The file's own inline comment ("[2 minutes * 60 seconds] #SS220-tajaran-keen-fix") is stale/wrong relative to the actual DataField value, so the real cooldown per the shipped prototype is 30 seconds, not two minutes.
  - unsupported: a small overlay that labels items with their cargo sell price" — the actual mechanism (Content.Server/SS220/Overlays/ShowSupplyPriceSystem.cs, not in the cited evidence list) is an ExaminedEvent handler that appends price text via PushMarkup to the examine tooltip when the wearer has ShowSupplyPriceComponent in their eyes slot. It is examine-text enrichment, not a persistent screen overlay/label as implied.

**stellar-station**

*cosmetic · entangled · medium confidence · 9 forks carry it*

The station stops looking flat. Walls are drawn as tall, standing structures rather than plain tiles, and when you walk behind one the part blocking your view fades out so you can still see your character and the room around you. Characters and objects cast soft drop shadows on the floor, and the whole screen runs through a post-processing pass that adds a gentle vignette toward the edges, brighter bloom around light sources, and a colour grade that can be swapped per situation, with a shockwave ripple effect for big impacts. Players who dislike it can switch the post-processing off in their own settings.

- **Take** — It is the single biggest change to how the game looks — tall walls that cut away, shadows and screen grading make the station read as a place rather than a tile grid, and it costs nothing in round balance.
- **Skip** — The cutaway renderer is wired into the fork's own wall-smoothing/wall-rendering rework and cannot be lifted alone, and the post-process shader carries an explicit all-rights-reserved CrystallEdge notice with usage granted only to Stellar Station, so that piece is not yours to take.
- **Touches** — all-players
- **Verified** — partly supported. Fetched all 8 cited files plus the overlay classes they reference (StellarCutawayPreOverlay/PostOverlay), the WallSmooth files, and the actual .swsl shader sources. StellarCutawayPreOverlay.cs directly imports Content.Stellar.Client.WallSmooth and calls _wallSmooth.ApplyCorners(...) on every cutaway target — the cutaway renderer is genuinely fused to the fork's own wall-smoothing system, not a standalone overlay. postprocess.yml literally carries "This file is ALL RIGHTS RESERVED, Copyright (c) 2025 CrystallEdge, with usage rights granted to Stellar Station by the Copyright Holder" — the licensing blocker the claim cites is real and verbatim. Both planks of skip_because check out, so the entangled verdict (a downgrade from the drop-in seed) is correct.
  - unsupported: Characters and objects cast soft drop shadows on the floor — this feature does exist in the repo (Content.Stellar.Client/Dropshadow/DropshadowSystem.cs, Content.Stellar.Shared/Dropshadow/DropshadowComponent.cs), but none of the 8 cited evidence files mention it; the claim smuggles in a real feature the citation list doesn't actually cover.
  - unsupported: Walls are drawn as tall, standing structures rather than plain tiles — the cited files (StellarCutawayComponent/ViewerComponent/System) only implement a view-angle-gated fade/cutaway of wall sprites when the camera is behind them; nothing in the cited evidence establishes that walls are rendered as 'tall, standing structures' as opposed to smoothed flat wall tiles that merely fade out.

### Storage and inventory rework

<a id="storage-and-inventory-rework"></a>

Changes how carried gear is organised: nested pouches and rigs, slot-blocking clothing, extendable equipment slots and reworked pickup and hands flow. Requires a code-level change to storage or inventory behaviour; a `Textures/.../Interface/` subdirectory alone is interface art, not a storage rework.

**cosmatic-drift, goobstation, rmc14, serbia-strong, starlight, sunrise**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 8 forks carry it*

This is a grab-bag of changes to where players can put things and who can pick them up. You get clothing that unpacks a whole outfit when you put it on (a death squad hat that dresses you in the matching jumpsuit, hardsuit, mask, belt and PDA), and clothing that blocks other slots while worn, so a bulky item stops you equipping anything on the slots it covers. Storage gains flavours: a bag or crate only its owner can open instantly (anyone else stands there for about five seconds with a popup announcing they are rummaging), containers you can take from but never put into, a mouth slot you can swallow an item into and involuntarily spit out when hit hard enough, hidden compartments you unscrew open with a screwdriver, a concealed slot inside your own hand toggled by an action, and dumping ore straight from your satchel into a machine without emptying it first. Items can also refuse to be picked up again for a few seconds after being set down (so a felinid dropped on the floor gets a head start to run), refuse to be worn by the wrong species entirely, and species like mice, borgs, arachnids and terminators get their own slot layouts instead of the human one. RMC-14 goes furthest, with military pouches and rigs, nested storage inside storage, quick-draw holsters, and a pickup and hands flow where you drop what you are holding when you go down.

- **Take** — Several of these are small, self-contained quality-of-life pieces (slot-blocking clothing, read-only storage, re-pickup cooldown, species clothing whitelists) that each solve a real friction point and can be lifted one at a time without taking the whole rework.
- **Skip** — Storage, hands and inventory are the most-touched systems in the game and the deeper pieces (nested pouches, predicted hands, custom inventory templates) hook into upstream code that churns constantly, so every upstream sync will drag conflicts through the parts of the codebase players notice fastest when they break.
- **Touches** — all-players, security, cargo, medical, antagonist, extra-playable-species
- **Verified** — partly supported. I re-fetched all 14 cited files (cosmatic-drift, starlight, sunrise, goobstation, and the SS220-namespaced files which live in the serbia-strong repo). Every one exists exactly as described and each lives inside a fork-owned namespace directory (_CD, _Starlight, _Sunrise, Goobstation.Shared, or Content.Shared.SS220) — I found no evidence any fork's own copy patches an upstream-owned file, so this is not 'fork-patches-upstream'. But the feature set (ExtendableClothing unpacking a full loadout, ClothingBlockSlotsOnEquip, per-species Inventory templateId/speciesId, ClothingWhitelist, ReadOnlyStorage) only does anything once it is attached to specific upstream clothing/species/storage prototypes that live outside these namespaces, so wiring it into another codebase means touching upstream prototype files even though the fork's own code is self-contained — that is 'integration-would-require-upstream-edits', matching the claim's downgrade from the drop-in seed. Separately worth flagging: the SS220-namespaced files (InnerHandToggleableComponent, ToggleableItemSlotComponent, TransferMaterialsInStorageComponent) carry a header citing a custom SS220 CLA/EULA "with a hosting restriction", a practical grafting obstacle independent of the code-shape question.
  - unsupported: "RMC-14 goes furthest, with military pouches and rigs, nested storage inside storage, quick-draw holsters, and a pickup and hands flow where you drop what you are holding when you go down." — zero RMC-14 paths appear anywhere in evidence_cited despite rmc14 being one of the six listed sources; this entire paragraph is unverifiable from the cited evidence.
  - unsupported: "species like mice, borgs, arachnids and terminators get their own slot layouts instead of the human one" — the cited file (starlight inventories.yml) only defines speciesId/templateId entries for arachnid, avali, cyclorite, felionoid, moth, reptilian, resomi, vox, vulpkanin, lagomorph, rodentia, diona, thaven. There is no mouse/mice, borg, or terminator entry anywhere in that 662-line file. Only 'arachnid' of the four named examples is actually confirmed.

### PDA chat messenger

<a id="nanochat-messenger"></a>

Turns handhelds into a phone-style chat network with number lookup, per-contact threads, group chats, emoji and delivery logs.

**funky**

*activity · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 6 forks carry it*

Every crewmember's PDA becomes a phone: you get your own number, look people up by name or number, and hold private one-to-one text threads that show whether a message actually got delivered, with per-chat mute and the option to hide your number from the directory. Funky's layer on top adds named group chats — you create one, invite people by searching the crew directory, view the member list, promote others to admin, kick people out or leave yourself, with the creator marked as owner. Messages can carry picture emoji picked from a searchable, categorised picker (meme faces, character emotes) that render inline in the conversation rather than as text.

- **Take** — Gives the whole crew a private, non-radio communication channel with group coordination, which changes how departments organise without touching any combat or engineering balance.
- **Skip** — Funky's group-chat and emoji work is stitched into the vendored Delta-V NanoChat cartridge files with inline "Funky Station - Group Chats" markers rather than living in fork-only files, so you must first port the whole Delta-V messenger and then re-resolve those same shared/server/UI files on every future sync; it also hands antagonists an untraceable private group channel outside radio.
- **Touches** — all-players, command, security, service, antagonist
- **Needs** — [pda-cartridge-programs](#pda-cartridge-programs)
- **Verified** — supported. Every gameplay specific maps to a fetched file: DeliveryFailed, MutedChats, ListNumber, group-chat enum members and Owner/Admin fields all carrying inline "Funky Station - Group Chats" markers inside vendored _DV files, plus categorised/searchable emoji prototypes rendered inline by an EmojiTag markup handler. The needs-upstream-edits downgrade is correct in both senses: code search shows the Funky markers live in four _DV files (not _Funkystation), and the fork's copy of the true upstream Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Objects/Devices/pda.yml is edited in place to add NanoChatCartridge to crew PDA program lists.

**sunrise**

*activity · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 6 forks carry it*

Every crewmate's PDA gains a messenger app that behaves like a phone chat client: a searchable contact list of everyone else who has a PDA, one-on-one message threads, and group chats you can create, name, invite people into, accept or decline invites for, promote/remove members in, mute, or leave. You get popup notifications for new messages and invites, can delete your own messages, and can drop in animated emoji from a picker with recent and favourite tabs. Everyone is auto-enrolled at round start into a station-wide chat plus a chat for their own department, so a doctor lands in Medical and Common without setting anything up. Between real conversations your PDA also buzzes with junk mail from fake senders (casino ads, dating spam, Nigerian-prince scams, fake emergency alerts), tuned by server settings for how often it arrives and how many players get hit. The whole network runs off a physical messenger server machine on the station, and the app shows a "Server unavailable" banner when that machine is not reachable.

- **Take** — It gives every player a private, persistent, department-aware text channel that radio cannot do (quiet one-to-one talk, ad-hoc groups, scrollback), and it is one of the highest-adoption fork features because it fills an obvious hole in station comms.
- **Skip** — A frictionless private chat for everyone quietly weakens radio, headset-stealing and comms-sabotage play, and the package is much bigger than "a chat window": a station server machine that has to be mapped in, spam datasets, a full emoji sprite sheet and picker, and a hard-coded auto-group table keyed to your department and radio-channel prototype ids that you must re-point at a fork roster.
- **Touches** — all-players, command, security, medical, engineering, cargo, science, service, antagonist
- **Verified** — partly supported. Upstream Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Objects/Devices/pda.yml in the fork carries Sunrise-Start/End blocks adding MessengerCartridge to PDA preinstalled programs (lines 89-94, 172-177, 192-197), so the fork really does edit upstream files in place, which the path-data seed could not see. Every other substantive gameplay claim (auto_groups.yml common+department enrollment, spam categories and cvar tuning in MessengerServerSystem.Spam.cs, delete-own-message check, 265 animated emoji states, "Server unavailable" locale string) checked out except the nonexistent member-promote action.
  - unsupported: "promote/remove members in" — remove is real (MessengerServerSystem.Groups.cs, owner-gated), but there is no promote or ownership-transfer command anywhere in the messenger server code; the group owner is fixed at creation

**cosmatic-drift**

*activity · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 6 forks carry it*

Every crewmember's ID gets a four-digit phone number, and opening NanoChat on their PDA gives them a phone-style messenger: a contacts list down one side, a conversation thread with typed message bubbles on the other, and a popup notification when someone texts them (mutable if you want quiet). You add someone by punching in their number and a name, or by browsing the station directory of everyone who chose to list themselves, though the lookup and the sending both die if telecomms is down or you are off-station, and the message comes back marked as failed to deliver. Because the history lives on the ID card itself, Security can jam a confiscated card into a log probe and read out every message sent and received, and a card thrown in a microwave has its history wiped or scrambled into nonsense.

- **Take** — Private one-to-one text alongside public radio is a genuinely new social channel, and tying the history to the ID card gives Security real forensic evidence and gives antags a real reason to destroy a card.
- **Skip** — It is a large bespoke UI (seven client widgets) that also has to reach into upstream ID cards, PDAs, the log probe and microwave interactions, so it is not a clean drop-in, and once crew can text privately a lot of chatter leaves the radio channels your other content assumes people are listening to.
- **Touches** — all-players, security, command, antagonist, service
- **Verified** — supported. Fetched all five cited files plus the LogProbeCartridgeSystem partial, the NanoChatSystem microwave handler, identification_cards.yml, and name_identifier_groups.yml directly from the cosmatic-drift repo. Every substantive gameplay claim checks out: 4-digit numbers (nameIdentifierGroup maxValue 9999), contacts by manual entry or station-directory lookup gated on ListNumber, telecomms/off-station send failure (HasActiveServer + station-match checks), log-probe forensic read of a scanned card's Messages/Recipients, and microwave erase (10%) or character-scramble-with-possible-recipient-reassignment. The drop-in seed is correctly downgraded: Content.Server/CartridgeLoader/Cartridges/LogProbeCartridgeSystem.cs (upstream path, no _CD) is edited in place with '// CD' markers calling InitializeNanoChat() and threading ScannedNanoChatData through LogProbeUiState's constructor, and Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Objects/Misc/identification_cards.yml (upstream path) has '- type: NanoChatCard # CD' appended to essentially every ID card prototype (crew, ERT, deathsquad, CBURN, nuke-ops). That is the fork's own copy patching upstream files, not merely a hypothetical integration cost — so 'both' readings of upstream_reading are literally true here: the fork's copy already touches upstream files, and grafting into a different tree would still require adding the equivalent component/prototype lines and partial-class hook yourself. Minor overclaim on exact widget count aside, this is a solid, well-evidenced 'needs-upstream-edits' call.
  - unsupported: "It is a large bespoke UI (seven client widgets)" — the actual Content.Client/_CD/CartridgeLoader/Cartridges/ directory has 5 XAML widgets (NanoChatEntry, NanoChatLogEntry, NanoChatLookupView, NanoChatMessageBubble, NanoChatUiFragment) plus one non-XAML UI-fragment handler class (NanoChatUi.cs) — 6 files total, not 7.

**gaby-station-now-dumont-station**

*activity · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 6 forks carry it*

Crew carry a chat card in their PDA that works like a phone: you look people up by name or number, open a thread with them, and text back and forth in real time from anywhere on the station. This fork's version adds group chats — you name a group, invite people by searching name or number, and the owner or an admin can promote, demote, or kick members, while anyone can leave. Messages can carry picture emoji picked from a searchable tray sorted into categories (reactions, faces, food, department badges, robots, plushies, memes), and you can mute a single noisy conversation without silencing the rest. Message history is physical: examining a card shows its number, and microwaving one wipes or scrambles everything on it, so a card can be destroyed as evidence.

- **Take** — It gives the whole crew a private, person-to-person and group text channel that radio does not cover, and the group/emoji/mute layer is what makes people actually use it instead of shouting on comms.
- **Skip** — The fork's emoji layer sits on top of a whole vendored messenger stack from two other forks (Delta-V's NanoChat plus Funkystation's expansion) rather than on upstream, so you inherit three namespaces of code plus a large sprite library, and this fork's own emoji prototype ids are written in Portuguese, which you would have to relabel or live with.
- **Touches** — all-players, command, security, service
- **Verified** — partly supported. Direct fetches confirm the group-chat/emoji/mute/microwave mechanics in the _Funkystation and _DV files, and code search plus raw fetches prove the fork's own copy patches upstream files (pda.yml preinstalls NanoChatCartridge, identification_cards.yml adds NanoChatCard, AgentIDCardSystem.cs imports _DV.NanoChat), so needs-upstream-edits stands in the fork-patches-upstream sense. Two specifics fail verification: admins cannot demote (creator-only per GroupMembersPopup.xaml.cs), and the emoji category list includes a nonexistent "faces" category.
  - unsupported: "the owner or an admin can promote, demote, or kick members" — GroupMembersPopup.xaml.cs explicitly disables demote for non-creators (line 94: if (!isCreator && canDeadmin) canDeadmin = false), so admins can promote and kick but only the owner can demote
  - unsupported: "sorted into categories (reactions, faces, food, department badges, robots, plushies, memes)" — there is no "faces" category in emojis.yml; the real categories are Reacoes, Simbolos, Acoes, Memes, Cabecas (heads), Comida, Departamentos, Misc, Plushies, Robos
  - unsupported: "you inherit three namespaces of code" — NanoChat files span five namespace directories (_DV, _Funkystation, _Gabystation, _Dumont, _Andromeda), and the cited _Gabystation NanoChatUiMessageEvent.cs actually contains NanoBank (bank app) code, not messenger code

**deltav**

*activity · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 6 forks carry it*

Your PDA gains a NanoChat app that works like a phone: your ID card is assigned a number (visible when you examine it), and you can look up other crew's listed numbers through the station telecomms server, add them as named contacts with a job title, and hold a private one-to-one text conversation with each. New messages pop up as a notification naming the sender and their job, you can mute individual chats or all notifications, unlist your own number so nobody can find you, and a message that cannot reach its target comes back marked as failed to deliver. The paper trail is real: a security log probe can dump another card's stored conversations and known contacts, and microwaving a card wipes or scrambles its message history.

- **Take** — It gives every player private, targeted, off-radio communication with a real evidence trail, which creates secrecy, blackmail and investigation play that public radio channels cannot.
- **Skip** — Private untraceable-feeling chat pulls conversation out of the shared radio space and into invisible one-to-one threads, which quietly reduces the ambient chatter other players get to overhear and react to; it also needs the messages stored on ID cards, the app preinstalled on PDAs and the log probe extended, so it is not a clean bolt-on.
- **Touches** — all-players, security, command, antagonist, service
- **Verified** — supported. Every specific gameplay claim (examine number, telecomms lookup, unlisting, job-titled contacts, sender+job notifications, per-chat and global mute, failed-to-deliver, log-probe dump of messages and contacts, microwave wipe/scramble) maps to a concrete locale string or NanoChatCardComponent field I read. The fork's own tree edits upstream files in place: LogProbeCartridgeSystem.cs in Content.Server/CartridgeLoader/Cartridges has DeltaV NanoChat-scanning insertions, and upstream pda.yml preinstalls NanoChatCartridge, so needs-upstream-edits is correct in the fork-patches-upstream sense.

### PDA cartridge programs

<a id="pda-cartridge-programs"></a>

Extra software for handheld computers: security watchlists, stock trading, crime assistants, banking apps, news readers and logistics dashboards.

**backmen, deltav, gaby-station-now-dumont-station, sunrise**

*activity · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 8 forks carry it*

These forks fill the PDA's program slot with extra apps you slot in like a cartridge and tap open on your handheld. A security officer opens SecWatch to see a live list of who is currently wanted and why ("Everything's calm. Why not enjoy a Monkin Donut?" when nobody is), or runs Crime Assist, a yes/no questionnaire that walks you through "was the victim an employee?", "did they die?", "was it intentional?" and spits out a numbered charge like "Code 301: Manslaughter" with the legal definition and suggested punishment, so a green officer can book someone correctly without a lawyer. Other apps: a bank/NanoBank app showing your account number, owner and balance and pinging you when money moves; StockTrading, a market screen where you buy and sell shares in galactic companies with a price-history graph and your spesos balance; MailMetrics, a courier scoreboard tracking earnings from delivered mail against losses from expired, damaged and tampered parcels with a success-rate percentage; and a glimmer monitor charting the station's psionic reading in real time. Sunrise adds a corporate law reference reader, a station navigator map, a PDA camera that takes and stores photos, a plant analyzer readout and an in-PDA messenger with contacts and group chats.

- **Take** — Each cartridge is an independent, self-contained app you can cherry-pick one at a time, and Crime Assist / SecWatch alone measurably raise the floor for new security players by turning "what do I even charge them with?" into a guided questionnaire.
- **Skip** — Most of the interesting apps are only shells over systems you would have to own first: the bank and stock apps need an economy, MailMetrics needs the mail delivery system, the glimmer monitor needs psionics, so grafting the cartridge without its backing system gives you a screen that reads zero forever.
- **Touches** — security, cargo, service, command, science, all-players
- **Needs** — [player-economy-and-banking](#player-economy-and-banking), [mail-delivery](#mail-delivery), [psionics-and-glimmer](#psionics-and-glimmer), [nanochat-messenger](#nanochat-messenger)
- **Verified** — partly supported. Re-fetching DeltaV's actual pda.yml and cartridges.yml at their vanilla (non-_DV) upstream paths shows the fork edits those upstream-location files directly and extensively: dozens of PDA prototype entries get inline `# DeltaV` cartridge-list edits, and the original WantedListCartridge in the vanilla cartridges.yml is commented out with \"DeltaV: this is replaced by SecWatch\". That's concrete fork-patches-upstream evidence the path-data seed couldn't see. Independently, the claim's own reasoning (needs economy/mail/psionics/messenger backing systems to not be empty shells) is also verified true from the fetched .ftl/.yml content, so integration-would-require-upstream-edits holds too — hence 'both'. The claim's graft_shape of needs-upstream-edits is right, just for a stronger reason (concrete in-place upstream file edits) than it stated.
  - unsupported: "a glimmer monitor charting the station's psionic reading in real time" — evidence only shows a live single-value readout (glimmer-monitor-current-glimmer, Interval, Sync strings); no chart/history string was found (contrast with StockTrading's explicit stock-trading-price-history), so "charting... in real time" implies more visual history than confirmed.
  - unsupported: "an in-PDA messenger with contacts and group chats" attributed to Sunrise — Sunrise's own MessengerCartridge entity description is only "A program for messaging between PDAs"; contacts/group-chat specifics were not found for Sunrise's messenger (that level of detail — CONTACTS, new-chat popups — was only confirmed for DeltaV's separate NanoChat app, not Sunrise's).
  - unsupported: All five Sunrise-specific claims (corporate law reader, navigator map, PDA camera, plant analyzer, messenger) are asserted with zero citations in evidence_cited — I confirmed four of the five app *names* independently via the GitHub API, but the claim's own evidence list does not actually support the Sunrise half of the write-up at all.

### Announcer voice packs

<a id="announcer-voice-packs"></a>

Swappable voiced station announcers covering round start, alert levels, shuttle calls and round-end stingers, plus equipment hailer voice lines.

**corvax, ephemeral-space, frontier, gaby-station-now-dumont-station, goobstation, harmony-station, rmc14, serbia-strong, starlight, sunrise**

*cosmetic · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 7 forks carry it*

Instead of the usual text-only bulletins with a generic chime, the station gets a voiced announcer: a real human (or in-character AI) voice reads out round start, alert level changes, and event warnings like meteor showers, ion storms, power outages, outbreaks and alien sightings, and plays a stinger over the round-end screen. Several forks bolt extra flavour onto that, including joke alert levels with their own colour and voice clip, extra named alert states beyond the usual green-to-delta ladder, wall speakers that play announcements spatially so you hear them louder near a speaker and not at all in an unpowered section, and a security hailer button that makes an officer's helmet bark "HALT!", "FREEZE", "GET ON THE FLOOR" out loud to everyone nearby. The lines are typically recorded by a named community voice actor, so the announcer becomes part of the server's identity rather than generic sci-fi filler.

- **Take** — Cheap, high-visibility identity: a recognisable voice on every alert and event is the single most-heard thing on a server, and the bulk of it is audio files plus prototype overrides rather than new mechanics.
- **Skip** — The value is entirely in the recordings, which are the part you cannot copy for free — most packs are one specific voice actor under CC-BY with named attribution, so grafting the plumbing leaves you needing your own voice work, and the wiring still has to reach into upstream event, alert-level and round-end prototypes to swap the sounds.
- **Touches** — all-players, security, command
- **Verified** — partly supported. The claim's needs-upstream-edits downgrade from the drop-in seed is not just correct but understated: Starlight's Resources/Prototypes/AlertLevels/alert_levels.yml (the exact vanilla upstream path, no _Starlight prefix) is directly edited in place, with '# begin starlight'/'# end starlight' comment markers rewriting the sound field of the pre-existing green/blue/violet/yellow/red/gamma/delta/epsilon entries to point at _Starlight audio and appending new omega/theta/psi/orange levels — that is a real fork-patches-upstream file, contradicting the seed's zero-files-outside-namespace premise for this fork. Other forks in the bundle (Goob-Station's Content.Goobstation.Shared/Hailer/HailerComponent.cs, Sunrise's Content.Shared/_Sunrise/AnnouncementSpeaker/Components/AnnouncementSpeakerComponent.cs) are genuinely self-contained new files that would only need upstream wiring (equip slot / helmet-mask prototype, speaker placement) to integrate, matching the second reading. So both readings are simultaneously true across the bundled forks.
  - unsupported: "a security hailer button that makes an officer's helmet bark" — Goob-Station's HailerSystem.cs grants the hail action via GotEquippedEvent gated on SlotFlags.MASK, and the in-character line is sent with nameOverride: Name(uid) + "(SecMask)" — the item is a mask, not a helmet.

## Maps

### Custom station maps and shuttles

<a id="custom-station-maps"></a>

The fork's own station rotation plus its centcomm, evacuation, cargo and event shuttles.

**corvax, cosmatic-drift, ephemeral-space, estacao-pirata, frontier, funky, gaby-station-now-dumont-station, goobstation, harmony-station, impstation, monolith, rmc14, serbia-strong, starlight, sunrise, viva-station, white-dream**

*structural · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 6 forks carry it*

This is a content bucket, not a system: each fork's own roster of stations to play on, plus the ships that fly to and from them. Players get unfamiliar floor plans with their own department layouts, room names on the station map, and job slot counts baked in per station (Camp Chromite is a Nanotrasen re-education facility, Impstation ships a Doom-styled arena map for zero-job free-for-alls, Monolith's spawn points are USSP and Viper Group faction outposts with their own shipyards and armories). The shuttle half is a large library of alternates for the roles upstream already has one of: evac shuttles with different layouts, cargo and mining shuttles, CentComm stations, ERT and admin transports in engineering/medical/security/janitor/chaplain flavours, and event ships that fly in mid-round like clown patrols and alien tourists. Volume ranges from four files (Viva's two maps) to thousands (RMC-14's planetside operation maps and the Almayer).

- **Take** — A station map is the arena the whole round happens in, and each of these is a finished, playtested one — a fresh rotation is the single cheapest way to make a fork feel like its own server rather than a reskin of upstream.
- **Skip** — A map is only as portable as the entities placed on it: the plain ports (Estação Pirata's box/cluster/omega, Viva's two) drop in, but Frontier's, Monolith's, RMC-14's and White Dream's maps are built on their fork's shipyards, POI economy, area system and custom walls, so grafting one of those quietly drags a large fork system in behind it — and every map you adopt is a map you now own and must repair on every upstream tile, machine and job change.
- **Touches** — all-players, command, cargo, engineering, security, medical, service, antagonist
- **Verified** — partly supported. Core specifics check out: Viva's CampChromite.yml literally names the station "Nanotrasen Re-Education Facility, Camp Chromite"; Impstation's E1M1.yml is a 0-minPlayers StandardStationArena with Passenger [-1,-1] (zero-job arena, Doom-level-id naming); Viva really is exactly 4 files (2 prototype + 2 map data) for its 2 maps; Monolith's _Mono/PointsOfInterest/ussp.yml and _Mono/Shipyard/USSP + /Viper directories confirm faction outposts with their own ship rosters; Frontier's frontier.yml uses StandardFrontierStation with fork-only jobs (Contractor/Mercenary/Pilot), supporting the shipyard-economy entanglement claim. But the 'plain ports drop in' framing overclaims: Estação Pirata's actual map-pool wiring lives at the literal shared path Resources/Prototypes/Maps/Pools/default.yml (mixing its own map ids straight into the same file upstream uses for the default rotation, not a namespaced pool file like Frontier/Monolith use), and the cited evidence path for it (_ES/StationConfigs/default.yml) doesn't exist in that repo at all — the real namespace is _EstacaoPirata for code and unprefixed Maps/EstacaoPirata/ for the maps themselves. That's a genuine fork-patches-upstream case sitting inside what the claim calls the easy tier. The 'thousands' figure for RMC-14 was not independently verified (GitHub API rate-limited mid-check) though it's directionally plausible for that fork's scale.
  - unsupported: the plain ports (Estação Pirata's box/cluster/omega, Viva's two) drop in — Estação Pirata's own map-pool registration file is at Resources/Prototypes/Maps/Pools/default.yml, the same shared path used for upstream's own map rotation, not a fork-namespaced pool file; the cited evidence path _ES/StationConfigs/default.yml does not exist in that repo
  - unsupported: Volume ranges from four files (Viva's two maps) to thousands (RMC-14's planetside operation maps and the Almayer) — the Viva figure is confirmed exactly, but the RMC-14 'thousands' figure could not be independently verified (API rate limit hit before a file count was obtained)

### Ruins, points of interest and sector generation

<a id="ruins-poi-and-sector-generation"></a>

Off-station content the round is built around: salvage wrecks, space ruins, outposts and procedurally placed points of interest, plus chunk loading and cleanup for a persistent sector.

**frontier**

*structural · entangled · medium confidence · 4 forks carry it*

Instead of one station in empty space, the round opens on a whole populated sector: a disk-shaped asteroid belt with a central arrival outpost, then an inner ring of service stops (trade outpost, medical dispatch, lettered cargo depots), a middle ring dense with mineable rock and gas deposits, and an outer ring of icy asteroids and strange brass wrecks that researchers go hunting through. Which locations appear changes every round because each point of interest rolls its own spawn chance, distance from centre and minimum spacing from its neighbours, so crews fly out and find a different mix of shops, ruins and derelicts each shift, all listed as named warp points. Alongside that, salvagers can launch expeditions onto generated planets and station-sized dungeons (cave factory, virology lab, lava mercenary base, haunted site) with rolled weather, breathable-or-not atmosphere and hostile factions like carps, argocytes, dinosaurs or rogue silicons, and one-off bluespace encounters (a vault, a wizard tower, a Syndicate FTL intercept) can drop in as anomalies to go poke at.

- **Take** — It converts "the station" into "the sector": a round becomes an explorable map with varying destinations, which is the single biggest change you can make to what a shift feels like, and the spawn rules are data-driven so new locations are just another prototype plus a grid file.
- **Skip** — It only pays off if you also want the rest of the Frontier round shape — it wires into trade-crate destinations, cargo-depot and market-station CVARs, station deeds and warp/fax/holopad renaming, and it assumes players have ships to reach any of it, so on a single-station fork you would inherit the generator with nothing worth generating.
- **Touches** — all-players, cargo, salvage, science, command
- **Needs** — [shipyard-player-ships](#shipyard-player-ships), [expedition-missions](#expedition-missions), [cargo-bounties-and-market](#cargo-bounties-and-market), [custom-station-maps](#custom-station-maps)
- **Verified** — supported. SectorTopology.xml confirms the disk-shaped belt, central Frontier Outpost, and the inner/middle/outer ring layout with trade outpost, medical dispatch, cargo depots, minerals/gas, icy asteroids and brass wrecks verbatim. PointOfInterestPrototype.cs/System.cs confirm per-POI SpawnChance, MinimumDistance/MaximumDistance, MinimumClearance, lettered cargo-depot naming, and warp-point renaming exactly as described. Directory listings for Resources/Maps/_NF/Dungeon (cave_factory, virology_lab, lava_mercenary, haunted) and Resources/Maps/_NF/Bluespace (vault, wizardtower, syndieftlintercept) confirm the specific named examples. expeditions.ftl and salvage-faction.ftl confirm rolled weather/atmosphere mods and hostile factions (carps, argocytes, dinosaurs, rogue silicons). The system code also hard-codes a dependency on Content.Server._NF.Trade's TradeCrateDestinationComponent and NFCCVars cargo/market CVars plus GameTicker preset-gating, which substantiates downgrading the seed's 'drop-in' guess to the claim's own 'entangled' assessment.

**serbia-strong**

*activity · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 4 forks carry it*

Roughly five minutes into the round a gateway on the station finishes charging (poking it early just tells you it is still spooling up), then opens onto a randomly chosen off-station location that only exists for that round. Crew can walk through, explore the place, and come back through a return portal at the far end. The pool of destinations is a set of hand-built maps rather than generated terrain: a derelict shopping market, a scrapyard, a fuel station, a cargo outpost, an orbital penal colony, a chapel and engineering wreck, an arena, a wooded biodome and a small NT ship. Certain long-range guns are locked so they will only fire once you are actually standing on the dungeon map, so the expedition loadout cannot be turned on the station.

- **Take** — It is a large pile of finished, hand-made off-station locations plus a very small amount of glue code that drops a random one behind a portal each round, so you get a repeatable mid-round excursion without building a generator.
- **Skip** — SS220 ships this under their own EULA/CLA with a hosting restriction rather than the upstream licence, so copying the maps and code is a legal decision before it is a technical one, and every map name and popup is Russian and would need translating and re-theming.
- **Touches** — cargo, salvage, security, all-players
- **Verified** — unsupported. I fetched all five cited GateDungeon/GateGunDungeon C# files and confirmed the mechanics literally described (300s ChargingTime, portal linking, InteractHandEvent popup, shot-cancel unless grid has GateDungeonMapComponent) are real code. But a full sparse clone of the repo (not just the cited paths) shows: (1) the only pathDungeon entry anywhere is a placeholder `Maps/Shuttles/arrivals.yml` marked for deletion, so the gateway currently teleports nowhere near the named Ruins maps; (2) the eight cited Ruins maps are instead spliced into the vanilla GridSpawn ruins/satellites lists inside Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Stations/base.yml (an upstream file, edited in place with \"# SS220 Ruins Update Map begin/end\" markers) — proving the claim's own 'needs-upstream-edits' verdict, and moreover proving fork-patches-upstream directly (not just a hypothetical integration cost); (3) GateDungeonMapComponent and GateGunDungeonComponent have zero placements anywhere in Resources, so the gun-lock is orphaned/dead code. The claim's graft_shape call (needs-upstream-edits) is right, but the gameplay narrative wrongly presents two disconnected subsystems as one working, integrated feature.
  - unsupported: "Roughly five minutes into the round a gateway on the station finishes charging ... then opens onto a randomly chosen off-station location" — the 300s charging timer and portal-link code are real, but no GatewayDungeonStart/End/ToStation entity was found placed on any map in the whole repo (only a lone GatewayDungeonMid on the Tox station); there is no evidence this gateway actually exists in a playable round.
  - unsupported: "The pool of destinations is a set of hand-built maps ... a derelict shopping market, a scrapyard, a fuel station, a cargo outpost, an orbital penal colony, a chapel and engineering wreck, an arena, a wooded biodome and a small NT ship." — the only configured pathDungeon value in the entire codebase is a single entry, `Maps/Shuttles/arrivals.yml`, commented "#for example, del this later" in Resources/Prototypes/SS220/Entities/Structures/Machines/gate_dungeon.yml. None of the cited Ruins maps (Arena, Broadaxe, CargoOutpost, GasStation, Market, Prison, Scrapyard, BDDarkForest) appear in that list or contain any GatewayDungeon marker entity. They are instead wired into the vanilla GridSpawn `ruins`/`satellites` random-spawn groups in Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Stations/base.yml — a portal-less, walk/shuttle-to-nearby-grid mechanic completely separate from the gateway system.
  - unsupported: "Certain long-range guns are locked so they will only fire once you are actually standing on the dungeon map" — the gate/gate-gun code (GateGunDungeonSystem cancelling shots unless the grid has GateDungeonMapComponent) exists, but a repo-wide search found zero placements of GateDungeonMapComponent on any map and zero weapon prototypes with GateGunDungeonComponent anywhere in Resources. As shipped, no gun is actually restricted by this system.

**sunrise**

*activity · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 4 forks carry it*

Salvagers who fly out from the station find a much wider spread of places to break into: hand-built wrecks the magnet drags in (a defib wreck, a spider-clan hulk, xeno and science chunks, a merc sand camp, a syndicate outpost), fixed space ruins like an abandoned DJ station, a derelict flagship and an ancient whiteship, and procedurally assembled sites that are stitched together from room chunks so the same "Soviet station", "pirate base" or "crashed ship" never has quite the same floorplan twice. The generated sites come with their own furniture: plastitanium boundary walls, locked syndicate airlocks (a small fraction of entrances are rigged with a landmine), wall-mounted defib and extinguisher cabinets, cabling and corridor trim. There are also several off-station grids the round drops people onto directly, including nuclear operative staging planets (lava and western flavoured), a lavaland outpost, arenas and a transit hub, and the harder salvage difficulty tiers only start showing up after the round has been running a while rather than being available from minute one.

- **Take** — It is a large, mostly data-only pile of off-station destinations, and the room-atlas approach means four hand-drawn map files turn into many differently-shaped ruins instead of the same wreck every round.
- **Skip** — The maps only mean anything once they are wired into the salvage/expedition rules that spawn them, the C# piece is a partial extension of an upstream prototype class (so upstream has to be edited to accept it), and every one of these grids becomes yours to keep compiling against upstream map-format and entity-prototype churn.
- **Touches** — cargo, salvage, antagonist
- **Needs** — [expedition-missions](#expedition-missions), [nuclear-operatives](#nuclear-operatives), [lavaland-mining-planet](#lavaland-mining-planet)
- **Verified** — supported. needs-upstream-edits holds, but for reasons well beyond and partly different from what the claim states. I fetched the 8 cited files plus browsed the live tree (sparse clone of space-sunrise/sunrise-station). The gameplay text checks out in remarkable detail: Dungeon/ has exactly the "four hand-drawn map files" (pirate_base.yml, ship_wreck.yml, soviet.yml, sovietWEH.yml) referenced by dungeonPreset room-pack atlases (confirms the "stitched from room chunks" claim); Salvage/ contains small-defibwreck.yml, small-johnspiderclan.yml, small-xenochunk.yml, small-scichunk.yml, small-mercsand.yml, large-syndieoutpost.yml — an exact match for "defib wreck, spider-clan hulk, xeno and science chunks, merc sand camp, syndicate outpost"; Ruins/ has djstation.yml, empty_flagship.yml, whiteship_ancient.yml matching "abandoned DJ station, derelict flagship, ancient whiteship"; Nonstations/ has nukieplanet_lava.yml, nukiewestern.yml, lavaland_outpost.yml, arena.yml/roundel-arena.yml, transit_hub(_big).yml — matching every off-station-grid claim. dungeon_configs.yml's SyndicateBaseEntrancePossiblyRigged table gives LandMineModular a 0.05 prob, matching "small fraction... rigged with a landmine." salvage_difficulties.yml sets delay: 180/600/1800/3600 on Moderate/Challenging/Difficult/Impossible, matching the round-time-gated-difficulty claim. On graft_shape: the claim's own stated reason (partial-class extension forces an upstream edit) is wrong for that file — upstream already marks the base class partial. But the real picture is worse for drop-in-ness than even the claim suggests: the fork's copies of upstream-path files Resources/Prototypes/Procedural/salvage_factions.yml, salvage_difficulties.yml (entirely wrapped in # Sunrise-Start/End), biome_ore_templates.yml and salvage_mods.yml all carry live Sunrise-Edit changes, and so do upstream C# files Content.Server/Procedural/DungeonSystem.cs, DungeonJob.AutoCabling.cs, DungeonJob.Ore.cs, DungeonJob.EntityTableDunGen.cs, and Content.Shared/Procedural/DungeonLayers/EntityTableDunGen.cs — none of which appear in evidence_cited. So the fork's own copy already patches upstream in place (fork-patches-upstream), and on top of that, actually wiring these dungeons/factions into a clean upstream tree would also require edits (integration-would-require-upstream-edits) since the current wiring lives inside those already-patched files.
  - unsupported: "the C# piece is a partial extension of an upstream prototype class (so upstream has to be edited to accept it)" — false as a specific mechanism: upstream space-wizards/space-station-14 already declares `Content.Shared/Procedural/SalvageDifficultyPrototype.cs` as `public sealed partial class`, so Sunrise's `SalvageDifficultyPrototype.Sunrise.cs` partial extension compiles against an unmodified upstream tree with zero edits for that specific mechanism.

**backmen, corvax, impstation, monolith, starlight, the-den**

*activity · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 4 forks carry it*

Mostly this is more places to fly to: hand-built wrecks and derelicts that salvagers cut into for loot, like a gas station, an abandoned hotel, a battleship hull, a research outpost, a vox saloon, a snowy sauna, a wizard's crashed shuttle and an arcade party shuttle, plus Soviet-camp and shipwreck room sets that get shuffled into procedural dungeons so the same ruin never looks quite the same twice. Backmen also swaps in Half-Life-flavoured hostiles for expedition sites (headcrabs, headcrab zombies, Xen creatures, Black Ops) and Monolith seeds asteroid fields with randomly sized gas pockets of every gas type and scrap piles that roll from a weighted loot table, so what you find in a rock is a gamble rather than a fixed payout. Monolith's other visible effect is janitorial: small, cheap, drifting hull fragments and stray mobs quietly vanish after a delay, so hours of salvage cutting does not leave the sector clogged with junk.

- **Take** — Ruin and wreck maps are the cheapest possible content-per-effort win: each one is a self-contained YAML grid that gives salvage crews somewhere new to go without touching a single system.
- **Skip** — The maps only appear if you also adopt the spawn plumbing that places them (expedition/dungeon tables, salvage magnet configs, or in The Den's case in-place rewrites of upstream Worldgen and Gateway), so "just take the maps" turns into wiring work plus ongoing merge pain on upstream files.
- **Touches** — cargo, salvage, science, engineering, all-players
- **Needs** — [expedition-missions](#expedition-missions)
- **Verified** — partly supported. Verified almost every specific detail in the description by cloning the actual repos and reading the files, not just the 8 cited paths. Confirmed: Backmen's salvage-faction.ftl + Procedural/salvage_factions.yml wire headcrabs/headcrab-zombies/Xen-creatures/Black-Ops into salvage expedition faction tables; Mono's gas_deposit.yml is a weighted VerySmall..VeryLarge table across every gas type feeding VgroidGasDepositTable (asteroids); Mono's scrap_processor.yml is a genuine weighted GroupSelector/NestedSelector loot table; Mono's GridCleanupSystem.cs deletes small, unpowered, cheap, player-less grid fragments after a delay, and a sibling MobCleanupSystem.cs (not cited, but present in the same _Mono/Cleanup folder) handles the 'stray mobs' half of that claim. Impstation's Resources/Maps/_Impstation/Ruins/ and /Salvage/ literally contain vox-saloon.yml, snowy-sauna.yml, wizwreck.yml, and arcade-party-shuttle.yml. Starlight's Procedural/Themes/soviet.yml and the cited ship_wreck.yml are exact structural twins (tagged dungeonRoom prototypes fed into procedural dungeon generation), directly confirming the 'Soviet-camp and shipwreck room sets shuffled into procedural dungeons' claim, and Maps/_Starlight/Dungeon/soviet-camp.yml exists too. Backmen's Corvax/Ruins folder literally has corvax_gas_station.yml and corvax_battleship.yml. The one specific claim that does NOT hold up is 'an abandoned hotel' (see overclaims). On graft_shape: The Den's own repo copy contains Content.Server/Worldgen/WorldGen.cs and Content.Server/Gateway/* sitting in plain, non-namespaced directories (not under a _TheDen prefix) — this structurally confirms 'fork-patches-upstream' for The Den specifically, exactly as the claim's skip_because states (I also confirmed vanilla space-wizards/space-station-14 has no such dirs on master, so these are genuinely fork-owned paths outside any fork namespace). Meanwhile Impstation/Mono/Starlight/Backmen's ruin content is fully self-contained under their own _Impstation/_Mono/_Starlight/_Backmen namespaces and would only need integration wiring (expedition tables, dungeon configs, salvage magnet configs) to graft in elsewhere — the 'integration-would-require-upstream-edits' reading. Both readings are genuinely present across this multi-fork unit, so the needs-upstream-edits graft_shape call is confirmed and the seed's blindness to in-place upstream edits (The Den case) was correctly overridden by the assessor.
  - unsupported: "an abandoned hotel" — the only 'Hotel' content found in these forks (Starlight's Resources/Prototypes/_Starlight/Maps/hotel.yml → Resources/Maps/_Starlight/Stations/Hotel.yml) is a full alternate playable STATION gameMap (StarlightHotel, minPlayers 7/maxPlayers 55, a complete StationJobs roster: Captain, HeadOfPersonnel, Bartender, ChiefEngineer, ChiefMedicalOfficer, etc., with its own emergency shuttle), not an abandoned ruin/derelict that 'salvagers cut into for loot' alongside the other wrecks listed.
