### Station goals

<a id="station-goals"></a>

A round-start, station-wide objective drawn from a prototype pool and delivered to the crew as a printed paper or fax announcement, with a CVar to enable it and an admin command to re-send it. Corvax-lineage and widely inherited. It is usually invisible to namespace-driven discovery because forks add it to un-namespaced `Content.Server/StationGoal/`, `Content.Shared/StationGoal/`, `Content.Shared/CCVar/CCVars.StationGoals.cs` and `Resources/Locale/en-US/station-goal/` rather than under a fork prefix.

**backmen, corvax, estacao-pirata, sunrise, the-den, white-dream**

*activity · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 2 forks carry it*

A few moments into the shift, every fax machine on the station prints an official-looking Central Command order (ASCII letterhead, station number, dated a thousand years out, signed by a randomly named CentComm officer) telling the whole crew what this round's project is. The orders are long, specific and station-wide: build a piloted shuttle with a named five-person crew, raise a museum with at least twenty exhibits and two per department, put up a singularity generator at a safe distance with class-3 containment, capture and document live space fauna in purpose-built xenobiology chambers, run a public lecture series with brochures, or hold a productivity banquet where heads award medals and then call the evac shuttle. Command reads the fax off the bridge printer and decides how hard to chase it; nothing enforces or scores completion, so it functions as a shared prompt that gives engineering, cargo, science and service a reason to work together instead of drifting. Admins can re-fax a specific goal by ID mid-round, and there is even a "bureaucratic error" goal that hands Command the job of inventing the station's objective themselves.

- **Take** — It is a very cheap way to give an otherwise aimless green-shift round a shared, department-crossing project, and the content is pure prose in a locale file, so tuning or writing new goals needs no code at all.
- **Skip** — Nothing tracks or rewards completion, so a goal only matters if the Captain and heads actually push it; on a low-pop or low-RP round the fax is read once and ignored, and the shipped Corvax-lineage goal texts are long, translated-from-Russian walls of numbered requirements that would need a full rewrite pass to sound like your fork.
- **Touches** — command, engineering, cargo, science, service, security, all-players
- **Verified** — supported. I fetched the actual TheDen fork files (all 4 cited evidence paths return 200 there, plus WWhiteDream duplicates them; Corvax's own implementation lives in a different namespaced location Content.Server/Corvax/StationGoal). The station-goals.ftl text confirms every specific claim verbatim: museum needs 20+ exhibits with 2 per department, xenobiology needs two containment chambers, the shuttle needs a 5-role crew (pilot/2 engineers/medic/security), the singularity goal requires class-3 containment, the productivity-banquet goal has heads award a medal then call the evac shuttle, and station-goal-bureaucraticerror literally hands Command the job of writing its own goal. StationGoalPaperSystem.cs confirms the fax-on-round-start mechanic, the DateTime.Now.AddYears(1000) thousand-years-out date, and the random signer name from a LocalizedDatasetPrototype; StationGoalCommand.cs confirms the admin-only `sendstationgoal <id>` console command. CCVars.StationGoals.cs and the system code show no completion tracking, supporting 'nothing enforces or scores completion.' Critically, I traced Content.Shared/Fax/Components/FaxMachineComponent.cs — a genuine upstream vanilla file (headers by DrSmugleaf, Eoin Mcloughlin, etc.) — and found it already carries a fork-added `ReceiveStationGoal` field at the vanilla path, proving the fork itself edited an upstream file in place to wire faxes into this feature. That confirms 'needs-upstream-edits' is correct, and both upstream_reading senses apply: the fork's own tree really does patch an upstream file, and grafting this into another codebase's Fax system would require the identical edit there.
  - unsupported: "build a piloted shuttle with a named five-person crew" — the actual station-goal-shuttle text specifies role counts (1 pilot, 2 engineers, 1 medic/chemist, 1 security officer = 5 total) but does not name individual crew members; "named" overstates what the FTL text contains.

### Xenoarchaeology and anomaly extensions

<a id="xenoarchaeology-and-anomalies"></a>

Additional artifact node effects and activation triggers, anomaly behaviours and the scanners and analysis consoles that probe them.

**impstation**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · high confidence · 1 forks carry it*

Artifacts get a much wider menu of things that set them off and things they do when they go off: a corpse being revived nearby, someone being stunned, an emote, a natural 20 on a die roll, and a long list of specific drinks splashed on them (a martini, a Manly Dorf, an ice cream, a Syndicate Bomb) each unlock certain nodes, so a scientist ends up dragging the bartender's stock and a defibrillator into the artifact chamber instead of just cycling gases. New node effects include getting your DNA permanently scrambled, being temporarily turned into a bee, a clown spider or an immovable rod, the artifact becoming a random instrument or a working gun, clouds of nasty drug foam, and a spawn table of angry fauna up to a dungeon dragon. Science can also build an Advanced Node Scanner, a linked machine that reveals one more layer of the node tree, shows the exact unlock timer, highlights which nodes fired this session, splits the console's "Down" button into left/right/random so you can steer the tree deliberately, and pays 5% more research points. Separately, anomalites are floating ghost-role critters born from anomaly cores (fire, gravity, ice, flesh and more) that can vent-crawl, be petted, carry a pinpointer to their own core, and are killed for a core when destroyed.

- **Take** — It turns xenoarchaeology from a gas-and-tool checklist into a scavenger hunt that pulls the scientist into contact with bar, medbay and the rest of the station, and the Advanced Node Scanner gives the role a real progression upgrade instead of more of the same.
- **Skip** — The trigger and effect tables overwrite the upstream random pools and reference dozens of specific reagent and mob prototype ids (including fork-only drinks like ThavenBad and VoxRocks), so it breaks on any upstream rebalance of xenoarch and needs a prototype-id audit before it will even load; the Advanced Node Scanner's extra readouts and the split Down button also have to be wired into the upstream analysis console UI.
- **Touches** — science, ghost-roles, service, medical, salvage
- **Needs** — [food-and-drink-expansion](#food-and-drink-expansion)
- **Verified** — partly supported. Directly fetched Resources/Prototypes/XenoArch/triggers.yml and effects.yml (vanilla, non-namespaced paths) and found hundreds of \"# imp edit\"/\"# imp addition\" comments threaded through the same prototype IDs (DefaultTriggers, and dozens of individual node effects) that the fork's own history shows it edited in place — not a separate override file, an actual in-place patch of the vanilla file. Content.Client/Xenoarchaeology/Ui/AnalysisConsoleMenu.xaml.cs (also non-namespaced) is similarly patched with \"//imp\" markers to wire in the Advanced Node Scanner's split Down button and point-bonus display. This fully substantiates the claim's own downgrade from the drop-in seed to needs-upstream-edits.
  - unsupported: "New node effects include ... the artifact becoming a random instrument or a working gun" — XenoArtifactBecomeRandomInstrument and XenoArtifactGun are pre-existing vanilla SS14 effect entities (defined at lines 518/650 of the vanilla Resources/Prototypes/XenoArch/effects.yml), not new effects authored by the fork. The fork's own "imp edit" comments show it disabled these two from the default handheld table ("removed until we have value-based system" / "conflicts with default interaction") and instead re-enabled them only for natural artifacts in a new _Impstation-only table. The player-visible outcome is real, but framing it as a new node effect the fork built is inaccurate.

**sunrise**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 1 forks carry it*

Artifacts do a lot more, and go wrong in more interesting ways. On top of the usual pool, a node can heal everyone nearby, quietly turn the artifact into a 20 kW power source, make it wander off across the lab on its own, bolt every airlock in the room, shatter windows, spit lightning arcs for ten seconds, starve or parch everyone in radius, set them on fire, EMP the department, or spawn an evil twin of a crewmember. A separate "funny" pool turns everyone caught in the blast into chairs, tables, watermelons, disposal bins or a loose appendix for two minutes, teleport-shuffles everybody within thirty tiles, scrambles nearby items into random other items, drags people in with a gravity well, or garbles all speech for ten minutes. Unlocking nodes also gets new levers: a node can be triggered by scanning the artifact with a health analyzer, or by dosing it with exotic gases like BZ, healium, nitrium, halon, pluoxium, zauker, hydrogen or electrovae, so xenoarchaeologists have to go bother atmos and chemistry to finish a node. Artifacts can vent those same gases back out when they fire. There is also a syndicate "anomagen" auto-injector: jab a humanoid with it and about a minute later, after cellular damage and rainbow hallucinations, they burst into a live anomaly, plus a thrown artifact-spawned version that injects whoever it hits.

- **Take** — It multiplies the payoff variety and the trigger vocabulary of an existing science loop, pulling atmos and medical gear into xenoarchaeology instead of leaving it a solo minigame.
- **Skip** — A third of the new content is bolted to non-upstream exotic gases, and several effects (paradox-clone spawns, random-prototype transformation with a hand-maintained blacklist, item shuffles over thirty tiles) are chaos generators you will spend admin time cleaning up after.
- **Touches** — science, epistemics, atmospherics, antagonist, all-players
- **Needs** — [exotic-gas-expansion](#exotic-gas-expansion), [paradox-clone](#paradox-clone)
- **Verified** — partly supported. Every specific mechanical claim checked out against source: effects.yml gave the 20kW PowerSupplier, 10s LightningArcShooter, 30-tile XAEShuffle, 600s (10 min) AnomalyAccent, 2-minute polymorph comments for chair/watermelon/appendix/disposal/table, and the hand-maintained ArtifactRandomTransformation blacklist. triggers.yml confirmed the health-analyzer trigger and the full exotic-gas trigger list (BZ, Healium, Nitrium, Halon, Pluoxium, Zauker, Hydrogen, Electrovae, plus a few more). The two syndicate components (AnomalyAutoInjectorComponent: 60s delay, 50 cellular damage, rainbow hallucination; XenoArtifactThrowingAutoInjectorComponent) matched the anomagen/thrown-injector description closely, down to the uplink localization keys and 'artifact particles' item description. Only the specific claim that finishing a node requires bothering chemistry (not just atmos) isn't shown by any file I read — the gas triggers are pure atmos/reagent-reaction hooks with no chemistry-department tie called out. On graft_shape: the path-data 'drop-in' seed is wrong and the assessor's 'needs-upstream-edits' is right for a stronger reason than the depends_on list states — I found actual in-place patches in vanilla (non-underscore) files: Content.Shared/Xenoarchaeology/Artifact/SharedXenoArtifactSystem.XAT.cs has a 'Sunrise added' block wiring EntityAnalyzedEvent into XAT relays and imports Content.Shared._Sunrise.Research.Artifact directly, Content.Shared/Xenoarchaeology/Artifact/XAT/BaseQueryUpdateXATSystem.cs has a 'Sunrise-Edit' marker gating the node-update loop on artifact attachment, and Content.Server/Xenoarchaeology/Equipment/ArtifactAnalyzerSystem.cs carries a 'Sunrise-Edit' comment too. That is fork-patches-upstream, not merely integration-would-require-edits. Separately, the depends_on claims (exotic-gas-expansion, paradox-clone) also verified: the exotic gases live in Resources/Prototypes/_Sunrise/Reagents/gases.yml (a distinct fork feature) and ParadoxCloneSpawn is a separate storytellerMetadata/game-rule entry in _Sunrise/GameRules/storyteller_metadata.yml, so this unit is entangled with two other fork subsystems on top of patching upstream.
  - unsupported: so xenoarchaeologists have to go bother atmos and chemistry to finish a node

**ephemeral-space**

*structural · entangled · high confidence · 1 forks carry it*

Partway through the round the station announces a "teleportation phenomenon" and extradimensional anomalies materialise around the station, each one flagged as a threat that must be dealt with before the station's warp drive terminal will finish charging. To clear one, a crewmember scans it with a probe (a short work timer per scan) which fills in that anomaly's collapse sequence on the "Probomaly Buster 30k" console: a four-step string of greek-letter frequencies, shown one revealed step at a time with the rest as question marks. A second tool, the resonator, is dialled to a frequency by right-click menu and beamed at the anomaly; hit the right frequency in sequence and it stabilises and shrinks, guess wrong and it fires a lethal radiation pulse at whoever is standing there. Station-wide announcements call out where each anomaly died and how many remain, and once the last one is cleared the warp drive can advance to its next stage, culminating in the station physically relocating and the round ending.

- **Take** — It turns anomalies into a genuine multi-person puzzle with a bluff-or-die failure state (wrong frequency irradiates you) and wires the result straight into round progression, so clearing them is something the whole station cares about rather than a science-department side task.
- **Skip** — It is not a standalone anomaly feature: the anomalies exist to gate a warp-drive charging sequence that also calls the shuttle and ends the round, and the code hangs off the fork's own announcement, spark, despawn-timer and station-stage systems, so grafting it means importing that whole round structure or rewriting the half that makes it matter.
- **Touches** — science, engineering, command, all-players
- **Needs** — [warp-drive](#warp-drive), [custom-station-events](#custom-station-events), [shared-utility-libraries](#shared-utility-libraries)
- **Verified** — unsupported. The claim's own downgrade from the seed's 'drop-in' guess to 'entangled' is directionally right and, if anything, understates the problem: this is not merely code entangled with the fork's warp-drive/announcement/utility systems, it appears to be an entirely superseded, unwired subsystem. I confirmed via a full-repo tarball search that ESPortalAnomalyComponent, ESPortalEventThreatComponent and ESPortalGeneratorComponent are never attached to any entity prototype, the anomaly console isn't placed on the fork's map, and the fork's own player-facing Guidebook entry for the Warp Drive describes a completely different mechanic (charge-over-time interrupted by clogged junk items, cleared by a 3-terminal security override shared with the traitor nuke system) with zero mention of anomalies, probes, resonators, or threats. The cited evidence files are real code that matches the claim's narrative almost verbatim, but that code path does not appear to be what actually runs in the live game — it reads as dead/legacy design replaced by ESWarpDriveSystem.cs. Grafting it would mean reviving orphaned code and writing the game-rule wiring the fork itself never finished, on top of the dependencies (ESSparksSystem, ESTimedDespawnSystem, ESAnnouncementSystem, the fork's custom announcement/round-end plumbing) the claim already lists — so 'entangled' still holds, arguably as a floor rather than an accurate ceiling.
  - unsupported: "Partway through the round the station announces a 'teleportation phenomenon' and extradimensional anomalies materialise around the station, each one flagged as a threat that must be dealt with before the station's warp drive terminal will finish charging." — the live in-game Guidebook entry for the Warp Drive (Resources/ServerInfo/_ES/Guidebook/Mechanics/WarpDrive.xml) describes charging being interrupted by random 'clogs' (junk items thrown/spawned into the drive that crew must pick up), with no mention of anomalies, threats, or announcements about them.
  - unsupported: "a crewmember scans it with a probe ... which fills in that anomaly's collapse sequence on the ... console: a four-step string of greek-letter frequencies" and "the resonator, is dialled to a frequency ... beamed at the anomaly ... guess wrong and it fires a lethal radiation pulse" — none of the components this loop depends on (ESPortalAnomalyComponent, ESPortalEventThreatComponent) are ever attached to any entity prototype anywhere in the repo (checked all 2049 .yml files), and the 'Probomaly Buster 30k' anomaly console (ESComputerAnomaly) is not placed on the fork's only station map (toast.yml), while the warp-drive terminal and machine are. There is no concrete GameRule that spawns an anomaly: GameRules/portal_events.yml defines only an abstract, never-subclassed ESBasePortalEvent.
  - unsupported: "once the last one is cleared the warp drive can advance to its next stage, culminating in the station physically relocating and the round ending" — the currently active warp-drive game rule (ESWarpDriveGameRuleComponent / ESWarpDriveSystem.cs, wired to the map-placed ESMachineScienceWarpDrive and ESBaseComputerTerminalWarpDrive) gates the round-ending final phase on charge percentage plus a 3-terminal security override shared with the crypto-nuke system, not on any anomaly/threat count — ESPortalGeneratorConsoleBuiState carries Charge/Interrupted/FinalPhase/AllTerminals fields, no ThreatsLeft field exists in the live UI state at all.

**frontier, goobstation, serbia-strong**

*activity · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 1 forks carry it*

Three small additions on top of the artifact and anomaly loop science already plays. Goob gives artifacts four new stimuli that only fire when you flood them with exotic gases (BZ, Nitrium, Healium, Pluoxium), so unlocking certain nodes means dragging a canister of the right gas over from atmos instead of just poking the thing. Frontier adds two new node reactions (one coughs up a handful of anomalite crystals, one spawns a hostile grimforged construct at your feet), renames the artifact danger tiers to a mystical scale from Hylic up to Monadic, and puts a points-earned and expected-anomalite-yield readout on the anomaly scanner while making anomaly vessels refuse to work if the anomaly drifts off your grid. SS220 hands out a random reward from a big loot table (crusher glaive, void jetpack, industrial welder, energy dagger, chameleon hat and so on) when a team fully explores an artifact, so finishing a tree is worth chasing rather than abandoning half-done.

- **Take** — Cheap, mostly-YAML content that gives xenoarchaeology more to do: new stimuli that pull atmos into science's problem, and a completion reward that makes finishing an artifact tree feel worth the shift.
- **Skip** — It is three unrelated bolt-ons rather than one system, and each one leans on something you may not have: the Goob triggers need the /tg/ exotic gases, the Frontier effects need anomalite and the grimforged mob, and the SS220 reward table names dozens of items and blueprints that would each have to exist or be swapped out.
- **Touches** — science, salvage, cargo, atmospherics
- **Needs** — [exotic-gas-expansion](#exotic-gas-expansion), [hostile-fauna-and-npcs](#hostile-fauna-and-npcs)
- **Verified** — supported. Every specific claim checks out: Goob's triggers.yml defines exactly the four gas stimuli named (BZ/Nitrium/Healium/Pluoxium, labeled '# /tg/ gas triggers'), and I confirmed via a sparse clone of vanilla space-station-14 that none of these four gases exist upstream at all - they're Goobstation's own _Goobstation/Reagents/gases.yml addition, so the xenoarch trigger really does depend on a sibling Goob unit. Frontier's effects.yml has exactly the two reactions described (MobGrimForged spawn, MaterialAnomalite1 x1-3 spawn), both of which resolve to real entities defined elsewhere in Frontier's own _NF tree (Entities/Mobs/NPCs/artifact_construct.yml, Entities/Materials/materials.yml), confirmed by sparse-cloning frontier-station-14. artifact-component.ftl has the exact 8-tier Hylic-to-Monadic scale, anomaly.ftl has the exact scanner readout strings and the vessel off-grid message. SS220's bonus-for-fully-discovered-tables.yml loot list contains every named item (crusher glaive, void jetpack, industrial welder, energy dagger, chameleon hat). Crucially, I went beyond the cited evidence and cloned SS220's Content.Shared/Xenoarchaeology tree: the consumer logic (CheckFullyDiscoveredBonus/SpawnBonus - 'all nodes unlocked, throw a random item from BonusTable') is not a separate SS220-namespaced file, it's spliced directly into upstream Content.Shared/Xenoarchaeology/Artifact/SharedXenoArtifactSystem.cs, SharedXenoArtifactSystem.Node.cs, and XenoArtifactComponent.cs with inline '// SS220-BonusForFullyDiscovered - start/end' markers. That is exactly the in-place upstream edit the seed's path-data-only view couldn't see (it only surfaced the standalone prototype yml, not the patched .cs files), so the drop-in seed is wrong and the claim's needs-upstream-edits label is right, just for a stronger reason than the claim gave (it argued only sibling-unit entanglement for Goob/Frontier and never mentioned SS220's actual upstream C# patch).

### Item enchantment and granted abilities

<a id="item-enchantment-and-grants"></a>

Frameworks that bolt extra powers onto items or people: magical enchantments, clothing that grants components, intrinsic augments, cantrips and recallable soul-bound items.

**starlight**

*loop-change · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 9 forks carry it*

Characters get a tray of personal ability buttons that come from what they are and what they are wearing or have installed, rather than from an item held in hand. A Resomi or a moth can leap across a room (moths get three short hops that recharge, cats get a quiet pounce), someone with a jetpack or a piledriver leg gets a longer jump, a small character can drop low and sneak under tables and machinery (you move unseen but you can't attack, pick things up or use anything until you stand back up), a spider can spin webs on the floor and lay eggs into a cocoon, a cyborg or augmented crewmember can toggle a limb off, pop open a storage compartment built into their leg, run a cooling unit, or snap out a set of claws that only work while gloves are on. Some abilities freeze a victim in place or wrap them up, and implants give one-shot panic buttons: teleport yourself far away, melt all your gear off your body, self-destruct. There is also a recall power that makes a bound item vanish and rematerialise in your hand on command ("The sword materialises in your hand!"), plus a mouth-storage slot others can notice when they examine you.

- **Take** — One shared plumbing layer lets any species, organ, implant or worn item grant a real ability button, so future fork content ships as a few lines of YAML instead of a new C# system each time.
- **Skip** — The framework is thin but the useful half of the catalogue is wired into Starlight's own cyber-limbs, storage organs, vent crawling, changeling and devil content, and every ability still has to be hung off an upstream species, organ or implant prototype by hand, so you inherit a permanent merge-conflict surface for content you may not want.
- **Touches** — all-players, antagonist, security, ghost-roles, medical
- **Needs** — [species-racial-abilities](#species-racial-abilities), [cybernetic-augments](#cybernetic-augments)
- **Verified** — partly supported. Nearly every concrete detail in the gameplay paragraph checks out against the actual fetched files: JumpMoth has LimitedCharges maxCharges 3 + AutoRecharge (three recharging hops), JumpCat has a commented-out sound line joking about being silent (quiet pounce), JumpJet/JumpPilebunkerLeg give longer jumps, crawl-under-objects.ftl confirms the can't-attack/pickup/use-while-sneaking restriction, spider.ftl confirms web placement and cocoon egg-injection, claws.yml confirms claws are gated on the gloves slot with isCybernetic:true, common.yml confirms limb toggle/leg storage/cooling unit actions, implant.yml confirms one-shot (LimitedCharges 1) teleport (bluespace/redspace, description literally says 'teleports the user far away'), gear-melt (GearAcidifier, 'melting your equipment but leaving your body intact'), and self-destruct (Terminator/Xenoroach) implants, summon.ftl confirms the recall/vanish item wording almost verbatim, and mouth-storage.ftl confirms the examine-visible mouth slot. The one detail I could not back with any cited or discovered file is 'freeze a victim in place or wrap them up' — flagged as an overclaim. On graft_shape: I dug past the cited evidence to find where JumpMoth actually gets attached (Resources/Prototypes/_Starlight/Entities/Mobs/Species/moth.yml, 'type: Jump / action: JumpMoth' on the BaseMobMoth entity) — that attachment file is itself inside the fork's own _Starlight namespace (Starlight fully re-declares species mob entities there rather than patching the vanilla file in place, consistent with their 'great migration' commits), so the claim's own wiring is self-contained today. But I also found genuine upstream-path files this feature's species dependency touches directly in place — Resources/Prototypes/Species/moth.yml (non-_Starlight path) carries inline '# Starlight' edits, and Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Mobs/Player/humanoid.yml likewise — confirming the fork does patch upstream files for the surrounding species system generally, even though the specific ability-grant wiring sits in fork-owned files. Both readings are therefore real: the fork's own tree does include edits to upstream-path files in the dependency chain, and separately, grafting this into another codebase's vanilla species/organ/implant prototypes would require editing those upstream files there too.
  - unsupported: "Some abilities freeze a victim in place or wrap them up" — none of the cited evidence files show a freeze/immobilize or wrap-up ability; the spider files only cover placing webs and injecting eggs into a cocoon (target-side mechanics, not a freeze/immobilize-the-victim ability), and no changeling/devil file was cited or found to back a freeze/wrap claim.

**goobstation**

*loop-change · entangled · medium confidence · 9 forks carry it*

Players can take gear to a magical altar, lay it out with a special "source" item and an enchanting tool, and watch a shimmering aura settle over it, permanently bolting on a named power that shows up when anyone examines the item. The roster is openly Minecraft-flavoured: Sharpness and Fire Aspect and Knockback for melee weapons, Thorns and Protection and Fire Protection for armour, Fortune for pickaxes and drills so mining pulls extra ore, Lavaforged boots that let you stroll through lava, Unslippable shoes, Slippery on anything you want to grease, Unbreaking so an item stops taking wear, and Insulated to turn any glove (or Hamlet) into real insuls. Most enchants stack in levels shown as roman numerals up to II-V, some enchants refuse to sit alongside their opposites, and the way you push an item to a higher tier is to kill a player-controlled mob on top of the altar, which announces to everyone nearby that their soul has empowered the item.

- **Take** — A single small framework that makes almost every existing item category more interesting, with an immediately legible Minecraft vocabulary players already understand and a built-in dark twist (soul sacrifice) that generates its own stories.
- **Skip** — The tier-upgrade path is a ritual murder mechanic wired directly into Goob's devil/Condemned system, so grafting it whole either drags that antag content along or means rewriting the upgrade loop; and the balance surface is wide (Sharpness V melee, Protection IV armour, free insuls, boosted ore yields all land at once) so it needs real tuning rather than a straight port.
- **Touches** — all-players, security, cargo, salvage, engineering, antagonist
- **Needs** — [devil-pacts](#devil-pacts)
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as needs upstream edits, corrected by the verifier. All 16 cited files check out almost exactly as described: the enchant roster (Sharpness/Fire Aspect/Knockback/Thorns/Protection/Fire Protection/Fortune/Lavaforged/Unslippable/Slippery/Unbreaking/Insulated), roman-numeral levels (maxLevel 2-5), incompatible-enchant blocking, and the sacrifice-based tier upgrade (EnchantSacrificeSystem.cs killing a player-mob on an altar, popping \"enchanting-sacrifice-single/multiple\") are all real and accurately paraphrased — this is a well-evidenced, carefully-read claim overall. But two things need correcting: (1) enchanting is gated to a CanEnchantComponent (Chaplain/Heretic/Wizard per the source comment), not open to \"players\" generally, and (2) the one real dependency I found (EnchantSacrificeSystem -> Devil.Condemned) is itself a fork-namespaced module, not an upstream file — I found zero evidence files or referenced components outside Content.Goobstation.*/Resources/Prototypes/_Goobstation/Resources/Locale/_Goobstation directories. That makes \"needs-upstream-edits\" an imprecise label for what is really a fork-internal entanglement with the devil-pacts feature; \"entangled\" is the more accurate shape, and neither of the two given upstream_reading definitions cleanly applies since the coupling isn't with upstream at all.
  - unsupported: "Players can take gear to a magical altar, lay it out with a special \"source\" item and an enchanting tool, and watch a shimmering aura settle over it" — implies any player can perform an enchant. Content.Goobstation.Shared/Enchanting/Components/CanEnchantComponent.cs gates this behind a component whose doc comment says \"Place this on any entity you want to allow to enchant... e.g. Chaplain, Heretic or Wizard\"; EnchanterSystem.cs pops \"enchanter-disallowed-enchant\" (\"You are not worthy!\") at anyone lacking it. This is a role-gated ritual for a handful of religious/magic-flavoured roles, not a general player action.
  - unsupported: The claim's own graft_shape="needs-upstream-edits" plus depends_on:["devil-pacts"] frames this as an upstream dependency, but the actual coupling (EnchantSacrificeSystem.cs importing Content.Goobstation.Shared.Devil.Condemned.CondemnedComponent) is entirely within the fork's own _Goobstation/Goobstation.* namespace — no evidence file, nor any file I could find in Content.Goobstation.Shared/Enchanting or Resources/Prototypes/_Goobstation/Enchants, touches an upstream directory. This is a fork-internal cross-feature dependency (entangled with the devil-pacts antagonist system), not an upstream-edit requirement in the sense the label implies.

**serbia-strong**

*cosmetic · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 9 forks carry it*

While you are temporarily turned into something else, a small two-digit countdown appears in your status icons ticking down the seconds you have left in that form, so you can time when to slip back before it drops you. The transformations shipped here are a wizard action that turns you into a spider ghost and a 35-second astral form for the fork's cult creature, each with its own entry and exit sound, and both snap you back to your real body if you go into crit or die. Separately, some items visibly flip between an on and an off look when you click them in hand, so a device reads as active or idle at a glance.

- **Take** — The countdown-digit alert is a genuinely reusable readability win: any timed transformation, buff or ability in your fork can show players exactly how many seconds remain instead of leaving them guessing.
- **Skip** — SS220 files carry an explicit EULA/CLA with a hosting restriction rather than AGPL, so grafting them is a licensing problem before it is a code problem, and what you actually get is a HUD widget plus two polymorph configs that point at their cult and wizard mobs, not a reusable enchantment framework.
- **Touches** — antagonist, all-players
- **Needs** — [wizard-magic](#wizard-magic), [blood-cult](#blood-cult)
- **Verified** — partly supported; assessed as drop-in, corrected by the verifier. The countdown's tick logic is not in the unit's SS220 files: SharedPolymorphTimerSystem only shows/clears the alert, while the actual AlertTime update lives in an SS220 patch block (//SS220-cult-hotfix-23-start #3988, ~lines 90-98) inside the upstream file Content.Server/Polymorph/Systems/PolymorphSystem.cs, which I read directly; without that upstream patch the recommended countdown widget never updates, so drop-in is wrong and the fork demonstrably patches upstream.
  - unsupported: "each with its own entry and exit sound" - only the MiGoInAstral polymorph defines polymorphSound/exitPolymorphSound (migo_astral_in/out.ogg); the full WizardSpiderGhost config contains no sound fields at all.
  - unsupported: "While you are temporarily turned into something else, a small two-digit countdown appears in your status icons" - implies both shipped transformations show it; only MobAstralMiGo carries PolymorphTimer (in migo_astral.yml), and the wizard spider ghost polymorph has no duration and no timer component, so it never shows a countdown.
  - unsupported: "some items visibly flip between an on and an off look when you click them in hand" - no item prototype consuming ToggleAppearanceOnUse was found in the cited files or via search, and the system subscribes to ActivateInWorldEvent, not an in-hand use event; the 'some items' consumer claim is unverified.

### Fishing minigame

<a id="fishing"></a>

Rods, lures and fishing spots with a timing minigame that yields fish, sometimes backed by its own points economy and vendor.

**goobstation, impstation, rmc14**

*activity · needs upstream edits · medium confidence · 4 forks carry it*

Grab a fishing rod, walk to a patch of "suspicious waves" (water, lava, plasma, or a toilet), and cast your lure. After a wait something bites, and you get a tug-of-war: you keep working the rod to fill a progress bar while the fish periodically fights back and drags it down, with messages like "You feel something clinging to the fishing lure!" and "You lost control over the rod!" if it pulls too far and snaps free. Win and you haul up the catch, which is usually junk (scrap, maintenance trash, the odd bit of salvage treasure or a tool) but sometimes a live fish that flops around suffocating in your hands, can be butchered into fish meat for the kitchen, or sold to cargo for a few hundred spesos. Rare pulls include joke catches like an alien fish, a fish shaped like the nuke disk, and a fish version of Ian. RMC-14's take is a slower version of the same idea: plant the pole, wait five to ten seconds, then react inside a one- or two-second bite window, with a bait slot you can load to shift the odds toward rarer loot (ores, high-capacity cells, a clown burger). Impstation's "fishing rod" is not really fishing at all, it fires a hook that reels whatever it hits back toward you, with a plasma variant and a changeling flesh-tentacle version that yanks people across the room.

- **Take** — A self-contained idle activity with a real skill check and a loot table, giving quiet crew and bored departments something to do that also feeds the kitchen and cargo sale loops.
- **Skip** — The rod and minigame are only half the feature: fishing spots are anchored entities that have to be hand-placed on your station maps (and the toilet-fishing variant means editing upstream toilet prototypes), so a clean file-level copy lands you a working rod with nowhere to use it, and the three forks' versions are incompatible designs you would have to pick between rather than combine.
- **Touches** — service, cargo, all-players, salvage, antagonist
- **Verified** — partly supported. Every load-bearing gameplay beat checks out against the actual files: fishing.ftl has the exact quoted strings, FishingRodComponent.cs/ActiveFisherComponent.cs implement the progress/struggle tug-of-war, fishingspots.yml names the spot "suspicious waves", loot_tables.yml has the scrap/trash/salvage/maint-tools split plus the named joke fish (FishAlien, FishNukeDisk, FishIan) and per-biome tables (Water/Lava/Plasma/Toilet), fish.yml shows Butcherable->FoodMeatFish and Asphyxiation-based suffocation with StaticPrice 250-750. Impstation's fishing_rods.yml confirms it is really a Gun/BasicEntityAmmoProvider harpoon, not a minigame, with a plasma variant and a changeling-only "FishingRodLing" that hooks people. RMC-14's RMCFishingComponents.cs confirms the deploy/wait/bite state machine (WaitMin 5s/WaitMax 10s) and a bait component that shifts rarity-tier weights, and fishing.yml lists the ore/PowerCellHigh/FoodBurgerClown loot named in the claim. The one soft overclaim is rounding RMC's 0.5-2s bite window to "one- or two-second." On graft_shape: I found direct proof the assessor's own graft_shape call is right, though not from the cited evidence list — Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Structures/Furniture/toilet.yml (a plain upstream path, outside any _Goobstation directory) has been patched in place with a `type: FishingSpot` component and a physics fixture, both bracketed by "# Goobstation - fishing" comments. That is fork-patches-upstream in the literal sense the path-data seed could not see. Separately, FishingSpotWater is a placement:SnapgridCenter anchored entity with no spawner system, so getting fishing spots onto any station's map (this fork's own or a recipient's) is a second, independent upstream-edit requirement — integration-would-require-upstream-edits. Both readings are true here, which also means the seed's 'drop-in' guess was wrong for a reason more concrete than the claim itself demonstrates.
  - unsupported: RMC-14's bite window is described as "one- or two-second" but RMCFishingRodComponent.cs sets BiteMin = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(0.5) and BiteMax = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2) — the true floor is half a second, not one full second.
